subject.detail: The SURF-007 verdict of this campaign read 'the built board's rows carry no trailing controls at all' and 'the build also truncates the column that exists to explain'. Photographed at the design's own 1156pt, every Cleanup row carries `Inspect` and `Remove...`. The controls were outside the 980pt capture the verdict was written against. This is the failure mode the campaign already knows in a different costume: a picture that claims a subject it cannot support. The subject here was right and the frame was wrong, which is harder to see, because nothing about a correctly-named capture of a too-narrow window looks incorrect. The old verdict is kept and marked superseded rather than deleted. Fixed by photographing at the design's window size with a setframe readback guard that refuses to write a capture the window clamped.
subject.title: a capture width narrower than the design's made real controls invisible, and a witness verdict recorded them as missing

subject.detail: `campaign.py` keeps defects in `inventory.json` under a `defect` list, and `add` assigns the next id from that list. `defects.in.json` is an input file. Twelve defects found in the sittings of 19 and 20 Aug were written straight into the input file with hand-written ids taken from that file's own length, which had stopped tracking the registry at DEF-006. The result: DEF-007 through DEF-018 each named one defect in the registry and a different one in the staging file, and neither file said so. Visible symptom, and the only reason it was caught: `RUN-2026-08-20.md` contains 'DEF-011 is the finding worth acting on ... Cleanup's' at line 96 and 'DEF-011 - the rendered-quality gate has never been able to run' at line 481, in one document, meaning two unrelated things. This is `capture-lineage`'s failure mode moved from pictures to identifiers: a name binding to two subjects with nothing checking the binding. Fixed by renumbering the twelve staged defects to DEF-034..DEF-045, merging them into the registry, and rewriting the fifteen references that meant the staged numbering. Every renumbered record carries `stagedAs` naming its old local id, so a reader meeting the old number in an untouched artifact can resolve it. The remaining 74 references were checked one at a time and meant the registry defect they already named. A fourth lesson, from the third instance's cleanup rather than from the collision itself. Reconstructing the concurrent session's two entries welded `text: ""` and `note: ""` onto both, and the first renumbering pass then used `"text" in d` to tell the two writers' entries apart -- so the artifact defeated the discriminator that would have caught it. Both authors independently read the empty values as harmless because they carried no content. The hazard is shape, not content: a membership test reads a key's PRESENCE, and an empty string defeats `"text" in d` exactly as thoroughly as a populated one would. `campaign.py add` injects only `id`, `status`, `evidence` and `armed`, so that key-shape occurred on exactly the two reconstructed entries and was traceable; the keys were stripped and the pass re-run discriminating on `title`. Recorded because "empty therefore harmless" is a reasonable-sounding wrong answer that both sessions gave.
subject.note: SECOND INSTANCE, 20 Aug 2026, in the case registry rather than the defect registry, and it landed the same way. A helper reported `next case id: CASE-0145` while cases.json already held CASE-0149 and CASE-0150; campaign.py's own `next_id` is max+1 and would have said CASE-0151, so the number that was trusted did not come from it. `add` takes an explicit id through `setdefault` and therefore appends a second entry rather than refusing, so CASE-0149 and CASE-0150 each came to name two cases -- an iOS Settings structural case against REQ-005 and a RouterCore write-failure case against REQ-019 -- and the `set` calls that followed wrote onto the pre-existing pair. Caught by an evidence-existence audit rather than by any gate: the new cases printed `3 evidence` where two were supplied. Restored from `git show HEAD:` (both pre-existing entries are byte-identical to HEAD again, verified by dict comparison) and the new pair renumbered to CASE-0153 and CASE-0154. The registry is sparse -- 74 gaps between 1 and 152 -- so a free-looking number is not evidence that it is free, and only max+1 is. THIRD INSTANCE, the same evening, and this one had two writers rather than one. A second Claude session working the same campaign allocated DEF-047 and DEF-048 at about 23:30 (the SDK -32603 message discard, and a detector defect in vacuity-check.py's blind pass) and committed planning/test-campaign as a directory in 6bdeea4, which also swept up this session's in-progress registry edits. This session allocated DEF-047 and DEF-048 for different defects minutes later, from a read taken before that commit landed. Resolved by renumbering THIS session's pair to DEF-049 and DEF-050 -- the later allocation moves, and the session that moves is the one that can enumerate its own references, which is the only reason the choice is safe rather than arbitrary. The peer's entries were not edited. Note for anyone reading the mechanism: `add` assigns from the registry list, so two writers holding a stale read get the same number, and no gate in the campaign detects it. The detection here was a peer message, and before that an evidence-existence audit; neither is a gate. campaign.py could refuse an explicit id that already exists -- `add` currently takes one through `setdefault` and appends a duplicate instead.
subject.title: the campaign's own defect ids named two different defects each, because the staging file numbered from its own length

subject.detail: DETECTOR DEFECT, recorded so its numbers are not published as product findings. `vacuity-check.py`'s `blind` pass asks whether any READER appears after the last MUTATING call in a test body, both matched by name prefix. Run with the shipped defaults it reports `examined=1820 mutating=3 blind=3` — and all three are false: DEFAULT_READERS is snake_case (`load_`, `get_`, `read_`, `list_`) while this is a camelCase Swift codebase, so NO Swift reader can ever match, and the three `mutating` hits matched the token `restart` in their own function names. Both flagged WatchRestartTests cases read extensively after the mutation. Run with a hand-derived camelCase verb list it reports `examined=1834 mutating=258 re-read-after=158 blind=100`. Two of the flagged real tests were read in full and BOTH re-read: `undoRestoresTheItem` calls `queue.all()` three times after `model.remove(...)`, and `resetReindexesAnIndexFailure` reads `client.calls` after `board.reset(...)`. Neither `all` nor `calls` was in the list. Of the 20 findings the script prints, only 6 are `@Test` functions at all; the other 14 are test doubles and helpers, because the population is every `func` in any file with `test` in its path. CONCLUSION: on this codebase the pass measures the verb list rather than the suite, and no verb list derived by hand is evidence of anything. It is recorded, not published, and the campaign claims no blind-mutation number. The pass's other two arms — `unclassed` and `uncensused` — are exact and are kept. ADDRESSED UPSTREAM in 0.9.2, confirmed by running it 21 Aug 2026. Commit 28ecd67 (`the blind-mutation check was measuring itself`) fixes four detector defects that each RAISED the blind count, and the pass now prints the vocabulary it used above its findings -- `vocabulary: defaults + campaign.blindVocabulary — 22 mutator(s), 20 reader(s)` followed by the reader list -- which was this defect's complaint: a number published without saying what configuration produced it. The denominator also moved, 1841 to 1657, because fixture helpers are no longer counted as tests. Left open rather than closed: the residual named on DEF-040 sits in the same pass. SUPERSEDED 21 Aug 2026 by DEF-055. The specific claim here — snake_case DEFAULT_READERS against a camelCase Swift codebase, giving examined=1820 mutating=3 blind=3 with all three false — was resolved by declaring campaign.json's blindVocabulary, which 0.9.2 reads. The general claim, that no hand-derived verb list is evidence of anything, is not resolved; it is now MEASURED rather than asserted. DEF-055 carries that measurement (7 of 7 sampled findings false, four named mechanisms, a two-way arm) and is the entry to read. Recorded as superseded rather than closed: the finding was real and its successor is open.
subject.title: test-campaign 0.9.1's blind-mutation pass is dominated by its own verb configuration on this codebase, in both directions

subject.detail: STILL PRESENT in 0.9.2, re-measured 21 Aug 2026 and the gap widened by one. witness-worklist.py reports `pairs=20 judgeable=17 WITHOUT a reference=3` and a comparable fraction of 85%, while capture-lineage.py --gate on the same registry reports `published captures: 16` and `JUDGED 16 of 16 judgeable (100%)`. Two gates in one skill version disagree about the judgeable denominator, 17 against 16, and neither names the other's population. CAUSE PINNED 21 Aug 2026. The disagreeing member is SURF-009, the Mac menu-bar popover, and it is the only one: witness-worklist's judgeable set and capture-lineage's judged set are identical apart from it. SURF-009 has a rendered design of record on disk (evidence/shots/mock/SURF-009.png), which is the sole condition witness-worklist tests, so it counts as the 17th judgeable pair. It has NO build capture at all — the popover cannot be opened without activating MCPRouter, which this campaign never does — so it never enters capture-lineage's population, which is built from published captures. capture-lineage therefore reports 'JUDGED 16 of 16 judgeable (100%)' on a registry holding 17 judgeable surfaces. That is the defect's whole shape, and it is the campaign's own first failure mode occurring INSIDE a gate written to prevent it: a denominator built from what was captured rather than from what was enumerated reads 100% precisely when a surface was never photographed. The direction is the dangerous one — an uncaptured surface raises the percentage instead of lowering it. Nothing is concealed in this campaign's own record: SURF-009 carries a shotNote naming the constraint, its three cases (CASE-0004, CASE-0006, CASE-0109) are n/a with the reason, and evidence/shots/pairs.json carries shot:null. The defect is that a reader of the gate line alone would not know to look for any of it. Remains open-detector: the fix is in the skill's scripts, which are not edited from this repo.
subject.note: DETECTOR DEFECT, recorded so its number is not published as a product finding. `witness-worklist.py:90` is `judgeable = [p for p in pairs if p.get("reference")]` -- it tests the reference half and never the shot half. SURF-009 (Mac menu-bar popover) has `shot: null` and an explicit `reason: build half uncaptured` in pairs.json, and is still counted, so the script reported `pairs=20 judgeable=17 comparable fraction: 85%` where the honest figure is 16 of 20, 80%. The script already defends the mirror-image failure and its own comment says why: a campaign reported 20 judgeable pairs whose references were all unrendered .html paths, and it now demotes those to unjudgeable with a named reason. The shot side has no equivalent test. Consequence here is one point of over-report and no false verdict, because capture-lineage.py computes judgeable from captures that exist and reported JUDGED 16 of 16 -- the two gates disagree by exactly this surface, and the disagreement is what found it. A campaign relying on the worklist alone would carry an uncompared surface inside a comparable fraction. Filed against the skill's script rather than this repo, so it is not fixed here.
subject.text: witness-worklist.py counts a pair as judgeable on the reference alone, so a surface with no build capture inflates the comparable fraction.

subject.detail:
DETECTOR DEFECT in test-campaign 0.9.1, found 20 Aug 2026 by the concurrent session at uds:/tmp/cc-socks/9881.sock and confirmed here against the artifact rather than against a model of it. The string `defect` does not appear as a registry key anywhere in evidence-page.py; measured with grep, zero occurrences. Its `

Defects

` at line 521 renders `[c for c in cases if state_of(c.get('status')) == 'fail']` -- failing CASES -- and the nav counter at line 305 is `counts['fail']`, the same population. So the page's Defects section counts 3 (the failing cases CASE-0010, CASE-0040, CASE-0110) while inventory.json holds 11 open defects, and the two numbers are about different things. MEASURED against the regenerated 124100-byte evidence.html: of the 11 open defects, 8 appear ZERO times -- DEF-008, DEF-040, DEF-041, DEF-042, DEF-043, DEF-047, DEF-048, DEF-051. The 3 that do appear are there by accident of prose: DEF-001 in two failing case notes and one passing one, DEF-033 and DEF-049 each inside a single PASSING case's note, rendered by the per-case table rather than by the Defects section. The peer reported 11 invisible; the true figure is 8, because writing a defect id into a case note is a convention doing a gate's job and it happened to fire three times. `campaign.py check` also exits 0 with all 11 open, so no gate holds on the registry either. This is the skill's own first-named failure mode -- covering a subset and reporting it as the whole -- arriving in its publisher: the gated half of the campaign is sound and the ungated half is the half people look at. The fix belongs in the installed skill (render inv['defect'], and count open defects in the nav), not in this repo; recorded rather than patched, precedent DEF-048 and DEF-051. SECOND PUBLISHER, same root cause, measured here: `campaign.py`'s own ledger writer (campaign.py:1210-1240) loads `inventory` and never reads `inventory['defect']` either, so ledger.md names zero defects across its 83 lines. Its header line is sharper than an omission -- it prints `73 pass . 3 fail . 0 skip . 4 n/a . 0 open . armed 73/73`, where `0 open` is the count of open CASES, on a campaign holding 12 open defects. A reader who takes that line at face value reads a campaign with nothing outstanding. ledger.md is generated rather than hand-kept, so it cannot be corrected in this repo: a fix that patched only evidence-page.py would leave the ledger short, and both publishers need to read the registry.
subject.title: evidence-page.py and campaign.py's ledger writer both skip the defect registry, so no published artifact lists a defect

subject.detail: Measured 2026-08-21, test-campaign 0.9.2. `ledger.md`'s header line reads `80 cases` and `73 pass · 3 fail · 0 skip · 4 n/a`; its table carries 72 rows. The eight absent cases are CASE-0145, 0146, 0147, 0148 (lane router-daemon) and CASE-0151, 0152, 0153, 0154 (lane swiftui). All eight pass. MECHANISM, exact. The writer at campaign.py:1218-1241 buckets every case with `by_surface.setdefault(c.get('surface', '—'), [])`, so a case whose `surface` is absent lands under the literal key `'—'`. It then emits rows with `for s in inventory['surface']: for c in by_surface.get(s['id'], [])`. `'—'` is not a surface id, so that bucket is never visited and its contents are never printed. Nothing warns; the count in the header comes from a different code path than the rows beneath it, which is why the two disagree without either being flagged. WHAT IS LOST. CASE-0145 through CASE-0148 are this campaign's four `effect-witness` cases — the rung that required building a recorder outside the product, and the most expensive evidence in the run. They are absent from the ledger entirely. A reader of ledger.md cannot learn that the campaign has an effect-witness rung at all. DIRECTION. The eight dropped are all passes, so the table under-states the work rather than over-stating it. That makes it the safer direction, and it does not make it safe: a reader counting 72 rows against a stated 80 meets an unexplained gap of exactly the kind this campaign is written to make impossible, and the campaign's own rule is that every sweep prints its denominator. SCOPE. Ledger-specific. evidence.html renders all eight (5 to 11 references each, measured by grep), so the HTML page is correct and only the markdown artifact is affected. Distinct from DEF-052, which is about the defect registry being absent from BOTH artifacts; this one is about cases, in one artifact, via a different mechanism. NOT FIXED FROM HERE: campaign.py lives in the installed skill cache, not this repo.
subject.title: campaign.py's ledger writer prints only cases filed under a surface, silently dropping 8 of 80 — including all four effect-witness cases

subject.detail: Measured 2026-08-21. `.gitmodules` vendors `.claude/plugins/fledgeling-plugins` at `main`, and `planning/features-to-triage/LEDGER.md`'s allocation notes state the reason: 'a runner reads mockup-fidelity, mac-craft, design-craft and ux-craft at a repo-relative path rather than depending on the machine.' For test-campaign that is not what happens. The submodule (HEAD baaf79a, branch main, clean) carries `plugins/test-campaign` at version 0.5.0, whose `skills/test-campaign/scripts` holds five files: attach-shots.py, campaign.py, evidence-page.py, strict-check.py, witness-worklist.py. It has no `vacuity-check.py` and no `capture-lineage.py`; `grep effect-witness strict-check.py` returns nothing and `grep -c blindVocabulary vacuity-check.py` cannot run because the file is absent. Every gate this campaign reports ran from `~/.claude/plugins/cache/fledgeling-plugins/test-campaign/0.9.2/`, on the machine. The vacuity census, the effect-witness rung, the blind-mutation pass, the capture-lineage ratchet and the strict score of 65 all come from code the submodule does not contain, four minor versions ahead of it. CONSEQUENCE FOR THE PIPELINE, and it is the reason this is filed rather than noted: DEF-051, DEF-052, DEF-054, DEF-055 and DEF-056 are defects in 0.9.2's scripts. None of that code is in this repo at any path, so no ship-feature runner working in an mcp-router worktree can fix them. They are upstream work in github.com/fledgeling-co/fledgeling-plugins, and closing them requires a change pushed to that repo plus a submodule bump here — a different repo and an outward-facing action. Separately, a fresh clone that follows the documented `git submodule update --init --recursive` gets 0.5.0 and would reproduce none of this campaign's numbers. Not fixed here: which version the submodule should track, and whether the campaign should run from it rather than the cache, is the owner's call.
subject.title: the vendored fledgeling-plugins submodule is test-campaign 0.5.0 while every gate in this campaign ran from the machine's 0.9.2 cache

subject.text: Measured by J2 on 2026-08-29, by trying to actuate SURF-004's declared controls and finding four with nothing to press. The design of record's capability-delta sheet offers a two-way decision — `Promote 2.3.0` and `Keep 2.2.0`, recorded as `Promote the held update` and `Keep the installed version` in `evidence/design-controls.json` under state `sheet:capability-delta`. `app/Sources/MCPRouterUI/Boards/SkillSheets.swift` declares three buttons and all three are `Button("Done") { board.sheet = nil }`, so the sheet a user opens to decide about a held update can only be dismissed. `SkillsBoardModel` carries no write at all: no promote, no keep, no never-run. Two further declared controls have no counterpart either — `Never run` is a filter chip the design draws and `SkillPresentation.Filter` (`all | held | local | needsAttention`) has no case for, and `Reveal repo in Finder` appears nowhere under `app/Sources/`. This is the third shape in `references/inert-ui.md` seen from the other side: not a control whose handler does nothing, but a promised control the build never drew, which no amount of testing the build reveals. It surfaced only because the census gave the surface a denominator and J2 tried to fill it — SURF-004 reaches 2 of 21 actuated and the four are recorded in `inventory.json` under `controlsUnactuatable` rather than quietly dropped.

subject.source: `Button(InsightsBoardCopy.analyseNow) {}`, app/Sources/MCPRouterUI/Boards/InsightsBoard.swift:247 at `83e5380`; `The window is fixed at 24`, app/Sources/MCPRouterUI/Boards/InsightsBoard.swift:14 at `83e5380`; `public static let analyseNow = "Analyse now"`, app/Sources/MCPRouterKit/Boards/BoardCopy.swift:150 at `83e5380`
subject.text: Measured by K3 on 2026-08-29 while trying to fill SURF-026's denominator, and it is the SkillSheets shape (DEF-062) a second time: a button drawn with an empty closure. `Button(InsightsBoardCopy.analyseNow) {}` is the whole of the analyst's action. It is `.disabled(true)` with `analyseUnavailable` as its help and its accessibility hint, which is `DESIGN.md` §3.4's dim-with-a-reason rather than an inert control — the refusal is the product's, not the campaign's — and the reason is that `PRD.md` §6 specifies a session analyst and nothing under `app/Sources` implements one. Three further declared readouts — `Analyst cadence`, `Analyst model`, `Second-opinion model` — have no counterpart at all: the build draws the panel's empty state where the design draws its configuration. The fifth declared control on that panel, `Insights window`, is NOT part of this defect and is recorded separately as a refusal: the window is fixed at 24 hours because the call log rotates and what a router can answer for is whatever survived, so a control offering seven days on a machine holding two would lie about its own range. That reasoning is already in the board's own header comment, which is why it is a stated reason rather than a finding. Recorded rather than trimmed, so five of SURF-026's seven declared controls sit in the denominator with a sentence each.
subject.title: The Insights analyst panel is an empty state with a dead button — three readouts and its one action are unbuilt

subject.source: app/Sources/RouterCore/Control/Describe.swift transportMembers; app/Sources/RouterCore/Control/ControlHandler.swift gate; src/control.ts is the reference half
subject.text: Found while building R22's redactor, filed rather than fixed. `Describe.row` emits `command` and `args` RAW, and `ControlHandler.gate` reads the token only for POST/DELETE/PATCH, so the complete command line of every stdio upstream is readable by anything that can open the loopback port. The same function is careful in the adjacent case — it emits `envKeys` and `headerKeys` and never a value, with B10's reasoning attached — so argv is the one credential-carrying position on that route that is published whole. It matters because argv IS a credential channel: `--token=`, `--api-key=` and a connection string with an inline password are ordinary MCP server invocations, and R22 scrubs args for exactly that reason. The exposure predates R22 and is not made worse by it: the bundle's args go through the value scrub, and this route's do not. NOT FIXED HERE, and the reason is a parity decision rather than effort. `GET /servers` is reference-diffed — `control-servers-get` in planning/parity/surface.tsv, verdict `proven` — so redacting args moves a surface R4 compares byte for byte, and the ungated GET is itself a ported defect this repository records rather than silently repairs. Closing it means changing both routers or declaring a divergence, and that is the owner's call. 2026-10-19 — FIXED IN BOTH ROUTERS by merge 74d15306 (Merge ai/argv-redact), whose subject records that GET /servers stops publishing secret-bearing argv. Unit evidence: ArgvRedactionTests (app/Tests/RouterCoreTests/ArgvRedactionTests.swift) and test/argv-redact.test.ts, with parity vectors in argv-redact.json. Verified 2026-10-19: the `ArgvRedactionTests` suite passed under `swift test`, and `node --test` on test/argv-redact.test.ts passed. Status is fixed · in-test. No campaign re-run is recorded against this row.
subject.title: GET /servers discloses every stdio upstream's full argv to an unauthenticated local caller

subject.evidence: scripts/windows/run-shell-selftest.ps1 exits 2 `NOT-RUN: no selftest.json after 180 s`. shell-startup.log records two launches, 08:09:47.250 and 08:13:14.882, each followed by `loaded at rasterization scale 1.5` and nothing further. subject.text: MEASURED, not inferred. `planning/test-campaign/cases.json` files CASE-0270, CASE-0271, CASE-0272, CASE-0273, CASE-0274 and CASE-0275 under `req: REQ-035`. All six are the R22 diagnostics-bundle lane: credential redaction in an exported bundle, the needle floor, percent-encoded secrets, and the POST/GET gate on the bundle route, all in lane `router-daemon` on plane `live-external`. REQ-035's own text in `inventory.json` is `On Windows the router daemon is supervised by a Scheduled Task registered against the user's own logon: it starts in the interactive user session ... it runs un-elevated, and it is restarted ...`. CASE-0308 is filed under the same REQ-035 and IS about that task - `execution-plane=windows-host`, actuating LogonTaskSupervisor.Register/Unregister, read back through Get-ScheduledTask. So one requirement id carries two case families that share no subject, and six of the seven cases under it measure something the requirement does not state. WHY IT MATTERS RATHER THAN BEING UNTIDY. reckon and `strict-check` both answer `what proves REQ-035` by the cases that cite it. Today that answer is six rows about a diagnostics bundle plus one about a scheduled task, so REQ-035 reads as far better evidenced than it is, and the diagnostics bundle - which is real, passing and armed - has NO requirement of its own anywhere in `inventory.json`. A feature with no requirement cannot be reported as unbuilt, unmeasured or done; it is simply outside every denominator. HOW IT WAS FOUND, said because it bears on how many more there may be: not by a gate. It surfaced while citing `daemon-diagnostics-bundle-export.md` to the six cases that actually measure its subject, which is the one reading that puts a case's `req` beside the requirement's text. WHAT IS NOT SETTLED. (1) Which way to fix it is an adjudication and not a runner's call: either a new requirement is written for the diagnostics bundle and the six cases are re-pointed at it, or REQ-035's text is widened - and widening it would make one requirement mean two things, which is the shape that produced this. (2) NO INSTRUMENT COVERS THIS. Nothing in `planning/` compares a case's `req` against the requirement's subject; `registry-drop-gate` and `target-resolution-gate` check that an id RESOLVES, not that it is the right one. A gate that could catch it would have to read meaning rather than membership, and no arm was added here rather than adding a green that would not have caught this. (3) Whether any other requirement in this registry is double-booked the same way is UNMEASURED - only REQ-035 was checked, because only REQ-035 was in front of me.

The design of record puts two scoping controls on this board and the build draws neither. `Servers` / `Skills` is a kind toggle: the mock filters its registry array on each row's `kind` and re-labels the table's own column with it. `RegistryEntry` carries no kind and the board searches one merged registry, so both halves of the toggle would draw the same list — there is nothing to filter on rather than a filter nobody wired. `24h` / `7d` / `30d` is a window over install velocity, and the mock's own caption says the Trending table ranks "by install velocity over {window}, not total". subject.detail: **The recorded cause was wrong, and this replaces it.** It said the shutter fired during a board transition and named the fix as a settle in `capture-mac-glass.sh`. Measured 20 Aug 2026 from the accessibility dumps the same script already writes, one per board, beside the pictures: | board | window | AXSplitGroup | clipped | |---|---|---|---| | Servers, Activity, Cleanup, Inbox, Settings | 980pt | 980pt | — | | Checks | 980pt | 988pt | 8pt | | Skills | 980pt | 1044pt | 64pt | | Discover | 980pt | 1119pt | 139pt | Every window in the run is the same 980x620 and every capture is the same 2096x1376, so no capture rect is wrong and no shutter is early. What differs is the shell **inside** the window: on three boards `NavigationSplitView` lays out wider than the window and centres the excess — the split group's origin moves left by exactly half the overflow in all three cases (180→148 for 64pt, 180→110.5 for 139pt, 180→176 for 8pt), which is what makes the clipping symmetrical. That is why the sidebar's section headers read `unning` and `brary` while the nav rows beside them are whole: the headers sit at a smaller leading inset and fall off first, and the header's trailing controls — `Manage marketplaces.`, `Review 2.3.0…` — fall off the right by the same amount. So this is a product defect on three boards rather than a lane defect on two captures, and it is worse than recorded: Checks overflows too, by 8pt, which is small enough that nobody reading the picture saw it. The app declares no minimum window width anywhere, so nothing stops a user reaching this state — the campaign's 980pt window is an ordinary size, not a stress case. The consequence that made it a defect stands unchanged and is now better founded: a clipped capture is admissible for what it shows and silent about what it cut, so a reader cannot tell an absent control from a cropped one. Both witness verdicts that depend on these captures say in their method field that the right-hand controls were read from the accessibility dump instead. `capture-mac-glass.sh` now prints `board width: examined=14 overflowing=3` every run, with a line naming each board and its excess. Reported rather than enforced, because three boards overflow today and a known red in `make all` either blocks unrelated work or gets its assertion softened. NOT FIXED, and the fix is a decision rather than a repair. Either the shell declares a minimum window width at least as wide as its widest board — one line, guarantees nothing ever clips, and costs users on small screens a window they cannot shrink — or the three boards compress, which keeps small screens usable and is per-board column work across all three. Discover at 1119pt is the one that decides how much that costs. PARTLY CLOSED 20 Aug 2026, on `ai/x4`, and the part that is not closed is named rather than left to look finished. The mechanism turned out to be a chain rather than a board: each row's fixed columns report a hard minimum width, the detail pane sums them, `NavigationSplitView` reports that as its own minimum, and nothing ever reads it back — this app opts into no minimum window size and `windowResizability` defaults to `.automatic` — so the window proposes 980pt and SwiftUI **places** the oversized child with default centre alignment. The symmetry was the tell. Referred to the xAI lane (grok-4.6, xhigh) with the measured table; it named the propagation as the bug, called both listed fixes second-best, and its Q3 answer — placement plus `.automatic` resizability rather than any documented split-view overflow mode — is what the one-line fix then confirmed. FIXED: `ContentZone` carries `.frame(minWidth: 0, maxWidth: .infinity, alignment: .leading)`. Measured on the rebuilt app through the same accessibility channel: all eight boards read `split=980` inside a `window=980`, overflowing 0 of 8, where the same probe on the previous build read 3 of 8. The sidebar is whole again — `Running`, `Library` and the footer readout all render in full where they were `unning` and `brary`. The leading alignment is the deliberate half: it decides who loses when the content still does not fit, and the answer is never the navigation. STILL OPEN: the boards' content is still wider than the detail pane on those three, so the trailing chrome is cut at the pane's right edge — Discover's search field reads `Search the regis` and a body sentence loses its last word. That is one-edge clipping where it was two, and it is the conventional behaviour of a too-narrow window rather than a split view eating its own sidebar, but it is still content going missing without saying so. Closing it needs the three boards' columns to flex, which is a design decision about what Discover looks like compressed and is the owner's rather than mine. GUARDED two ways, and the two see different things. `capture-mac-glass.sh` now **fails** on any board whose split group exceeds its window, and refuses to pass on `examined=0`; all three arms were exercised on 20 Aug 2026 — red at 3 of 14, green at 0 of 14, and exit 1 with no dumps at all. `ShellDetailWidthTests` asserts the modifier in `ShellWindow`'s detail column so a revert is red in `make test` rather than on the next glass run. That test's own first version was a detector defect found by arming: it searched the raw source slice, and the modifier it looks for is named in the doc comment three lines above it, so deleting the modifier left the assertion green. Comments are stripped before matching now, and both halves were re-armed separately. CLOSED 20 Aug 2026, and the second half corrected the first half's diagnosis of *which* content was too wide. The brief written from the split-group numbers said three boards' table columns needed to flex. A pane-level probe — every leaf's right edge against the window's, read from the same dumps — says otherwise, and it says so only after the probe itself was fixed: the first version read the frame's **y** where it meant **x** and reported clipping on seven of eight boards, which the pixels flatly denied. The Settings capture is whole, and looking at it is what caught the field offset. A frame's last five fields are x, y, w, h and a flag; the split-group gate only ever compared widths, which is why it was right while the leaf probe was wrong. Corrected, the drivers are: - **Discover**: content wants 823pt against a 684pt pane. Not the table — cutting `nameColumn` from 216pt to 96pt moved the number by **zero**. It is the controls row: a `.fixedSize()` segmented picker measuring 567pt beside a search field pinned at 240pt. - **Skills**: 748pt against 684pt, same shape — a 516pt fixed picker and a 216pt pinned field. - **Checks**: not a content defect at all. Its real content ends at 1152pt inside a 1160pt pane; the only thing past the edge is `KeyClaimProbe`, the `#if DEBUG` test surface A21 names, overhanging by 4pt. It is absent from any build a user runs, and it is what the whole 8pt split-group excess on this board was. FIXED by giving each board a `searchMinWidth` of four units and declaring the field `minWidth:idealWidth:maxWidth:` rather than `width:`. The picker cannot give a point back — that is what `.fixedSize()` means, and it is right, because a segmented control has nowhere to put a truncated label — so the field is the only control in the row that can. It renders at its full width wherever there is room and shows about eight characters at the narrowest window this app is used at, which is less than anyone wants and more than nothing: it still takes focus, accepts a query and submits. Measured after: every board reads `split=980` in a `window=980`, and the only leaf past the pane edge on any of the eight is a 1pt scrollbar — plus the Debug key probe's 4pt on Checks. Before, Discover's rows and footnote sat at 1283pt against an edge of 1160. GUARDED by a second test in `ShellDetailWidthTests`, armed 20 Aug 2026: restoring `.frame(width: DiscoverBoardMetrics.searchWidth)` reddens all three of its assertions. It names the two boards rather than looping over every file, because those are the two the measurement covers — a third board growing this problem is a new measurement, not a case this test silently already made.

subject.detail: Measured 2026-08-27 by G16 while enumerating SURF-026, and independently by G15. M15 made Settings a Scene and removed the case from `Destination`, and capture-mac-glass.sh still ran `axkit select Settings`. That select fails — `axkit: no sidebar row starting 'Settings'` — the app stays on whichever board the loop visited last, and the shutter filed THAT board's pixels under SURF-011: byte-identical to the Cleanup board on one loop ordering and to the Insights board on another. THE CAMPAIGN'S OWN INSTRUMENTS CAUGHT IT FROM TWO DIRECTIONS, which is the part worth keeping. glass-assert.py's raster uniqueness check went red because two cases shared a sha256; `--discriminate` reported the neighbouring board's predicate wrongly accepting SURF-011's dump, because that dump IS the neighbouring board; and the capture manifest's readback recorded the picture's target as the neighbour's route under subject SURF-011, contradicting its own filename. FIXED HERE, NARROWLY: the capture script now refuses to photograph a select that did not take, and says which board the window is actually showing. That is the script's own standing rule rather than a new one — it already declines to substitute a picture for the pairing sheet and the status item, and its header records the run that filed the Inbox board as SURF-010. The title and the dump are still written from what the app is really showing, so the failure stays visible downstream; what is withheld is the photograph, because a misattributed picture is the one artefact nothing downstream can correct. STILL OPEN, and deliberately not fixed here: 1. SURF-011 has no route to the Settings SCENE. It needs Cmd-comma or the app menu, not a sidebar select that cannot succeed. CASE-0016 and CASE-0111 fail until it does. 2. THE MENU MAP IS PRE-M22. Committed SURF-001.menu.txt binds Cmd-4 to `Discover`; the running app binds Cmd-4 to `Harnesses`, exactly as Destination.selectionDigit declares (activity 1, servers 2, skills 3, harnesses 4, discover 5, inbox 6, evals 7, cleanup 8, insights 9). glass-assert.py's SURF-001 `menu` dict is the old map, so CASE-0001 asserts five bindings this build does not have. Correcting it is editing an assertion to restore a green, which this campaign forbids — it is owed as its own item, from Destination.selectionDigit rather than by hand. WHY IT IS THE SAME FINDING AS G14'S, ONE LAYER DOWN. G14 found the surface LIST had stopped growing while the product did. This is the EVIDENCE not having been re-taken since the build moved: the committed glass artefacts were last written on 20 Aug by cef3729, before M22 added two destinations and renumbered four accelerators. In both cases a completeness gate reported clean because what it measured was a stale artefact rather than the product. CLOSED ON THE EVIDENCE SIDE, 2026-08-27 (G21/G29). The frame this defect produced was still published: `inventory.json` gave SURF-011 the shot `evidence/shots/SURF-011.build.png`, and at `519aebc` those bytes were the Insights board. `capture-lineage.py --gate` reported it UNTIED because the capture step's own row said `target: app://mac/insights` while the filename said SURF-011 -- the manifest was right and the wall was wrong. Two moves, both provable from git. The Insights frame is renamed `evidence/shots/DEF-059.insights-filed-as-SURF-011.png`, keeping every capture-time field, so the defect keeps its exhibit and no filename match can offer it to SURF-011 again. The Settings capture it overwrote is restored to `SURF-011.build.png` from `cef3729`, TOGETHER WITH ITS MANIFEST ROW from the same commit -- the last commit where those bytes and that row agreed (sha 3b5a26ef, `target: app://mac/settings`, readback `Settings`, 2026-08-20T11:32:58Z). Restoring the pair from one commit is a recovery of a capture-time record; restamping the row against the new bytes would have been the manifest-after-the-fact defect. What is NOT closed is the cause: `axkit select Settings` still fails, so the campaign still has no Settings capture newer than 2026-08-20 and the glass script still declines to take one. THE CAUSE NOW HAS A READER, 2026-09-02 (wa5). `axkit select Settings` still fails, and the campaign still has no Settings capture newer than 2026-08-20 -- unchanged. What has changed is that the age is no longer invisible: `bin/glass-build-gate.py` reports `evidence/shots/SURF-011.build.png` and `evidence/ax/SURF-011.*` as STALE against the build this tree would produce, so the lane cannot be green over them again without somebody re-taking them. `bin/capture-mac-glass.sh`'s refusal to photograph a select that did not take is the other half and is unchanged. Both halves of the remaining work -- a route to the Settings SCENE, and the re-capture -- are macOS work and are not attempted here. CLOSED 2026-10-19 on glass. capture-mac-glass.sh opens Settings with ⌘, (backgrounded), selects the Router pane in the Settings window's own source list, photographs that window as SURF-011 (target app://mac/settings), dumps the Security pane as a second dump of the same surface, and closes the window. glass-assert at the current build: checked=435 failures=0; --decoy SURF-011 reddens 6.

subject.detail: DETECTOR DEFECT in test-campaign 0.9.2, found 21 Aug 2026. attach-shots.py iterates every image under evidence/shots and assigns `hit['shot'] = rel` on each match, last write wins, with no preference for a build capture over a design render. This campaign keeps six directories under evidence/shots (16 root, 8 design-size, 16 fidelity, 9 ios, 17 mock, 11 mock-hidpi), so for SURF-001 the candidates in iteration order are SURF-001.build.png, SURF-001.shell.png, mock/SURF-001.png, mock-hidpi/SURF-001.full.png -- and the last one wins. MEASURED for SURF-001, SURF-002 and SURF-006: `--apply` would repoint each surface's `shot` from its build capture to `evidence/shots/mock-hidpi/SURF-00N.full.png`, which is the render of the DESIGN, not the build. That is the skill's own headline failure mode -- publishing a picture of one thing under the name of another -- arriving in a sibling of the plane built to prevent it, and it would do so while every other gate stayed green, because capture-lineage.py gates the 16 captures cited by CASES and the surface wall is a different population. The report compounds it: the UNCORROBORATED block prints surface ids (SURF-001 ... SURF-011) rather than the file each verdict is about, so a reader sees eleven surfaces apparently lacking provenance when in fact each surface's ACTUAL `shot` field points at a corroborated build capture and the complaint is about a mock render nobody intended to attach. Distinguishing the two costs a re-derivation of the matcher by hand. Recorded rather than patched, precedent DEF-048, DEF-051, DEF-052 and DEF-053. The campaign's standing refusal to run `--apply` here predates this and was based on the DEF-006 mis-wire; it now has a measured mechanism behind it. Separately closed while investigating: this campaign's design-size captures carried their provenance in a second manifest, evidence/shots/design-size/captures.json, in a different schema ({captures:[...]} against the root's bare list) that no gate reads. Its 8 entries were merged into the root manifest with `target` derived from the root's declared target for the same subject and corroborated by each capture's own windowTitleReadback -- Servers, Activity, Skills, Discover, Inbox, Checks, Cleanup, Settings, every one matching -- recorded at capture time, and each carries `targetDerivedFrom` saying so. That was the campaign's own inconsistency and is fixed here; it was not the cause of the 11. RE-MEASURED 2026-08-27 (G21) after `evidence/shots/captures.json` was made a derived file. The uncorroborated count is 12 and stays 12: SURF-001..011 and SURF-022. Eleven of them are this defect -- `mock-hidpi/` sorts last, so it is the row that decides each surface's `shotProvenance`. The mock rows in the manifest deliberately carry NO `target`; the address the channel was pointed at is recorded in full as `renderedFrom`, with an `attachHazard` field naming this defect. Measured both ways on this tree: writing that address as `target` instead drops the uncorroborated count from 12 to 1 and DISARMS `--apply`'s refusal, because `attach-shots.py` only checks the field is present and never compares it to the subject's route -- which is item 5 of X8's work order. So the report going quiet would have been this defect getting worse while looking fixed. The twelfth, SURF-022, is not this defect: see DEF-061.
subject.title: attach-shots --apply would attach the design mock render as the build's surface shot for 11 surfaces, and its report names the surface rather than the file

subject.detail: Measured 2026-08-21 against test-campaign 0.9.2 on app/Tests. The pass reports examined=1661 mutating=320 blind=88. Two structural errors and two idiom errors inflate that number. STRUCTURAL. (1) It scans every `func`, not every test. Restricted to swift-testing's own discriminator (a func whose nearest preceding annotation is @Test) the denominator is 1531, not 1661: 130 of the examined functions are not tests. (2) Its helper exclusion at vacuity-check.py:162 is file-scoped — a name is a helper only if called more than once in the file that declares it. A shared stub declared in TestSupport.swift and called from other files therefore reads as a test, so MemoryFileSystem's `write`, `removeItem` and `moveItem`, HTTPStub's `stop` and WatchTestSupport's `remove` are each counted as a blind test. 21 of the 88 are support-file functions. IDIOM, on the mutator side. (3) The lookbehind `(?<![A-Za-z0-9_])` cannot exclude a dot, so a Swift enum case constructor matches a mutator verb: `ServerRowAction.forServer(s, pendingAuth: nil) == .reset(.clearPlacard)` reports ServerPresentationTests::trippedOutranksHeld as mutating via 'reset', where `.reset` is the expected VALUE inside the assertion. 41 of 72 re-measured findings are dot-prefixed. (4) It takes the last mutator by source POSITION and calls everything after it the tail, which misreads three Swift constructs: a mutator inside the assertion (`await #expect(throws: Never.self) { try await store.delete() }` — nothing can follow it by construction), a mutator in a `defer` block (source-early, execution-last, so the whole test body reads as 'after'), and a mutator as the last statement of a loop body whose observation is the next iteration (CallbackLifecycleTests::stopReleasesTheSocket rebinds the port ten times; the read of cycle N is the start() of cycle N+1). SAMPLE. Of the 15 findings with zero assertions after the last mutator — the highest-yield stratum — 9 were read in full. Two (DiscoveryTests::servers, CapabilityPlateTests::install) are helpers. All 7 remaining are real tests that do observe after mutating, through idioms no reader verb names: `client.calls.last?.operation`, `seen.filter { ... }`, a rebind that throws. Precision on that stratum is 0 of 7. ARMED, two ways, evidence/arming/blind-mutation.arming.log. A probe @Test that mutates and never observes was added and removed: blind moved 88 -> 89 -> 88 and examined/mutating moved by exactly 1 each time. The check does bite; it is the false-positive rate that is at issue, not the sensitivity. NOT REMEDIED BY VOCABULARY. The reader side is deliberately loose because a false reader match suppresses a finding. Adding this codebase's read idioms (`calls`, `operation`, `filter`) would lower the number without improving what the pass knows, and the terms are generic enough to suppress true findings too. The 88 stands recorded as a worklist with its measured precision beside it rather than tuned to look better. RE-MEASURED 2026-08-27 by G22, which declared `testRoot` and gave this pass a corpus for the first time. THE 88 DOES NOT REPRODUCE. Vendored 0.9.2 over `app/Tests` today reports examined=2133 mutating=3 blind=3, against the 1661/320/88 above. The denominator moving up while `mutating` collapses 320 → 3 is not tree churn: 0.9.1 and 0.9.2 ship IDENTICAL DEFAULT_MUTATORS and DEFAULT_READERS, and neither list holds `reset`, `write`, `removeItem`, `moveItem` or `remove` — the verbs this entry's idiom argument turns on. So the 2026-08-21 sitting ran an expanded vocabulary passed on the command line, and `campaign.json` declares none, which makes 88 a figure no documented invocation returns. Its cited evidence, `evidence/arming/blind-mutation.arming.log`, has never existed on any branch of this repository (`git log --all -- '*blind-mutation*'` is empty), so the arming claim above is not checkable from the tree. The measured structural and idiom errors are not withdrawn; what is withdrawn is the population they were measured over. TODAY'S POPULATION, AND ITS PRECISION. With `testRoot: app` the pass reports examined=2179 mutating=3 re-read-after=0 blind=3, and 0.15.0 returns the same three findings from the same corpus. All THREE were read in full — 3 of 3, not a sample — and all three are false positives. Precision 0 of 3. A FOURTH CAUSE, NOT IN THE ORIGINAL ENTRY, AND THE ONE THAT PRODUCES TWO OF THE THREE. The body slice is `src[pos:end]` where `pos` is the start of the DECLARATION, so a test whose own name begins with a mutator verb matches itself. `WatchRestartTests::restartIsIssuedBeforeTheStagingWrite` and `::restartIsOwedBeforeTheWriteLands` contain no mutating call at all: the only `restart\w*\(` in each is `func restart…(` on its own declaration line. Both then read — `WatchWorld.read(scratch.logPath)`, `WatchState.load(path:)`, `WatchWorld.serverNames(in:)` — and assert on `state.mcpServersHash` and `state.restartPending`. The third, `PhoneStorageFailureTests::restartRechecksTheCamera`, does call `await model.restart()` and then asserts twice, on `model.step` and on `model.entry.characters`: property reads that no reader verb names, which is cause (4)'s shape rather than a new one. This cause survives into 0.15.0 unchanged. NOT ENROLLED IN A GATE, and `blindVocabulary` still not declared, for the reason the entry already gives. A related gap measured at the same sitting: pointed at `src/` — the TypeScript tree, which has no tests — the pass prints `corpus: … (0 file(s))` and `examined=0 mutating=0 blind=0` and contributes nothing to `--gate`. It reports its empty corpus and does not fail on it, so a mis-declared `testRoot` reads as a clean pass. VOCABULARY DECLARED 2026-08-29 by K4, and the entry's own 'NOT REMEDIED BY VOCABULARY' paragraph is narrowed rather than withdrawn. That paragraph reasons entirely from the READER side, and on the reader side it is still right: adding this codebase's read idioms lowers the count without improving what the pass knows, which is why the declared reader list stops short of `expect` and `require` -- swift-testing's assertion macros, 5781 and 383 occurrences, either of which would mark every test that asserts after mutating as re-reading and collapse the count to near zero while the pass learned nothing. THE MUTATOR SIDE WAS NEVER ARGUED, AND THAT IS WHERE THE PASS WAS BLIND. Measured over the same 2282 test bodies at `83e5380`: the nine snake_case defaults find 3 mutating call sites; a camelCase list derived from this corpus finds 481. So `blind=3` was a reading of 3 of 481, a recall of 0.6%, and the entry's `precision 0 of 3` was a precision over a population the instrument could barely see. `campaign.json` now carries `blindVocabulary` with `only: true`, 19 mutators and 34 readers, derived mechanically -- a verb is kept only where method calls on a receiver are at least half its corpus sites and its own `func` declaration lines at most a quarter, which is causes (3) and (4) of this entry turned into a selection rule. THE THREE FINDINGS ARE ADJUDICATED, and each clears for a different checkable reason rather than all three for one. `restartIsIssuedBeforeTheStagingWrite`: one fitted mutator, `WatchWorld.remove(scratch)` inside a `defer`, and four declared readers after it -- `load`, `read`, `parse`, `servers`. NOT blind, positively. `restartIsOwedBeforeTheWriteLands`: three fitted mutators, the last `WatchState(restartPending: true).save(`, with `load` after it. NOT blind, positively. `restartRechecksTheCamera`: ZERO fitted mutator call sites in its body. It was flagged only because `restart` is a shipped default and this entry's fourth cause -- the body slice beginning at the declaration -- made `func restartRechecksTheCamera(` match itself. `restart` fails the selection rule (1 method call against 3 declaration lines, of 5 sites), so it is not in the vocabulary and the finding is withdrawn. WHAT THAT DOES NOT MEAN: its real mutation `await model.restart()` is now invisible to the pass, and its reads are still the property comparisons `model.step` and `model.entry.characters` that no reader verb names. It is UNEXAMINED by this instrument, not clean, and that is this entry's ceiling stated once more rather than closed. ARMED, AND ENROLLED, which the entry recorded as missing. `planning/test-campaign/bin/blind-vocabulary-arm.py` runs on every `make lint`: two plants identical but for one line, each measured alone and again inside a `shutil.copytree` of the real corpus, requiring examined+1 mutating+1 blind+1 for the blind plant and examined+1 mutating+1 blind+0 for the reading one. The specificity arm is the half a sensitivity arm alone cannot give: a detector that flagged every mutating body would pass the first and say nothing. 6 of 6 as expected on `cache 0.16.0` and again on the `vendor/` pin via `--instrument`. The two disagree only on the denominator -- 2282 against 2277, the five arrow-style `it/test(` blocks 0.9.3 added block detection for -- and agree on blind=111. THE 111 IS A WORKLIST AND THE CAMPAIGN STILL PUBLISHES NO BLIND NUMBER. Nothing above touches the structural causes: the pass still examines every `func` rather than every `@Test`, its helper exclusion is still file-scoped, and a `defer` mutator still reads as source-early -- which is exactly why the first of the three findings above needed reading rather than counting. This entry stays OPEN; what it now carries is a measured recall beside its measured precision.
subject.title: vacuity-check's blind-mutation pass examines non-tests and mis-reads Swift idiom; 7 of 7 sampled findings are false positives

subject.detail: Measured 2026-09-03 (WE3) on LUKESFF, Windows 11, CPython 3.13, console codepage 1252. `campaign.py`'s loader is `return json.loads(p.read_text())` with no `encoding=`. `Path.read_text()` defaults to `locale.getencoding()`, which is cp1252 here. This campaign's `inventory.json` holds em dashes and middots, so: $ python vendor/test-campaign/.../campaign.py check planning/test-campaign UnicodeDecodeError: 'charmap' codec can't decode byte 0x9d in position 284168 exit 1 It is a traceback rather than a verdict, and `exit 1` is the same code the gate uses for 'not ready to report'. A caller reading the exit status alone cannot tell a campaign that failed its checks from one the checker could not open. `PYTHONUTF8=1` makes it run; with that set it reaches its checks and reports normally, which is how the rest of this session's `campaign.py` measurements were taken. SCOPE. Windows hosts only -- macOS and most Linux default to UTF-8, which is why the campaign never met this on the Mac. It is not confined to `campaign.py`: `vacuity-check.py`, `strict-check.py` and `attach-shots.py` in the pinned 0.9.2 read and WRITE with the same bare calls, so on this host `attach-shots.py --apply` would write `inventory.json` back in cp1252 and mangle every em dash in the register. That one is a data-loss path rather than a crash, and it is the reason this is filed at detector severity rather than as a nuisance.
subject.title: campaign.py reads the registry with no encoding, so on a Windows console it dies on the first non-ASCII byte and checks nothing

subject.detail: THE CHANGE WAS RIGHT AND THE RECORD IS WRONG, which is why this is a record defect and not a revert. The pin's own withdrawn comment said so: MEASURED, not chosen ... the reference's own `saveManifest` throws. That is a real divergence. It was a divergence, and 5a51776c closed it. Measured here for the first time rather than argued: `scripts/acceptance/r21-approve-write-denied.mjs` drives the shipped node route against a filesystem that refuses the save and records `500`, so Swift's old 200 disagreed with the reference and its new 500 agrees. The pin was doing exactly the job its comment claimed - making the change deliberate the day somebody made it - and the day came. What is missing is anybody writing that down, so a reader arriving at either the brief or the LEDGER cell today is told not to make a change that has been on `main` since 24 Aug 2026. NOT FIXED HERE, and the boundary is the point: correcting a shipped brief's status word is `shipped-brief-gate.py`'s axis, and R21 is one of the thirteen briefs that gate holds under R6 because DEF-049 is still open against its subject. Writing a terminal word onto R21 now would take a live defect off the total, which is the one direction that gate exists to refuse. So the contradiction is recorded and the words are left alone. SWIFT WAS NOT COMPILED AND NOT RUN FOR THIS ROW. `swift` and `xcodebuild` are both absent on the machine this was written on (LUKESFF, Windows 11; `Get-Command` found neither), so every statement here about Swift source is READ off the tree at 42aef112 and none of it is a test result. Where a claim is measured, the command that measured it is named.
subject.text: `planning/features-to-triage/LEDGER.md:145` opens with **Done** - merged `5a51776` ... handleApprove answers 500 when ManifestIO.save fails and closes with **Do not move the status code** - `ControlApproveDispatchTests.swift:114-118` at `1d95734` pins 200 deliberately. One cell, two instructions, and the second is about the change the first records as merged. `planning/features-to-triage/R21-approve-answers-200-over-a-discarded-write.md` still carries `Status: Ready for AI` and the same prohibition, plus an acceptance line reading `ControlApproveDispatchTests` stays green unedited - and commit `5a51776c` edited that very test, replacing the 200 expectation with 500.
subject.title: R21's LEDGER row records the status change and instructs against it in the same cell, and the brief it points at still forbids what shipped

subject.detail: parity-gate.sh, 20 Aug 2026 on main at e5755d0. The suite lane's citation run of scripts/acceptance/parity-oauth.sh exited non-zero and recorded `control-auth-post-http fail — the Swift router never reached the token endpoint`. The dedicated oauth lane, later in the same gate, ran the same script and recorded ok over 21 checks. The gate reported the row DIVERGED and printed 81 of 83. WHY IT IS UNEXPLAINED, established 21 Aug 2026 from disk without re-running anything. The run survives as evidence/runs/parity-gate-2026-08-20-oauth-flake.log, written 20:39:30. Its line 163 is the whole of what the citation run reported: `FAIL scripts/acceptance/parity-oauth.sh the gate reported findings`, and the next line is the following `ok` row. The script itself does not fail that quietly -- its failure branch (parity-oauth.sh:308-329) prints the POST /auth status, the browser hop, the tail of the router log and the first 20 requests the provider saw. Every one of those bytes existed and was discarded by the caller: `parity-suite.sh`'s `run_script` sent both streams to /dev/null at the time. So this defect is not a run that left no diagnostic, it is a run whose diagnostic the harness threw away, and no amount of re-reading the log can recover it. The instrument was repaired in commit 21d559b at 20:41:28 -- one minute and 58 seconds after this log was written, in the same commit that recorded the defect -- so `run_script` now keeps the log and prints its last 20 lines inline. A recurrence would therefore arrive with the cause attached. That is what closes this: the next occurrence, not more thought about this one. It stays open because there is still no cause and no reproduction; what changed is that the reason it could not be diagnosed is now known and no longer true. One candidate mechanism examined and NOT adopted. The R9 lane reported (21 Aug 2026, via uds:/tmp/cc-socks/9881.sock) that a stale $TMPDIR/mcp-router-parity.lock had made a gate fail its manifest-check for a non-real reason. That is a different symptom -- a manifest-check failure before the comparison, against this defect's completed run that reached `control-auth-post-http` and recorded a row -- and parity-oauth.sh takes that same lock at line 126 and preflights every port at 143-145, so the two lanes inside one gate could not have overlapped. Recorded as ruled out rather than left unmentioned, so the next reader does not spend the lead twice.
subject.text: Observed once, in one of two whole-gate runs, and not reproduced by: a standalone run of `parity-oauth.sh`, a second standalone run of it immediately afterwards (which exercised the same port-reuse wait, 9s and 12s), a standalone run of `parity-suite.sh`, or a second whole `parity-gate.sh` on the same tree. The second gate reported 82 of 83, 0 DIVERGED, and its suite lane reported the citation clean. **What it is not.** The lane distinguishes an environment failure from a finding on purpose, and this was the finding branch: `record control-auth-post-http fail` at `parity-oauth.sh:329`, reached only when the reference side completed an authorization and the Swift side did not. An unbindable port exits 2 through `wait_for_ports_bindable` and records `blocked`, not `fail`, so the port-reuse race is ruled out by the code path that fired. **Why it went undiagnosed, and what changed.** `parity-suite.sh`'s `run_script` sent both streams to `/dev/null` and printed `the gate reported findings` — a verdict with no evidence under it. The bytes naming which guard failed had already been thrown away by the time anyone read the gate's summary. `run_script` now keeps the log, prints its last 20 lines inline and names the file it kept, armed 20 Aug 2026 against a deliberately failing citation. A recurrence will say which of the 21 checks went red. **Why the duplicate run stays.** `control-auth-post-http` is proven on the wire by its own lane and also cites the script, so the gate runs it twice. That is now documented in `parity-suite.sh` rather than deduplicated, because the duplicate is what caught this: a single run would have reported a clean 82 of 83 and nobody would have known. Both record under the same row id and a `fail` wins. **Burn-in, 20 Aug 2026: 8 standalone runs of the lane, all green, 21 checks each.** Three immediately after the failure and five consecutively afterwards, plus one clean whole gate. One failure in roughly ten whole-lane executions, cause unrecoverable because that invocation's stdout was discarded. A green burn-in does not close this: the original failure is uninspectable, so the runs measure only that the lane is not reliably broken. What would close it is a captured reproduction, or a stated gate met — several consecutive whole gates including the cold port-reuse path — decided as its own question rather than inferred from a streak, which is the `install-launchd-watch` mistake this repository already paid for once (G1: name a fix per term and fix a bound IN ADVANCE, never a green streak). Not a UI defect and not a blocker on the cutover count — CASE-0036's measurement is the second run — but it is an unexplained non-determinism in the router or the lane, and it is recorded rather than absorbed.
subject.title: the OAuth parity lane failed once inside a full gate and has not reproduced

subject.detail: Measured 2026-09-03 (WE3) while adjudicating `an-effect-class-the-census-cannot-name-reads-as-no-effect.md`. That brief cites one requirement. The requirement axis is clean -- all 44 declare a class in `EFFECT_CLASSES` -- and the finding is on the axis nobody counted: 31 of the 49 cases that name a `witness.effect` name a class the vocabulary does not carry, and every one of the 31 is `oracle: effect-witness` at `status: pass`. machine-state 25 CASE-0366..0371, 0420..0426, 0470..0477, 0490..0493 file 2 CASE-0342, CASE-0386 notification 1 CASE-0441 os-record 1 CASE-0387 process 1 CASE-0440 ui-state 1 CASE-0346 WHY NOBODY SAW IT, and this is the half that makes it a defect rather than a chore. `campaign.py:702` DOES check the field, and its blocker line reads `40 effect-witness claim(s) with no recorder, no effect class, or a count of zero`. That 40 is 31 bad classes plus 9 missing recorders and counts, verified by replicating the loop. The report then caps its detail at twelve lines -- which on this campaign are twelve lines about four cases with missing recorders and null counts. **All 31 class findings are inside the 40 and not one of them is printed.** A reader of the campaign report cannot learn from it that any case names an unrecognised class, and the number reads as a recorder problem. WHY THE 31 ARE NOT REMAPPED HERE, deliberately and on the record. Some are a rename: `process` on CASE-0440, whose recorder is `Get-ScheduledTaskInfo`, is `subprocess`. Some are a harder question a rename would bury: `machine-state` on CASE-0423..0426 and CASE-0490..0493 is recorded over *"the router's own /servers listing, read over the control API"*, which is a recorder INSIDE the product -- whether those cases belong at the `effect-witness` rung at all is a judgement about the case, not about a word. Picking the nearest legal spelling for all 31 would turn 31 rows green while answering neither question, and every one of them belongs to the Windows waves rather than to this runner. `references/effect-boundary.md` is what settles them.
subject.title: 31 of the 49 cases naming a witness effect class name one the census cannot recognise, and campaign.py counts them into a 40 whose printed detail names none of them

An age that could not be measured is null and never 0 — a zero reads as just-refreshed — and a catalogue whose newest file is stamped AHEAD of the router's clock is null too, because reported as a negative number it would exceed no window and read fresh forever. parity-gate.sh on main at e5755d0, 20 Aug 2026: **82 of 83 rows proven (4 of them by suite only, not by wire comparison), 0 DIVERGED, 1 blocked.** REQ-014's contract is the owner's cutover target of 82 of 83 with `fixture-registry-search` a standing exclusion, and that is what was measured. The two rows that stood between 80 and 82 closed the same day: `install-launchd-watch` by ai/p8, which made the `reran` term attributable — it had read yes on 2 of 6 decoy trials where no stimulus could reach the watched path — and `control-auth-post-http` by ai/p7, which built a real OAuth client and now agrees with the reference across the discovery cascade, the registration bytes, the PKCE parameters, the token exchange, the callback page, the credential file and the re-authorization branch. **The gate exits 1 and that is not this case failing.** It exits 1 while any row is blocked, deliberately, and the one blocked row is the standing exclusion the requirement names. The gate prints the distinction itself: `82 proven is at or past the target of 82. That is a count, not a licence`. Read as a pass on the requirement, not as a licence to flip the installer — that is the owner's call on R4-C's evidence, which this case does not make. **Armed, and one arm was not planned.** The mechanical arm is `parity-lane-selftest`, which runs every lane against a deliberately broken Swift router and requires each to go red; it ran green in the same `make all` that carried this tree, printing `every new lane went red against a broken router. The lanes can fail.` The unplanned arm is the first whole-gate run of the day, kept at `evidence/runs/parity-gate-2026-08-20-oauth-flake.log`: the same script on the same tree reported `81 of 83 rows proven … 1 DIVERGED … This is NOT a pass`, so the aggregate verdict is live rather than a constant. That run's cause is unexplained and is recorded as DEF-033 rather than absorbed into this note.

subject.evidence: Four registrations on this host, each started and then killed, with Get-ScheduledTaskInfo and Win32_Process as recorders: (1) the product's own document - LogonTrigger, RestartOnFailure PT60S count 3, MultipleInstancesPolicy IgnoreNew - started on demand, process killed. LastTaskResult became 0xFFFFFFFF and no replacement process appeared in 130 s. (2) the same with UseUnifiedSchedulingEngine false. Identical. (3) the same started by a real TimeTrigger rather than on demand, so the run was a triggered one. Identical, watched 150 s. (4) POSITIVE CONTROL: the same settings with a Command naming a file that does not exist. LastTaskResult 0x80070002, and LastRunTime advanced at 02:58:08, 02:59:09 and 03:00:10 - three restarts at exactly the configured interval and count. So the instrument can see a restart, and RestartOnFailure governs a task that fails to LAUNCH rather than one whose action launched and later died - which is the only case LifecyclePresentation's "restarts on crash" was ever about.
subject.title: The logon task's RestartOnFailure block never restarted a crashed daemon, under a UI promising it did

cell.dataShape: two claims inside one renotify window

subject.note: R26. The throttle withholds a REPEAT and never an ESCALATION. The brief asks that a recurring error not generate alert spam, and the naive reading -- one alert per server per window -- swallows the one transition that matters. Four things make a notice due: nothing has been said yet, the KIND changed, the EXPIRY moved, or the window elapsed. E13 runs with `renotifyAfterMs` set to a year so nothing can go out on elapsed time, watches `expiring` become `expired` one millisecond past the boundary, and then asserts the repeat after it IS withheld -- so the arm is the escalation rather than the throttle being broken.

R26. Reading the report does not consume the notice; claiming it does. That is why there are two routes rather than one: folding them together would make `GET /upstreams/auth-expiry` spend the notification a caller was about to be shown, so opening a settings pane would silence the next alert. It is the same rule this repository enforces on its own gates -- a check that mutates the tree as a side effect of checking is not a check. E16 asserts it on the monitor and E24 through the routes; the lane asserts it as `count:2` after two GETs.

cell.dataShape: a credential record with no expires_in

subject.note: R26. THE VACUITY CASE, and the reason this item exists in the shape it does. A token whose stored record declares no lifetime has no derivable expiry, and the tempting reading -- it has not expired, therefore it is fine -- is the class this campaign keeps finding: a state that reads healthy because nothing measured it. `AuthExpiryRecord.state` has NO path from a missing number to `valid`; it returns `unknown` and the wire carries `unknownReason` saying which half is missing (`no-lifetime-declared` when `expires_in` is absent, `unreadable-authorized-at` when the stamp is). Asserted at both planes: E5/E6/E17/E21 in the suites, and the lane reads `state`, `unknownReason` and the ABSENCE of any invented `expiresAt` off a record it planted itself. Not `expiresAt: null` -- absent, so there is nothing there for a careless reader to round to fine.

cell.dataShape: an authExpiry block below the floor

subject.note: R26. A configured value the router will not take is REFUSED and reported with its key, its value as written, the floor that rejected it and its scope -- never clamped. A clamp invents a number nobody wrote, so the file says 500 and the behaviour is 60000 with nothing anywhere saying which is real. `warnWithinMs`'s floor is this item's own vacuity rule and ZERO IS NOT ACCEPTED: at zero a token passes straight from valid to expired and `expiring` is unreachable, which is R27's `tripAfter >= 2` one item earlier. E2 asserts that in both directions -- under a zero window a token one millisecond from death reads `valid`, and under the resolved policy the same token reads `expiring`.

cell.dataShape: a credential re-authorised between two claims

subject.note: R26. *Resolving authentication immediately clears the warning status* -- the brief's third bullet, and it is a CLEAR rather than an age-out. A server that stops deserving a notice has its delivery record DROPPED, so the next thing that goes wrong is reported at once instead of waiting out a six-hour window. The lane proves it against a wall clock: it re-authorises the record from outside, claims, breaks it again, claims again, and the notice arrives seconds later under the default six-hour renotify. A throttle that merely aged out could not produce that. The absence half is paired -- a SECOND server is broken in the same step, so 'the re-authorised one is gone' is read off a reply that carries another server rather than off an empty one.

cell.dataShape: no monitor, and the wrong verb, token and content type

subject.note: R26. With no monitor both routes answer 503 NAMING the missing capability, the shape `/harnesses`, `/extensions`, `/caches` and `/upstreams/health` use -- an empty report would be indistinguishable from a router holding no credentials at all. Beside it the wire refusals: 405 on the wrong verb for each path, 401 untokened, 415 with no content type, and a 404 rather than a 405 on `/upstreams/auth-expiryx`, because claiming a prefix collision would turn a typo into an answer that reads as 'the method is wrong'.

cell.dataShape: five upstreams, four planted records, one stdio server

subject.note: R26. THE PAIRED ABSENCE, and the load-bearing case. The claim is that the expiry is DERIVED from files the router already wrote rather than asked of the upstream, and half of that claim is an absence: nothing was spawned. An absence asserted alone is satisfied by a feature that does nothing, which is REQ-035's recorded lesson. So the lane never asserts it alone. It reads the daemon's child count off the process table -- zero, and zero running the stdio fixture's own script -- in the same run in which it REWRITES a planted credential record between two requests and requires the reported `expiresAt` and `state` to move with it. Zero children beside a report that follows the file is the claim; zero children alone is not.

subject.cell: execution-plane=static-source-read - data-shape=the registry as committed
subject.note: The surface DENOMINATOR reconciled against the product rather than against itself. R1 every id in DestinationCatalog.All has a surface row; R2 every Label is a declared control on the shell surface; R3 every requirement sourced from app/windows/ that has a case reaches a surface that exists; R4 every Windows surface declaring controls says where the list came from, and every control it names appears verbatim in the files that source names. What makes this more than the registry checking the registry: the denominator is parsed out of C# the WinUI compiler enforces - ShellWindow builds its pane by iterating DestinationCatalog.All, so a destination cannot reach a user without appearing in the list this reads - and out of the boards' own XAML. Typing a row into inventory.json cannot make R1, R2 or R4 pass. It found two real things on the tree it was written against: SURF-045's controlsSource named a path that does not exist (LogonTaskSupervisor.cs is under Lifecycle/), and SURF-030 declared a control called 'NavigationView pane' that appears in no source file at all. WHAT IT DOES NOT CHECK: that a declared control is drawn, reachable, or does anything - that is control-census.py's actuated count and the UIA lane behind it - and that a board's list is COMPLETE, because affordances built in a DataTemplate or in code-behind carry no literal a static reader can see. Every such row says so in its controlsSourceNote and the count is a floor.

subject.cell: execution-plane=static-source-read - data-shape=one registry fact removed per arm
subject.note: Seven arms, each removing exactly one fact and requiring the exit code to move: the Harnesses surface row deleted (R1 red), `Insights` removed from the shell's controls (R2 red), CASE-0341 stripped of its surface link (R3 red), SURF-036's controlsSource removed (R4 red), SURF-031's source path misspelt (R4 red), a control invented on SURF-039 (R4 red), and DestinationCatalog.cs emptied - which must exit 2 and REFUSE a verdict rather than reporting a clean registry, because a reader that finds nothing must not report a pass. 7/7 moved. The arm restores every file in a finally, and its last act is to re-run the reader and require green, so a half-applied mutation cannot be left behind as a passing run.
