subject.source: found while writing brief citations for DEF-090, 2026-09-03, by reading every case's `req` against the requirement it names
subject.text: MEASURED, not inferred. `planning/test-campaign/cases.json` files CASE-0270, CASE-0271, CASE-0272, CASE-0273, CASE-0274 and CASE-0275 under `req: REQ-035`. All six are the R22 diagnostics-bundle lane: credential redaction in an exported bundle, the needle floor, percent-encoded secrets, and the POST/GET gate on the bundle route, all in lane `router-daemon` on plane `live-external`. REQ-035's own text in `inventory.json` is `On Windows the router daemon is supervised by a Scheduled Task registered against the user's own logon: it starts in the interactive user session ... it runs un-elevated, and it is restarted ...`. CASE-0308 is filed under the same REQ-035 and IS about that task - `execution-plane=windows-host`, actuating LogonTaskSupervisor.Register/Unregister, read back through Get-ScheduledTask. So one requirement id carries two case families that share no subject, and six of the seven cases under it measure something the requirement does not state. WHY IT MATTERS RATHER THAN BEING UNTIDY. reckon and `strict-check` both answer `what proves REQ-035` by the cases that cite it. Today that answer is six rows about a diagnostics bundle plus one about a scheduled task, so REQ-035 reads as far better evidenced than it is, and the diagnostics bundle - which is real, passing and armed - has NO requirement of its own anywhere in `inventory.json`. A feature with no requirement cannot be reported as unbuilt, unmeasured or done; it is simply outside every denominator. HOW IT WAS FOUND, said because it bears on how many more there may be: not by a gate. It surfaced while citing `daemon-diagnostics-bundle-export.md` to the six cases that actually measure its subject, which is the one reading that puts a case's `req` beside the requirement's text. WHAT IS NOT SETTLED. (1) Which way to fix it is an adjudication and not a runner's call: either a new requirement is written for the diagnostics bundle and the six cases are re-pointed at it, or REQ-035's text is widened - and widening it would make one requirement mean two things, which is the shape that produced this. (2) NO INSTRUMENT COVERS THIS. Nothing in `planning/` compares a case's `req` against the requirement's subject; `registry-drop-gate` and `target-resolution-gate` check that an id RESOLVES, not that it is the right one. A gate that could catch it would have to read meaning rather than membership, and no arm was added here rather than adding a green that would not have caught this. (3) Whether any other requirement in this registry is double-booked the same way is UNMEASURED - only REQ-035 was checked, because only REQ-035 was in front of me.
subject.title: Six diagnostics-bundle cases are filed under REQ-035, which is the Windows logon-task requirement

subject.text: Measured by K3 on 2026-08-29 while trying to fill SURF-005's denominator. The design of record puts two scoping controls on this board and the build draws neither. `Servers` / `Skills` is a kind toggle: the mock filters its registry array on each row's `kind` and re-labels the table's own column with it. `RegistryEntry` carries no kind and the board searches one merged registry, so both halves of the toggle would draw the same list — there is nothing to filter on rather than a filter nobody wired. `24h` / `7d` / `30d` is a window over install velocity, and the mock's own caption says the Trending table ranks "by install velocity over {window}, not total". The response carries `useCount`, a single total, with no series behind it, so a window control would have nothing to re-scope. The build's one segmented control is `RegistryPresentation.Ordering` — Best match / Most used on Smithery / Recently added to Smithery — which is a third thing the mock does not draw. So this is a divergence in both directions rather than an omission, and it surfaced only because the census gave the surface a denominator: five of SURF-005's nine declared controls are recorded under `controlsUnactuatable` rather than trimmed out, since a control removed from the denominator is a control nobody will ever ask about again.

IT IS NOT THE AMBIENT POLL THIS ITEM'S NEIGHBOUR ADDED. Deaths were observed on builds with the poll deliberately removed (planning/evidence/WIN-SHELL/arming/def-301-planted-lane.txt, three deaths in one run) as well as on the shipping build, and the last three runs of the shipping build were 10-of-10, 10-of-10-with-one-crash, and 10-of-10 clean. subject.evidence: CAUSE FOUND AND FIXED, 2026-09-03. shell-lane.ps1's Start-Shell stopped stale shells with `Get-Process 'MCPRouter.Shell'`, which names every process of that name on the MACHINE. Two runners in a fleet wave run this lane from two worktrees at once, so each one's Start-Shell terminated the other's shell partway through its sweep. The victim reported a destination CRASH at whichever destination it happened to be reading - which is why the four deaths landed on four different destinations, why none left an `unhandled:` line in shell-startup.log, and why none produced an Application Error or Windows Error Reporting event: nothing faulted, the process was killed. Four deaths in eleven runs on 2026-09-03, on BOTH trees - the DEF-302 branch and, after stashing app/windows back to main's and rebuilding clean, main's own. THE OTHER RUNNER WAS THEN SEEN DIRECTLY: with the fix in place the lane logged `leaving a shell that is not this lane's subject, pid=40292 at C:\Dev\mcp-router\.worktrees\wd1-ambient-truth\...\MCPRouter.Shell.exe` - a second runner's shell, live in the same interactive session, exactly the process the old code would have killed. run-shell-lane.ps1's own header already records the same collision one level up, on the scheduled TASK NAME, from 2026-09-02.

subject.evidence: `discover()` reads the git INDEX through `git ls-files` and separately walks the DISK through `os.walk` + `os.path.relpath`, then names the difference as briefs the gate did not read. `git ls-files` prints POSIX separators on every platform; `os.path.relpath` prints the platform's. On Windows the two sets therefore never intersect and the difference is the WHOLE corpus. Measured before the fix on this branch: the same run printed `brief discovery read 226 items of the git index ...; kept 219` and, four lines later, `219 brief(s) on disk are NOT in the index and are outside this verdict`, listing ten of them and `... and 209 more`. Both sentences cannot be true. The verdict and the partition were correct throughout - it is the accounting sentence above them that was false.

subject.detail: **The recorded cause was wrong, and this replaces it.** It said the shutter fired during a board transition and named the fix as a settle in `capture-mac-glass.sh`. Measured 20 Aug 2026 from the accessibility dumps the same script already writes, one per board, beside the pictures: | board | window | AXSplitGroup | clipped | |---|---|---|---| | Servers, Activity, Cleanup, Inbox, Settings | 980pt | 980pt | — | | Checks | 980pt | 988pt | 8pt | | Skills | 980pt | 1044pt | 64pt | | Discover | 980pt | 1119pt | 139pt | Every window in the run is the same 980x620 and every capture is the same 2096x1376, so no capture rect is wrong and no shutter is early. What differs is the shell **inside** the window: on three boards `NavigationSplitView` lays out wider than the window and centres the excess — the split group's origin moves left by exactly half the overflow in all three cases (180→148 for 64pt, 180→110.5 for 139pt, 180→176 for 8pt), which is what makes the clipping symmetrical. That is why the sidebar's section headers read `unning` and `brary` while the nav rows beside them are whole: the headers sit at a smaller leading inset and fall off first, and the header's trailing controls — `Manage marketplaces.`, `Review 2.3.0…` — fall off the right by the same amount. So this is a product defect on three boards rather than a lane defect on two captures, and it is worse than recorded: Checks overflows too, by 8pt, which is small enough that nobody reading the picture saw it. The app declares no minimum window width anywhere, so nothing stops a user reaching this state — the campaign's 980pt window is an ordinary size, not a stress case. The consequence that made it a defect stands unchanged and is now better founded: a clipped capture is admissible for what it shows and silent about what it cut, so a reader cannot tell an absent control from a cropped one. Both witness verdicts that depend on these captures say in their method field that the right-hand controls were read from the accessibility dump instead. `capture-mac-glass.sh` now prints `board width: examined=14 overflowing=3` every run, with a line naming each board and its excess. Reported rather than enforced, because three boards overflow today and a known red in `make all` either blocks unrelated work or gets its assertion softened. NOT FIXED, and the fix is a decision rather than a repair. Either the shell declares a minimum window width at least as wide as its widest board — one line, guarantees nothing ever clips, and costs users on small screens a window they cannot shrink — or the three boards compress, which keeps small screens usable and is per-board column work across all three. Discover at 1119pt is the one that decides how much that costs. PARTLY CLOSED 20 Aug 2026, on `ai/x4`, and the part that is not closed is named rather than left to look finished. The mechanism turned out to be a chain rather than a board: each row's fixed columns report a hard minimum width, the detail pane sums them, `NavigationSplitView` reports that as its own minimum, and nothing ever reads it back — this app opts into no minimum window size and `windowResizability` defaults to `.automatic` — so the window proposes 980pt and SwiftUI **places** the oversized child with default centre alignment. The symmetry was the tell. Referred to the xAI lane (grok-4.6, xhigh) with the measured table; it named the propagation as the bug, called both listed fixes second-best, and its Q3 answer — placement plus `.automatic` resizability rather than any documented split-view overflow mode — is what the one-line fix then confirmed. FIXED: `ContentZone` carries `.frame(minWidth: 0, maxWidth: .infinity, alignment: .leading)`. Measured on the rebuilt app through the same accessibility channel: all eight boards read `split=980` inside a `window=980`, overflowing 0 of 8, where the same probe on the previous build read 3 of 8. The sidebar is whole again — `Running`, `Library` and the footer readout all render in full where they were `unning` and `brary`. The leading alignment is the deliberate half: it decides who loses when the content still does not fit, and the answer is never the navigation. STILL OPEN: the boards' content is still wider than the detail pane on those three, so the trailing chrome is cut at the pane's right edge — Discover's search field reads `Search the regis` and a body sentence loses its last word. That is one-edge clipping where it was two, and it is the conventional behaviour of a too-narrow window rather than a split view eating its own sidebar, but it is still content going missing without saying so. Closing it needs the three boards' columns to flex, which is a design decision about what Discover looks like compressed and is the owner's rather than mine. GUARDED two ways, and the two see different things. `capture-mac-glass.sh` now **fails** on any board whose split group exceeds its window, and refuses to pass on `examined=0`; all three arms were exercised on 20 Aug 2026 — red at 3 of 14, green at 0 of 14, and exit 1 with no dumps at all. `ShellDetailWidthTests` asserts the modifier in `ShellWindow`'s detail column so a revert is red in `make test` rather than on the next glass run. That test's own first version was a detector defect found by arming: it searched the raw source slice, and the modifier it looks for is named in the doc comment three lines above it, so deleting the modifier left the assertion green. Comments are stripped before matching now, and both halves were re-armed separately. CLOSED 20 Aug 2026, and the second half corrected the first half's diagnosis of *which* content was too wide. The brief written from the split-group numbers said three boards' table columns needed to flex. A pane-level probe — every leaf's right edge against the window's, read from the same dumps — says otherwise, and it says so only after the probe itself was fixed: the first version read the frame's **y** where it meant **x** and reported clipping on seven of eight boards, which the pixels flatly denied. The Settings capture is whole, and looking at it is what caught the field offset. A frame's last five fields are x, y, w, h and a flag; the split-group gate only ever compared widths, which is why it was right while the leaf probe was wrong. Corrected, the drivers are: - **Discover**: content wants 823pt against a 684pt pane. Not the table — cutting `nameColumn` from 216pt to 96pt moved the number by **zero**. It is the controls row: a `.fixedSize()` segmented picker measuring 567pt beside a search field pinned at 240pt. - **Skills**: 748pt against 684pt, same shape — a 516pt fixed picker and a 216pt pinned field. - **Checks**: not a content defect at all. Its real content ends at 1152pt inside a 1160pt pane; the only thing past the edge is `KeyClaimProbe`, the `#if DEBUG` test surface A21 names, overhanging by 4pt. It is absent from any build a user runs, and it is what the whole 8pt split-group excess on this board was. FIXED by giving each board a `searchMinWidth` of four units and declaring the field `minWidth:idealWidth:maxWidth:` rather than `width:`. The picker cannot give a point back — that is what `.fixedSize()` means, and it is right, because a segmented control has nowhere to put a truncated label — so the field is the only control in the row that can. It renders at its full width wherever there is room and shows about eight characters at the narrowest window this app is used at, which is less than anyone wants and more than nothing: it still takes focus, accepts a query and submits. Measured after: every board reads `split=980` in a `window=980`, and the only leaf past the pane edge on any of the eight is a 1pt scrollbar — plus the Debug key probe's 4pt on Checks. Before, Discover's rows and footnote sat at 1283pt against an edge of 1160. GUARDED by a second test in `ShellDetailWidthTests`, armed 20 Aug 2026: restoring `.frame(width: DiscoverBoardMetrics.searchWidth)` reddens all three of its assertions. It names the two boards rather than looping over every file, because those are the two the measurement covers — a third board growing this problem is a new measurement, not a case this test silently already made.
subject.title: three Mac boards lay out wider than their window, so both edges clip in silence

subject.detail: Measured 2026-08-27 by G16 while enumerating SURF-026, and independently by G15. M15 made Settings a Scene and removed the case from `Destination`, and capture-mac-glass.sh still ran `axkit select Settings`. That select fails — `axkit: no sidebar row starting 'Settings'` — the app stays on whichever board the loop visited last, and the shutter filed THAT board's pixels under SURF-011: byte-identical to the Cleanup board on one loop ordering and to the Insights board on another. THE CAMPAIGN'S OWN INSTRUMENTS CAUGHT IT FROM TWO DIRECTIONS, which is the part worth keeping. glass-assert.py's raster uniqueness check went red because two cases shared a sha256; `--discriminate` reported the neighbouring board's predicate wrongly accepting SURF-011's dump, because that dump IS the neighbouring board; and the capture manifest's readback recorded the picture's target as the neighbour's route under subject SURF-011, contradicting its own filename. FIXED HERE, NARROWLY: the capture script now refuses to photograph a select that did not take, and says which board the window is actually showing. That is the script's own standing rule rather than a new one — it already declines to substitute a picture for the pairing sheet and the status item, and its header records the run that filed the Inbox board as SURF-010. The title and the dump are still written from what the app is really showing, so the failure stays visible downstream; what is withheld is the photograph, because a misattributed picture is the one artefact nothing downstream can correct. STILL OPEN, and deliberately not fixed here: 1. SURF-011 has no route to the Settings SCENE. It needs Cmd-comma or the app menu, not a sidebar select that cannot succeed. CASE-0016 and CASE-0111 fail until it does. 2. THE MENU MAP IS PRE-M22. Committed SURF-001.menu.txt binds Cmd-4 to `Discover`; the running app binds Cmd-4 to `Harnesses`, exactly as Destination.selectionDigit declares (activity 1, servers 2, skills 3, harnesses 4, discover 5, inbox 6, evals 7, cleanup 8, insights 9). glass-assert.py's SURF-001 `menu` dict is the old map, so CASE-0001 asserts five bindings this build does not have. Correcting it is editing an assertion to restore a green, which this campaign forbids — it is owed as its own item, from Destination.selectionDigit rather than by hand. WHY IT IS THE SAME FINDING AS G14'S, ONE LAYER DOWN. G14 found the surface LIST had stopped growing while the product did. This is the EVIDENCE not having been re-taken since the build moved: the committed glass artefacts were last written on 20 Aug by cef3729, before M22 added two destinations and renumbered four accelerators. In both cases a completeness gate reported clean because what it measured was a stale artefact rather than the product. CLOSED ON THE EVIDENCE SIDE, 2026-08-27 (G21/G29). The frame this defect produced was still published: `inventory.json` gave SURF-011 the shot `evidence/shots/SURF-011.build.png`, and at `519aebc` those bytes were the Insights board. `capture-lineage.py --gate` reported it UNTIED because the capture step's own row said `target: app://mac/insights` while the filename said SURF-011 -- the manifest was right and the wall was wrong. Two moves, both provable from git. The Insights frame is renamed `evidence/shots/DEF-059.insights-filed-as-SURF-011.png`, keeping every capture-time field, so the defect keeps its exhibit and no filename match can offer it to SURF-011 again. The Settings capture it overwrote is restored to `SURF-011.build.png` from `cef3729`, TOGETHER WITH ITS MANIFEST ROW from the same commit -- the last commit where those bytes and that row agreed (sha 3b5a26ef, `target: app://mac/settings`, readback `Settings`, 2026-08-20T11:32:58Z). Restoring the pair from one commit is a recovery of a capture-time record; restamping the row against the new bytes would have been the manifest-after-the-fact defect. What is NOT closed is the cause: `axkit select Settings` still fails, so the campaign still has no Settings capture newer than 2026-08-20 and the glass script still declines to take one. THE CAUSE NOW HAS A READER, 2026-09-02 (wa5). `axkit select Settings` still fails, and the campaign still has no Settings capture newer than 2026-08-20 -- unchanged. What has changed is that the age is no longer invisible: `bin/glass-build-gate.py` reports `evidence/shots/SURF-011.build.png` and `evidence/ax/SURF-011.*` as STALE against the build this tree would produce, so the lane cannot be green over them again without somebody re-taking them. `bin/capture-mac-glass.sh`'s refusal to photograph a select that did not take is the other half and is unchanged. Both halves of the remaining work -- a route to the Settings SCENE, and the re-capture -- are macOS work and are not attempted here. CLOSED 2026-10-19 on glass. capture-mac-glass.sh opens Settings with ⌘, (backgrounded), selects the Router pane in the Settings window's own source list, photographs that window as SURF-011 (target app://mac/settings), dumps the Security pane as a second dump of the same surface, and closes the window. glass-assert at the current build: checked=435 failures=0; --decoy SURF-011 reddens 6.
subject.title: `Settings` is no longer a sidebar row, so the glass capture filed a neighbouring board's pixels under SURF-011 — and the committed glass evidence predates M22

subject.detail: Measured 2026-08-27 by G15, while enumerating SURF-025. The committed glass evidence under planning/test-campaign/evidence/ax was last written by commit cef3729 on 20 Aug. M22 then added two destinations and RENUMBERED four accelerators, and nothing re-took the pictures. Running bin/capture-mac-glass.sh against the current build turns four previously-passing cases red, and in every one of them the PRODUCT is right and the recorded evidence is stale: 1. THE MENU MAP. Committed SURF-001.menu.txt binds Cmd-4 to `Discover`; the running app binds Cmd-4 to `Harnesses`, exactly as Destination.swift's selectionDigit declares (activity 1, servers 2, skills 3, harnesses 4, discover 5, inbox 6, evals 7, cleanup 8, insights 9). glass-assert.py's SURF-001 `menu` dict is the pre-M22 map, so CASE-0001 asserts five bindings the shipped build does not have. 2. SETTINGS IS NOT A SIDEBAR ROW. M15 made Settings a Scene and removed the case from Destination, and capture-mac-glass.sh still does `axkit select Settings`. That select now fails — `axkit: no sidebar row starting 'Settings'` — the app stays on Cleanup, and the script photographs the CLEANUP board and files it as SURF-011. CASE-0016 and CASE-0111 fail against it. THE CAMPAIGN'S OWN INSTRUMENTS CAUGHT BOTH, WHICH IS THE ONE GOOD PART. The capture manifest's readback records that picture as target `app://mac/cleanup` under subject SURF-011, contradicting its own filename — the exact mechanism the script was rebuilt around. Independently, glass-assert.py --discriminate reports LEAK SURF-007 wrongly accepted 1 of 8 foreign board dumps: SURF-011 — because SURF-011's dump IS the Cleanup board. Two instruments, one cause. WHY THIS IS THE SAME FINDING AS G14'S, ONE LAYER DOWN. G14 found the surface LIST had not grown since it was written. This is the EVIDENCE not having been re-taken since the build moved. In both cases a completeness gate reported clean because the thing it measured was a stale artefact rather than the product. NOT FIXED HERE, DELIBERATELY. G15's remit is the Harnesses enumeration, and correcting glass-assert.py's menu map or the Settings navigation would be editing an assertion to restore a green — even though the product is right, that is the move this campaign forbids, and the stale assertion is the instrument that found this. The four cases are set to `fail` with this id in their notes. Owed: re-map SURF-001's menu dict from Destination.selectionDigit, and give SURF-011 a route to the Settings SCENE (Cmd-comma or the app menu) instead of a sidebar select that cannot succeed. INSTRUMENTED 2026-09-02 (wa5), NOT CLOSED. The cause this row names -- a committed capture carrying no tie to the build it came from -- is now measurable. `planning/test-campaign/bin/glass-build-gate.py` binds every artifact the macos-glass lane cites to the git blob identity of the Mac app's build inputs (the set `scripts/acceptance/build-freshness.sh` compiles from) and exits 2 when that identity is not the one the lane is being read against. It is RED on this tree over all 56 artifacts, in 7 capture groups spanning 20-29 Aug: `evidence/runs/glass-build-gate.log`. The stamps it reads are marked `reconstructed-from-git` and are deliberately the weaker claim -- git can prove which commit last wrote each artifact, so the record establishes the build the evidence CANNOT BE NEWER THAN rather than the build it was taken from. `bin/capture-mac-glass.sh` now calls `glass-build-gate.py --emit` in the run that takes the pictures, stamping from the bundle's own CFBundleShortVersionString/CFBundleVersion and the `.mcprouter-build-stamp` the Makefile writes after `xcodebuild` exits 0, so a re-capture replaces each reconstructed row with a capture-time one. Watched both ways: `evidence/runs/glass-build-gate.selftest.log`, four arms, green over a current capture and red over a stale one, an uncovered one and an undatable row. Case CASE-0342. WHAT IS NOT SETTLED. The re-capture itself, which is the whole of what this defect asks for. It needs a macOS host with Xcode and a display server; the work above was done on Windows, where there is no Swift toolchain, no xcodebuild and no way to open the app's window. The four cases stay `fail` with `owed` recording the re-capture and its owner. The second half of the row -- SURF-001's menu map, to be re-read from `Destination.selectionDigit` rather than by hand -- is equally macOS work and equally untouched. Nothing here edits an assertion, a stamp or a recorded identity to restore a green.
subject.title: the macos-glass lane is green over window evidence captured from a pre-M22 build, and four of its cases assert a shell that no longer ships

subject.detail: Measured 2026-08-21 against test-campaign 0.9.2 on app/Tests. The pass reports examined=1661 mutating=320 blind=88. Two structural errors and two idiom errors inflate that number. STRUCTURAL. (1) It scans every `func`, not every test. Restricted to swift-testing's own discriminator (a func whose nearest preceding annotation is @Test) the denominator is 1531, not 1661: 130 of the examined functions are not tests. (2) Its helper exclusion at vacuity-check.py:162 is file-scoped — a name is a helper only if called more than once in the file that declares it. A shared stub declared in TestSupport.swift and called from other files therefore reads as a test, so MemoryFileSystem's `write`, `removeItem` and `moveItem`, HTTPStub's `stop` and WatchTestSupport's `remove` are each counted as a blind test. 21 of the 88 are support-file functions. IDIOM, on the mutator side. (3) The lookbehind `(?<![A-Za-z0-9_])` cannot exclude a dot, so a Swift enum case constructor matches a mutator verb: `ServerRowAction.forServer(s, pendingAuth: nil) == .reset(.clearPlacard)` reports ServerPresentationTests::trippedOutranksHeld as mutating via 'reset', where `.reset` is the expected VALUE inside the assertion. 41 of 72 re-measured findings are dot-prefixed. (4) It takes the last mutator by source POSITION and calls everything after it the tail, which misreads three Swift constructs: a mutator inside the assertion (`await #expect(throws: Never.self) { try await store.delete() }` — nothing can follow it by construction), a mutator in a `defer` block (source-early, execution-last, so the whole test body reads as 'after'), and a mutator as the last statement of a loop body whose observation is the next iteration (CallbackLifecycleTests::stopReleasesTheSocket rebinds the port ten times; the read of cycle N is the start() of cycle N+1). SAMPLE. Of the 15 findings with zero assertions after the last mutator — the highest-yield stratum — 9 were read in full. Two (DiscoveryTests::servers, CapabilityPlateTests::install) are helpers. All 7 remaining are real tests that do observe after mutating, through idioms no reader verb names: `client.calls.last?.operation`, `seen.filter { ... }`, a rebind that throws. Precision on that stratum is 0 of 7. ARMED, two ways, evidence/arming/blind-mutation.arming.log. A probe @Test that mutates and never observes was added and removed: blind moved 88 -> 89 -> 88 and examined/mutating moved by exactly 1 each time. The check does bite; it is the false-positive rate that is at issue, not the sensitivity. NOT REMEDIED BY VOCABULARY. The reader side is deliberately loose because a false reader match suppresses a finding. Adding this codebase's read idioms (`calls`, `operation`, `filter`) would lower the number without improving what the pass knows, and the terms are generic enough to suppress true findings too. The 88 stands recorded as a worklist with its measured precision beside it rather than tuned to look better. RE-MEASURED 2026-08-27 by G22, which declared `testRoot` and gave this pass a corpus for the first time. THE 88 DOES NOT REPRODUCE. Vendored 0.9.2 over `app/Tests` today reports examined=2133 mutating=3 blind=3, against the 1661/320/88 above. The denominator moving up while `mutating` collapses 320 → 3 is not tree churn: 0.9.1 and 0.9.2 ship IDENTICAL DEFAULT_MUTATORS and DEFAULT_READERS, and neither list holds `reset`, `write`, `removeItem`, `moveItem` or `remove` — the verbs this entry's idiom argument turns on. So the 2026-08-21 sitting ran an expanded vocabulary passed on the command line, and `campaign.json` declares none, which makes 88 a figure no documented invocation returns. Its cited evidence, `evidence/arming/blind-mutation.arming.log`, has never existed on any branch of this repository (`git log --all -- '*blind-mutation*'` is empty), so the arming claim above is not checkable from the tree. The measured structural and idiom errors are not withdrawn; what is withdrawn is the population they were measured over. TODAY'S POPULATION, AND ITS PRECISION. With `testRoot: app` the pass reports examined=2179 mutating=3 re-read-after=0 blind=3, and 0.15.0 returns the same three findings from the same corpus. All THREE were read in full — 3 of 3, not a sample — and all three are false positives. Precision 0 of 3. A FOURTH CAUSE, NOT IN THE ORIGINAL ENTRY, AND THE ONE THAT PRODUCES TWO OF THE THREE. The body slice is `src[pos:end]` where `pos` is the start of the DECLARATION, so a test whose own name begins with a mutator verb matches itself. `WatchRestartTests::restartIsIssuedBeforeTheStagingWrite` and `::restartIsOwedBeforeTheWriteLands` contain no mutating call at all: the only `restart\w*\(` in each is `func restart…(` on its own declaration line. Both then read — `WatchWorld.read(scratch.logPath)`, `WatchState.load(path:)`, `WatchWorld.serverNames(in:)` — and assert on `state.mcpServersHash` and `state.restartPending`. The third, `PhoneStorageFailureTests::restartRechecksTheCamera`, does call `await model.restart()` and then asserts twice, on `model.step` and on `model.entry.characters`: property reads that no reader verb names, which is cause (4)'s shape rather than a new one. This cause survives into 0.15.0 unchanged. NOT ENROLLED IN A GATE, and `blindVocabulary` still not declared, for the reason the entry already gives. A related gap measured at the same sitting: pointed at `src/` — the TypeScript tree, which has no tests — the pass prints `corpus: … (0 file(s))` and `examined=0 mutating=0 blind=0` and contributes nothing to `--gate`. It reports its empty corpus and does not fail on it, so a mis-declared `testRoot` reads as a clean pass. VOCABULARY DECLARED 2026-08-29 by K4, and the entry's own 'NOT REMEDIED BY VOCABULARY' paragraph is narrowed rather than withdrawn. That paragraph reasons entirely from the READER side, and on the reader side it is still right: adding this codebase's read idioms lowers the count without improving what the pass knows, which is why the declared reader list stops short of `expect` and `require` -- swift-testing's assertion macros, 5781 and 383 occurrences, either of which would mark every test that asserts after mutating as re-reading and collapse the count to near zero while the pass learned nothing. THE MUTATOR SIDE WAS NEVER ARGUED, AND THAT IS WHERE THE PASS WAS BLIND. Measured over the same 2282 test bodies at `83e5380`: the nine snake_case defaults find 3 mutating call sites; a camelCase list derived from this corpus finds 481. So `blind=3` was a reading of 3 of 481, a recall of 0.6%, and the entry's `precision 0 of 3` was a precision over a population the instrument could barely see. `campaign.json` now carries `blindVocabulary` with `only: true`, 19 mutators and 34 readers, derived mechanically -- a verb is kept only where method calls on a receiver are at least half its corpus sites and its own `func` declaration lines at most a quarter, which is causes (3) and (4) of this entry turned into a selection rule. THE THREE FINDINGS ARE ADJUDICATED, and each clears for a different checkable reason rather than all three for one. `restartIsIssuedBeforeTheStagingWrite`: one fitted mutator, `WatchWorld.remove(scratch)` inside a `defer`, and four declared readers after it -- `load`, `read`, `parse`, `servers`. NOT blind, positively. `restartIsOwedBeforeTheWriteLands`: three fitted mutators, the last `WatchState(restartPending: true).save(`, with `load` after it. NOT blind, positively. `restartRechecksTheCamera`: ZERO fitted mutator call sites in its body. It was flagged only because `restart` is a shipped default and this entry's fourth cause -- the body slice beginning at the declaration -- made `func restartRechecksTheCamera(` match itself. `restart` fails the selection rule (1 method call against 3 declaration lines, of 5 sites), so it is not in the vocabulary and the finding is withdrawn. WHAT THAT DOES NOT MEAN: its real mutation `await model.restart()` is now invisible to the pass, and its reads are still the property comparisons `model.step` and `model.entry.characters` that no reader verb names. It is UNEXAMINED by this instrument, not clean, and that is this entry's ceiling stated once more rather than closed. ARMED, AND ENROLLED, which the entry recorded as missing. `planning/test-campaign/bin/blind-vocabulary-arm.py` runs on every `make lint`: two plants identical but for one line, each measured alone and again inside a `shutil.copytree` of the real corpus, requiring examined+1 mutating+1 blind+1 for the blind plant and examined+1 mutating+1 blind+0 for the reading one. The specificity arm is the half a sensitivity arm alone cannot give: a detector that flagged every mutating body would pass the first and say nothing. 6 of 6 as expected on `cache 0.16.0` and again on the `vendor/` pin via `--instrument`. The two disagree only on the denominator -- 2282 against 2277, the five arrow-style `it/test(` blocks 0.9.3 added block detection for -- and agree on blind=111. THE 111 IS A WORKLIST AND THE CAMPAIGN STILL PUBLISHES NO BLIND NUMBER. Nothing above touches the structural causes: the pass still examines every `func` rather than every `@Test`, its helper exclusion is still file-scoped, and a `defer` mutator still reads as source-early -- which is exactly why the first of the three findings above needed reading rather than counting. This entry stays OPEN; what it now carries is a measured recall beside its measured precision.
subject.title: vacuity-check's blind-mutation pass examines non-tests and mis-reads Swift idiom; 7 of 7 sampled findings are false positives

subject.detail: Measured 2026-09-03 (WE3) while establishing whether `vendor/test-campaign` and the `.claude/plugins` copy are the same version, which DEF-057 asserts and this session was asked to establish rather than repeat. `.claude/plugins/fledgeling-plugins` at HEAD `baaf79a` carries `plugins/test-campaign/` with TWO manifests naming different versions: * `plugins/test-campaign/plugin.json` -> `"version": "0.6.0"` * `plugins/test-campaign/.claude-plugin/plugin.json` -> `"version": "0.5.0"` DEF-057 and the G5 brief both quote 0.5.0, so both read the second file, and both are right about the file they read. Neither is wrong; the artifact is. `vendor/test-campaign` carries both files too and they agree at 0.9.2, and the machine's cache carries only `.claude-plugin/plugin.json`, so the contradiction is specific to the older marketplace layout the submodule is pinned at. WHY IT IS FILED RATHER THAN NOTED. A version number is the whole of the evidence behind 'this defect is fixed upstream' and 'this script is four minor versions behind'. This session had to decide, per row, whether a defect in a vendored script is about a file anything here executes; a readback that returns a different answer depending which of two files in the same directory you open is not a readback. The practical consequence is small today -- the submodule is not on any gate's path and no worktree in this fleet initialises it -- and the shape is the one this campaign keeps filing: an instrument reporting confidently on two different questions under one name. NOT FIXABLE HERE: `.claude/plugins/` is a different repository, pinned, and out of bounds for this fleet by the same rule as `vendor/`.
subject.title: the vendored submodule's test-campaign carries two version files that disagree, so a version readback names 0.5.0 or 0.6.0 depending which one is read

subject.detail: Measured 2026-09-03 (WE3) on LUKESFF, Windows 11, CPython 3.13, console codepage 1252. `campaign.py`'s loader is `return json.loads(p.read_text())` with no `encoding=`. `Path.read_text()` defaults to `locale.getencoding()`, which is cp1252 here. This campaign's `inventory.json` holds em dashes and middots, so: $ python vendor/test-campaign/.../campaign.py check planning/test-campaign UnicodeDecodeError: 'charmap' codec can't decode byte 0x9d in position 284168 exit 1 It is a traceback rather than a verdict, and `exit 1` is the same code the gate uses for 'not ready to report'. A caller reading the exit status alone cannot tell a campaign that failed its checks from one the checker could not open. `PYTHONUTF8=1` makes it run; with that set it reaches its checks and reports normally, which is how the rest of this session's `campaign.py` measurements were taken. SCOPE. Windows hosts only -- macOS and most Linux default to UTF-8, which is why the campaign never met this on the Mac. It is not confined to `campaign.py`: `vacuity-check.py`, `strict-check.py` and `attach-shots.py` in the pinned 0.9.2 read and WRITE with the same bare calls, so on this host `attach-shots.py --apply` would write `inventory.json` back in cp1252 and mangle every em dash in the register. subject.note: Added by G17. `filesystem-read` is a new value in this campaign's effect vocabulary — the five that existed were none, inbound-socket, outbound-socket, subprocess and filesystem-write, and none of them describes a route that reads a directory it was told about. The requirement itself is not new work: M19 and M30 both shipped against it and the campaign had no row for it, so the feature had no denominator and no case could have failed on it. Reach limit, stated rather than buried: the route serves only servers declaring a package directory and 0 of the 21 upstreams on this machine declare one (M30, planning/evidence/M30-reach.txt), so every case citing this requirement is measured against a CONSTRUCTED server. RECONCILED 2026-08-27. This row was allocated REQ-026 by G17 and G19 at the same time, off the same `main`. G19's REQ-026 keeps the number and states the WIRE contract: what GET /servers/:name/document serves and the exact refusal each rule names. This row keeps the half G19's does not carry -- that those documents are DRAWN in the Mac capability document panel, that a figure resolves from inside the package and nothing else is fetched, and that each refusal identifies itself on screen. Its cases are the swiftui lane's (CASE-0185..0190, CASE-0194) and they need a requirement to trace to; folding them into a router-daemon requirement would put a panel assertion inside a route's contract. G17's one WIRE case, CASE-0184, traces to REQ-026 instead, because that is the requirement its assertion is of. The two rows overlap on 'read out of the declared package directory' deliberately: neither text was rewritten, so the overlap is visible rather than resolved by editing delivered work. The `filesystem-read` effect class is left exactly as G17 declared it and is NOT in campaign.py's closed EFFECT_CLASSES -- `check` has flagged that since G17 landed and still does; G19's REQ-026 note records the same gap from the other side, having declined to name a class the vocabulary does not hold. Reconciling the vocabulary is the campaign owner's, not this renumber's. VOCABULARY RECONCILED 2026-08-29 by K4, which is the campaign-owner decision the paragraph above defers. `filesystem-read` is NOT added to the census vocabulary and this row no longer declares it as its `effect`. The list is the instrument's and it is closed: 24 copies of `campaign.py` and `vacuity-check.py` visible to this repository -- the `vendor/` pin and eleven cache versions from 0.9.3 to 0.16.0 -- carry the same nine-member tuple, `vendor/README.md` forbids editing the vendored copy ('a script that behaves one way in this repository and another way everywhere else stops being evidence of anything'), and upstream is a different repository. So the branch taken is the acceptance sketch's first: declare a class the census knows. THE CLASS IS `none`, AND `none` HERE MEANS `no representable class`, NOT `no external interaction`. The router does read the filesystem and the row still says so, in `effectUnrepresentable`, which `planning/test-campaign/bin/effect-class-census.py` reads and holds to a HARDER obligation than an ordinary row rather than a softer one: the named class must be outside the instrument's set, `effect` must be exactly `none` so the narrowing is stated rather than implied, and `provider` must RESOLVE against `campaign.json`'s `sourceRoot` through vacuity-check's own `resolve_provider`. Measured 2026-08-29 at `83e5380`: it resolves by path on `RouterCore/Control/ControlDocument.swift`, so deleting the read site reddens this row even though it has left the external-effect census. WHY NOT `inbound-socket`, which is the option a second reader picked. The route is served on the loopback listener and the class is defensible, but declaring it would trade one blocker for another and neither reader had the fact: `campaign.py`'s `unbacked_effects` (campaign.py:1078) blocks a requirement that names an external effect, is recorded `observed`, and has no passing case at the `effect-witness` rung. REQ-027's seven cases are structural, structural-visual, raster-visual and metamorphic; none is a witness, and the eight witnesses this campaign holds belong to other requirements. Choosing `inbound-socket` therefore means BUILDING a witness with a recorder, a non-zero count and a sabotage arm -- real engineering, and its subject would be the accept that CASE-0183 already witnesses for REQ-026. Recorded as the alternative it beat, with the axis it is better on: `inbound-socket` keeps the row inside the instrument's own external-effect denominator, where `none` moves that obligation into a repository-owned gate. WHAT THIS DOES NOT SETTLE. The gate proves a provider exists in production source. That is the census floor, not a witness, and no case here observes a read at the boundary. The reach limit recorded above is unchanged.

FLOW-006.02, and the claim nothing had ever made: an image inside a served document DRAWS. This case does not fix that by adding a node: a node would say two views differ, and what needed saying is that bytes arrived and were painted. The pixels answer it. 65.7% of the figure card's own frame in readme.served.png is the constructed band's authored colour, read at the scale derived from the dump's size rather than assumed to be 2, with a 25% floor and a tolerance on the colour because the backing store resolves in the display's space (authored #2F9C9C reads back near #519A9B). The 'outside the package' refusal, rendered and distinguishable. Both halves matter: the node says WHICH refusal landed, which no dump could say before, and the pixels say the card really is a placeholder rather than a picture nobody checked. The node costs the readme fidelity census nothing, because it is drawn only when a reference is refused and the M19 fixture's one image resolves. J2. Every sidebar row is selected in turn and the effect is read in the RESTORATION STORE, which is a different channel from the one that struck: `ShellModel.selection`'s `didSet` calls `store.save(destination:)`, so a real selection leaves a value in a scratch `UserDefaults` suite that nothing in the test wrote, and that a relaunch reads. `model.selection == .servers` after `model.select(.servers)` was deliberately NOT used — it reads the property the call just wrote, which is the actuation side of the vacuous assertion (`references/inert-ui.md`, `detector-defects.md` §11). Each row is approached from a DIFFERENT destination, because `didSet` guards on `oldValue != selection` and a loop starting where the model boots would have the first row write nothing at all. The destination-collapse relation is asserted as a count rather than as seven separate greens: seven presses, seven DISTINCT persisted values, so a shell whose rows all led to one place fails on the cardinality. A second model built on the same store comes up where the last row left it, which is the read-back a relaunch actually performs. `Settings` is the eighth control and is not a destination: M15 moved it to a scene of its own, so the effect read is the installed opener firing exactly once AND the console's persisted destination not moving. Both halves, because an implementation that opened the scene and also selected a board would pass the first alone. LIMIT, stated rather than left implicit: a persisted destination proves the selection took. It does not prove a different board was DRAWN — SwiftUI's view tree is opaque to a SwiftPM test and `ContentZone`'s switch is unreachable from here. That half is CASE-0001's, on glass, and it is FAILING (DEF-058, DEF-059), so it counts nothing. This is the in-process half and says which half it is.

J2. `Held` and `All` are the two filter chips SURF-004 declares, driven off one loaded reading of the fixture. `Held` is asserted in both directions against `Skill.held?.wantsMore` — every row it draws has an update held, and every row it hid does not — and `All` is asserted as the RESTORATION, which is the assertion that fails if a segment latches. SURF-004 reaches 2 of 21 and the remaining four state-changing controls are recorded in `inventory.json` under `controlsUnactuatable` rather than left in the denominator unexplained: the build draws none of them. That is DEF-062, and it is the finding this case produced — `references/inert-ui.md`'s own stated limit is that no amount of testing the build reveals what the build lacks, and giving the surface a denominator is what made the four visible.

N8. The inertness guard on the untrusted-input boundary, made capable of failing. M19 shipped `MarkdownSecurityTests.htmlIsInert` with four spellings that named `javascript:`, no scheme, or nothing, and two assertions -- no link, no `imageURL` -- that `MarkdownInline.sanitized` makes true of every input it touches. It could not go red. M30 wired `ControlAPICapabilityDocumentSource` into the shipped UI, so router-served third-party text now reaches this renderer in a Release build, and the guard on it measured nothing. MEASURED, not assumed: the platform parser does keep inline HTML inert -- under `MarkdownInline`'s own options it hands each tag back as characters and marks it `.inlineHTML`, an intent naming no destination, and it does so under all four combinations of `allowsExtendedAttributes` and `interpretedSyntax`. Swift 6.2, macOS 26.6.2 (25G83), Debug, `swift test`. So this was an evidence defect and not a live vulnerability, and the fix is the assertion rather than new sanitisation. Two `https` spellings were added, because `https` is the one scheme the allowlist keeps and therefore the only one that can carry an interpreted `<a>` through to the assertion; a presence control runs the same reader over the markdown twin of the same destination first; and two clauses were added that the old body did not have -- handed back verbatim, and no attribute beyond the `.inlineHTML` marker. That last clause also corrects the test's own claim: the parser DOES attach one attribute to inline HTML and `sanitized` carries it, so the old name -- `inline HTML acquires no attribute of any kind` -- was false as written as well as unfailable, which is why nobody found out.

MEASURED, not assumed: the platform parser does keep inline HTML inert -- under `MarkdownInline`'s own options it hands each tag back as characters and marks it `.inlineHTML`, an intent naming no destination, and it does so under all four combinations of `allowsExtendedAttributes` and `interpretedSyntax`. Swift 6.2, macOS 26.6.2 (25G83), Debug, `swift test`. So this was an evidence defect and not a live vulnerability, and the fix is the assertion rather than new sanitisation. Two `https` spellings were added, because `https` is the one scheme the allowlist keeps and therefore the only one that can carry an interpreted `<a>` through to the assertion; a presence control runs the same reader over the markdown twin of the same destination first; and two clauses were added that the old body did not have -- handed back verbatim, and no attribute beyond the `.inlineHTML` marker. That last clause also corrects the test's own claim: the parser DOES attach one attribute to inline HTML and `sanitized` carries it, so the old name -- `inline HTML acquires no attribute of any kind` -- was false as written as well as unfailable, which is why nobody found out.

M38. A held tool surface is not served, and approving it is what starts serving it. The strike is POST /servers/:name/approve through the real ControlHandler; the read-back is MCPEndpoint.listTools() over a ManifestStore built before the strike and never handed to the handler — the two lines a client's tools/list runs. Never the approve response, which is the writer's account of its own write. An untouched sibling server in the same manifest is the control: every assertion about the promoted server is also passed by a route that promoted the whole file.

M38. Over a real router and the MCP SDK's own client: approving a held surface announces notifications/tools/list_changed, the announcement is ATTRIBUTED to the approval in the router's log rather than to the three-second poller's 'rebuilt outside this process', and the client's re-fetch carries the text the user accepted. The notification COUNT is not the oracle — the poller supplies one either way — so the log line is what the case stands on. scripts/e2e-live-reload.mjs.

M39's honesty control, and the reason it is filed against REQ-016 rather than REQ-015. REQ-016 is vacuous: no symbol in production source opens a connection to a paired device (DEF-001), so a guarantee about what happens after contact cannot be violated by a build that never contacts anything. M39 adds presentation on top of that and must not be readable as progress against it. What this case asserts is the frame: ShellPairingFactory.choice returns .noTransport for every scenario name in a Release build, so Phase.live -- the only phase drawing a ring or a fallback line -- is unreachable outside a Debug build with MCPROUTER_PAIRING set. No effect-witness case exists in this item because the item claims no effect: no recorder, no effect class, no count.

subject.text: DETECTOR DEFECT in test-campaign, measured 2026-08-27 (G29) against the vendored 0.9.2 and the machine's 0.15.0, which carry a byte-identical `tie()`. SURF-028's route is `app://mac/servers/{server}/document` -- a family of addresses, one per server. `bin/g17-document-flow.sh` rendered its frames against three of them and recorded each target honestly. `tie()` normalises scheme, host, port, query and fragment away and then asks for string equality or a suffix match, so `mac/servers/g17-capability/document` against `mac/servers/{server}/document` fails all three tests and the gate reports UNTIED -- 'the recorded target does not resolve to the subject's route'. Nothing was pointed at the wrong thing. `references/capture-lineage.md` says resolution is 'deliberately loose on the parts a harness legitimately varies'; a `{server}` segment is exactly such a part, and it is the one case the looseness does not cover. THE FIX BELONGS UPSTREAM, and is not applied here. `vendor/README.md` pins the tree by checksum so the gates can be re-run from a clone, and a `tie()` that behaves one way in this repository and another way everywhere else stops being evidence -- the same reasoning that keeps X7 and X8 open. Referred out of family (gpt-5.6-sol, high effort, 2026-08-27) and it reached the same conclusion independently: patch upstream, cut a release, re-vendor and re-pin, rather than forking the pinned copy. The patch is one function: treat a route segment of the form `{name}`, `:name` or `*` as matching exactly one non-empty target segment, leaving literal segments, the source-file refusal and the normalisation untouched, and leaving the seeded swap red. WHAT THIS REPOSITORY DID INSTEAD, and why it is not a workaround. The three served frames are published by the FLOW-006 steps that rendered them, each carrying the concrete route its own capture recorded, and SURF-028 publishes none. That is the registry becoming more accurate rather than less: the surface is a template and has no single portrait, while a step is that surface at one address and can name it. Every frame is now filed at the address the channel was pointed at. The detector limit is unchanged and is what this row records.
subject.title: The capture-lineage tie pass has no notion of a route template, so a parameterised surface's capture is reported as a wrong subject

DEF-015's closed half — the shell's overflow treatment, which DESIGN.md §5 names and the build got wrong in a way no assertion could see. Every board's `AXSplitGroup` width is read back out of the running app and compared against its own `AXWindow` width, board by board, through the channel that already writes those dumps beside the pictures. It read 3 of 8 overflowing — Checks 988, Skills 1044, Discover 1119 inside a 980pt window, each origin moved left by exactly half its excess — and reads 0 of 8 after `.frame(minWidth: 0, maxWidth: .infinity, alignment: .leading)` on `ContentZone`. `outcome` rather than `raster-visual` on purpose: the claim is a measured relation between two frames the app publishes, not a comparison of pixels, and the pictures are what made the defect *visible* rather than what proves it fixed. Armed 20 Aug 2026, three ways on the gate and two on the test. The gate exits 1 against the pre-fix dumps, 0 against the post-fix ones, and 1 with no dumps at all — `examined=0` is a check that never ran and is never a pass. Removing the modifier reddens `ShellDetailWidthTests` with `passes its boards' minimum width up to the split view`, and dropping just `alignment: .leading` reddens the second half alone. That test's first version did NOT bite: it searched the raw source and matched the doc comment naming the modifier, so deleting the modifier left it green. Comments are stripped before matching now — a predicate satisfied by the prose explaining it is not a predicate. What this case does not cover, because `overflowing=0` reads like `nothing is clipped` and is not that claim: content that overflows the detail PANE stays inside the window and is invisible to this oracle. That half is CASE-0134, measured with a second probe against every leaf's right edge — and that probe was wrong on its first run, reading the frame's y where it meant x and reporting clipping on seven of eight boards. The Settings capture is whole, and looking at it is what caught it.

Re-rated to `source-analysis`: it reads CleanupSheets.swift and no assertion in it proves a sheet was drawn, which its own previous note already said. The rendered claim is covered at an effect rung by CASE-0140 (outcome, macos-glass), which presses `Read first…` on the running build and reads the sheet's three fields and the absence of all four invented strings out of evidence/ax/SURF-007.provenance-sheet.window.txt. Kept and counted rather than retired, at the rung that describes what it actually does. PREVIOUSLY: The sheet `Read first…` opens is where REQ-007 was most at risk on this board, because the design's version of it is almost entirely invented. `prototype.html:1249` lists an owner at install (`@jbailey`), a default branch `force-pushed 11d ago`, an installed hash `a3f19c2 — no longer in history`, and `Its evals fail 5 of 8`. The router reports none of them, and one is not computable at all: `SkillProvenance` records in its own doc comment that the client's files carry a commit and never an owner, so `changed since you installed it` cannot be derived — which is why the sheet's date is labelled as the router's own first sighting and why `CleanupPresentation.provenanceLimit` says so on screen rather than leaving the reader to infer it. `theSheetReportsOnlyObservations` asserts the sheet renders all three fields `SkillProvenance` actually carries and states none of the four invented strings. The negative half enumerates them by name rather than being a blanket not-that predicate, so it fires on the specific thing that would regress. Armed 20 Aug 2026 twice: deleting the `firstSeenAt` field reads `never renders firstSeenAt`, and adding `field("Owner at install", "@jbailey")` reads `the sheet states 'Owner at install', which the router never reported`.

subject.note: The router spawning a child process, seen by two parties that are not the router. `bin/witness-effects.sh` runs `MCPRouterCLI index --force` against a scratch home holding one stdio server, and records the pid the shell launched (`$!`) beside the pid the CHILD reports for its own parent through `getppid()`. The child writes that into a file whose path arrives in its environment and which the router never reads back, so neither record passes through the product. They agree: shell launched 30913, child 30920 names 30913. A ps(1) sample runs alongside and usually misses, because the index verb spawns, handshakes and exits inside one scheduling quantum; two earlier versions of this witness depended on ps alone and could report only that the child had A parent, not whose child it was. Armed: against a config declaring no servers the same recorder reports count=0, and against the populated one count=1 with the parents agreeing.

subject.cell: execution-plane=daemon · network=loopback only
subject.note: The router binding and accepting on loopback, seen by the kernel's socket table through lsof(8). Before: 0 LISTEN rows on 127.0.0.1:8973. After `serve --port 8973`: one LISTEN row owned by pid 15760, which is the pid the shell launched. A client then held a socket open across the sample — a raw /dev/tcp connection with a real HTTP request written into it — and lsof reported 3 ESTABLISHED rows on the port, 1 of them owned by the router: the accepted half of the pair, which is the half that proves the process took the connection rather than merely reserving the port. A separate request returned HTTP 200. After the process is killed, 0 LISTEN rows. The first version of this witness sampled after curl had already closed and recorded ESTABLISHED=0 — a real accepted connection the recorder was pointed at a moment too late to see. Armed: pointed at port 8974, which nothing was told to bind, the same recorder reports 0 while reporting 1 for 8973 in the same run.

subject.cell: execution-plane=daemon · data-shape=a server whose health block is out of range in two keys
subject.note: A configured value the router will not take is REFUSED and reported, never clamped in silence. The lane's `r27-refused` server writes `tripAfter: 1` and `probeIntervalMs: 10`; the report carries both refusals with the value as written, the floor that rejected it, and a `scope` saying which block to fix, while `policy` reports the value actually in force. The `tripAfter` floor of 2 is this item's own version of the vacuity rule: with a threshold of 1 the first failure trips, `degraded` is unreachable, and the guarantee that an upstream is flagged degraded before it is tripped would hold only because nothing can enter the state it names. Refusing rather than clamping is the other half — a clamp reports 2 over a file that says 1, and the operator's next reading of their own file disagrees with the router for a reason neither can see.

The lane builds ~/.cursor/skills under its own scratch HOME with `alive` resolving and `design-craft` pointing at a directory it then removes — which is exactly how the 27 dangling links of the 87 in the real ~/.cursor/skills came to be, every one of them into ~/.claude/plugins/cache, which an upgrade replaces. subject.detail: Three consecutive runs, same build, same booted iPhone 16 Pro, no product change between them: run 1 failed 3 of 5, runs 2 and 3 failed 4 of 5. The case that moved is `tapping 'X' did not produce a navigation bar titled 'X'` — green for all five tabs in run 1, red on the first tab in runs 2 and 3. The only edit between run 1 and run 2 was adding XCTAttachment captures to a different test, so the code under assertion did not change. A plausible mechanism is DEF-008: the tab button's accessibility identifier is the SF Symbol name while its label is the tab title, so `buttons["Discover"]` resolves on one attribute or the other depending on which the tree publishes first. Not diagnosed further here — this campaign records the instrument's reliability rather than repairing another branch's test. Consequence: the lane's outcome-rung claims are recorded inconclusive, because green twice is the campaign's own bar and this lane did not clear it. CLOSED 20 Aug 2026. Diagnosed from run 3's exported App UI hierarchy: at the failure the navigation bar's identifier was 'Settings' and the Settings tab carried Selected, so the opening tap had never landed. Run 1 passed because a freshly installed app launches on Discover, making its first selectTab a no-op; runs 2 and 3 restored to Settings and tapped a tab bar that existed but was not yet hittable. Existence is not hittability. `selectTab` now waits on a `hittable == true` predicate and retries the tap up to three times against the tab button's own `isSelected`, which is the tab bar's answer to 'which tab am I on'. Green twice since, across all three affected tests. DEF-008 was not the mechanism.

subject.source: app/Sources/MCPRouterKit/Control/Scenario.swift; evidence/runs/make-test-3.log (clean build, 1512 tests in 188 suites); app/Scripts/enum-layout-stamp.py; Makefile target enum-layout-stamp; evidence/runs/make-test-4.log
subject.text: Adding a 14th case to `Scenario` made `make test` fail with 31 issues, two of which cannot be true of the source: `Expectation failed: (… → .live) == (.live → .fixture(…cleanupSkills))` in ShellClientFactoryTests and TriageSourceGuardTests, both asserting a Release-posture guard that returns .live unconditionally. `git stash` of the two changed source files → 19 tests pass; unstash → the same failures return, which reads as a real regression. It is not. `Choice.live` is encoded in the spare inhabitants of `Scenario`'s tag, so a new Scenario case shifts that encoding, and stale MCPRouterUI object files compiled against the old layout compare a value that no longer means what they think. `rm -rf app/.build` then rebuild: 5/5 pass, then 1512/1512. The hazard for this campaign is the mirror case — a stale build can as easily produce a green — so any test evidence taken across an enum change is taken from a clean build. MITIGATED 2026-08-20: `app/Scripts/enum-layout-stamp.py` hashes the ordered case list of every enum in the package (212 of them) and removes `app/.build` when that hash moves; `make test` now depends on it. The stamp is the case lists rather than the source, so it holds still for an ordinary edit and for a `switch` over the enum — the false positive a naive grep for `^\s*case` would hit — and moves for an added or renamed case. Armed on all four: comment SAME, switch statement SAME, added Scenario case MOVED, renamed Scenario case MOVED, restore back to baseline. The SwiftPM behaviour itself is unchanged and still upstream; what is fixed is this repo's exposure to it.

subject.detail: `campaign.py` keeps defects in `inventory.json` under a `defect` list, and `add` assigns the next id from that list. `defects.in.json` is an input file. Twelve defects found in the sittings of 19 and 20 Aug were written straight into the input file with hand-written ids taken from that file's own length, which had stopped tracking the registry at DEF-006. The result: DEF-007 through DEF-018 each named one defect in the registry and a different one in the staging file, and neither file said so. Visible symptom, and the only reason it was caught: `RUN-2026-08-20.md` contains 'DEF-011 is the finding worth acting on ... Cleanup's' at line 96 and 'DEF-011 - the rendered-quality gate has never been able to run' at line 481, in one document, meaning two unrelated things. This is `capture-lineage`'s failure mode moved from pictures to identifiers: a name binding to two subjects with nothing checking the binding. Fixed by renumbering the twelve staged defects to DEF-034..DEF-045, merging them into the registry, and rewriting the fifteen references that meant the staged numbering. Every renumbered record carries `stagedAs` naming its old local id, so a reader meeting the old number in an untouched artifact can resolve it. The remaining 74 references were checked one at a time and meant the registry defect they already named. A fourth lesson, from the third instance's cleanup rather than from the collision itself. Reconstructing the concurrent session's two entries welded `text: ""` and `note: ""` onto both, and the first renumbering pass then used `"text" in d` to tell the two writers' entries apart -- so the artifact defeated the discriminator that would have caught it. Both authors independently read the empty values as harmless because they carried no content. The hazard is shape, not content: a membership test reads a key's PRESENCE, and an empty string defeats `"text" in d` exactly as thoroughly as a populated one would. `campaign.py add` injects only `id`, `status`, `evidence` and `armed`, so that key-shape occurred on exactly the two reconstructed entries and was traceable; the keys were stripped and the pass re-run discriminating on `title`. Recorded because "empty therefore harmless" is a reasonable-sounding wrong answer that both sessions gave.
subject.note: SECOND INSTANCE, 20 Aug 2026, in the case registry rather than the defect registry, and it landed the same way. A helper reported `next case id: CASE-0145` while cases.json already held CASE-0149 and CASE-0150; campaign.py's own `next_id` is max+1 and would have said CASE-0151, so the number that was trusted did not come from it. `add` takes an explicit id through `setdefault` and therefore appends a second entry rather than refusing, so CASE-0149 and CASE-0150 each came to name two cases -- an iOS Settings structural case against REQ-005 and a RouterCore write-failure case against REQ-019 -- and the `set` calls that followed wrote onto the pre-existing pair. Caught by an evidence-existence audit rather than by any gate: the new cases printed `3 evidence` where two were supplied. Restored from `git show HEAD:` (both pre-existing entries are byte-identical to HEAD again, verified by dict comparison) and the new pair renumbered to CASE-0153 and CASE-0154. The registry is sparse -- 74 gaps between 1 and 152 -- so a free-looking number is not evidence that it is free, and only max+1 is. THIRD INSTANCE, the same evening, and this one had two writers rather than one. A second Claude session working the same campaign allocated DEF-047 and DEF-048 at about 23:30 (the SDK -32603 message discard, and a detector defect in vacuity-check.py's blind pass) and committed planning/test-campaign as a directory in 6bdeea4, which also swept up this session's in-progress registry edits. This session allocated DEF-047 and DEF-048 for different defects minutes later, from a read taken before that commit landed. Resolved by renumbering THIS session's pair to DEF-049 and DEF-050 -- the later allocation moves, and the session that moves is the one that can enumerate its own references, which is the only reason the choice is safe rather than arbitrary. The peer's entries were not edited. Note for anyone reading the mechanism: `add` assigns from the registry list, so two writers holding a stale read get the same number, and no gate in the campaign detects it. The detection here was a peer message, and before that an evidence-existence audit; neither is a gate. campaign.py could refuse an explicit id that already exists -- `add` currently takes one through `setdefault` and appends a duplicate instead.

subject.detail: STILL PRESENT in 0.9.2, re-measured 21 Aug 2026 and the gap widened by one. witness-worklist.py reports `pairs=20 judgeable=17 WITHOUT a reference=3` and a comparable fraction of 85%, while capture-lineage.py --gate on the same registry reports `published captures: 16` and `JUDGED 16 of 16 judgeable (100%)`. Two gates in one skill version disagree about the judgeable denominator, 17 against 16, and neither names the other's population. CAUSE PINNED 21 Aug 2026. The disagreeing member is SURF-009, the Mac menu-bar popover, and it is the only one: witness-worklist's judgeable set and capture-lineage's judged set are identical apart from it. SURF-009 has a rendered design of record on disk (evidence/shots/mock/SURF-009.png), which is the sole condition witness-worklist tests, so it counts as the 17th judgeable pair. It has NO build capture at all — the popover cannot be opened without activating MCPRouter, which this campaign never does — so it never enters capture-lineage's population, which is built from published captures. capture-lineage therefore reports 'JUDGED 16 of 16 judgeable (100%)' on a registry holding 17 judgeable surfaces. That is the defect's whole shape, and it is the campaign's own first failure mode occurring INSIDE a gate written to prevent it: a denominator built from what was captured rather than from what was enumerated reads 100% precisely when a surface was never photographed. The direction is the dangerous one — an uncaptured surface raises the percentage instead of lowering it. Nothing is concealed in this campaign's own record: SURF-009 carries a shotNote naming the constraint, its three cases (CASE-0004, CASE-0006, CASE-0109) are n/a with the reason, and evidence/shots/pairs.json carries shot:null. The defect is that a reader of the gate line alone would not know to look for any of it. Remains open-detector: the fix is in the skill's scripts, which are not edited from this repo.
subject.note: DETECTOR DEFECT, recorded so its number is not published as a product finding. `witness-worklist.py:90` is `judgeable = [p for p in pairs if p.get("reference")]` -- it tests the reference half and never the shot half. SURF-009 (Mac menu-bar popover) has `shot: null` and an explicit `reason: build half uncaptured` in pairs.json, and is still counted, so the script reported `pairs=20 judgeable=17 comparable fraction: 85%` where the honest figure is 16 of 20, 80%. The script already defends the mirror-image failure and its own comment says why: a campaign reported 20 judgeable pairs whose references were all unrendered .html paths, and it now demotes those to unjudgeable with a named reason. The shot side has no equivalent test. Consequence here is one point of over-report and no false verdict, because capture-lineage.py computes judgeable from captures that exist and reported JUDGED 16 of 16 -- the two gates disagree by exactly this surface, and the disagreement is what found it. A campaign relying on the worklist alone would carry an uncompared surface inside a comparable fraction. Filed against the skill's script rather than this repo, so it is not fixed here.
subject.text: witness-worklist.py counts a pair as judgeable on the reference alone, so a surface with no build capture inflates the comparable fraction.

subject.detail: DETECTOR DEFECT in test-campaign 0.9.1, found 21 Aug 2026 while accounting for the 19 unchecked cases. Two scripts in the SAME skill version disagree about what asserts an effect, and both carry a comment claiming to define it. `campaign.py:123` -- `EFFECT_RUNGS = ('outcome', 'metamorphic', 'effect-witness', 'raster-visual', 'interactive-glass')`, under the comment `A critical flow promises an effect. Only these rungs assert one.` `strict-check.py:54` -- `EFFECT_RUNGS = {'outcome', 'metamorphic', 'raster-visual', 'interactive-glass'}`, under `Only these assert an effect`, and its comment ends `See campaign.py` -- pointing at the file it contradicts. MEASURED here: this campaign holds 4 effect-witness cases (CASE-0145 through CASE-0148), all pass, all armed, each carrying an independent kernel recorder (the shell's $! plus the child's own getppid(); lsof(8)'s LISTEN row and the accepted ESTABLISHED half; stat(2) inode and mtime) and each backed by a denial control that flips it. strict-check.py scores all four into the `only proves something rendered` bucket, which is why that bucket reads 12 when only 8 cases sit at a structural rung. The gate therefore reports CHECKED 61 of 80; counting effect-witness as campaign.py does, and as SKILL.md's ladder does, the figure is 65 of 80 (81%). The consequence is worse than an understatement. effect-witness is the most expensive rung in the ladder -- it requires a recorder the product does not control, a non-zero count, and a sabotage control -- and a campaign optimising for the strict number is steered AWAY from it toward `outcome`, which costs less and scores more. A gate that pays less for harder evidence inverts the incentive the whole skill exists to create. The fix is one token in strict-check.py:54. It belongs in the installed skill and is recorded rather than patched from here, precedent DEF-048, DEF-051 and DEF-052. The ratchet is deliberately left at the gate's own 61 rather than raised to the corrected 65: the ratchet is the gate's record of itself, and editing it to a number the gate does not compute would be the campaign marking its own homework. RESOLVED 21 Aug 2026, and the fix predates the finding. test-campaign 0.9.2 is installed at ~/.claude/plugins/cache/fledgeling-plugins/test-campaign/0.9.2 and its strict-check.py:59 already reads `EFFECT_RUNGS = {'outcome', 'metamorphic', 'effect-witness', 'raster-visual', 'interactive-glass'}`, under a comment naming the same incentive inversion independently derived here: `a campaign that built a real witness watched its strict score stay flat, which is precisely the wrong incentive to attach to the most expensive rung.` Confirmed by running it: 0.9.2 reports CHECKED 65 of 80 (81%) with 8 in the rendered-only bucket, against 0.9.1's 61 of 80 and 12 -- exactly the four effect-witness cases and no others. This session had been running 0.9.1's scripts throughout while 0.9.2 sat installed alongside it, which is the reason the defect was visible here at all.
subject.title: strict-check.py omits effect-witness from EFFECT_RUNGS, so the ladder's top rung scores as 'only proves something rendered' and the gate penalises the hardest available work

subject.detail: Measured 2026-08-21, test-campaign 0.9.2. `ledger.md`'s header line reads `80 cases` and `73 pass · 3 fail · 0 skip · 4 n/a`; its table carries 72 rows. The eight absent cases are CASE-0145, 0146, 0147, 0148 (lane router-daemon) and CASE-0151, 0152, 0153, 0154 (lane swiftui). All eight pass. MECHANISM, exact. The writer at campaign.py:1218-1241 buckets every case with `by_surface.setdefault(c.get('surface', '—'), [])`, so a case whose `surface` is absent lands under the literal key `'—'`. It then emits rows with `for s in inventory['surface']: for c in by_surface.get(s['id'], [])`. `'—'` is not a surface id, so that bucket is never visited and its contents are never printed. Nothing warns; the count in the header comes from a different code path than the rows beneath it, which is why the two disagree without either being flagged. WHAT IS LOST. CASE-0145 through CASE-0148 are this campaign's four `effect-witness` cases — the rung that required building a recorder outside the product, and the most expensive evidence in the run. They are absent from the ledger entirely. A reader of ledger.md cannot learn that the campaign has an effect-witness rung at all. DIRECTION. The eight dropped are all passes, so the table under-states the work rather than over-stating it. That makes it the safer direction, and it does not make it safe: a reader counting 72 rows against a stated 80 meets an unexplained gap of exactly the kind this campaign is written to make impossible, and the campaign's own rule is that every sweep prints its denominator. SCOPE. Ledger-specific. evidence.html renders all eight (5 to 11 references each, measured by grep), so the HTML page is correct and only the markdown artifact is affected. Distinct from DEF-052, which is about the defect registry being absent from BOTH artifacts; this one is about cases, in one artifact, via a different mechanism. NOT FIXED FROM HERE: campaign.py lives in the installed skill cache, not this repo.
subject.title: campaign.py's ledger writer prints only cases filed under a surface, silently dropping 8 of 80 — including all four effect-witness cases

subject.detail: Measured 2026-08-21. `.gitmodules` vendors `.claude/plugins/fledgeling-plugins` at `main`, and `planning/features-to-triage/LEDGER.md`'s allocation notes state the reason: 'a runner reads mockup-fidelity, mac-craft, design-craft and ux-craft at a repo-relative path rather than depending on the machine.' For test-campaign that is not what happens. The submodule (HEAD baaf79a, branch main, clean) carries `plugins/test-campaign` at version 0.5.0, whose `skills/test-campaign/scripts` holds five files: attach-shots.py, campaign.py, evidence-page.py, strict-check.py, witness-worklist.py. It has no `vacuity-check.py` and no `capture-lineage.py`; `grep effect-witness strict-check.py` returns nothing and `grep -c blindVocabulary vacuity-check.py` cannot run because the file is absent. Every gate this campaign reports ran from `~/.claude/plugins/cache/fledgeling-plugins/test-campaign/0.9.2/`, on the machine. The vacuity census, the effect-witness rung, the blind-mutation pass, the capture-lineage ratchet and the strict score of 65 all come from code the submodule does not contain, four minor versions ahead of it. CONSEQUENCE FOR THE PIPELINE, and it is the reason this is filed rather than noted: DEF-051, DEF-052, DEF-054, DEF-055 and DEF-056 are defects in 0.9.2's scripts. None of that code is in this repo at any path, so no ship-feature runner working in an mcp-router worktree can fix them. They are upstream work in github.com/fledgeling-co/fledgeling-plugins, and closing them requires a change pushed to that repo plus a submodule bump here — a different repo and an outward-facing action. Separately, a fresh clone that follows the documented `git submodule update --init --recursive` gets 0.5.0 and would reproduce none of this campaign's numbers. Not fixed here: which version the submodule should track, and whether the campaign should run from it rather than the cache, is the owner's call.
subject.title: the vendored fledgeling-plugins submodule is test-campaign 0.5.0 while every gate in this campaign ran from the machine's 0.9.2 cache
