subject.note: DEF-011's affordance half, re-expressed against the running window rather than against `CleanupBoardRow.swift`. The source read asserted that the row declares `accessibilityElement(children: .contain)` and not `.combine`; what that modifier decides is whether each row's buttons are separately addressable, and relation `SURF-007/row-actions` in bin/glass-assert.py reads THAT off two dumps of a real window. Measured: 3 candidate rows in evidence/ax/SURF-007.window.txt and 5 in evidence/ax/SURF-007.cleanup-skills.window.txt, and all 8 own their own AXButtons one level below their own group — which a combined row cannot do, because combining flattens them into the group's label and publishes none. The action set is a function of the row and not of the board: exactly [Inspect, Remove…] on the 7 rows carrying no provenance note and exactly [Read first…] on the 1 that does. `metamorphic` rather than `structural` because the claim spans two different row populations: a column drawn at a fixed size fails the count and a combined row fails the ownership, and a single-window presence check can see neither. The Swift suite it replaces (app/Tests/MCPRouterUITests/CleanupRowActionsTests.swift) is kept and still runs — it is the faster signal — but it is no longer what this case stands on.

DEF-015's closed half — the shell's overflow treatment, which DESIGN.md §5 names and the build got wrong in a way no assertion could see. Every board's `AXSplitGroup` width is read back out of the running app and compared against its own `AXWindow` width, board by board, through the channel that already writes those dumps beside the pictures. It read 3 of 8 overflowing — Checks 988, Skills 1044, Discover 1119 inside a 980pt window, each origin moved left by exactly half its excess — and reads 0 of 8 after `.frame(minWidth: 0, maxWidth: .infinity, alignment: .leading)` on `ContentZone`. `outcome` rather than `raster-visual` on purpose: the claim is a measured relation between two frames the app publishes, not a comparison of pixels, and the pictures are what made the defect *visible* rather than what proves it fixed. Armed 20 Aug 2026, three ways on the gate and two on the test. The gate exits 1 against the pre-fix dumps, 0 against the post-fix ones, and 1 with no dumps at all — `examined=0` is a check that never ran and is never a pass. Removing the modifier reddens `ShellDetailWidthTests` with `passes its boards' minimum width up to the split view`, and dropping just `alignment: .leading` reddens the second half alone. That test's first version did NOT bite: it searched the raw source and matched the doc comment naming the modifier, so deleting the modifier left it green. Comments are stripped before matching now — a predicate satisfied by the prose explaining it is not a predicate. What this case does not cover, because `overflowing=0` reads like `nothing is clipped` and is not that claim: content that overflows the detail PANE stays inside the window and is invisible to this oracle. That half is CASE-0134, measured with a second probe against every leaf's right edge — and that probe was wrong on its first run, reading the frame's y where it meant x and reporting clipping on seven of eight boards. The Settings capture is whole, and looking at it is what caught it.

DEF-011's last open half, the one the row was left open for: `Read first…`, which the design keys on `k.provenance` and which `CleanupBoardModel.Candidate` had no field to key on. It now carries `provenance: String?`, read through `SkillChecks.originUnchanged` rather than off `skill.provenance` directly, so this board and the Checks board cannot disagree about what counts as moved. Three assertions, all against the model rather than the pixel. `aMovedMarketplaceReachesTheRow` compares the row's note against that check's own `reason` rather than against a literal, because a literal would stay green while the two boards drifted apart. `anUnmovedRowCarriesNoNote` is the half that makes the first one mean something — a field that is always populated cannot mark a row — and covers both an unmoved skill and a server, which has no marketplace to have moved from. `readFirstOpensItsSheet` asserts the sheet is keyed by the skill's resolved path (`prov:/skills/pr-summariser`), that `skill(atPath:)` finds the skill behind it, and that opening it leaves `M7RecordingClient.writes` empty. Armed 20 Aug 2026 four ways: making `provenanceNote` return nil reads `(moved.provenance → nil) == "The router first saw it at …"`; dropping its guard so an unmoved skill is flagged reads `(unmoved.provenance → "its marketplace moved") == nil`; giving the server call site a note reads the `allSatisfy` failure; collapsing the sheet id to `"prov"` reads `(board.sheet?.id → "prov") == "prov:/skills/pr-summariser"`; and keying `skill(atPath:)` on the name instead of the path reads the provenance comparison failing against nil.

REQ-019 on the one control that has to refuse: the skill row's `Remove…`. The control API is read-only for skills — removing one means writing files the client applications hold open — and the row does not hide the button or offer it and fail. It draws it disabled (AX enabled 0) and states that reason in its help text, which is the shape REQ-019 asks for: no success affordance for work that cannot happen, and the refusal is the server's own. Pixels: `SURF-007.cleanup-skills.png`, 519568 bytes, sha 94dd9d06f87d, window-scoped off CGWindowID 103249 owned by the launched pid, recorded in `evidence/shots/captures.json` with the scenario that produced it. Byte-identical across two consecutive capture runs. It does NOT claim agreement with the design of record: the reference is an HTML mock rasterised at another size, and no macOS API exposes a cross-process computed style.

REQ-019 where DEF-001 makes it matter: this build ships no pairing transport, and the sheet says so instead of drawing a code it cannot complete a pairing with. The AXSheet carries `Pair iPhone`, `Pairing is not available in this build`, and the sentence that keeps the reader from debugging their own network — `this build ships no way to listen for one. Nothing is wrong with your phone or your network.` The negative half is the one that would catch a regression: nothing in the window matches Crockford base-32 at the length REQ-015 specifies, checked by pattern rather than against a literal, so a code this predicate's author never saw would still trip it. This case does NOT make REQ-015 pass — CASE-0010 and CASE-0110 fail against it and keep failing. The sheet is honest about a capability that is missing; the capability is still missing.

The refusal's pixels: `SURF-010.build.png`, window-scoped off the CGWindowID the launched pid owns, an AXSheet at 512×173 over the Inbox window. Recorded in `evidence/shots/captures.json` with the title read back as Inbox — the sheet does not change the window title, so the manifest carries both the readback and the `app://mac/pairing` target rather than letting one stand for the other. This surface had no picture at all for three runs: the capture script pressed for a pairing control while the app was on the Servers board, where none exists, and recorded the surface unreachable for a reason that was its own navigation. Selecting Inbox first opened it on the first attempt.

The fixture half of CASE-0138/CASE-0139, checked in the harness rather than on glass. Those two photograph the Cleanup board drawing `Read first…` on one row and a disabled `Remove…` on the other; this asserts the fixture behind them actually contains one moved skill and one unmoved one, which is what makes the photograph a discrimination rather than a picture of whatever the fixture happened to hold. It also guards the reason the scenario is separate: `cleanupSkills` extends `populated` rather than editing it, because SURF-004's on-glass copy asserts the count `populated` publishes (`6 skills from 4 marketplaces · 1 held for review`) and a seventh row there would have broken an existing predicate. The test additionally asserts the servers half of the board survives the scenario, so a fixture that drew skills by losing servers would fail.

Driven through the UI Automation plane against the real MCPRouter.Shell binary in the interactive session, out of process, with the target never foregrounded. The pane item named 'Checks' was actuated with SelectionItemPattern.Select(), and the reads were taken AFTER that actuation: the window title, the realised control-view tree, and a fingerprint over the tree's names. The fingerprint is what makes this more than a presence check - a destination whose tree is identical to the previous one is recorded as a COLLAPSE and fails, which is the shape where six sidebar items opened one placeholder view and every gate passed.

subject.text: CleanupBoardRow carries three treatments for a skill row — the `Read first…` substitution when SkillChecks.originUnchanged fails, the skill-kind `Remove…` drawn disabled because the router removes servers and never files on disk, and the candidacy reason — and none of them had a rendered path in any configuration of the product. A skill is proposed for cleanup only when every readable client lacks it, and all six skills in SkillFixtures.populated are installed somewhere, so the Debug Cleanup board drew three servers and zero skills. Release reaches the branch only if a real user happens to hold an orphaned skill. CASE-0136 asserted the branch exists by reading CleanupBoardRow and said in its own note why it stopped there; what nobody could say was that a build had ever drawn it. Fixed in-campaign by adding a Debug-only `cleanupSkills` scenario and two SkillFixtures.uninstalled rows, kept separate from `populated` because SURF-004's on-glass predicate asserts the count populated publishes. No view code was touched and no assertion was weakened. Now photographed by CASE-0138/CASE-0139 and guarded in the harness by CASE-0144.

subject.detail: CLOSED 2026-08-20. The cause was two independent framing errors, both invisible because the gate could not run to report them. The design references came from `obscura fetch --screenshot`, which captures at a fixed 1280x720 dpr1 viewport with no viewport flag, so every reference was clipped rather than merely small - the bottom row of one carried 578 non-background pixels of 640 sampled. And the build captures were 980x620 against the design's 1156x680 window, aspect 1.581 against 1.700, which no crop reconciles. Fixed by rasterising the design through CDP with `Emulation.setDeviceMetricsOverride` at 1280x900 dpr2 (readback asserted `[1280, 900, 2]` before any capture), re-photographing the eight Mac boards at the design's own 1156x680 with a setframe readback guard, and cropping both halves to the window's own content box. prescan goes from framingComparable 0/16 to 8/8, aspectRatioOfRatios 1.0 and scaleRatio 1.0 on every pair (evidence/runs/prescan-fidelity.json). Eight verdicts written: 2 pass, 5 fail, 1 unoracled.
subject.text: The campaign names design-review and be-my-witness as gates and has never run either, and the reason was never measured — it read as a skip. It is not. be-my-witness 0.2.0's deterministic prescan over all 16 pairs that hold both halves reports isEvidence 16/16, settled 16/16, framingComparable 0/16, proceed 0/16. Not a dead predicate: the scale ratios differ per lane (0.466x on the SURF-001 sidebar crop, 1.64x on the Mac boards, 0.942x on the phone) rather than returning a constant. Every reference was rasterised at a 1280x720 dpr-1 viewport, inside which prototype.html draws a fixed artboard rather than filling the frame, so rendering larger pads rather than enlarges. Re-rendering the reference does not fix it either: the design's Mac window is #win at 1156x680, aspect 1.700, and the build's is 980x620, aspect 1.581. The build half crops exactly — scale=(2096-1376)/(980-620)=2.0, margin=(2096-980*2)/2=68, content rect (68,68,1960,1240), precisely 2x the AX frame — but no crop reconciles two different window shapes. What would make them comparable is re-capturing the app at the design's window size, which means driving the app again and photographing a window shape the product does not use. Left unresolved deliberately: the structural and lexical differential in evidence/differential.md is the comparison that is valid here, and it ran.

subject.detail: `vacuity-check.py`'s blind pass reports `examined=1820 mutating=3 re-read-after=0 blind=3` over this test tree. All three read after the mutation: `restartIsIssuedBeforeTheStagingWrite` reads `WatchWorld.serverNames`, the log, `kicks.issued` and `WatchState.load`; `restartIsOwedBeforeTheWriteLands` reads `WatchState.load` inside the lock and `WatchWorld.serverNames` on both sides of the rename; `restartRechecksTheCamera` reads `model.entry.characters`. The heuristic looks for a read AFTER the last occurrence of a mutating verb, and in this product the verb `restart` is also the name of the thing being observed — `restartPending`, `restarted scratch-label` — so the last `restart` in the file sits inside the final assertion and nothing is textually after it. Recorded rather than acted on: the tests are correct as written, and rewording an assertion to satisfy a text heuristic would make the suite worse. The pass is still worth running; 3 of 1820 is a reviewable rate, and it is the check that would have caught 26 of 32 on the campaign it was built from. CAUSE CORRECTED 21 Aug 2026; the diagnosis recorded above was wrong. It said the mutator's name is the observable's name (`restart` inside `restartPending`). Measured against 0.9.2's actual patterns, that cannot happen: the mutator scan at vacuity-check.py:180 requires `(?<![A-Za-z0-9_])` + verb + `\w*\s*\(`, so `state.restartPending == false` never matches for want of the call parenthesis. The real cause is that the seven default readers are all snake_case -- list_, get_, read_, fetch_, sample_, count_, load_ -- and the nine default mutators mostly are too (stop_all, stop_runner, clear_, cancel_). This is a camelCase Swift codebase, so NEITHER side could fire. The pass examined 1657 test bodies and found 3 mutating, 0 re-reading and 3 blind: `blind=3` reads as almost nothing wrong, and meant almost nothing looked at. The denominator was printed and nobody read 3-of-1657 as the alarm it was. Fixed by declaring the project's own vocabulary, which 0.9.2 added for exactly this: campaign.json now carries `blindVocabulary` with 14 camelCase mutators and 13 readers, and the pass reports examined=1657 mutating=320 re-read-after=232 blind=88, with the vocabulary it used printed above the findings. Two of the three original findings resolved on their real reads (`WatchState.load(`, `WatchWorld.read(`). The third, restartRechecksTheCamera, stays flagged and correctly so for a verb heuristic: its only reads are property comparisons -- `model.step`, `model.entry.characters` -- which carry no verb at all. That is the ceiling of this instrument rather than a defect in the test, and it is why the 88 is a worklist and not a verdict: the vocabulary is hand-declared and unvalidated. Of the 21 findings the tool prints, 15 carry a @Test attribute and 5 are fixture helpers in dedicated client files that 0.9.2's per-file helper heuristic does not exclude, because it keys on a function being called more than once in its OWN file and these are called from their importers.
subject.title: the blind-test pass flags three tests that do read after mutating, because the mutator's name is the observable's name

subject.detail: `campaign.py` keeps defects in `inventory.json` under a `defect` list, and `add` assigns the next id from that list. `defects.in.json` is an input file. Twelve defects found in the sittings of 19 and 20 Aug were written straight into the input file with hand-written ids taken from that file's own length, which had stopped tracking the registry at DEF-006. The result: DEF-007 through DEF-018 each named one defect in the registry and a different one in the staging file, and neither file said so. Visible symptom, and the only reason it was caught: `RUN-2026-08-20.md` contains 'DEF-011 is the finding worth acting on ... Cleanup's' at line 96 and 'DEF-011 - the rendered-quality gate has never been able to run' at line 481, in one document, meaning two unrelated things. This is `capture-lineage`'s failure mode moved from pictures to identifiers: a name binding to two subjects with nothing checking the binding. Fixed by renumbering the twelve staged defects to DEF-034..DEF-045, merging them into the registry, and rewriting the fifteen references that meant the staged numbering. Every renumbered record carries `stagedAs` naming its old local id, so a reader meeting the old number in an untouched artifact can resolve it. The remaining 74 references were checked one at a time and meant the registry defect they already named. A fourth lesson, from the third instance's cleanup rather than from the collision itself. Reconstructing the concurrent session's two entries welded `text: ""` and `note: ""` onto both, and the first renumbering pass then used `"text" in d` to tell the two writers' entries apart -- so the artifact defeated the discriminator that would have caught it. Both authors independently read the empty values as harmless because they carried no content. The hazard is shape, not content: a membership test reads a key's PRESENCE, and an empty string defeats `"text" in d` exactly as thoroughly as a populated one would. `campaign.py add` injects only `id`, `status`, `evidence` and `armed`, so that key-shape occurred on exactly the two reconstructed entries and was traceable; the keys were stripped and the pass re-run discriminating on `title`. Recorded because "empty therefore harmless" is a reasonable-sounding wrong answer that both sessions gave.
subject.note: SECOND INSTANCE, 20 Aug 2026, in the case registry rather than the defect registry, and it landed the same way. A helper reported `next case id: CASE-0145` while cases.json already held CASE-0149 and CASE-0150; campaign.py's own `next_id` is max+1 and would have said CASE-0151, so the number that was trusted did not come from it. `add` takes an explicit id through `setdefault` and therefore appends a second entry rather than refusing, so CASE-0149 and CASE-0150 each came to name two cases -- an iOS Settings structural case against REQ-005 and a RouterCore write-failure case against REQ-019 -- and the `set` calls that followed wrote onto the pre-existing pair. Caught by an evidence-existence audit rather than by any gate: the new cases printed `3 evidence` where two were supplied. Restored from `git show HEAD:` (both pre-existing entries are byte-identical to HEAD again, verified by dict comparison) and the new pair renumbered to CASE-0153 and CASE-0154. The registry is sparse -- 74 gaps between 1 and 152 -- so a free-looking number is not evidence that it is free, and only max+1 is. THIRD INSTANCE, the same evening, and this one had two writers rather than one. A second Claude session working the same campaign allocated DEF-047 and DEF-048 at about 23:30 (the SDK -32603 message discard, and a detector defect in vacuity-check.py's blind pass) and committed planning/test-campaign as a directory in 6bdeea4, which also swept up this session's in-progress registry edits. This session allocated DEF-047 and DEF-048 for different defects minutes later, from a read taken before that commit landed. Resolved by renumbering THIS session's pair to DEF-049 and DEF-050 -- the later allocation moves, and the session that moves is the one that can enumerate its own references, which is the only reason the choice is safe rather than arbitrary. The peer's entries were not edited. Note for anyone reading the mechanism: `add` assigns from the registry list, so two writers holding a stale read get the same number, and no gate in the campaign detects it. The detection here was a peer message, and before that an evidence-existence audit; neither is a gate. campaign.py could refuse an explicit id that already exists -- `add` currently takes one through `setdefault` and appends a duplicate instead.
subject.title: the campaign's own defect ids named two different defects each, because the staging file numbered from its own length

subject.note: `#expect(result.tools != nil, ...)` at ShellTests.swift:133. `ReindexResult.tools` is a non-optional `Int` (MCPRouterKit/Control/Models.swift:263), so the comparison could not fail. The Swift compiler emitted `comparing non-optional value of type 'Int' to 'nil' always returns true` on every build of the test target; it was the only such warning in the suite. The intent was stated in the comment directly above it -- `.success` is distinguished from `.populated` by `a reindex that comes back with no error and a tool count` -- so the assertion was one character from doing its job. Repaired to `result.tools == 14`, the value FixtureControlAPIClient+Writes.swift:33 overrides for `.success`, which discriminates against the base `reindex-failure.json` fixture it starts from (`{"tools":0,"error":"fetch failed"}`). Armed in evidence/arming/CASE-0152.arming.log: with the override changed to 0 the assertion goes red (`(result.tools -> 0) == 14`), and the log records that the pre-repair form would have stayed green under the same mutation.
subject.text: A ShellTests assertion on the `.success` reindex scenario compared a non-optional Int to nil, so it was always true and read nothing.

subject.detail: Measured 2026-08-21. `.gitmodules` vendors `.claude/plugins/fledgeling-plugins` at `main`, and `planning/features-to-triage/LEDGER.md`'s allocation notes state the reason: 'a runner reads mockup-fidelity, mac-craft, design-craft and ux-craft at a repo-relative path rather than depending on the machine.' For test-campaign that is not what happens. The submodule (HEAD baaf79a, branch main, clean) carries `plugins/test-campaign` at version 0.5.0, whose `skills/test-campaign/scripts` holds five files: attach-shots.py, campaign.py, evidence-page.py, strict-check.py, witness-worklist.py. It has no `vacuity-check.py` and no `capture-lineage.py`; `grep effect-witness strict-check.py` returns nothing and `grep -c blindVocabulary vacuity-check.py` cannot run because the file is absent. Every gate this campaign reports ran from `~/.claude/plugins/cache/fledgeling-plugins/test-campaign/0.9.2/`, on the machine. The vacuity census, the effect-witness rung, the blind-mutation pass, the capture-lineage ratchet and the strict score of 65 all come from code the submodule does not contain, four minor versions ahead of it. CONSEQUENCE FOR THE PIPELINE, and it is the reason this is filed rather than noted: DEF-051, DEF-052, DEF-054, DEF-055 and DEF-056 are defects in 0.9.2's scripts. None of that code is in this repo at any path, so no ship-feature runner working in an mcp-router worktree can fix them. They are upstream work in github.com/fledgeling-co/fledgeling-plugins, and closing them requires a change pushed to that repo plus a submodule bump here — a different repo and an outward-facing action. Separately, a fresh clone that follows the documented `git submodule update --init --recursive` gets 0.5.0 and would reproduce none of this campaign's numbers. Not fixed here: which version the submodule should track, and whether the campaign should run from it rather than the cache, is the owner's call.
subject.title: the vendored fledgeling-plugins submodule is test-campaign 0.5.0 while every gate in this campaign ran from the machine's 0.9.2 cache

Type a code"`, app/Sources/MCPRouterKit/Inbox/InboxCopy.swift:232 at `83e5380`; `ScanView(onTypeInstead: model.typeInstead)`, app/Sources/MCPRouterUI/Phone/PairingFlowView.swift:167 at `83e5380`; `The control API has no devices endpoint.`, app/Sources/MCPRouterUI/Settings/Panes/SecurityPane.swift:79 at `83e5380`; `Button(SettingsPaneCopy.pairedDevicesAction) { shell.select(.inbox) }`, app/Sources/MCPRouterUI/Settings/Panes/SecurityPane.swift:94 at `83e5380`
subject.text: Measured by K3 on 2026-08-29 while trying to fill SURF-010's and SURF-011's denominators. Three declared controls have nothing to press, for three different reasons, and only one of them is a gap in the product. `Can't scan? Type a code` is declared on both the Mac pairing sheet and Settings' pair-another sheet. The copy exists — `InboxCopy.Pairing.typeInstead` — and the only view that draws it is the PHONE's `PairingFlowView`. REQ-015 says the phone can scan or type; the Mac sheet offers `Show a new code` and `Done`, so the typed path is reachable from one device and the design puts the affordance on the other. `Unpair` cannot be built as drawn: the control API has no devices endpoint, so what this Mac knows about a paired phone is the name on the inbox snapshot the shell is already polling. `SecurityPane` states that in its own words and offers `Manage…` — which routes to the Inbox — in its place. A refusal with a reason rather than an omission, but the design still promises a control the surface does not carry. `Reset history` is the confirm button of a sheet the Settings window does not host. The act itself ships and is proven: `ActivityModel.resetHistory()` and `CleanupBoardModel.resetHistory()` reach the same endpoint and `Reset history` is actuated on SURF-003 by a passing case. What is absent is this surface's entry point. M39 DISPOSITION, 2026-08-29, for the FIRST of the three only. The defect stays open because `Unpair` and `Reset history` are untouched. `Can't scan? Type a code` is answered by deciding it should not be a control on the Mac at all, rather than by adding one. The copy is the phone's button and switches `PairingFlowView` from the camera to a keypad; the Mac has no second screen to switch to, already draws the eight characters under the QR, and is not the device that types them. A Mac button would change no state and reveal nothing, which is this defect again rather than its repair. What shipped is the instruction the brief asked for -- `InboxCopy.Pairing.typeInsteadDetail`, drawn by `PairingSheet.typedFallback` in the live state, in the design of record's own wording. CASE-0289 asserts the sentence is drawn and that the action bar did not gain a fourth control; the surface's `controlsUnactuatable` row now records the decision instead of the absence.
subject.title: Three Settings and pairing controls the design draws have no counterpart on the Mac

A refusal with a reason rather than an omission, but the design still promises a control the surface does not carry. `Reset history` is the confirm button of a sheet the Settings window does not host. The act itself ships and is proven: `ActivityModel.resetHistory()` and `CleanupBoardModel.resetHistory()` reach the same endpoint and `Reset history` is actuated on SURF-003 by a passing case. What is absent is this surface's entry point. M39 DISPOSITION, 2026-08-29, for the FIRST of the three only. The defect stays open because `Unpair` and `Reset history` are untouched. `Can't scan? Type a code` is answered by deciding it should not be a control on the Mac at all, rather than by adding one. The copy is the phone's button and switches `PairingFlowView` from the camera to a keypad; the Mac has no second screen to switch to, already draws the eight characters under the QR, and is not the device that types them. A Mac button would change no state and reveal nothing, which is this defect again rather than its repair. What shipped is the instruction the brief asked for -- `InboxCopy.Pairing.typeInsteadDetail`, drawn by `PairingSheet.typedFallback` in the live state, in the design of record's own wording. CASE-0289 asserts the sentence is drawn and that the action bar did not gain a fourth control; the surface's `controlsUnactuatable` row now records the decision instead of the absence.

subject.detail: `TypedEntryView` rendered eight styled boxes, a helper line and a submit button, and no input affordance of any kind — no TextField, no keypad, no focus state. `PairingCodeEntry` had carried `append(contentsOf:)` and `deleteBackward()` since it was written and nothing in the UI called either, so `.disabled(!entry.isComplete)` on the submit button could never become false. The typed path is the documented fallback for every camera state — the source cites A16 — and for `.restricted`, where iOS Settings is a dead end the user may not be able to clear, it is the *primary* recovery. So the one surface a user reaches by deliberately choosing it was the one that could not be completed. Fixed with a real `TextField` behind the boxes: it carries the system keyboard, hardware keys on iPad, paste and dictation, and it is what `app.textFields` resolves to on glass. Deliberately NOT `.textContentType(.oneTimeCode)` — that AutoFill reads codes out of Messages and Mail, and this code is read off the Mac's own screen, so it would offer suggestions that are always wrong. The boxes became decoration (`accessibilityHidden`) and the field is the single element labelled 'Pairing code', because `children: .ignore` on a display is right and on an editor strips the trait VoiceOver and XCUITest need. Approach checked against an out-of-family lane (grok-4.6, xhigh) before implementing; it named the same shape and the same reason for avoiding `.oneTimeCode`. Guarded by `PhoneSurfaceTests.testTypedEntryPublishesAFieldToTypeInto`, armed 20 Aug 2026.

subject.detail: DETECTOR DEFECT in test-campaign 0.9.2, found 21 Aug 2026. attach-shots.py iterates every image under evidence/shots and assigns `hit['shot'] = rel` on each match, last write wins, with no preference for a build capture over a design render. This campaign keeps six directories under evidence/shots (16 root, 8 design-size, 16 fidelity, 9 ios, 17 mock, 11 mock-hidpi), so for SURF-001 the candidates in iteration order are SURF-001.build.png, SURF-001.shell.png, mock/SURF-001.png, mock-hidpi/SURF-001.full.png -- and the last one wins. MEASURED for SURF-001, SURF-002 and SURF-006: `--apply` would repoint each surface's `shot` from its build capture to `evidence/shots/mock-hidpi/SURF-00N.full.png`, which is the render of the DESIGN, not the build. That is the skill's own headline failure mode -- publishing a picture of one thing under the name of another -- arriving in a sibling of the plane built to prevent it, and it would do so while every other gate stayed green, because capture-lineage.py gates the 16 captures cited by CASES and the surface wall is a different population. The report compounds it: the UNCORROBORATED block prints surface ids (SURF-001 ... SURF-011) rather than the file each verdict is about, so a reader sees eleven surfaces apparently lacking provenance when in fact each surface's ACTUAL `shot` field points at a corroborated build capture and the complaint is about a mock render nobody intended to attach. Distinguishing the two costs a re-derivation of the matcher by hand. Recorded rather than patched, precedent DEF-048, DEF-051, DEF-052 and DEF-053. The campaign's standing refusal to run `--apply` here predates this and was based on the DEF-006 mis-wire; it now has a measured mechanism behind it. Separately closed while investigating: this campaign's design-size captures carried their provenance in a second manifest, evidence/shots/design-size/captures.json, in a different schema ({captures:[...]} against the root's bare list) that no gate reads. Its 8 entries were merged into the root manifest with `target` derived from the root's declared target for the same subject and corroborated by each capture's own windowTitleReadback -- Servers, Activity, Skills, Discover, Inbox, Checks, Cleanup, Settings, every one matching -- recorded at capture time, and each carries `targetDerivedFrom` saying so. That was the campaign's own inconsistency and is fixed here; it was not the cause of the 11. RE-MEASURED 2026-08-27 (G21) after `evidence/shots/captures.json` was made a derived file. The uncorroborated count is 12 and stays 12: SURF-001..011 and SURF-022. Eleven of them are this defect -- `mock-hidpi/` sorts last, so it is the row that decides each surface's `shotProvenance`. The mock rows in the manifest deliberately carry NO `target`; the address the channel was pointed at is recorded in full as `renderedFrom`, with an `attachHazard` field naming this defect. Measured both ways on this tree: writing that address as `target` instead drops the uncorroborated count from 12 to 1 and DISARMS `--apply`'s refusal, because `attach-shots.py` only checks the field is present and never compares it to the subject's route -- which is item 5 of X8's work order. So the report going quiet would have been this defect getting worse while looking fixed. The twelfth, SURF-022, is not this defect: see DEF-061.

subject.detail: Measured 2026-08-21 against test-campaign 0.9.2 on app/Tests. The pass reports examined=1661 mutating=320 blind=88. Two structural errors and two idiom errors inflate that number. STRUCTURAL. (1) It scans every `func`, not every test. Restricted to swift-testing's own discriminator (a func whose nearest preceding annotation is @Test) the denominator is 1531, not 1661: 130 of the examined functions are not tests. (2) Its helper exclusion at vacuity-check.py:162 is file-scoped — a name is a helper only if called more than once in the file that declares it. A shared stub declared in TestSupport.swift and called from other files therefore reads as a test, so MemoryFileSystem's `write`, `removeItem` and `moveItem`, HTTPStub's `stop` and WatchTestSupport's `remove` are each counted as a blind test. 21 of the 88 are support-file functions. IDIOM, on the mutator side. (3) The lookbehind `(?<![A-Za-z0-9_])` cannot exclude a dot, so a Swift enum case constructor matches a mutator verb: `ServerRowAction.forServer(s, pendingAuth: nil) == .reset(.clearPlacard)` reports ServerPresentationTests::trippedOutranksHeld as mutating via 'reset', where `.reset` is the expected VALUE inside the assertion. 41 of 72 re-measured findings are dot-prefixed. (4) It takes the last mutator by source POSITION and calls everything after it the tail, which misreads three Swift constructs: a mutator inside the assertion (`await #expect(throws: Never.self) { try await store.delete() }` — nothing can follow it by construction), a mutator in a `defer` block (source-early, execution-last, so the whole test body reads as 'after'), and a mutator as the last statement of a loop body whose observation is the next iteration (CallbackLifecycleTests::stopReleasesTheSocket rebinds the port ten times; the read of cycle N is the start() of cycle N+1). SAMPLE. Of the 15 findings with zero assertions after the last mutator — the highest-yield stratum — 9 were read in full. Two (DiscoveryTests::servers, CapabilityPlateTests::install) are helpers. All 7 remaining are real tests that do observe after mutating, through idioms no reader verb names: `client.calls.last?.operation`, `seen.filter { ... }`, a rebind that throws. Precision on that stratum is 0 of 7. ARMED, two ways, evidence/arming/blind-mutation.arming.log. A probe @Test that mutates and never observes was added and removed: blind moved 88 -> 89 -> 88 and examined/mutating moved by exactly 1 each time. The check does bite; it is the false-positive rate that is at issue, not the sensitivity. NOT REMEDIED BY VOCABULARY. The reader side is deliberately loose because a false reader match suppresses a finding. Adding this codebase's read idioms (`calls`, `operation`, `filter`) would lower the number without improving what the pass knows, and the terms are generic enough to suppress true findings too. The 88 stands recorded as a worklist with its measured precision beside it rather than tuned to look better. RE-MEASURED 2026-08-27 by G22, which declared `testRoot` and gave this pass a corpus for the first time. THE 88 DOES NOT REPRODUCE. Vendored 0.9.2 over `app/Tests` today reports examined=2133 mutating=3 blind=3, against the 1661/320/88 above. The denominator moving up while `mutating` collapses 320 → 3 is not tree churn: 0.9.1 and 0.9.2 ship IDENTICAL DEFAULT_MUTATORS and DEFAULT_READERS, and neither list holds `reset`, `write`, `removeItem`, `moveItem` or `remove` — the verbs this entry's idiom argument turns on. So the 2026-08-21 sitting ran an expanded vocabulary passed on the command line, and `campaign.json` declares none, which makes 88 a figure no documented invocation returns. Its cited evidence, `evidence/arming/blind-mutation.arming.log`, has never existed on any branch of this repository (`git log --all -- '*blind-mutation*'` is empty), so the arming claim above is not checkable from the tree. The measured structural and idiom errors are not withdrawn; what is withdrawn is the population they were measured over. TODAY'S POPULATION, AND ITS PRECISION. With `testRoot: app` the pass reports examined=2179 mutating=3 re-read-after=0 blind=3, and 0.15.0 returns the same three findings from the same corpus. All THREE were read in full — 3 of 3, not a sample — and all three are false positives. Precision 0 of 3. A FOURTH CAUSE, NOT IN THE ORIGINAL ENTRY, AND THE ONE THAT PRODUCES TWO OF THE THREE. The body slice is `src[pos:end]` where `pos` is the start of the DECLARATION, so a test whose own name begins with a mutator verb matches itself. `WatchRestartTests::restartIsIssuedBeforeTheStagingWrite` and `::restartIsOwedBeforeTheWriteLands` contain no mutating call at all: the only `restart\w*\(` in each is `func restart…(` on its own declaration line. Both then read — `WatchWorld.read(scratch.logPath)`, `WatchState.load(path:)`, `WatchWorld.serverNames(in:)` — and assert on `state.mcpServersHash` and `state.restartPending`. The third, `PhoneStorageFailureTests::restartRechecksTheCamera`, does call `await model.restart()` and then asserts twice, on `model.step` and on `model.entry.characters`: property reads that no reader verb names, which is cause (4)'s shape rather than a new one. This cause survives into 0.15.0 unchanged. NOT ENROLLED IN A GATE, and `blindVocabulary` still not declared, for the reason the entry already gives. A related gap measured at the same sitting: pointed at `src/` — the TypeScript tree, which has no tests — the pass prints `corpus: … (0 file(s))` and `examined=0 mutating=0 blind=0` and contributes nothing to `--gate`. It reports its empty corpus and does not fail on it, so a mis-declared `testRoot` reads as a clean pass. VOCABULARY DECLARED 2026-08-29 by K4, and the entry's own 'NOT REMEDIED BY VOCABULARY' paragraph is narrowed rather than withdrawn. That paragraph reasons entirely from the READER side, and on the reader side it is still right: adding this codebase's read idioms lowers the count without improving what the pass knows, which is why the declared reader list stops short of `expect` and `require` -- swift-testing's assertion macros, 5781 and 383 occurrences, either of which would mark every test that asserts after mutating as re-reading and collapse the count to near zero while the pass learned nothing. THE MUTATOR SIDE WAS NEVER ARGUED, AND THAT IS WHERE THE PASS WAS BLIND. Measured over the same 2282 test bodies at `83e5380`: the nine snake_case defaults find 3 mutating call sites; a camelCase list derived from this corpus finds 481. So `blind=3` was a reading of 3 of 481, a recall of 0.6%, and the entry's `precision 0 of 3` was a precision over a population the instrument could barely see. `campaign.json` now carries `blindVocabulary` with `only: true`, 19 mutators and 34 readers, derived mechanically -- a verb is kept only where method calls on a receiver are at least half its corpus sites and its own `func` declaration lines at most a quarter, which is causes (3) and (4) of this entry turned into a selection rule. THE THREE FINDINGS ARE ADJUDICATED, and each clears for a different checkable reason rather than all three for one. `restartIsIssuedBeforeTheStagingWrite`: one fitted mutator, `WatchWorld.remove(scratch)` inside a `defer`, and four declared readers after it -- `load`, `read`, `parse`, `servers`. NOT blind, positively. `restartIsOwedBeforeTheWriteLands`: three fitted mutators, the last `WatchState(restartPending: true).save(`, with `load` after it. NOT blind, positively. `restartRechecksTheCamera`: ZERO fitted mutator call sites in its body. It was flagged only because `restart` is a shipped default and this entry's fourth cause -- the body slice beginning at the declaration -- made `func restartRechecksTheCamera(` match itself. `restart` fails the selection rule (1 method call against 3 declaration lines, of 5 sites), so it is not in the vocabulary and the finding is withdrawn. WHAT THAT DOES NOT MEAN: its real mutation `await model.restart()` is now invisible to the pass, and its reads are still the property comparisons `model.step` and `model.entry.characters` that no reader verb names. It is UNEXAMINED by this instrument, not clean, and that is this entry's ceiling stated once more rather than closed. ARMED, AND ENROLLED, which the entry recorded as missing. `planning/test-campaign/bin/blind-vocabulary-arm.py` runs on every `make lint`: two plants identical but for one line, each measured alone and again inside a `shutil.copytree` of the real corpus, requiring examined+1 mutating+1 blind+1 for the blind plant and examined+1 mutating+1 blind+0 for the reading one. The specificity arm is the half a sensitivity arm alone cannot give: a detector that flagged every mutating body would pass the first and say nothing. 6 of 6 as expected on `cache 0.16.0` and again on the `vendor/` pin via `--instrument`. The two disagree only on the denominator -- 2282 against 2277, the five arrow-style `it/test(` blocks 0.9.3 added block detection for -- and agree on blind=111. THE 111 IS A WORKLIST AND THE CAMPAIGN STILL PUBLISHES NO BLIND NUMBER. Nothing above touches the structural causes: the pass still examines every `func` rather than every `@Test`, its helper exclusion is still file-scoped, and a `defer` mutator still reads as source-early -- which is exactly why the first of the three findings above needed reading rather than counting. This entry stays OPEN; what it now carries is a measured recall beside its measured precision.
subject.title: vacuity-check's blind-mutation pass examines non-tests and mis-reads Swift idiom; 7 of 7 sampled findings are false positives

subject.detail: parity-gate.sh, 20 Aug 2026 on main at e5755d0. The suite lane's citation run of scripts/acceptance/parity-oauth.sh exited non-zero and recorded `control-auth-post-http fail — the Swift router never reached the token endpoint`. The dedicated oauth lane, later in the same gate, ran the same script and recorded ok over 21 checks. The gate reported the row DIVERGED and printed 81 of 83. WHY IT IS UNEXPLAINED, established 21 Aug 2026 from disk without re-running anything. The run survives as evidence/runs/parity-gate-2026-08-20-oauth-flake.log, written 20:39:30. Its line 163 is the whole of what the citation run reported: `FAIL scripts/acceptance/parity-oauth.sh the gate reported findings`, and the next line is the following `ok` row. The script itself does not fail that quietly -- its failure branch (parity-oauth.sh:308-329) prints the POST /auth status, the browser hop, the tail of the router log and the first 20 requests the provider saw. Every one of those bytes existed and was discarded by the caller: `parity-suite.sh`'s `run_script` sent both streams to /dev/null at the time. So this defect is not a run that left no diagnostic, it is a run whose diagnostic the harness threw away, and no amount of re-reading the log can recover it. The instrument was repaired in commit 21d559b at 20:41:28 -- one minute and 58 seconds after this log was written, in the same commit that recorded the defect -- so `run_script` now keeps the log and prints its last 20 lines inline. A recurrence would therefore arrive with the cause attached. That is what closes this: the next occurrence, not more thought about this one. It stays open because there is still no cause and no reproduction; what changed is that the reason it could not be diagnosed is now known and no longer true. One candidate mechanism examined and NOT adopted. The R9 lane reported (21 Aug 2026, via uds:/tmp/cc-socks/9881.sock) that a stale $TMPDIR/mcp-router-parity.lock had made a gate fail its manifest-check for a non-real reason. That is a different symptom -- a manifest-check failure before the comparison, against this defect's completed run that reached `control-auth-post-http` and recorded a row -- and parity-oauth.sh takes that same lock at line 126 and preflights every port at 143-145, so the two lanes inside one gate could not have overlapped. Recorded as ruled out rather than left unmentioned, so the next reader does not spend the lead twice.
subject.text: Observed once, in one of two whole-gate runs, and not reproduced by: a standalone run of `parity-oauth.sh`, a second standalone run of it immediately afterwards (which exercised the same port-reuse wait, 9s and 12s), a standalone run of `parity-suite.sh`, or a second whole `parity-gate.sh` on the same tree. The second gate reported 82 of 83, 0 DIVERGED, and its suite lane reported the citation clean. **What it is not.** The lane distinguishes an environment failure from a finding on purpose, and this was the finding branch: `record control-auth-post-http fail` at `parity-oauth.sh:329`, reached only when the reference side completed an authorization and the Swift side did not. An unbindable port exits 2 through `wait_for_ports_bindable` and records `blocked`, not `fail`, so the port-reuse race is ruled out by the code path that fired. **Why it went undiagnosed, and what changed.** `parity-suite.sh`'s `run_script` sent both streams to `/dev/null` and printed `the gate reported findings` — a verdict with no evidence under it. The bytes naming which guard failed had already been thrown away by the time anyone read the gate's summary. `run_script` now keeps the log, prints its last 20 lines inline and names the file it kept, armed 20 Aug 2026 against a deliberately failing citation. A recurrence will say which of the 21 checks went red. **Why the duplicate run stays.** `control-auth-post-http` is proven on the wire by its own lane and also cites the script, so the gate runs it twice. That is now documented in `parity-suite.sh` rather than deduplicated, because the duplicate is what caught this: a single run would have reported a clean 82 of 83 and nobody would have known. Both record under the same row id and a `fail` wins. **Burn-in, 20 Aug 2026: 8 standalone runs of the lane, all green, 21 checks each.** Three immediately after the failure and five consecutively afterwards, plus one clean whole gate. One failure in roughly ten whole-lane executions, cause unrecoverable because that invocation's stdout was discarded. A green burn-in does not close this: the original failure is uninspectable, so the runs measure only that the lane is not reliably broken. What would close it is a captured reproduction, or a stated gate met — several consecutive whole gates including the cold port-reuse path — decided as its own question rather than inferred from a streak, which is the `install-launchd-watch` mistake this repository already paid for once (G1: name a fix per term and fix a bound IN ADVANCE, never a green streak). Not a UI defect and not a blocker on the cutover count — CASE-0036's measurement is the second run — but it is an unexplained non-determinism in the router or the lane, and it is recorded rather than absorbed.

subject.note: F6. Nothing in this item refreshes a catalogue, so every verdict travels with the age of what it was compared against. An age that could not be measured is null and never 0 — a zero reads as just-refreshed — and a catalogue whose newest file is stamped AHEAD of the router's clock is null too, because reported as a negative number it would exceed no window and read fresh forever. ARMED: red-green M6 reports the negative age as a number and G10 and U7 go red; M10 folds the age problem into the read problem, which suppressed every comparison against a catalogue that parsed fine, and the same two go red.

parity-gate.sh on main at e5755d0, 20 Aug 2026: **82 of 83 rows proven (4 of them by suite only, not by wire comparison), 0 DIVERGED, 1 blocked.** REQ-014's contract is the owner's cutover target of 82 of 83 with `fixture-registry-search` a standing exclusion, and that is what was measured. The two rows that stood between 80 and 82 closed the same day: `install-launchd-watch` by ai/p8, which made the `reran` term attributable — it had read yes on 2 of 6 decoy trials where no stimulus could reach the watched path — and `control-auth-post-http` by ai/p7, which built a real OAuth client and now agrees with the reference across the discovery cascade, the registration bytes, the PKCE parameters, the token exchange, the callback page, the credential file and the re-authorization branch. **The gate exits 1 and that is not this case failing.** It exits 1 while any row is blocked, deliberately, and the one blocked row is the standing exclusion the requirement names. The gate prints the distinction itself: `82 proven is at or past the target of 82. That is a count, not a licence`. Read as a pass on the requirement, not as a licence to flip the installer — that is the owner's call on R4-C's evidence, which this case does not make. **Armed, and one arm was not planned.** The mechanical arm is `parity-lane-selftest`, which runs every lane against a deliberately broken Swift router and requires each to go red; it ran green in the same `make all` that carried this tree, printing `every new lane went red against a broken router. The lanes can fail.` The unplanned arm is the first whole-gate run of the day, kept at `evidence/runs/parity-gate-2026-08-20-oauth-flake.log`: the same script on the same tree reported `81 of 83 rows proven … 1 DIVERGED … This is NOT a pass`, so the aggregate verdict is live rather than a constant. That run's cause is unexplained and is recorded as DEF-033 rather than absorbed into this note.

subject.note: WHAT THIS ROW SPEAKS FOR, AND WHAT IT DOES NOT. It measures the NODE reference only. `swift` and `xcodebuild` are absent on this machine, so nothing here is a Swift test result and this case must not be read as coverage of `AuthRoutes.promote`; the Swift side of REQ-019 is still carried by `ControlApproveDispatchTests` and this campaign has not run it. Three arms over the shipped `handleControl` out of `dist/`: a writable home answering 200 with `pending` gone from disk; the same call with the save's temp path occupied by a directory, answering 500 with the errno message and `pending` still on disk; and the occupation removed, answering 200 again. The denial is the filesystem's own `EISDIR` at exactly the step that makes the change durable - not a mocked `FileSystem` - and the lock sidecar and the manifest read are left working on purpose, because a denial that also stopped the lock would produce a 500 carrying the LOCK's sentence and prove nothing about the save. ACLs were tried first and are recorded in the lane's header as a control that did not arm: `icacls <file> /deny <user>:(D,WD,AD,WEA,WA)` and `icacls <dir> /deny <user>:(DC)` both apply, read back as DENY aces, and `renameSync` over the target succeeds anyway on this machine. An ACL that is set and does not bite produces a green arm that never armed, which is why the temp-path occupation replaced it. What it found: the reference answers 500, so Swift's pre-R21 200 was a divergence and R21's change closed it (DEF-442), while the error BODIES still differ (DEF-441). `deps.liveReload` and `deps.manifest` are stubs - they are the announcement collaborators the 200 path calls after the write - and the route, the lock, `loadManifest` and `saveManifest` are the shipped ones.

subject.detail: This is small and it is filed rather than fixed for a reason worth stating: the fix is one line in Swift, and this machine cannot compile Swift, so changing it would trade a measured divergence for an unmeasured edit. `planning/parity/surface.tsv`'s `control-approve-post` row declares that the 200 promotion path is proven Swift-side only and says nothing at all about the failed-write path, so this divergence was in neither the proven set nor the declared set. It is now declared in that row. The remedy is a choice between two one-line edits and it is not obviously the port's: dropping Swift's prefix matches the reference byte for byte, and adding the prefix to node makes both sentences readable at the cost of moving the reference. Whoever takes it should take it on a machine with a Swift toolchain and re-run `scripts/acceptance/r21-approve-write-denied.mjs` on the node side either way. SWIFT WAS NOT COMPILED AND NOT RUN FOR THIS ROW. `swift` and `xcodebuild` are both absent on the machine this was written on (LUKESFF, Windows 11; `Get-Command` found neither), so every statement here about Swift source is READ off the tree at 42aef112 and none of it is a test result. Where a claim is measured, the command that measured it is named.
subject.text: MEASURED on the reference, READ on the port. Node's `POST /servers/:name/approve` against a manifest write the filesystem refuses answers `500` with `{"error":"<the errno message verbatim>"}` - the run recorded `{"error":"EISDIR: illegal operation on a directory, open '...\\manifest.json.tmp-4752'"}` - and leaves `pending` on disk. Swift's `AuthRoutes.promote` catches the same failure at `app/Sources/RouterCore/Auth/AuthRoutes.swift:171-177` and answers `500` with `{"error": "failed to write manifest: <error.localizedDescription>"}`. The STATUS agrees; the BODY does not, because the port prefixes a sentence of its own that the reference does not write.
subject.title: The two approve routes agree on 500 when the manifest write is refused and disagree on what they put in the body

subject.note: FLOW-006.02. The panel drew a document THE ROUTER SERVED, not M19's fixture: the titlebar names g17-capability, the package's own H1 and prose are on screen, all three tab controls are drawn, and 'trawl' — the fixture capability every previous dump and capture of this panel was a picture of, M23's included — appears nowhere in the tree. The server is CONSTRUCTED by the harness and labelled so in three places — the harness header, the package's own read me, and every row of evidence/g17-document/captures.json. 0 of the 21 upstreams on this machine declare a package directory (M30, planning/evidence/M30-reach.txt), so there is no real one to point at. The 'outside the package' refusal, rendered and distinguishable. The node costs the readme fidelity census nothing, because it is drawn only when a reference is refused and the M19 fixture's one image resolves. Check G17-P5. --- ARTIFACT CORRECTED by J3, on the same finding as CASE-0186 and from the other side of it. G17-P5 reads the `figure-refusal` node's own frame and requires under 1% figure colour, so the pixels are real and the picture was the whole frame the other two cases also cited. It now cites the crop of the refusal card — 708x28 of drawn sentence and no picture, which is exactly what the check asserts.

G17-P6 asked whether a heading carrying the tab's own name is in the dump, which is true of a panel that draws a heading — so this case sat one rung below an effect and its own note said it moved no count. G17-P6W ties the drawn body to the wire: the words of six letters or more that `wire-served.json` carries ONLY in the changelog are COMPUTED from the response rather than written into the check, and all 4 of them are in the panel's own body while none of the 20 unique to the read me is. G17-P6R reads the same step in pixels — 22.7% of the body region's 1,572,864 pixels differ from the read me frame's, against a 1% floor, where a tab that repainted nothing reads 0.0%. Each crop is taken from its own frame's dump at its own scale, so the titlebar and the tab bar cannot supply the difference. Both denominators are checked before the result: a wire response whose three documents shared every word gives both word lists empty, and a clean answer from an empty search is the reading this harness exists against. Rated `metamorphic` rather than `raster-visual` for two reasons — the claim is a RELATION (vary the tab, require the drawn body to track the document the router served) rather than a comparison against a reference image, and these frames come off the hosting view's own backing store rather than off a display server, which is what `raster-visual` names. K3. `Install` is driven at `DiscoverBoardModel.install` and the effect is read as the DECLARATION THE CLIENT RECORDED — name, command and args, checked against the row that was pressed rather than against the function that built them. Two entries are staged with different install blocks and both are pressed, so a handler that declares a fixed payload, or the row it happened to have selected, fails on the second press; one press and one assertion cannot tell those apart. The read refused is `board.rows[0].installed == true`. `markInstalled` writes that from the board's own copy of the response, so it is true whether or not anything reached the router — the app's report that it worked, which is what the arm leaves standing.

M38. A refused manifest write leaves the served catalog exactly where it was AND leaves the change pending, so the decision is still available to be taken. R21 fixed the status code; this reads the same refusal at the catalog, which is where the user's question actually lives. The failure is injected on the FileSystem method names (writeFile, moveItem) — a key naming an operation nothing performs would let the case pass by writing successfully.

M38. The negative control for CASE-0265: an approve that promoted nothing (409) announces nothing — no notification and no new live-reload log line. Without it the arm above is satisfied by a route that announces on every approve, which would send every attached session to re-fetch a list that did not move.

Found by a denial control in the effect-witness pass rather than by reading code: `bin/witness-arm-denial.sh` points the CLI at a router home with mode dr-x------, which the process may read and traverse but not write. `index --force` then prints `ok witness-fixture (1 tools)`, prints `0 tools cached -> /tmp/.../manifest.json` eight lines later, and exits 0 over a manifest.json that does not exist. Cause: ManifestIndexer.record at RouterCore/Service/ServicePorts.swift:341 calls `try? ManifestIO.save(...)`. ManifestIO.save throws correctly and its own doc comment is careful about the disk-full case -- it deliberately leaves the temp file behind as evidence -- but all three call sites discard the error (AuthRoutes.swift:120, WatchIndexing.swift:150, ServicePorts.swift:341). The verb's closing count is honest, because MCPRouterCLI.swift:167-173 re-reads the manifest from disk to compute it; nothing compares that count against the per-server line above it. The same `try?` on the control-API path is already characterised and deliberate -- ControlApproveDispatchTests.approveWithARefusingFileSystem pins the 200, registered in spec-P1 section 8, as R5's shipped behaviour that P1 does not move. This is the second call site, and until CASE-0153, CASE-0154 and CASE-0151 no test in the repo named ManifestIndexer at all, which is why the swallow survived here after being characterised there. The iOS side of the same requirement was found and fixed -- PhoneStorageFailureTests covers `try? await store.save(mac)` letting a success surface render over a refused write. Left open-owner rather than fixed in campaign: propagating the error changes the CLI's exit code, which is a shipped-contract decision, and the project has already taken the opposite decision once on a sibling path. CASE-0153, CASE-0154 and CASE-0151 characterise today's behaviour so the day someone changes it, the change is deliberate. RE-READ AT 42aef112 ON 2026-09-03, BECAUSE THIS NOTE HAD GONE STALE IN THE DIRECTION THAT MATTERS. It says all three call sites discard the error and cites `ServicePorts.swift:341`. Two of the three no longer discard it and the file it names no longer holds the indexer. * The indexer moved to `app/Sources/RouterCore/Service/ManifestIndexer.swift`. Its `record` is a `do`/`catch` at `:193-223` that returns a `cacheFailure`, which reaches the CLI's `IndexReport.add` (`MCPRouterCLI.swift:331-334`) and prints a `not cached <server> ...` line deliberately kept out of the ordinary pass/fail pair, plus a closing sentence about what was not recorded (`MCPRouterCLIIndex.swift:99-135`). A server whose row was lost no longer gets an `ok` line. That is R10, merged at `8241e0f`. * The approve route is a `do`/`catch` at `app/Sources/RouterCore/Auth/AuthRoutes.swift:171-177` returning `(500, {"error": "failed to write manifest: ..."})`. That is R21, merged at `5a51776`, and it CHANGED THE WIRE STATUS this note records as deliberate - see DEF-442, and note that the change agrees with the reference, measured at DEF-441. * `app/Sources/RouterCore/Watch/WatchIndexing.swift:209` is still `try? ManifestIO.save(...)`. R10's brief declares it out of scope in those words - it has no output to contradict itself with - and that is still true. WHAT KEEPS THIS ROW OPEN is unchanged and is the half neither brief would take: `index` still EXITS 0 when every write was refused, and moving that is a shipped-contract decision the owner has not taken. SWIFT WAS NOT COMPILED FOR THIS RE-READ - `swift` and `xcodebuild` are absent on the machine it was written on - so every line above is read off the tree and none of it is a test result. `app/Tests/RouterCoreTests/CLIIndexWriteDeniedTests.swift` and `ManifestIndexerWriteFailureTests.swift` exist and pin this behaviour; whether they pass at 42aef112 is not known here and must not be assumed.

Re-rated from `structural-visual` to `source-analysis`: it reads source text and runs nothing, so it was never one rung below an effect — it is off the product ladder entirely, and `structural-visual` put it on that ladder where it read as movable. The rendered half of this claim is not missing: CASE-0011 (outcome, macos-glass) carries `Reset history…` in the predicate it asserts over the running Activity window, and evidence/ax/SURF-003.window.txt draws it. What is left here is the part no rendered assertion reaches — that the control is declared in `header` and not inside the rows conditional, which is a property of where the source puts it. A render proves the state it was taken in; this is the claim about the other eight, and the campaign has no empty-Activity dump to relate it against. PREVIOUSLY: DEF-016's affordance half and DEF-012's first rename, at the rung they honestly reach. `theResetActionIsInTheHeader` slices `ActivityBoard.header` from its declaration to `content`'s and asserts the slice carries `CleanupPresentation.resetLabel` and opens `model.sheet = .resetHistory`; `theHeaderLabelIsTheDesigns` asserts that constant is `Reset history…` per `prototype.html:716` and `:930`, not the Settings-Danger wording at `:999` the build had shipped. Recorded as `structural-visual` rather than `outcome` and counted against the strict total on purpose: both read source text, and no assertion here proves a header rendered. It is written that way because the claim is about the header in **all nine** DESIGN.md §5 states — the design puts the control outside the rows conditional precisely so the empty state has it — and a rendered assertion over one state would leave the other eight unchecked while buying effect credit. Watched to fail for real rather than by a staged arm: an earlier script aborted before writing the header change, and this assertion reported `the header draws no reset action` against the tree that was genuinely missing it. Reverting `resetLabel` reads `the header action is called Reset call history…`.

Its load-bearing half is that neither SkillsBoard.swift nor MenuCommand.swift writes the marketplaces label as a literal any more, and a literal and a constant RENDER IDENTICALLY — `Text("Add marketplace…")` and `Text(SkillPresentation.marketplacesAction)` produce the same pixels and the same accessibility node. There is no product-side observable, so no rung on the ladder can ever carry this, which is exactly the shape DEF-057 opened the off-axis rung for. The half that IS observable is already covered: CASE-0012 (outcome, macos-glass) asserts `Add marketplace…` on the running Skills window, evidence/ax/SURF-004.window.txt. PREVIOUSLY: DEF-012's second rename. `theMarketplacesActionIsNamedOnce` asserts `SkillPresentation.marketplacesAction == "Add marketplace…"` per `prototype.html:786`, and then that neither `SkillsBoard.swift` nor `MenuCommand.swift` writes either label as a literal any more. The second half is the assertion that bites: the board had shipped `Manage marketplaces…` while the menu item opening the **same sheet** said `Add marketplace…`, so a match-the-strings check would have passed the day before the fix as easily as the day after. Asserting the literals are absent is what stops them drifting apart again. `structural-visual` for the same reason as CASE-0128 — it reads source. subject.note: DEF-011's affordance half, re-expressed against the running window rather than against `CleanupBoardRow.swift`. The source read asserted that the row declares `accessibilityElement(children: .contain)` and not `.combine`; what that modifier decides is whether each row's buttons are separately addressable, and relation `SURF-007/row-actions` in bin/glass-assert.py reads THAT off two dumps of a real window. Measured: 3 candidate rows in evidence/ax/SURF-007.window.txt and 5 in evidence/ax/SURF-007.cleanup-skills.window.txt, and all 8 own their own AXButtons one level below their own group — which a combined row cannot do, because combining flattens them into the group's label and publishes none. The action set is a function of the row and not of the board: exactly [Inspect, Remove…] on the 7 rows carrying no provenance note and exactly [Read first…] on the 1 that does. `metamorphic` rather than `structural` because the claim spans two different row populations: a column drawn at a fixed size fails the count and a combined row fails the ownership, and a single-window presence check can see neither. The Swift suite it replaces (app/Tests/MCPRouterUITests/CleanupRowActionsTests.swift) is kept and still runs — it is the faster signal — but it is no longer what this case stands on.

DEF-015's closed half — the shell's overflow treatment, which DESIGN.md §5 names and the build got wrong in a way no assertion could see. Every board's `AXSplitGroup` width is read back out of the running app and compared against its own `AXWindow` width, board by board, through the channel that already writes those dumps beside the pictures. It read 3 of 8 overflowing — Checks 988, Skills 1044, Discover 1119 inside a 980pt window, each origin moved left by exactly half its excess — and reads 0 of 8 after `.frame(minWidth: 0, maxWidth: .infinity, alignment: .leading)` on `ContentZone`. `outcome` rather than `raster-visual` on purpose: the claim is a measured relation between two frames the app publishes, not a comparison of pixels, and the pictures are what made the defect *visible* rather than what proves it fixed. Armed 20 Aug 2026, three ways on the gate and two on the test. The gate exits 1 against the pre-fix dumps, 0 against the post-fix ones, and 1 with no dumps at all — `examined=0` is a check that never ran and is never a pass. Removing the modifier reddens `ShellDetailWidthTests` with `passes its boards' minimum width up to the split view`, and dropping just `alignment: .leading` reddens the second half alone. That test's first version did NOT bite: it searched the raw source and matched the doc comment naming the modifier, so deleting the modifier left it green. Comments are stripped before matching now — a predicate satisfied by the prose explaining it is not a predicate. What this case does not cover, because `overflowing=0` reads like `nothing is clipped` and is not that claim: content that overflows the detail PANE stays inside the window and is invisible to this oracle. That half is CASE-0134, measured with a second probe against every leaf's right edge — and that probe was wrong on its first run, reading the frame's y where it meant x and reporting clipping on seven of eight boards. The Settings capture is whole, and looking at it is what caught it.

DEF-011's last open half, the one the row was left open for: `Read first…`, which the design keys on `k.provenance` and which `CleanupBoardModel.Candidate` had no field to key on. It now carries `provenance: String?`, read through `SkillChecks.originUnchanged` rather than off `skill.provenance` directly, so this board and the Checks board cannot disagree about what counts as moved. Three assertions, all against the model rather than the pixel. `aMovedMarketplaceReachesTheRow` compares the row's note against that check's own `reason` rather than against a literal, because a literal would stay green while the two boards drifted apart. `anUnmovedRowCarriesNoNote` is the half that makes the first one mean something — a field that is always populated cannot mark a row — and covers both an unmoved skill and a server, which has no marketplace to have moved from. `readFirstOpensItsSheet` asserts the sheet is keyed by the skill's resolved path (`prov:/skills/pr-summariser`), that `skill(atPath:)` finds the skill behind it, and that opening it leaves `M7RecordingClient.writes` empty. Armed 20 Aug 2026 four ways: making `provenanceNote` return nil reads `(moved.provenance → nil) == "The router first saw it at …"`; dropping its guard so an unmoved skill is flagged reads `(unmoved.provenance → "its marketplace moved") == nil`; giving the server call site a note reads the `allSatisfy` failure; collapsing the sheet id to `"prov"` reads `(board.sheet?.id → "prov") == "prov:/skills/pr-summariser"`; and keying `skill(atPath:)` on the name instead of the path reads the provenance comparison failing against nil.

REQ-019 on the one control that has to refuse: the skill row's `Remove…`. The control API is read-only for skills — removing one means writing files the client applications hold open — and the row does not hide the button or offer it and fail. It draws it disabled (AX enabled 0) and states that reason in its help text, which is the shape REQ-019 asks for: no success affordance for work that cannot happen, and the refusal is the server's own. Pixels: `SURF-007.cleanup-skills.png`, 519568 bytes, sha 94dd9d06f87d, window-scoped off CGWindowID 103249 owned by the launched pid, recorded in `evidence/shots/captures.json` with the scenario that produced it. Byte-identical across two consecutive capture runs. It does NOT claim agreement with the design of record: the reference is an HTML mock rasterised at another size, and no macOS API exposes a cross-process computed style.

REQ-019 where DEF-001 makes it matter: this build ships no pairing transport, and the sheet says so instead of drawing a code it cannot complete a pairing with. The AXSheet carries `Pair iPhone`, `Pairing is not available in this build`, and the sentence that keeps the reader from debugging their own network — `this build ships no way to listen for one. Nothing is wrong with your phone or your network.` The negative half is the one that would catch a regression: nothing in the window matches Crockford base-32 at the length REQ-015 specifies, checked by pattern rather than against a literal, so a code this predicate's author never saw would still trip it. This case does NOT make REQ-015 pass — CASE-0010 and CASE-0110 fail against it and keep failing. The sheet is honest about a capability that is missing; the capability is still missing.

The refusal's pixels: `SURF-010.build.png`, window-scoped off the CGWindowID the launched pid owns, an AXSheet at 512×173 over the Inbox window. Recorded in `evidence/shots/captures.json` with the title read back as Inbox — the sheet does not change the window title, so the manifest carries both the readback and the `app://mac/pairing` target rather than letting one stand for the other. This surface had no picture at all for three runs: the capture script pressed for a pairing control while the app was on the Servers board, where none exists, and recorded the surface unreachable for a reason that was its own navigation. Selecting Inbox first opened it on the first attempt.

The fixture half of CASE-0138/CASE-0139, checked in the harness rather than on glass. Those two photograph the Cleanup board drawing `Read first…` on one row and a disabled `Remove…` on the other; this asserts the fixture behind them actually contains one moved skill and one unmoved one, which is what makes the photograph a discrimination rather than a picture of whatever the fixture happened to hold. It also guards the reason the scenario is separate: `cleanupSkills` extends `populated` rather than editing it, because SURF-004's on-glass copy asserts the count `populated` publishes (`6 skills from 4 marketplaces · 1 held for review`) and a seventh row there would have broken an existing predicate. The test additionally asserts the servers half of the board survives the scenario, so a fixture that drew skills by losing servers would fail.

Driven through the UI Automation plane against the real MCPRouter.Shell binary in the interactive session, out of process, with the target never foregrounded. The pane item named 'Checks' was actuated with SelectionItemPattern.Select(), and the reads were taken AFTER that actuation: the window title, the realised control-view tree, and a fingerprint over the tree's names. The fingerprint is what makes this more than a presence check - a destination whose tree is identical to the previous one is recorded as a COLLAPSE and fails, which is the shape where six sidebar items opened one placeholder view and every gate passed.

subject.text: CleanupBoardRow carries three treatments for a skill row — the `Read first…` substitution when SkillChecks.originUnchanged fails, the skill-kind `Remove…` drawn disabled because the router removes servers and never files on disk, and the candidacy reason — and none of them had a rendered path in any configuration of the product. A skill is proposed for cleanup only when every readable client lacks it, and all six skills in SkillFixtures.populated are installed somewhere, so the Debug Cleanup board drew three servers and zero skills. Release reaches the branch only if a real user happens to hold an orphaned skill. CASE-0136 asserted the branch exists by reading CleanupBoardRow and said in its own note why it stopped there; what nobody could say was that a build had ever drawn it. Fixed in-campaign by adding a Debug-only `cleanupSkills` scenario and two SkillFixtures.uninstalled rows, kept separate from `populated` because SURF-004's on-glass predicate asserts the count populated publishes. No view code was touched and no assertion was weakened. Now photographed by CASE-0138/CASE-0139 and guarded in the harness by CASE-0144.

subject.detail: CLOSED 2026-08-20. The cause was two independent framing errors, both invisible because the gate could not run to report them. The design references came from `obscura fetch --screenshot`, which captures at a fixed 1280x720 dpr1 viewport with no viewport flag, so every reference was clipped rather than merely small - the bottom row of one carried 578 non-background pixels of 640 sampled. And the build captures were 980x620 against the design's 1156x680 window, aspect 1.581 against 1.700, which no crop reconciles. Fixed by rasterising the design through CDP with `Emulation.setDeviceMetricsOverride` at 1280x900 dpr2 (readback asserted `[1280, 900, 2]` before any capture), re-photographing the eight Mac boards at the design's own 1156x680 with a setframe readback guard, and cropping both halves to the window's own content box. prescan goes from framingComparable 0/16 to 8/8, aspectRatioOfRatios 1.0 and scaleRatio 1.0 on every pair (evidence/runs/prescan-fidelity.json). Eight verdicts written: 2 pass, 5 fail, 1 unoracled.
subject.text: The campaign names design-review and be-my-witness as gates and has never run either, and the reason was never measured — it read as a skip. It is not. be-my-witness 0.2.0's deterministic prescan over all 16 pairs that hold both halves reports isEvidence 16/16, settled 16/16, framingComparable 0/16, proceed 0/16. Not a dead predicate: the scale ratios differ per lane (0.466x on the SURF-001 sidebar crop, 1.64x on the Mac boards, 0.942x on the phone) rather than returning a constant. Every reference was rasterised at a 1280x720 dpr-1 viewport, inside which prototype.html draws a fixed artboard rather than filling the frame, so rendering larger pads rather than enlarges. Re-rendering the reference does not fix it either: the design's Mac window is #win at 1156x680, aspect 1.700, and the build's is 980x620, aspect 1.581. The build half crops exactly — scale=(2096-1376)/(980-620)=2.0, margin=(2096-980*2)/2=68, content rect (68,68,1960,1240), precisely 2x the AX frame — but no crop reconciles two different window shapes. What would make them comparable is re-capturing the app at the design's window size, which means driving the app again and photographing a window shape the product does not use. Left unresolved deliberately: the structural and lexical differential in evidence/differential.md is the comparison that is valid here, and it ran.
