The design references came from `obscura fetch --screenshot`, which captures at a fixed 1280x720 dpr1 viewport with no viewport flag, so every reference was clipped rather than merely small - the bottom row of one carried 578 non-background pixels of 640 sampled. And the build captures were 980x620 against the design's 1156x680 window, aspect 1.581 against 1.700, which no crop reconciles. Fixed by rasterising the design through CDP with `Emulation.setDeviceMetricsOverride` at 1280x900 dpr2 (readback asserted `[1280, 900, 2]` before any capture), re-photographing the eight Mac boards at the design's own 1156x680 with a setframe readback guard, and cropping both halves to the window's own content box. prescan goes from framingComparable 0/16 to 8/8, aspectRatioOfRatios 1.0 and scaleRatio 1.0 on every pair (evidence/runs/prescan-fidelity.json). Eight verdicts written: 2 pass, 5 fail, 1 unoracled.
subject.text: The campaign names design-review and be-my-witness as gates and has never run either, and the reason was never measured — it read as a skip. It is not. be-my-witness 0.2.0's deterministic prescan over all 16 pairs that hold both halves reports isEvidence 16/16, settled 16/16, framingComparable 0/16, proceed 0/16. Not a dead predicate: the scale ratios differ per lane (0.466x on the SURF-001 sidebar crop, 1.64x on the Mac boards, 0.942x on the phone) rather than returning a constant. Every reference was rasterised at a 1280x720 dpr-1 viewport, inside which prototype.html draws a fixed artboard rather than filling the frame, so rendering larger pads rather than enlarges. Re-rendering the reference does not fix it either: the design's Mac window is #win at 1156x680, aspect 1.700, and the build's is 980x620, aspect 1.581. The build half crops exactly — scale=(2096-1376)/(980-620)=2.0, margin=(2096-980*2)/2=68, content rect (68,68,1960,1240), precisely 2x the AX frame — but no crop reconciles two different window shapes. What would make them comparable is re-capturing the app at the design's window size, which means driving the app again and photographing a window shape the product does not use. Left unresolved deliberately: the structural and lexical differential in evidence/differential.md is the comparison that is valid here, and it ran.
subject.title: the rendered-quality gate has never been able to run, and nothing said why

subject.detail: `vacuity-check.py`'s blind pass reports `examined=1820 mutating=3 re-read-after=0 blind=3` over this test tree. All three read after the mutation: `restartIsIssuedBeforeTheStagingWrite` reads `WatchWorld.serverNames`, the log, `kicks.issued` and `WatchState.load`; `restartIsOwedBeforeTheWriteLands` reads `WatchState.load` inside the lock and `WatchWorld.serverNames` on both sides of the rename; `restartRechecksTheCamera` reads `model.entry.characters`. The heuristic looks for a read AFTER the last occurrence of a mutating verb, and in this product the verb `restart` is also the name of the thing being observed — `restartPending`, `restarted scratch-label` — so the last `restart` in the file sits inside the final assertion and nothing is textually after it. Recorded rather than acted on: the tests are correct as written, and rewording an assertion to satisfy a text heuristic would make the suite worse. The pass is still worth running; 3 of 1820 is a reviewable rate, and it is the check that would have caught 26 of 32 on the campaign it was built from. CAUSE CORRECTED 21 Aug 2026; the diagnosis recorded above was wrong. It said the mutator's name is the observable's name (`restart` inside `restartPending`). Measured against 0.9.2's actual patterns, that cannot happen: the mutator scan at vacuity-check.py:180 requires `(?<![A-Za-z0-9_])` + verb + `\w*\s*\(`, so `state.restartPending == false` never matches for want of the call parenthesis. The real cause is that the seven default readers are all snake_case -- list_, get_, read_, fetch_, sample_, count_, load_ -- and the nine default mutators mostly are too (stop_all, stop_runner, clear_, cancel_). This is a camelCase Swift codebase, so NEITHER side could fire. The pass examined 1657 test bodies and found 3 mutating, 0 re-reading and 3 blind: `blind=3` reads as almost nothing wrong, and meant almost nothing looked at. The denominator was printed and nobody read 3-of-1657 as the alarm it was. Fixed by declaring the project's own vocabulary, which 0.9.2 added for exactly this: campaign.json now carries `blindVocabulary` with 14 camelCase mutators and 13 readers, and the pass reports examined=1657 mutating=320 re-read-after=232 blind=88, with the vocabulary it used printed above the findings. Two of the three original findings resolved on their real reads (`WatchState.load(`, `WatchWorld.read(`). The third, restartRechecksTheCamera, stays flagged and correctly so for a verb heuristic: its only reads are property comparisons -- `model.step`, `model.entry.characters` -- which carry no verb at all. That is the ceiling of this instrument rather than a defect in the test, and it is why the 88 is a worklist and not a verdict: the vocabulary is hand-declared and unvalidated. Of the 21 findings the tool prints, 15 carry a @Test attribute and 5 are fixture helpers in dedicated client files that 0.9.2's per-file helper heuristic does not exclude, because it keys on a function being called more than once in its OWN file and these are called from their importers.
subject.title: the blind-test pass flags three tests that do read after mutating, because the mutator's name is the observable's name

subject.detail: `campaign.py` keeps defects in `inventory.json` under a `defect` list, and `add` assigns the next id from that list. `defects.in.json` is an input file. Twelve defects found in the sittings of 19 and 20 Aug were written straight into the input file with hand-written ids taken from that file's own length, which had stopped tracking the registry at DEF-006. The result: DEF-007 through DEF-018 each named one defect in the registry and a different one in the staging file, and neither file said so. Visible symptom, and the only reason it was caught: `RUN-2026-08-20.md` contains 'DEF-011 is the finding worth acting on ... Cleanup's' at line 96 and 'DEF-011 - the rendered-quality gate has never been able to run' at line 481, in one document, meaning two unrelated things. This is `capture-lineage`'s failure mode moved from pictures to identifiers: a name binding to two subjects with nothing checking the binding. Fixed by renumbering the twelve staged defects to DEF-034..DEF-045, merging them into the registry, and rewriting the fifteen references that meant the staged numbering. Every renumbered record carries `stagedAs` naming its old local id, so a reader meeting the old number in an untouched artifact can resolve it. The remaining 74 references were checked one at a time and meant the registry defect they already named. A fourth lesson, from the third instance's cleanup rather than from the collision itself. Reconstructing the concurrent session's two entries welded `text: ""` and `note: ""` onto both, and the first renumbering pass then used `"text" in d` to tell the two writers' entries apart -- so the artifact defeated the discriminator that would have caught it. Both authors independently read the empty values as harmless because they carried no content. The hazard is shape, not content: a membership test reads a key's PRESENCE, and an empty string defeats `"text" in d` exactly as thoroughly as a populated one would. `campaign.py add` injects only `id`, `status`, `evidence` and `armed`, so that key-shape occurred on exactly the two reconstructed entries and was traceable; the keys were stripped and the pass re-run discriminating on `title`. Recorded because "empty therefore harmless" is a reasonable-sounding wrong answer that both sessions gave.
subject.note: SECOND INSTANCE, 20 Aug 2026, in the case registry rather than the defect registry, and it landed the same way. A helper reported `next case id: CASE-0145` while cases.json already held CASE-0149 and CASE-0150; campaign.py's own `next_id` is max+1 and would have said CASE-0151, so the number that was trusted did not come from it. `add` takes an explicit id through `setdefault` and therefore appends a second entry rather than refusing, so CASE-0149 and CASE-0150 each came to name two cases -- an iOS Settings structural case against REQ-005 and a RouterCore write-failure case against REQ-019 -- and the `set` calls that followed wrote onto the pre-existing pair. Caught by an evidence-existence audit rather than by any gate: the new cases printed `3 evidence` where two were supplied. Restored from `git show HEAD:` (both pre-existing entries are byte-identical to HEAD again, verified by dict comparison) and the new pair renumbered to CASE-0153 and CASE-0154. The registry is sparse -- 74 gaps between 1 and 152 -- so a free-looking number is not evidence that it is free, and only max+1 is. THIRD INSTANCE, the same evening, and this one had two writers rather than one. A second Claude session working the same campaign allocated DEF-047 and DEF-048 at about 23:30 (the SDK -32603 message discard, and a detector defect in vacuity-check.py's blind pass) and committed planning/test-campaign as a directory in 6bdeea4, which also swept up this session's in-progress registry edits. This session allocated DEF-047 and DEF-048 for different defects minutes later, from a read taken before that commit landed. Resolved by renumbering THIS session's pair to DEF-049 and DEF-050 -- the later allocation moves, and the session that moves is the one that can enumerate its own references, which is the only reason the choice is safe rather than arbitrary. The peer's entries were not edited. Note for anyone reading the mechanism: `add` assigns from the registry list, so two writers holding a stale read get the same number, and no gate in the campaign detects it. The detection here was a peer message, and before that an evidence-existence audit; neither is a gate. campaign.py could refuse an explicit id that already exists -- `add` currently takes one through `setdefault` and appends a duplicate instead.
subject.title: the campaign's own defect ids named two different defects each, because the staging file numbered from its own length

subject.note: `#expect(result.tools != nil, ...)` at ShellTests.swift:133. `ReindexResult.tools` is a non-optional `Int` (MCPRouterKit/Control/Models.swift:263), so the comparison could not fail. The Swift compiler emitted `comparing non-optional value of type 'Int' to 'nil' always returns true` on every build of the test target; it was the only such warning in the suite. The intent was stated in the comment directly above it -- `.success` is distinguished from `.populated` by `a reindex that comes back with no error and a tool count` -- so the assertion was one character from doing its job. Repaired to `result.tools == 14`, the value FixtureControlAPIClient+Writes.swift:33 overrides for `.success`, which discriminates against the base `reindex-failure.json` fixture it starts from (`{"tools":0,"error":"fetch failed"}`). Armed in evidence/arming/CASE-0152.arming.log: with the override changed to 0 the assertion goes red (`(result.tools -> 0) == 14`), and the log records that the pre-repair form would have stayed green under the same mutation.
subject.text: A ShellTests assertion on the `.success` reindex scenario compared a non-optional Int to nil, so it was always true and read nothing.

subject.detail: Measured 2026-08-21. `.gitmodules` vendors `.claude/plugins/fledgeling-plugins` at `main`, and `planning/features-to-triage/LEDGER.md`'s allocation notes state the reason: 'a runner reads mockup-fidelity, mac-craft, design-craft and ux-craft at a repo-relative path rather than depending on the machine.' For test-campaign that is not what happens. The submodule (HEAD baaf79a, branch main, clean) carries `plugins/test-campaign` at version 0.5.0, whose `skills/test-campaign/scripts` holds five files: attach-shots.py, campaign.py, evidence-page.py, strict-check.py, witness-worklist.py. It has no `vacuity-check.py` and no `capture-lineage.py`; `grep effect-witness strict-check.py` returns nothing and `grep -c blindVocabulary vacuity-check.py` cannot run because the file is absent. Every gate this campaign reports ran from `~/.claude/plugins/cache/fledgeling-plugins/test-campaign/0.9.2/`, on the machine. The vacuity census, the effect-witness rung, the blind-mutation pass, the capture-lineage ratchet and the strict score of 65 all come from code the submodule does not contain, four minor versions ahead of it. CONSEQUENCE FOR THE PIPELINE, and it is the reason this is filed rather than noted: DEF-051, DEF-052, DEF-054, DEF-055 and DEF-056 are defects in 0.9.2's scripts. None of that code is in this repo at any path, so no ship-feature runner working in an mcp-router worktree can fix them. They are upstream work in github.com/fledgeling-co/fledgeling-plugins, and closing them requires a change pushed to that repo plus a submodule bump here — a different repo and an outward-facing action. Separately, a fresh clone that follows the documented `git submodule update --init --recursive` gets 0.5.0 and would reproduce none of this campaign's numbers. Not fixed here: which version the submodule should track, and whether the campaign should run from it rather than the cache, is the owner's call.
subject.title: the vendored fledgeling-plugins submodule is test-campaign 0.5.0 while every gate in this campaign ran from the machine's 0.9.2 cache

subject.text: Measured by K3 on 2026-08-29 while trying to fill SURF-010's and SURF-011's denominators. Three declared controls have nothing to press, for three different reasons, and only one of them is a gap in the product. `Can't scan? Type a code` is declared on both the Mac pairing sheet and Settings' pair-another sheet. The copy exists — `InboxCopy.Pairing.typeInstead` — and the only view that draws it is the PHONE's `PairingFlowView`. REQ-015 says the phone can scan or type; the Mac sheet offers `Show a new code` and `Done`, so the typed path is reachable from one device and the design puts the affordance on the other. `Unpair` cannot be built as drawn: the control API has no devices endpoint, so what this Mac knows about a paired phone is the name on the inbox snapshot the shell is already polling. `SecurityPane` states that in its own words and offers `Manage…` — which routes to the Inbox — in its place. A refusal with a reason rather than an omission, but the design still promises a control the surface does not carry. `Reset history` is the confirm button of a sheet the Settings window does not host. The act itself ships and is proven: `ActivityModel.resetHistory()` and `CleanupBoardModel.resetHistory()` reach the same endpoint and `Reset history` is actuated on SURF-003 by a passing case. What is absent is this surface's entry point. M39 DISPOSITION, 2026-08-29, for the FIRST of the three only. The defect stays open because `Unpair` and `Reset history` are untouched. `Can't scan? Type a code` is answered by deciding it should not be a control on the Mac at all, rather than by adding one. The copy is the phone's button and switches `PairingFlowView` from the camera to a keypad; the Mac has no second screen to switch to, already draws the eight characters under the QR, and is not the device that types them. A Mac button would change no state and reveal nothing, which is this defect again rather than its repair. What shipped is the instruction the brief asked for -- `InboxCopy.Pairing.typeInsteadDetail`, drawn by `PairingSheet.typedFallback` in the live state, in the design of record's own wording. CASE-0289 asserts the sentence is drawn and that the action bar did not gain a fourth control; the surface's `controlsUnactuatable` row now records the decision instead of the absence.
subject.title: Three Settings and pairing controls the design draws have no counterpart on the Mac

subject.detail: **The recorded cause was wrong, and this replaces it.** It said the shutter fired during a board transition and named the fix as a settle in `capture-mac-glass.sh`. Measured 20 Aug 2026 from the accessibility dumps the same script already writes, one per board, beside the pictures: | board | window | AXSplitGroup | clipped | |---|---|---|---| | Servers, Activity, Cleanup, Inbox, Settings | 980pt | 980pt | — | | Checks | 980pt | 988pt | 8pt | | Skills | 980pt | 1044pt | 64pt | | Discover | 980pt | 1119pt | 139pt | Every window in the run is the same 980x620 and every capture is the same 2096x1376, so no capture rect is wrong and no shutter is early. What differs is the shell **inside** the window: on three boards `NavigationSplitView` lays out wider than the window and centres the excess — the split group's origin moves left by exactly half the overflow in all three cases (180→148 for 64pt, 180→110.5 for 139pt, 180→176 for 8pt), which is what makes the clipping symmetrical. That is why the sidebar's section headers read `unning` and `brary` while the nav rows beside them are whole: the headers sit at a smaller leading inset and fall off first, and the header's trailing controls — `Manage marketplaces.`, `Review 2.3.0…` — fall off the right by the same amount. So this is a product defect on three boards rather than a lane defect on two captures, and it is worse than recorded: Checks overflows too, by 8pt, which is small enough that nobody reading the picture saw it. The app declares no minimum window width anywhere, so nothing stops a user reaching this state — the campaign's 980pt window is an ordinary size, not a stress case. The consequence that made it a defect stands unchanged and is now better founded: a clipped capture is admissible for what it shows and silent about what it cut, so a reader cannot tell an absent control from a cropped one. Both witness verdicts that depend on these captures say in their method field that the right-hand controls were read from the accessibility dump instead. `capture-mac-glass.sh` now prints `board width: examined=14 overflowing=3` every run, with a line naming each board and its excess. Reported rather than enforced, because three boards overflow today and a known red in `make all` either blocks unrelated work or gets its assertion softened. NOT FIXED, and the fix is a decision rather than a repair. Either the shell declares a minimum window width at least as wide as its widest board — one line, guarantees nothing ever clips, and costs users on small screens a window they cannot shrink — or the three boards compress, which keeps small screens usable and is per-board column work across all three. Discover at 1119pt is the one that decides how much that costs. PARTLY CLOSED 20 Aug 2026, on `ai/x4`, and the part that is not closed is named rather than left to look finished. The mechanism turned out to be a chain rather than a board: each row's fixed columns report a hard minimum width, the detail pane sums them, `NavigationSplitView` reports that as its own minimum, and nothing ever reads it back — this app opts into no minimum window size and `windowResizability` defaults to `.automatic` — so the window proposes 980pt and SwiftUI **places** the oversized child with default centre alignment. The symmetry was the tell. Referred to the xAI lane (grok-4.6, xhigh) with the measured table; it named the propagation as the bug, called both listed fixes second-best, and its Q3 answer — placement plus `.automatic` resizability rather than any documented split-view overflow mode — is what the one-line fix then confirmed. FIXED: `ContentZone` carries `.frame(minWidth: 0, maxWidth: .infinity, alignment: .leading)`. Measured on the rebuilt app through the same accessibility channel: all eight boards read `split=980` inside a `window=980`, overflowing 0 of 8, where the same probe on the previous build read 3 of 8. The sidebar is whole again — `Running`, `Library` and the footer readout all render in full where they were `unning` and `brary`. The leading alignment is the deliberate half: it decides who loses when the content still does not fit, and the answer is never the navigation. STILL OPEN: the boards' content is still wider than the detail pane on those three, so the trailing chrome is cut at the pane's right edge — Discover's search field reads `Search the regis` and a body sentence loses its last word. That is one-edge clipping where it was two, and it is the conventional behaviour of a too-narrow window rather than a split view eating its own sidebar, but it is still content going missing without saying so. Closing it needs the three boards' columns to flex, which is a design decision about what Discover looks like compressed and is the owner's rather than mine. GUARDED two ways, and the two see different things. `capture-mac-glass.sh` now **fails** on any board whose split group exceeds its window, and refuses to pass on `examined=0`; all three arms were exercised on 20 Aug 2026 — red at 3 of 14, green at 0 of 14, and exit 1 with no dumps at all. `ShellDetailWidthTests` asserts the modifier in `ShellWindow`'s detail column so a revert is red in `make test` rather than on the next glass run. That test's own first version was a detector defect found by arming: it searched the raw source slice, and the modifier it looks for is named in the doc comment three lines above it, so deleting the modifier left the assertion green. Comments are stripped before matching now, and both halves were re-armed separately. CLOSED 20 Aug 2026, and the second half corrected the first half's diagnosis of *which* content was too wide. The brief written from the split-group numbers said three boards' table columns needed to flex. A pane-level probe — every leaf's right edge against the window's, read from the same dumps — says otherwise, and it says so only after the probe itself was fixed: the first version read the frame's **y** where it meant **x** and reported clipping on seven of eight boards, which the pixels flatly denied. The Settings capture is whole, and looking at it is what caught the field offset. A frame's last five fields are x, y, w, h and a flag; the split-group gate only ever compared widths, which is why it was right while the leaf probe was wrong. Corrected, the drivers are: - **Discover**: content wants 823pt against a 684pt pane. Not the table — cutting `nameColumn` from 216pt to 96pt moved the number by **zero**. It is the controls row: a `.fixedSize()` segmented picker measuring 567pt beside a search field pinned at 240pt. - **Skills**: 748pt against 684pt, same shape — a 516pt fixed picker and a 216pt pinned field. - **Checks**: not a content defect at all. Its real content ends at 1152pt inside a 1160pt pane; the only thing past the edge is `KeyClaimProbe`, the `#if DEBUG` test surface A21 names, overhanging by 4pt. It is absent from any build a user runs, and it is what the whole 8pt split-group excess on this board was. FIXED by giving each board a `searchMinWidth` of four units and declaring the field `minWidth:idealWidth:maxWidth:` rather than `width:`. The picker cannot give a point back — that is what `.fixedSize()` means, and it is right, because a segmented control has nowhere to put a truncated label — so the field is the only control in the row that can. It renders at its full width wherever there is room and shows about eight characters at the narrowest window this app is used at, which is less than anyone wants and more than nothing: it still takes focus, accepts a query and submits. Measured after: every board reads `split=980` in a `window=980`, and the only leaf past the pane edge on any of the eight is a 1pt scrollbar — plus the Debug key probe's 4pt on Checks. Running bin/capture-mac-glass.sh against the current build turns four previously-passing cases red, and in every one of them the PRODUCT is right and the recorded evidence is stale: 1. THE MENU MAP. Committed SURF-001.menu.txt binds Cmd-4 to `Discover`; the running app binds Cmd-4 to `Harnesses`, exactly as Destination.swift's selectionDigit declares (activity 1, servers 2, skills 3, harnesses 4, discover 5, inbox 6, evals 7, cleanup 8, insights 9). glass-assert.py's SURF-001 `menu` dict is the pre-M22 map, so CASE-0001 asserts five bindings the shipped build does not have. 2. SETTINGS IS NOT A SIDEBAR ROW. M15 made Settings a Scene and removed the case from Destination, and capture-mac-glass.sh still does `axkit select Settings`. That select now fails — `axkit: no sidebar row starting 'Settings'` — the app stays on Cleanup, and the script photographs the CLEANUP board and files it as SURF-011. CASE-0016 and CASE-0111 fail against it. THE CAMPAIGN'S OWN INSTRUMENTS CAUGHT BOTH, WHICH IS THE ONE GOOD PART. The capture manifest's readback records that picture as target `app://mac/cleanup` under subject SURF-011, contradicting its own filename — the exact mechanism the script was rebuilt around. Independently, glass-assert.py --discriminate reports LEAK SURF-007 wrongly accepted 1 of 8 foreign board dumps: SURF-011 — because SURF-011's dump IS the Cleanup board. Two instruments, one cause. WHY THIS IS THE SAME FINDING AS G14'S, ONE LAYER DOWN. G14 found the surface LIST had not grown since it was written. This is the EVIDENCE not having been re-taken since the build moved. In both cases a completeness gate reported clean because the thing it measured was a stale artefact rather than the product. NOT FIXED HERE, DELIBERATELY. Owed: re-map SURF-001's menu dict from Destination.selectionDigit, and give SURF-011 a route to the Settings SCENE (Cmd-comma or the app menu) instead of a sidebar select that cannot succeed. subject.detail: DETECTOR DEFECT in test-campaign 0.9.2, found 21 Aug 2026. attach-shots.py iterates every image under evidence/shots and assigns `hit['shot'] = rel` on each match, last write wins, with no preference for a build capture over a design render. This campaign keeps six directories under evidence/shots (16 root, 8 design-size, 16 fidelity, 9 ios, 17 mock, 11 mock-hidpi), so for SURF-001 the candidates in iteration order are SURF-001.build.png, SURF-001.shell.png, mock/SURF-001.png, mock-hidpi/SURF-001.full.png -- and the last one wins. MEASURED for SURF-001, SURF-002 and SURF-006: `--apply` would repoint each surface's `shot` from its build capture to `evidence/shots/mock-hidpi/SURF-00N.full.png`, which is the render of the DESIGN, not the build. That is the skill's own headline failure mode -- publishing a picture of one thing under the name of another -- arriving in a sibling of the plane built to prevent it, and it would do so while every other gate stayed green, because capture-lineage.py gates the 16 captures cited by CASES and the surface wall is a different population. The report compounds it: the UNCORROBORATED block prints surface ids (SURF-001 ... SURF-011) rather than the file each verdict is about, so a reader sees eleven surfaces apparently lacking provenance when in fact each surface's ACTUAL `shot` field points at a corroborated build capture and the complaint is about a mock render nobody intended to attach. Distinguishing the two costs a re-derivation of the matcher by hand. Recorded rather than patched, precedent DEF-048, DEF-051, DEF-052 and DEF-053. The campaign's standing refusal to run `--apply` here predates this and was based on the DEF-006 mis-wire; it now has a measured mechanism behind it. Separately closed while investigating: this campaign's design-size captures carried their provenance in a second manifest, evidence/shots/design-size/captures.json, in a different schema ({captures:[...]} against the root's bare list) that no gate reads. Its 8 entries were merged into the root manifest with `target` derived from the root's declared target for the same subject and corroborated by each capture's own windowTitleReadback -- Servers, Activity, Skills, Discover, Inbox, Checks, Cleanup, Settings, every one matching -- recorded at capture time, and each carries `targetDerivedFrom` saying so. That was the campaign's own inconsistency and is fixed here; it was not the cause of the 11. RE-MEASURED 2026-08-27 (G21) after `evidence/shots/captures.json` was made a derived file. The uncorroborated count is 12 and stays 12: SURF-001..011 and SURF-022. Eleven of them are this defect -- `mock-hidpi/` sorts last, so it is the row that decides each surface's `shotProvenance`. The mock rows in the manifest deliberately carry NO `target`; the address the channel was pointed at is recorded in full as `renderedFrom`, with an `attachHazard` field naming this defect. Measured both ways on this tree: writing that address as `target` instead drops the uncorroborated count from 12 to 1 and DISARMS `--apply`'s refusal, because `attach-shots.py` only checks the field is present and never compares it to the subject's route -- which is item 5 of X8's work order. So the report going quiet would have been this defect getting worse while looking fixed. The twelfth, SURF-022, is not this defect: see DEF-061.
subject.title: attach-shots --apply would attach the design mock render as the build's surface shot for 11 surfaces, and its report names the surface rather than the file

subject.detail: Measured 2026-09-03 (WE3) on LUKESFF, Windows 11, CPython 3.13, console codepage 1252. `campaign.py`'s loader is `return json.loads(p.read_text())` with no `encoding=`. `Path.read_text()` defaults to `locale.getencoding()`, which is cp1252 here. This campaign's `inventory.json` holds em dashes and middots, so: $ python vendor/test-campaign/.../campaign.py check planning/test-campaign UnicodeDecodeError: 'charmap' codec can't decode byte 0x9d in position 284168 exit 1 It is a traceback rather than a verdict, and `exit 1` is the same code the gate uses for 'not ready to report'. A caller reading the exit status alone cannot tell a campaign that failed its checks from one the checker could not open. `PYTHONUTF8=1` makes it run; with that set it reaches its checks and reports normally, which is how the rest of this session's `campaign.py` measurements were taken. SCOPE. Windows hosts only -- macOS and most Linux default to UTF-8, which is why the campaign never met this on the Mac. It is not confined to `campaign.py`: `vacuity-check.py`, `strict-check.py` and `attach-shots.py` in the pinned 0.9.2 read and WRITE with the same bare calls, so on this host `attach-shots.py --apply` would write `inventory.json` back in cp1252 and mangle every em dash in the register. That one is a data-loss path rather than a crash, and it is the reason this is filed at detector severity rather than as a nuisance.
subject.title: campaign.py reads the registry with no encoding, so on a Windows console it dies on the first non-ASCII byte and checks nothing

subject.detail: Found 20 Aug 2026 while building R8's gate against both routers. Against a fixture returning `-32603` with the message `Internal error: Authentication required`, the reference records `MCP error -32603: Internal error: Authentication required` and the Swift router records `[-32603] Internal error`. The upstream's own message is gone. CAUSE, cited exactly: modelcontextprotocol/swift-sdk 0.12.1, `Sources/MCP/Base/Error.swift:217-240`. The decoder reads the server's `message`, then maps the code — `-32700`, `-32600`, `-32601` and `-32602` each pass `unwrapDetail(message)`, and `-32603` alone passes `unwrapDetail(nil)`. `unwrapDetail(fallback)` returns `data.detail` when present and the fallback otherwise, so a server that answers -32603 with a message and no `data.detail` has its message discarded, and `Error.swift:91` renders `"Internal error" + (detail.map { ": \($0)" } ?? "")` as the bare canonical name. -32603 is the code servers use for an arbitrary application error, so it is the one that loses the most. TWO consequences: for the whole class of -32603 upstream errors the Swift router tells the user strictly less than the reference does; and R8's Swift half cannot detect a credential refusal at all, because there is no text left to match. This is a coverage gap in the parity suite as much as a defect in the SDK — no parity scenario had ever exercised a JSON-RPC error carrying a detailed message, which is why 82 proven rows never saw it. Remedies, none taken: report upstream and take a fixed release; pin a patched fork; or read the JSON-RPC error before the SDK types it, which needs a seam below the client.
subject.title: the Swift MCP SDK discards an upstream's error message for code -32603, so the router reports less than the reference does

subject.detail: Measured 2026-09-03 (WE3) while adjudicating `an-effect-class-the-census-cannot-name-reads-as-no-effect.md`. That brief cites one requirement. The requirement axis is clean -- all 44 declare a class in `EFFECT_CLASSES` -- and the finding is on the axis nobody counted: 31 of the 49 cases that name a `witness.effect` name a class the vocabulary does not carry, and every one of the 31 is `oracle: effect-witness` at `status: pass`. machine-state 25 CASE-0366..0371, 0420..0426, 0470..0477, 0490..0493 file 2 CASE-0342, CASE-0386 notification 1 CASE-0441 os-record 1 CASE-0387 process 1 CASE-0440 ui-state 1 CASE-0346 WHY NOBODY SAW IT, and this is the half that makes it a defect rather than a chore. `campaign.py:702` DOES check the field, and its blocker line reads `40 effect-witness claim(s) with no recorder, no effect class, or a count of zero`. That 40 is 31 bad classes plus 9 missing recorders and counts, verified by replicating the loop. The report then caps its detail at twelve lines -- which on this campaign are twelve lines about four cases with missing recorders and null counts. **All 31 class findings are inside the 40 and not one of them is printed.** A reader of the campaign report cannot learn from it that any case names an unrecognised class, and the number reads as a recorder problem. WHY THE 31 ARE NOT REMAPPED HERE, deliberately and on the record. Some are a rename: `process` on CASE-0440, whose recorder is `Get-ScheduledTaskInfo`, is `subprocess`. Some are a harder question a rename would bury: `machine-state` on CASE-0423..0426 and CASE-0490..0493 is recorded over *"the router's own /servers listing, read over the control API"*, which is a recorder INSIDE the product -- whether those cases belong at the `effect-witness` rung at all is a judgement about the case, not about a word. Picking the nearest legal spelling for all 31 would turn 31 rows green while answering neither question, and every one of them belongs to the Windows waves rather than to this runner. `references/effect-boundary.md` is what settles them.
subject.title: 31 of the 49 cases naming a witness effect class name one the census cannot recognise, and campaign.py counts them into a 40 whose printed detail names none of them

subject.cell: execution-plane=windows-host - data-shape=package not installed
subject.note: A real MSIX, built, deployed and removed, with a recorder at each step that is not the thing that wrote it. MakeAppx packs and .NET's ZipArchive reads the OPC container back - so the identity assertion is made against the PACKED ARTIFACT rather than against the file on disk that was handed to the packer. `winget validate` is the winget client applying a schema this repository does not own. Add-AppxPackage deploys and Get-AppxPackage reports: Fledgeling.MCPRouter_0.1.0.0_x64__facmrsw33693e. THE INSTALL ARM IS WHAT TURNS A FILE INTO A PACKAGE. A manifest can pack cleanly, validate cleanly, and be refused at deployment for a capability, an architecture or a signature - and every static check in the world passes right up to that point. 'CLEAN UNINSTALL RULES' IS THE HALF WORTH READING TWICE. UninstallGuidance promises that uninstalling preserves %USERPROFILE%\.claude\mcp-router. That is a promise about what SURVIVES, and a promise about survival cannot be checked by any amount of reading - only by an uninstall that actually ran. The lane plants a marker, installs, removes, and requires both that the deployment stack reports the package gone and that the marker is still there. WHAT THE LANE PUTS BACK: a self-signed certificate is added to LocalMachine\TrustedPeople so an unsigned developer package can deploy at all, and removed in a finally block however the run ends. Verified afterwards: zero Fledgeling.* packages, zero witness certificates. A lane that left a trusted publisher behind would have changed what this machine will install, silently and for every future run. NOT SETTLED: that anyone can obtain the package. Nothing publishes it, the winget InstallerUrl is a deliberate example.invalid placeholder, and this lane asserts the placeholder is PRESENT so the manifest cannot be mistaken for a shipping one. DEF-083 carries the publishing step, which needs a signing certificate and a pull request into a third-party repository.

subject.cell: execution-plane=windows-host - data-shape=one capability queued
subject.note: The toast itself, in the Action Center, read by a process that cannot raise one. DEF-082 filed this as unmeasurable and gave a reason: UserNotificationListener's userNotificationListener capability is only grantable to a packaged application, and MCPRouter.Shell is WindowsPackageType=None, so the row was said to be downstream of WIN19's MSIX. THE REASON WAS WRONG, AND IT WAS WRONG BEFORE WIN19 LANDED. Measured on this host from an ordinary unpackaged Win32 console process with no package identity at all - Package.Current throws InvalidOperationException, which the lane asserts rather than assumes - UserNotificationListener.Current resolves, RequestAccessAsync returns Allowed with no consent prompt, and GetNotificationsAsync returns the toasts that are really there. On the first run those included three raised by win22-toast-witness the day before, carrying the exact strings NotificationPresentation writes. No MSIX, no capability, no packaged identity. WHAT IS STILL NOT AVAILABLE UNPACKAGED, and it bounds this case: every member of UserNotification.AppInfo throws NotImplementedException 0x80004001 for a caller with no package identity, so the listener can say what a notification SAYS and when it arrived and cannot say who raised it. Attribution here is the payload text, which the product owns, inside a time window this run opened - weaker than a publisher identity, and recorded as such. THE RECORDER IS NOT THE WRITER AND IS NOT EVEN THE SAME PROCESS: app/windows/MCPRouter.Witness.ActionCenter shares no code with the shell and cannot raise a notification. The shell's toast-probe.json is carried as the writer's self-report and graded by nothing. THE PRESENCE CONTROL is a removal: the matched notification is taken back out through the listener and the Action Center is read a third time, and the recorder is required to say no about it.

subject.cell: execution-plane=windows-host - data-shape=one capability queued
subject.note: The COM activator the Windows notification platform wrote, read out of the registry by a process that did not write it. The writer is AppNotificationManager.Register() inside the shell; the recorder is HKCU through PowerShell's registry provider, and nothing of this repository's sits between them. Four arms. BASELINE requires the AUMID key to be ABSENT before the shell launches, so what the other three read is this launch. The three EFFECT arms read the key, the CustomActivator CLSID it names, and that CLSID's LocalServer32 - which came back as MCPRouter.Shell.exe carrying the platform's own ----AppNotificationActivated: argument, a string this repository does not write anywhere. THE ACTIVATOR IS THE ARM THAT CARRIES THE ITEM. A toast outlives the process that raised it; when somebody presses Review an hour later, Windows COM-activates the LocalServer32 registered for that CLSID. Without it the toast still appears and pressing it does nothing, which is the failure that looks most like success and exactly what a screenshot of a notification would have certified. WHAT THIS CASE DOES NOT SETTLE: that a toast is drawn, and that a press re-activates the app. Both need UserNotificationListener, whose capability is only grantable to a packaged application; DEF-082 carries them and is downstream of DEF-073. The shell's own report that the platform accepted a Show is carried in the evidence as writerSelfReport and is graded by nothing, because a process reporting its own effect is the shape of claim DEF-072 was about.

subject.cell: execution-plane=windows-host - data-shape=no task registered
subject.note: The Windows task scheduler holding a task the product registered, read by an API that did not write it. The writer is MCPRouter.Shell.Live's LogonTaskSupervisor driving schtasks.exe with the Task Scheduler XML it builds; the recorder is Get-ScheduledTask, the ScheduledTasks module over the scheduler's WMI provider - a different API, a different process and a different vocabulary for the same facts. The XML says RunLevel LeastPrivilege and the recorder answers RunLevel Limited, and nothing in this repository translates between them. The scheduler also normalised the interval this run asked for, PT60S, into PT1M, which is the plainest available evidence that the read did not come back through anything this code wrote. EIGHT ARMS, AND TWO ARE ABOUT THE INSTRUMENT. BASELINE requires the recorder to report the task ABSENT before registration - without it, a task left behind by an interrupted run makes every other arm pass over a run that registered nothing. SILENCE requires it to report absence again after removal, which is what separates a reader from an echo: a recorder that always answered yes would satisfy the six product arms by construction. The other six read the three claims LifecyclePresentation prints to the operator - triggered at logon, un-elevated, restarting on failure - plus the executable and port this run asked for, plus presence and removal. WHAT IT DOES NOT SETTLE, and the reason it is one case rather than the whole of REQ-035: nothing here logs the user out, so the trigger has never been watched to fire, and nothing here starts or kills a daemon, so the restart has never been watched to happen. DEF-081 carries those two. This case settles that the registration the product performs produces, in the Windows task scheduler, a task carrying the properties the product's own UI describes - which before 2026-09-02 was unmeasured entirely, and which DEF-074 recorded as a supervision model nothing performed.

subject.cell: execution-plane=windows-host - data-shape=a supervised process that dies
subject.note: The half of WIN23's supervision promise that had never been watched: a daemon the Windows task scheduler starts, loses, and starts again. DEF-081 filed it as unmeasurable and named the blocker as a missing Windows daemon binary; the blocker was real and is gone - app/windows/MCPRouter.Witness.Daemon is a harness process that starts, records its own start and waits to be killed, so there is something for the scheduler to supervise. WHAT THE MEASUREMENT FOUND IS NOT WHAT THE ROW EXPECTED. The registration the product wrote carried RestartOnFailure with a 60-second interval and a count of 3, and it did not restart the daemon at all. Killed, watched 150 seconds, on the unified scheduling engine and the legacy one, for a run started by a trigger and one started on demand: four registrations, no restart. The same block DID restart, three times at exactly 60 seconds, a task whose Command named a file that does not exist - so the instrument can see a restart, and RestartOnFailure governs a task that fails to LAUNCH rather than one whose action launched and later died. DEF-320 carries that, and the product now writes a Repetition on the trigger alongside MultipleInstancesPolicy IgnoreNew. THE RECORDERS ARE TWO AND NEITHER WROTE ANYTHING: Get-ScheduledTaskInfo for the scheduler's own account of its runs, and Get-CimInstance Win32_Process for the process identity, which is what makes 'it came back' a different process id rather than a report from the thing that came back. The daemon's own run log is carried and graded by nothing. EIGHT ARMS, THREE OF THEM ABOUT THE INSTRUMENT: BASELINE requires both tasks absent and no daemon running, so nothing below is inherited from an interrupted run; CLAIM.repetition and CLAIM.ignorenew read the product's own unmodified logon registration back through the WMI provider; SILENCE requires both recorders to say no once the tasks are gone. ONE SUBSTITUTION, SAID OUT LOUD: a trigger repetition does not apply to an on-demand start - measured, twice - so the live task carries a TimeTrigger where the product writes a LogonTrigger, because this lane must not log the machine out. Every Setting, the repetition interval, the principal, the action and the instances policy are the product's own document. That the trigger fires AT LOGON is still unwitnessed and DEF-081 keeps it.

The iOS unit lane's own instrument. `PhoneSurfaceTests.testTheAccessibilityEngineCanBeSwitchedOn` asserts that `_AXSSetAutomationEnabled` resolves and that a hosted `ScrollView { Text }` publishes its label back through the same walk every other assertion in the target uses. Without it the target's 35 surface assertions are vacuous in a way that reads exactly like a product rendering no copy — DEF-029, where they were vacuous for ten consecutive runs. Armed three ways on 20 Aug 2026: renaming the symbol fails this case alone; mutating the call to `(false)` on a device created for the arm reads 53 failures across 36 tests, which is what proves the other 35 depend on it; and the first run ever taken on a device whose engine had never been live is clean, which proves the fix needs no warm-up on a fresh device. A device left explicitly disabled does need one, and `test-ios` now runs a throwaway process before the graded one for that reason.

subject.cell: execution-plane=in-process · state=a server with a probe interval that is not live
subject.note: A scheduled sweep observes; it does not create the thing it is observing. `UpstreamHealthMonitorTests` H16 stages a server with a 60-second interval that the pool reports as not live, runs one sweep, and asserts on the PROBER rather than on the record: the thing that would spawn a child was never called, and the record says so with a reason rather than a failure. That is REQ-001 stated from inside this feature — at rest there are zero child processes — and it is the whole reason background probing defaults to off as well. H11 is the other half: a decline never counts against `consecutiveFailures`, so a sweep that declines twenty-one idle servers forever cannot trip them. The witness run records the same property from outside the process: before any probe, the report is `unprobed` and `ps(1)` shows no child of the daemon.

subject.evidence: vacuous
subject.note: HISTORICAL FINDING (2026-08-29, source revision 83e5380): the following absence finding describes that revision, not the current production transport. I5 measured neither side implements a transport; the phone stores a paired-Mac record for a Mac it never contacted. RE-CLASSED `contradicted` -> `vacuous` on 2026-08-29 by K4, per references/effect-boundary.md SS2: contradicted means the product does the thing and does it differently from the document; vacuous means the product does not do the thing at all, so there is nothing for the constraint to be true or false about. The two want different remedies and reading them as one sends a missing subsystem to the place that fixes a wrong one. SS3 names this row's exact shape -- a requirement whose declared effect class has no provider in production source is vacuous at phase 1, before any test is written. MEASURED AT `83e5380`, and the narrow true thing rather than the general one (SS7: absence is a fact about this commit). `PairingService` has exactly ONE conformance in production source, `public struct FixturePairingService: PairingService`, `app/Sources/MCPRouterKit/Pairing/PairingService.swift:31`; the shipped shell wires it by default, `pairing: any PairingService = FixturePairingService()`, `app/Sources/MCPRouterUI/Phone/PhoneShell.swift:63`. No `URLSession`, `NWConnection`, `NWListener` or `Network.NW` symbol appears anywhere under `app/Sources/MCPRouterKit/Pairing/` (9 files); the fourteen files in `app/Sources` that do hold one are OAuth, control-plane, registry and loopback-server code, none of it reachable from the pairing path. The protocol's own docstring states the decision rather than leaving it inferred: 'No live implementation ships in this item, and that is a decision rather than a gap.' SO THE CLAIM IS NOT BOUND, AND THE `provider` FIELD STAYS EMPTY DELIBERATELY. There is no symbol that opens the socket to bind it to. `vacuity-check.py --gate` therefore continues to report REQ-016 as uncensused, correctly, and that finding is a dispositioned expectation rather than a silence: it is the vacuity, visible. What the re-class buys is that `campaign.py check` stops counting REQ-016 as an effect somebody failed to witness -- `unwitnessed_effects` excludes `vacuous` (campaign.py:1099) -- and starts reporting it as the product gap it is. The remedy is to build the transport (I5, DEF-001) or to withdraw the requirement; neither is K4's.

subject.note: J2. Every sidebar row is selected in turn and the effect is read in the RESTORATION STORE, which is a different channel from the one that struck: `ShellModel.selection`'s `didSet` calls `store.save(destination:)`, so a real selection leaves a value in a scratch `UserDefaults` suite that nothing in the test wrote, and that a relaunch reads. `model.selection == .servers` after `model.select(.servers)` was deliberately NOT used — it reads the property the call just wrote, which is the actuation side of the vacuous assertion (`references/inert-ui.md`, `detector-defects.md` §11). Each row is approached from a DIFFERENT destination, because `didSet` guards on `oldValue != selection` and a loop starting where the model boots would have the first row write nothing at all. The destination-collapse relation is asserted as a count rather than as seven separate greens: seven presses, seven DISTINCT persisted values, so a shell whose rows all led to one place fails on the cardinality. A second model built on the same store comes up where the last row left it, which is the read-back a relaunch actually performs. `Settings` is the eighth control and is not a destination: M15 moved it to a scene of its own, so the effect read is the installed opener firing exactly once AND the console's persisted destination not moving. Both halves, because an implementation that opened the scene and also selected a board would pass the first alone. LIMIT, stated rather than left implicit: a persisted destination proves the selection took. It does not prove a different board was DRAWN — SwiftUI's view tree is opaque to a SwiftPM test and `ContentZone`'s switch is unreachable from here. That half is CASE-0001's, on glass, and it is FAILING (DEF-058, DEF-059), so it counts nothing. This is the in-process half and says which half it is.

J2. `Remove` is driven with the history checkbox both ways and the effect is read as the operation the client recorded — `remove(keepHistory)` then `remove`. The sheet closing and the selection dropping are the app's own report that it worked and are deliberately not the observable: `references/inert-ui.md` §3 is exactly a handler that changes a banner and does nothing else.

K3. `Install` is driven at `DiscoverBoardModel.install` and the effect is read as the DECLARATION THE CLIENT RECORDED — name, command and args, checked against the row that was pressed rather than against the function that built them. Two entries are staged with different install blocks and both are pressed, so a handler that declares a fixed payload, or the row it happened to have selected, fails on the second press; one press and one assertion cannot tell those apart. The read refused is `board.rows[0].installed == true`. `markInstalled` writes that from the board's own copy of the response, so it is true whether or not anything reached the router — the app's report that it worked, which is what the arm leaves standing.

N8. The inertness guard on the untrusted-input boundary, made capable of failing. M19 shipped `MarkdownSecurityTests.htmlIsInert` with four spellings that named `javascript:`, no scheme, or nothing, and two assertions -- no link, no `imageURL` -- that `MarkdownInline.sanitized` makes true of every input it touches. It could not go red. M30 wired `ControlAPICapabilityDocumentSource` into the shipped UI, so router-served third-party text now reaches this renderer in a Release build, and the guard on it measured nothing. MEASURED, not assumed: the platform parser does keep inline HTML inert -- under `MarkdownInline`'s own options it hands each tag back as characters and marks it `.inlineHTML`, an intent naming no destination, and it does so under all four combinations of `allowsExtendedAttributes` and `interpretedSyntax`. Swift 6.2, macOS 26.6.2 (25G83), Debug, `swift test`. So this was an evidence defect and not a live vulnerability, and the fix is the assertion rather than new sanitisation. Two `https` spellings were added, because `https` is the one scheme the allowlist keeps and therefore the only one that can carry an interpreted `<a>` through to the assertion; a presence control runs the same reader over the markdown twin of the same destination first; and two clauses were added that the old body did not have -- handed back verbatim, and no attribute beyond the `.inlineHTML` marker. That last clause also corrects the test's own claim: the parser DOES attach one attribute to inline HTML and `sanitized` carries it, so the old name -- `inline HTML acquires no attribute of any kind` -- was false as written as well as unfailable, which is why nobody found out.

subject.note: R22. The requirement is written as an honesty guardrail rather than a behaviour because the load-bearing half is a promise about what is NOT in the output, and this campaign's own history is that such a promise is satisfied trivially by producing nothing. The writer is not the reader: overflow-actuate.ps1 expands in its own process and writes only the ExpandCollapseState it saw, while every element reading comes from uia-dump.ps1 started separately. TWO FINDINGS FROM THE FIRST RUN, neither planted, both corrected in the manifest rather than in the assertion. (1) probe-expectation.json predicted that opening the overflow would cost the never-activated guarantee, and IT WAS RIGHT: the probe held the foreground at none of the three baseline samples and at all six effect and silence samples, so Expand activates the window and Collapse does not hand the foreground back. That cost is now DECLARED as `overflow.activationCost` and compared both ways, so the day WinUI stops activating, this arm reddens rather than quietly acquiring a guarantee nobody re-checked. (2) each command resolves to TWO tree paths with the overflow open, because WinUI publishes the OverflowPopup subtree once through a Microsoft.UI.Content.PopupWindowSiteBridge child and once in place beneath the ApplicationBar. Both copies agree on name, controlType, className, isEnabled, isOffscreen, accessKey, patterns and bounding rectangle, so it is one control on two routes; the assertion now permits several matches only while they agree on everything a caller would act on, and plant (H) watches that a genuinely different control under one id still fails. subject.note: The health probe becoming a real child process, seen by two parties that are not the router. `bin/witness-health-probe.sh` drives `POST /servers/witness-fixture/probe` over the DAEMON's own socket — a production entry point, not the prober called from a test — and records the pid the shell launched beside the pid the child reports for its own parent. THE LANE IS THE PORTABLE FLOOR AND SAYS SO: a real spawned process writing a sentinel the witness then reads. There is no bpf, no eslogger and no root here, so the kernel bar is not available and is not claimed. ONE MORE READING on the same run, and it is the one this feature is arranged around. subject.cell: execution-plane=daemon · data-shape=a server whose health block is out of range in two keys
subject.note: A configured value the router will not take is REFUSED and reported, never clamped in silence. The lane's `r27-refused` server writes `tripAfter: 1` and `probeIntervalMs: 10`; the report carries both refusals with the value as written, the floor that rejected it, and a `scope` saying which block to fix, while `policy` reports the value actually in force. The `tripAfter` floor of 2 is this item's own version of the vacuity rule: with a threshold of 1 the first failure trips, `degraded` is unreachable, and the guarantee that an upstream is flagged degraded before it is tripped would hold only because nothing can enter the state it names. Refusing rather than clamping is the other half — a clamp reports 2 over a file that says 1, and the operator's next reading of their own file disagrees with the router for a reason neither can see.

subject.cell: execution-plane=daemon · data-shape=the same credential quoted back inside a router log line
subject.note: Layer 2, and the channel layer 1 structurally cannot reach. A credential arrives in a diagnostics export by more routes than the field it was configured in: an upstream that rejects a call and quotes the token back in its error text, a command line carrying `--token=`, a log line somebody wrote by hand. Those are strings the bundle has every reason to carry, and the only thing distinguishing the secret inside one is its VALUE. The scrub runs over the value tree ONCE, as the last step, so every string goes through it by construction rather than because each site remembered to call it — the property that survives the next person adding a section. Object keys are scrubbed as well as values. `occurrencesRemoved` is asserted non-zero, because a scrubber that ran and a scrubber that had something to do read as the same clean bundle and only one of them is evidence.

subject.cell: execution-plane=daemon · data-shape=an env value of three characters beside a log line containing it
subject.note: The needle floor, which is a correctness rule rather than a performance one. An env value of `1`, `true` or `dev` used as a scrub needle deletes every occurrence of that text from every log line in the bundle — the timestamps, the ports, the word `device`. The result READS as thorough redaction and is a corrupted document, and nobody looking at it can tell which. So a value below 8 characters is not used as a needle, is named in `unscrubbable` with the reason, and is still withheld by layer 1. The assertion that bites is the positive one: `dev-server on port 3000` must survive intact. BOTH out-of-family reviewers proposed an entropy filter on top of the floor, to stop a value like `production` scrubbing that word out of the logs. Declined, and the reason is the direction of the error: an over-redaction announces itself in place as `<redacted:MODE>` and a reader can see exactly what happened; an under-redaction is silent. A second exclusion tuned by entropy moves values from the first class to the second on a judgement nobody can audit from the bundle.

subject.cell: execution-plane=daemon · data-shape=the same credential percent-encoded and base64-encoded in log lines
subject.note: A secret does not always reach a log line as itself. It reaches it percent-encoded when it travelled in a URL and base64-encoded when it travelled in a `Basic` credential, and a scrubber that knows only the literal reports a clean bundle over both. Both out-of-family lanes raised this independently and it is the one addition of theirs taken wholesale. JSON escaping is DELIBERATELY NOT a third variant, and that is where this departs from both reviews. They are right that a token containing a quote appears in the SERIALISED document as `\"` and would survive a needle search over the finished bytes. The scrub does not search the finished bytes: it walks the value tree before serialisation, where every string is still unescaped. Scrubbing earlier removes the whole class rather than enumerating its members.

subject.note: DEF-084, the live rung. The lane actuates Discover through the plane, waits for the registry search to publish rows, scopes a ListItem sweep to each band by its automation id and reads every row's Name and AutomationId out of process. THE ASSERTION IS NOT "the name is non-empty": the defect published "MCPRouter.Shell.Views.DiscoverRow" for every row, which is non-empty, so a presence check would have passed on it. What is required is that no name is the type name and that the names are pairwise distinct within the band - the two properties that actually failed. Read 2026-09-02: 60 rows in each band, 60 distinct names, 60 distinct ids, none of them the type name. The command the lane ran is scripts/windows/uia/run-shell-lane.ps1; `actuates` carries the two band containers the surface declares, which is what control-census.py counts. WHAT THIS DOES NOT SETTLE: that the sentence is a good one to hear read aloud, and that an id is unique across BOTH bands - an entry in both carries the same id in each.

subject.detail: Found by auditing the other reads once DEF-009 was fixed, not by a failing test — so no case watched it fail and it earns no arming credit. `usageSummary()` returned the recorded four-server summary for every scenario, and it is the only call CleanupBoardModel makes. Under `.empty` the Cleanup board therefore offered four never-used servers to cull on a router with nothing declared. Fixed the same way as DEF-009: `.empty` returns no servers and keeps `since` from the recording, because a router that has been counting since a moment and has nothing to report is a different statement from one with no window at all. Audit result for the record: of the seventeen methods, seven do not branch on the scenario and six of those are writes, where a read-scenario legitimately does not apply and guardFailure() already covers offline/unauthorized/error. The seventh is `server(named:)`, which answers about a server the caller has already named and has no meaningful empty form; no surface calls it.
subject.title: the fixture client's usageSummary ignored the scenario, so Cleanup had no empty state

The built board draws no control there at all. Not an honesty guardrail: the router can reset its call history, and the Cleanup board carries 'Reset call history', so the capability exists and only this entry point is missing. subject.text: Closed 20 Aug 2026, on the owner's decision that `design/mocks/prototype.html` remains the design of record for the Mac console. `prototype.html:716` puts `Reset history…` in the Activity header's right slot, OUTSIDE the rows conditional, so the design specifies it in the empty state as much as the populated one — which is where somebody actually reaches for it. The built board drew no control there at all, and no honesty guardrail explained the absence: the router can reset its call history and the Cleanup board already carries the same act, so the capability existed and only this entry point was missing. Found by the witness pass on SURF-003 and independently by the control differential (designControls=1 buildControls=0 for this board). FIXED by giving `ActivityModel` a `sheet` and a `resetHistory()` against the same `POST /usage/reset` the Cleanup board uses, and `ActivityBoard.header` a trailing `Button(CleanupPresentation.resetLabel)` disabled until `records` exists — offering it before the router has answered would let a click discard a history nobody has seen. The dialog is `ActivityResetHistorySheet`, whose every string is `CleanupPresentation`'s by call and never by copy, because two boards offering one irreversible act must not describe it two ways (DESIGN.md §6). It passes `window: nil`, which is a fact rather than a gap: Cleanup judges over a span and Activity holds a rolling feed, so the sentence reads "recorded so far". GUARDED by `ActivityResetEntryPointTests`, four assertions, all armed 20 Aug 2026. The header assertion was watched to fail for real before the fix landed — an earlier script aborted before writing the header change, and the test reported `the header draws no reset action` against the tree that had it missing. Removing `_ = try await client.resetUsage()` was rejected as an arm because it fails to compile (typed throws), which is a red for the wrong reason; duplicating the call instead reads `confirming the dialog sent 2 resets`.
subject.title: Activity's 'Reset history…' is specified and never drawn

subject.text: CAUSE FOUND AND FIXED 20 Aug 2026; this record replaces one that said the cause was unknown and named machine saturation as a candidate. The candidate was wrong. The process-wide accessibility engine was OFF, so SwiftUI's `_UIHostingView` built its accessibility container and vended an EMPTY element array — `accessibilityElements == []`, not nil — and every label assertion in the target read empty and reported its own honest verdict, `nothing was measured, so this proved nothing`. That is indistinguishable, from inside the suite, from a product that renders no copy. A probe settled it: calling `_AXSSetAutomationEnabled(true)` took the same hosted view's published element count from 0 to 1. THE ENGINE HAD BEEN ON BY ACCIDENT — something else on this machine had switched it on — which is why this suite was green for months while depending on ambient host state no file in this repo controls, and why it went red with no change to the branch. THREE CHANGES ARE THE FIX, and the third was found only because the first two were not enough. (1) `PhoneSurfaceTests` resolves `_AXSSetAutomationEnabled` out of `/usr/lib/libAccessibility.dylib` (falling back to `AccessibilityUtilities.framework`) via dlopen/dlsym and calls it once per process, before the first `host()`. (2) The walker reads `accessibilityElements` first, because SwiftUI publishes through the array and leaves `accessibilityElementCount()` at 0 — measured on iOS 26.5, where one hosted `Text` reported `accessibilityElements.count == 1` and `accessibilityElementCount() == 0` in the same breath, so reading only the indexed API walked past every element SwiftUI had. Those two took `make test-ios` from 52 failures to 0 — and then `make all`, run immediately afterwards on the same device, came back with 39. (3) THE STATE IS DEVICE-SCOPED AND THE CALL LANDS ON THE NEXT PROCESS, NOT THIS ONE. On a device left in the disabled state, the run that re-enables it fails a DETERMINISTIC set of 15 test cases — identical set, measured three times, verified with `comm` in both directions — and the run after it, with no change to anything, is clean. The 15 are exactly the cases that host a `ScrollView`; the tests that pass alongside them are geometry, counts and negative assertions, all of which an empty tree satisfies, so the green half of that run was vacuous too. `test-ios` therefore runs a throwaway single-test process before the graded one and discards its exit code. MEASURED END TO END: three consecutive runs with the call mutated to `(false)` drive `MCPRouter-Unit` into the disabled state (54 failures each, the whole suite red, which is correct for a dead engine); the very next `make test-ios`, with the warm-up in the recipe, is 36 tests and 0 failures in 1.4s. THE INSTRUMENT CHECK IS ITSELF INSTRUMENTED. `testTheAccessibilityEngineCanBeSwitchedOn` blocks on a probe that hosts `ScrollView { Text }` and reads it back through the same walk every other assertion uses, with a 20s deadline. Two narrower probes were built first and both were wrong in opposite directions, which is why the shape is stated rather than assumed: a bare `Text` read either way reports the engine live at t=0 of a run in which 15 cases went on to read empty, and a `ScrollView` read through the accessibility-container path alone reports the engine dead on a device where all 35 other tests pass. A probe that answers differently from the thing it stands for answers a different question. On a dead engine the deadline fires and the case fails with `no hosted Text published a label within 20s`, measured. ARMED THREE WAYS. (a) Renaming the symbol to `_AXSSetAutomationEnabledXXX` on a device whose engine is already live fails exactly one test — the instrument check — and leaves the other 35 green, which is correct for that arm and proves only the resolution assertion. (b) With the call mutated to `(false)`, the first run on `MCPRouter-Arm`, a device created for the arm, recorded 53 failures across 36 tests: that is what proves the other 35 depend on the engine. (c) The first run ever taken on `MCPRouter-Arm2`, a device whose engine had never been live, is 36 tests and 0 failures, so a fresh device needs no warm-up and only an explicitly disabled one does. Both arm devices were deleted afterwards; `make test-ios IOS_UNIT_DEVICE=<name>` recreates either. TWO HARDENING CHANGES from the investigation are kept and neither is the fix: `test-ios` creates and owns `MCPRouter-Unit` instead of sorting booted devices first — the exact picker DEF-020 condemned, still live in this recipe — and the walk retains every element it visits so `ObjectIdentifier` is unique among live objects as its use assumes. A third, waiting on a product surface's tree over a two-second deadline, was written, measured to change nothing, and removed: it cost 130 seconds a run and bought no measurement. The wait that IS kept differs from it in the one way that matters — it waits on a probe whose answer is known, so a timeout is a fact about the instrument rather than about the view. THE DEPENDENCY IS ON A PRIVATE SYMBOL, in the test target only, never linked into the app; the instrument check fails loudly if a future runtime renames it, so this target goes red rather than quietly empty. Carried as CASE-0126.
subject.title: the iOS unit lane read an empty accessibility tree because the engine was off

subject.text: Measured 20 Aug 2026. `make test` failed with 4 issues at a one-minute load average of ~700 and passed all 1473 tests in 179 suites at load 46, on the same source, minutes apart. The four were `ActivityReconnectTests` (`a reconnect over a feed that stays live releases its guard`), `DiscoverBoardTests` (`client.searchQueries.count` reading 1 where the baseline said 2), and `SettingsAndMenuBarTests` twice (`model.trackerState` still nil). An earlier run at the same load failed only the first, so the set was not stable either — which is what separated this from a product defect. A suite that reports a defect the product does not have is the failure this campaign has already paid for once, in DEF-029, where a dead instrument read as a dead product for ten consecutive runs. CLOSED by making each wait a condition rather than a deadline, at three sites: 1. `ShellTestSupport.waitUntil` — ceiling 5s → 30s. It returns the moment the condition holds, so a passing test pays nothing for the larger bound; the bound exists only so a condition that never arrives fails instead of hanging. Five seconds was inside the scheduling noise of a contended host, which is the whole finding. 2. `ActivityReconnectTests.completes` — 2s → 30s, same argument. The defect it bounds is a call that *never* returns, so it exhausts any budget and a generous one costs only the time a genuine hang takes to report. 3. `DiscoverBoardTests.searchIsDebounced` — a fixed sleep replaced by two waits, because the claim has two halves and one sleep proved neither on a slow host. First a bounded wait for the debounce to fire at all; then a full debounce window of quiet with the count still at one, which is what rules out one request per keystroke. The second is a real quiet period rather than a deadline, so load cannot shorten it into a false pass — the wait on its own is satisfied by the *first* request and would pass against exactly the defect this test exists to catch. Armed 20 Aug 2026, all three, each watched to fail with its own message: `waitUntil` at `.seconds(0)` reads `no poll ran at all`, `the poll died with the scene that started it` and `five keystrokes issued 0 requests`; `completes` at `.milliseconds(1)` reads `reconnect did not return while the feed stayed live`; and a `queryChanged()` inserted inside the quiet period reads `a later request arrived: five keystrokes issued 2 requests in total`. The original trigger is not reproducible on demand from here — the load came from another project's Rust test binary, two node processes and `lsdiagnose` — so the fix is proven by the arms rather than by reproducing the contention.
subject.title: four async package tests asserted on a deadline the machine could miss

subject.text: Measured 20 Aug 2026 on two different worktrees the same afternoon. A fresh `git worktree` has no `node_modules` and no `dist`; `parity-selftest` is the last target `make all` runs, and its own environment check therefore fires only after lint, both builds, 1483 package tests, the iOS lane and the on-glass lane have all passed. Both runs came back `exit=2` on a tree where nothing was wrong with the code — roughly forty minutes each, twice. It is a lane defect rather than a product one, and the shape is familiar: the gate was honest (it said `the MCP SDK is not installed. Run npm install.` rather than skipping) and it was honest at the wrong moment. A check that can only fail on the environment belongs where the environment is checked. CLOSED by moving both checks into the `tools` target, which `all` runs first: `node_modules` must exist, and `dist/index.js` must exist because without it `parity-lane-selftest` SKIPS, and a skip is not a pass. Each names the command that fixes it. Armed 20 Aug 2026 in a bare directory holding nothing but the Makefile: with no `node_modules` it exits 1 naming `npm install && npm run build`, and with `node_modules` present but no `dist` it exits 1 naming `npm run build` and saying why a skip is not a pass. Costs a millisecond on a tree that has both.
subject.title: the whole-repo gate discovered a missing environment forty minutes in, twice

subject.detail: CLOSED 2026-08-20. The cause was two independent framing errors, both invisible because the gate could not run to report them. The design references came from `obscura fetch --screenshot`, which captures at a fixed 1280x720 dpr1 viewport with no viewport flag, so every reference was clipped rather than merely small - the bottom row of one carried 578 non-background pixels of 640 sampled. And the build captures were 980x620 against the design's 1156x680 window, aspect 1.581 against 1.700, which no crop reconciles. Fixed by rasterising the design through CDP with `Emulation.setDeviceMetricsOverride` at 1280x900 dpr2 (readback asserted `[1280, 900, 2]` before any capture), re-photographing the eight Mac boards at the design's own 1156x680 with a setframe readback guard, and cropping both halves to the window's own content box. prescan goes from framingComparable 0/16 to 8/8, aspectRatioOfRatios 1.0 and scaleRatio 1.0 on every pair (evidence/runs/prescan-fidelity.json). Eight verdicts written: 2 pass, 5 fail, 1 unoracled.
subject.text: The campaign names design-review and be-my-witness as gates and has never run either, and the reason was never measured — it read as a skip. It is not. be-my-witness 0.2.0's deterministic prescan over all 16 pairs that hold both halves reports isEvidence 16/16, settled 16/16, framingComparable 0/16, proceed 0/16. Not a dead predicate: the scale ratios differ per lane (0.466x on the SURF-001 sidebar crop, 1.64x on the Mac boards, 0.942x on the phone) rather than returning a constant. Every reference was rasterised at a 1280x720 dpr-1 viewport, inside which prototype.html draws a fixed artboard rather than filling the frame, so rendering larger pads rather than enlarges. Re-rendering the reference does not fix it either: the design's Mac window is #win at 1156x680, aspect 1.700, and the build's is 980x620, aspect 1.581. The build half crops exactly — scale=(2096-1376)/(980-620)=2.0, margin=(2096-980*2)/2=68, content rect (68,68,1960,1240), precisely 2x the AX frame — but no crop reconciles two different window shapes. What would make them comparable is re-capturing the app at the design's window size, which means driving the app again and photographing a window shape the product does not use. Left unresolved deliberately: the structural and lexical differential in evidence/differential.md is the comparison that is valid here, and it ran.
