subject.cell: execution-plane=daemon · data-shape=one stdio upstream declared
subject.note: The router spawning a child process, seen by two parties that are not the router. `bin/witness-effects.sh` runs `MCPRouterCLI index --force` against a scratch home holding one stdio server, and records the pid the shell launched (`$!`) beside the pid the CHILD reports for its own parent through `getppid()`. The child writes that into a file whose path arrives in its environment and which the router never reads back, so neither record passes through the product. They agree: shell launched 30913, child 30920 names 30913. A ps(1) sample runs alongside and usually misses, because the index verb spawns, handshakes and exits inside one scheduling quantum; two earlier versions of this witness depended on ps alone and could report only that the child had A parent, not whose child it was. Armed: against a config declaring no servers the same recorder reports count=0, and against the populated one count=1 with the parents agreeing.

The half of REQ-028 the app's own menu will answer for. `scripts/acceptance/menu-reason-plane.sh` launches the Debug build with `open -g`, never activates it, and reads its real menu bar off the accessibility plane: 220 menu items, 11 of them carrying a reason ShellMenuReasons wrote, and every sentence one MenuCommandAvailability declares — the vocabulary is derived from the source file at run time rather than copied, so the two cannot drift. WHAT THIS DOES NOT CLAIM: it does not read the badge. SwiftUI does not publish an NSMenuItem's badge to this plane and this app's menu bar is SwiftUI's, which the same lane asserts and `menu-badge-lane.sh` measured first on a fixture. The badge's CONTENT follows from the reason through MenuReasonBadgePairingTests, which proves one reason never appears beside two badges; the badge as DRAWN is CASE-0197 and is unoracled. Armed: `menu-reason-plane-selftest.sh` hands each of the five assertions a doctored dump and requires it to fire, then requires none of them to fire on the dump today's platform produces.

subject.cell: execution-plane=daemon · data-shape=one stdio upstream that answers and one whose command does not exist
subject.note: The health probe becoming a real child process, seen by two parties that are not the router. `bin/witness-health-probe.sh` drives `POST /servers/witness-fixture/probe` over the DAEMON's own socket — a production entry point, not the prober called from a test — and records the pid the shell launched beside the pid the child reports for its own parent. They agree: the shell launched the daemon as one pid, the child names that same pid, and ps(1) shows the row. The route reported the upstream healthy in the same breath, so the reading and the effect agree rather than one standing in for the other. THE LANE IS THE PORTABLE FLOOR AND SAYS SO: a real spawned process writing a sentinel the witness then reads. There is no bpf, no eslogger and no root here, so the kernel bar is not available and is not claimed. ONE MORE READING on the same run, and it is the one this feature is arranged around. Before any probe the report says every upstream is `unprobed` and the process table holds no fixture child — REQ-001 is that at rest there are zero child processes, and a health check that cold-started every server would invert it.

subject.cell: execution-plane=daemon · data-shape=a server whose health block is out of range in two keys
subject.note: A configured value the router will not take is REFUSED and reported, never clamped in silence. The lane's `r27-refused` server writes `tripAfter: 1` and `probeIntervalMs: 10`; the report carries both refusals with the value as written, the floor that rejected it, and a `scope` saying which block to fix, while `policy` reports the value actually in force. The `tripAfter` floor of 2 is this item's own version of the vacuity rule: with a threshold of 1 the first failure trips, `degraded` is unreachable, and the guarantee that an upstream is flagged degraded before it is tripped would hold only because nothing can enter the state it names. Refusing rather than clamping is the other half — a clamp reports 2 over a file that says 1, and the operator's next reading of their own file disagrees with the router for a reason neither can see.

subject.cell: execution-plane=daemon · data-shape=the same credential quoted back inside a router log line
subject.note: Layer 2, and the channel layer 1 structurally cannot reach. A credential arrives in a diagnostics export by more routes than the field it was configured in: an upstream that rejects a call and quotes the token back in its error text, a command line carrying `--token=`, a log line somebody wrote by hand. Those are strings the bundle has every reason to carry, and the only thing distinguishing the secret inside one is its VALUE. The scrub runs over the value tree ONCE, as the last step, so every string goes through it by construction rather than because each site remembered to call it — the property that survives the next person adding a section. Object keys are scrubbed as well as values. `occurrencesRemoved` is asserted non-zero, because a scrubber that ran and a scrubber that had something to do read as the same clean bundle and only one of them is evidence.

subject.cell: execution-plane=daemon · data-shape=an env value of three characters beside a log line containing it
subject.note: The needle floor, which is a correctness rule rather than a performance one. An env value of `1`, `true` or `dev` used as a scrub needle deletes every occurrence of that text from every log line in the bundle — the timestamps, the ports, the word `device`. The result READS as thorough redaction and is a corrupted document, and nobody looking at it can tell which. So a value below 8 characters is not used as a needle, is named in `unscrubbable` with the reason, and is still withheld by layer 1. The assertion that bites is the positive one: `dev-server on port 3000` must survive intact. BOTH out-of-family reviewers proposed an entropy filter on top of the floor, to stop a value like `production` scrubbing that word out of the logs. Declined, and the reason is the direction of the error: an over-redaction announces itself in place as `<redacted:MODE>` and a reader can see exactly what happened; an under-redaction is silent. A second exclusion tuned by entropy moves values from the first class to the second on a judgement nobody can audit from the bundle.

subject.cell: execution-plane=daemon · data-shape=the same credential percent-encoded and base64-encoded in log lines
subject.note: A secret does not always reach a log line as itself. It reaches it percent-encoded when it travelled in a URL and base64-encoded when it travelled in a `Basic` credential, and a scrubber that knows only the literal reports a clean bundle over both. Both out-of-family lanes raised this independently and it is the one addition of theirs taken wholesale. JSON escaping is DELIBERATELY NOT a third variant, and that is where this departs from both reviews. They are right that a token containing a quote appears in the SERIALISED document as `\"` and would survive a needle search over the finished bytes. The scrub does not search the finished bytes: it walks the value tree before serialisation, where every string is still unescaped. Scrubbing earlier removes the whole class rather than enumerating its members.

subject.cell: execution-plane=daemon · data-shape=an untokened GET against a router holding a planted secret
subject.note: The preview is a GET and GET is UNGATED in this router — `ControlHandler.gate` reads the token only for POST/DELETE/PATCH, matching the reference, recorded there as a ported defect rather than quietly fixed. So the preview is written to one rule: it discloses nothing `GET /servers` does not already disclose. Category names, counts, key names, and the redaction plan. The assertion that makes this a real constraint rather than a restatement of `no secret leaked` is the canary one: the preview must NOT contain the public log canary either. A preview carrying no secret is satisfied by a preview that carries the whole log with the secret scrubbed out; a preview carrying no log LINE is not.

subject.cell: execution-plane=daemon · data-shape=the bundle path asked three ways: untokened POST, GET, tokened POST
subject.note: The verb IS the gate, and it is not describing a mutation. The bundle changes nothing. It is a POST because stage 2 of `ControlHandler.handle` gates the token on POST/DELETE/PATCH only, so the verb is the only thing deciding whether this router hands its whole diagnostic corpus — log lines included — to any unauthenticated caller that can open the loopback port, which per `ControlToken` includes a web page the user merely visits. All three answers are pinned — 401 untokened, 405 on GET, 200 on a tokened POST — so a later tidy-up that makes the verb 'correct' goes red rather than silently opening the route. The 200 is asserted beside the other two so they read as refusals rather than as an absent route.

Does every committed piece of macos-glass evidence name the build it was taken from, and is that build the one this lane is being read against? `bin/glass-build-gate.py` binds each artifact to the git blob identity of the Mac app's own build inputs -- the set `scripts/acceptance/build-freshness.sh` compiles from, read out of that file rather than copied, so a Mac input added there and missed here fails as INPUT DRIFT instead of quietly narrowing every verdict below it. Blob ids are line-ending normalised, so the verdict is identical on macOS and on Windows for one commit; this row was produced on Windows. --- FAILING, and the finding is true: all 56 artifacts the lane cites are stale, in 7 capture groups spanning 20-29 Aug, and `app/Sources/MCPRouterKit`, `app/Sources/MCPRouterUI` and `app/Package.swift` have all moved since the newest of them. This is DEF-058 with an instrument on it. It goes green when a macOS host re-runs `bin/capture-mac-glass.sh`, and not before -- there is no edit to this repository that should turn it green.

Can every published glass capture be shown to have been written AT THE SHUTTER rather than afterwards? A manifest that post-dates its capture records what somebody believed, not what the channel did, so it is not lineage -- which is the finding `capture-lineage.py`'s RECONSTRUCTED pass raised against SURF-028 and which `bin/capture-manifest.py` closed on the derivation side. This is the ordering side: the gate requires each published row to carry `capturedAt`, `conditions.windowTitleReadback` and `conditions.cgWindowID`, none of which can be recovered after the fact, or an explicit `provenanceGap` saying that it cannot. WHAT IT DOES NOT PROVE, stated rather than folded in: it establishes that the row COULD only have been written by something standing at the shutter, not that it was. Only the capture channel writing its own row does that, which `bin/capture-mac-glass.sh` does and which no reader can verify from the artifact alone.

subject.detail: Found by auditing the other reads once DEF-009 was fixed, not by a failing test — so no case watched it fail and it earns no arming credit. `usageSummary()` returned the recorded four-server summary for every scenario, and it is the only call CleanupBoardModel makes. Under `.empty` the Cleanup board therefore offered four never-used servers to cull on a router with nothing declared. Fixed the same way as DEF-009: `.empty` returns no servers and keeps `since` from the recording, because a router that has been counting since a moment and has nothing to report is a different statement from one with no window at all. Audit result for the record: of the seventeen methods, seven do not branch on the scenario and six of those are writes, where a read-scenario legitimately does not apply and guardFailure() already covers offline/unauthorized/error. The seventh is `server(named:)`, which answers about a server the caller has already named and has no meaningful empty form; no surface calls it.
subject.title: the fixture client's usageSummary ignored the scenario, so Cleanup had no empty state

subject.detail: prototype.html:716 puts 'Reset history…' in the Activity header's right slot, outside the rows conditional, so the design specifies it in both the empty and the populated state. The built board draws no control there at all. Not an honesty guardrail: the router can reset its call history, and the Cleanup board carries 'Reset call history', so the capability exists and only this entry point is missing. Found by the witness pass on SURF-003 and independently by the control differential, which reports designControls=1 buildControls=0 for this board. Distinct from DEF-012, which records the rename of the same action on the board that does carry it.
subject.text: Closed 20 Aug 2026, on the owner's decision that `design/mocks/prototype.html` remains the design of record for the Mac console. `prototype.html:716` puts `Reset history…` in the Activity header's right slot, OUTSIDE the rows conditional, so the design specifies it in the empty state as much as the populated one — which is where somebody actually reaches for it. The built board drew no control there at all, and no honesty guardrail explained the absence: the router can reset its call history and the Cleanup board already carries the same act, so the capability existed and only this entry point was missing. Found by the witness pass on SURF-003 and independently by the control differential (designControls=1 buildControls=0 for this board). FIXED by giving `ActivityModel` a `sheet` and a `resetHistory()` against the same `POST /usage/reset` the Cleanup board uses, and `ActivityBoard.header` a trailing `Button(CleanupPresentation.resetLabel)` disabled until `records` exists — offering it before the router has answered would let a click discard a history nobody has seen. The dialog is `ActivityResetHistorySheet`, whose every string is `CleanupPresentation`'s by call and never by copy, because two boards offering one irreversible act must not describe it two ways (DESIGN.md §6). It passes `window: nil`, which is a fact rather than a gap: Cleanup judges over a span and Activity holds a rolling feed, so the sentence reads "recorded so far". GUARDED by `ActivityResetEntryPointTests`, four assertions, all armed 20 Aug 2026. The header assertion was watched to fail for real before the fix landed — an earlier script aborted before writing the header change, and the test reported `the header draws no reset action` against the tree that had it missing. Removing `_ = try await client.resetUsage()` was rejected as an arm because it fails to compile (typed throws), which is a red for the wrong reason; duplicating the call instead reads `confirming the dialog sent 2 resets`.
subject.title: Activity's 'Reset history…' is specified and never drawn

subject.text: CAUSE FOUND AND FIXED 20 Aug 2026; this record replaces one that said the cause was unknown and named machine saturation as a candidate. The candidate was wrong. The process-wide accessibility engine was OFF, so SwiftUI's `_UIHostingView` built its accessibility container and vended an EMPTY element array — `accessibilityElements == []`, not nil — and every label assertion in the target read empty and reported its own honest verdict, `nothing was measured, so this proved nothing`. That is indistinguishable, from inside the suite, from a product that renders no copy. A probe settled it: calling `_AXSSetAutomationEnabled(true)` took the same hosted view's published element count from 0 to 1. THE ENGINE HAD BEEN ON BY ACCIDENT — something else on this machine had switched it on — which is why this suite was green for months while depending on ambient host state no file in this repo controls, and why it went red with no change to the branch. THREE CHANGES ARE THE FIX, and the third was found only because the first two were not enough. (1) `PhoneSurfaceTests` resolves `_AXSSetAutomationEnabled` out of `/usr/lib/libAccessibility.dylib` (falling back to `AccessibilityUtilities.framework`) via dlopen/dlsym and calls it once per process, before the first `host()`. (2) The walker reads `accessibilityElements` first, because SwiftUI publishes through the array and leaves `accessibilityElementCount()` at 0 — measured on iOS 26.5, where one hosted `Text` reported `accessibilityElements.count == 1` and `accessibilityElementCount() == 0` in the same breath, so reading only the indexed API walked past every element SwiftUI had. Those two took `make test-ios` from 52 failures to 0 — and then `make all`, run immediately afterwards on the same device, came back with 39. (3) THE STATE IS DEVICE-SCOPED AND THE CALL LANDS ON THE NEXT PROCESS, NOT THIS ONE. On a device left in the disabled state, the run that re-enables it fails a DETERMINISTIC set of 15 test cases — identical set, measured three times, verified with `comm` in both directions — and the run after it, with no change to anything, is clean. The 15 are exactly the cases that host a `ScrollView`; the tests that pass alongside them are geometry, counts and negative assertions, all of which an empty tree satisfies, so the green half of that run was vacuous too. `test-ios` therefore runs a throwaway single-test process before the graded one and discards its exit code. MEASURED END TO END: three consecutive runs with the call mutated to `(false)` drive `MCPRouter-Unit` into the disabled state (54 failures each, the whole suite red, which is correct for a dead engine); the very next `make test-ios`, with the warm-up in the recipe, is 36 tests and 0 failures in 1.4s. THE INSTRUMENT CHECK IS ITSELF INSTRUMENTED. `testTheAccessibilityEngineCanBeSwitchedOn` blocks on a probe that hosts `ScrollView { Text }` and reads it back through the same walk every other assertion uses, with a 20s deadline. Two narrower probes were built first and both were wrong in opposite directions, which is why the shape is stated rather than assumed: a bare `Text` read either way reports the engine live at t=0 of a run in which 15 cases went on to read empty, and a `ScrollView` read through the accessibility-container path alone reports the engine dead on a device where all 35 other tests pass. A probe that answers differently from the thing it stands for answers a different question. On a dead engine the deadline fires and the case fails with `no hosted Text published a label within 20s`, measured. ARMED THREE WAYS. (a) Renaming the symbol to `_AXSSetAutomationEnabledXXX` on a device whose engine is already live fails exactly one test — the instrument check — and leaves the other 35 green, which is correct for that arm and proves only the resolution assertion. (b) With the call mutated to `(false)`, the first run on `MCPRouter-Arm`, a device created for the arm, recorded 53 failures across 36 tests: that is what proves the other 35 depend on the engine. (c) The first run ever taken on `MCPRouter-Arm2`, a device whose engine had never been live, is 36 tests and 0 failures, so a fresh device needs no warm-up and only an explicitly disabled one does. Both arm devices were deleted afterwards; `make test-ios IOS_UNIT_DEVICE=<name>` recreates either. TWO HARDENING CHANGES from the investigation are kept and neither is the fix: `test-ios` creates and owns `MCPRouter-Unit` instead of sorting booted devices first — the exact picker DEF-020 condemned, still live in this recipe — and the walk retains every element it visits so `ObjectIdentifier` is unique among live objects as its use assumes. A third, waiting on a product surface's tree over a two-second deadline, was written, measured to change nothing, and removed: it cost 130 seconds a run and bought no measurement. The wait that IS kept differs from it in the one way that matters — it waits on a probe whose answer is known, so a timeout is a fact about the instrument rather than about the view. THE DEPENDENCY IS ON A PRIVATE SYMBOL, in the test target only, never linked into the app; the instrument check fails loudly if a future runtime renames it, so this target goes red rather than quietly empty. Carried as CASE-0126.
subject.title: the iOS unit lane read an empty accessibility tree because the engine was off

subject.text: Measured 20 Aug 2026. `make test` failed with 4 issues at a one-minute load average of ~700 and passed all 1473 tests in 179 suites at load 46, on the same source, minutes apart. The four were `ActivityReconnectTests` (`a reconnect over a feed that stays live releases its guard`), `DiscoverBoardTests` (`client.searchQueries.count` reading 1 where the baseline said 2), and `SettingsAndMenuBarTests` twice (`model.trackerState` still nil). An earlier run at the same load failed only the first, so the set was not stable either — which is what separated this from a product defect. A suite that reports a defect the product does not have is the failure this campaign has already paid for once, in DEF-029, where a dead instrument read as a dead product for ten consecutive runs. CLOSED by making each wait a condition rather than a deadline, at three sites: 1. `ShellTestSupport.waitUntil` — ceiling 5s → 30s. It returns the moment the condition holds, so a passing test pays nothing for the larger bound; the bound exists only so a condition that never arrives fails instead of hanging. Five seconds was inside the scheduling noise of a contended host, which is the whole finding. 2. `ActivityReconnectTests.completes` — 2s → 30s, same argument. The defect it bounds is a call that *never* returns, so it exhausts any budget and a generous one costs only the time a genuine hang takes to report. 3. `DiscoverBoardTests.searchIsDebounced` — a fixed sleep replaced by two waits, because the claim has two halves and one sleep proved neither on a slow host. First a bounded wait for the debounce to fire at all; then a full debounce window of quiet with the count still at one, which is what rules out one request per keystroke. The second is a real quiet period rather than a deadline, so load cannot shorten it into a false pass — the wait on its own is satisfied by the *first* request and would pass against exactly the defect this test exists to catch. Armed 20 Aug 2026, all three, each watched to fail with its own message: `waitUntil` at `.seconds(0)` reads `no poll ran at all`, `the poll died with the scene that started it` and `five keystrokes issued 0 requests`; `completes` at `.milliseconds(1)` reads `reconnect did not return while the feed stayed live`; and a `queryChanged()` inserted inside the quiet period reads `a later request arrived: five keystrokes issued 2 requests in total`. The original trigger is not reproducible on demand from here — the load came from another project's Rust test binary, two node processes and `lsdiagnose` — so the fix is proven by the arms rather than by reproducing the contention.
subject.title: four async package tests asserted on a deadline the machine could miss

subject.text: Measured 20 Aug 2026 on two different worktrees the same afternoon. A fresh `git worktree` has no `node_modules` and no `dist`; `parity-selftest` is the last target `make all` runs, and its own environment check therefore fires only after lint, both builds, 1483 package tests, the iOS lane and the on-glass lane have all passed. Both runs came back `exit=2` on a tree where nothing was wrong with the code — roughly forty minutes each, twice. It is a lane defect rather than a product one, and the shape is familiar: the gate was honest (it said `the MCP SDK is not installed. Run npm install.` rather than skipping) and it was honest at the wrong moment. A check that can only fail on the environment belongs where the environment is checked. CLOSED by moving both checks into the `tools` target, which `all` runs first: `node_modules` must exist, and `dist/index.js` must exist because without it `parity-lane-selftest` SKIPS, and a skip is not a pass. Each names the command that fixes it. Armed 20 Aug 2026 in a bare directory holding nothing but the Makefile: with no `node_modules` it exits 1 naming `npm install && npm run build`, and with `node_modules` present but no `dist` it exits 1 naming `npm run build` and saying why a skip is not a pass. Costs a millisecond on a tree that has both.
subject.title: the whole-repo gate discovered a missing environment forty minutes in, twice

subject.detail: CLOSED 2026-08-20. The cause was two independent framing errors, both invisible because the gate could not run to report them. The design references came from `obscura fetch --screenshot`, which captures at a fixed 1280x720 dpr1 viewport with no viewport flag, so every reference was clipped rather than merely small - the bottom row of one carried 578 non-background pixels of 640 sampled. And the build captures were 980x620 against the design's 1156x680 window, aspect 1.581 against 1.700, which no crop reconciles. Fixed by rasterising the design through CDP with `Emulation.setDeviceMetricsOverride` at 1280x900 dpr2 (readback asserted `[1280, 900, 2]` before any capture), re-photographing the eight Mac boards at the design's own 1156x680 with a setframe readback guard, and cropping both halves to the window's own content box. prescan goes from framingComparable 0/16 to 8/8, aspectRatioOfRatios 1.0 and scaleRatio 1.0 on every pair (evidence/runs/prescan-fidelity.json). Eight verdicts written: 2 pass, 5 fail, 1 unoracled.
subject.text: The campaign names design-review and be-my-witness as gates and has never run either, and the reason was never measured — it read as a skip. It is not. be-my-witness 0.2.0's deterministic prescan over all 16 pairs that hold both halves reports isEvidence 16/16, settled 16/16, framingComparable 0/16, proceed 0/16. Not a dead predicate: the scale ratios differ per lane (0.466x on the SURF-001 sidebar crop, 1.64x on the Mac boards, 0.942x on the phone) rather than returning a constant. Every reference was rasterised at a 1280x720 dpr-1 viewport, inside which prototype.html draws a fixed artboard rather than filling the frame, so rendering larger pads rather than enlarges. Re-rendering the reference does not fix it either: the design's Mac window is #win at 1156x680, aspect 1.700, and the build's is 980x620, aspect 1.581. The build half crops exactly — scale=(2096-1376)/(980-620)=2.0, margin=(2096-980*2)/2=68, content rect (68,68,1960,1240), precisely 2x the AX frame — but no crop reconciles two different window shapes. What would make them comparable is re-capturing the app at the design's window size, which means driving the app again and photographing a window shape the product does not use. Left unresolved deliberately: the structural and lexical differential in evidence/differential.md is the comparison that is valid here, and it ran.
subject.title: the rendered-quality gate has never been able to run, and nothing said why

subject.detail: STILL PRESENT in 0.9.2, re-measured 21 Aug 2026 and the gap widened by one. witness-worklist.py reports `pairs=20 judgeable=17 WITHOUT a reference=3` and a comparable fraction of 85%, while capture-lineage.py --gate on the same registry reports `published captures: 16` and `JUDGED 16 of 16 judgeable (100%)`. Two gates in one skill version disagree about the judgeable denominator, 17 against 16, and neither names the other's population. CAUSE PINNED 21 Aug 2026. The disagreeing member is SURF-009, the Mac menu-bar popover, and it is the only one: witness-worklist's judgeable set and capture-lineage's judged set are identical apart from it. SURF-009 has a rendered design of record on disk (evidence/shots/mock/SURF-009.png), which is the sole condition witness-worklist tests, so it counts as the 17th judgeable pair. It has NO build capture at all — the popover cannot be opened without activating MCPRouter, which this campaign never does — so it never enters capture-lineage's population, which is built from published captures. capture-lineage therefore reports 'JUDGED 16 of 16 judgeable (100%)' on a registry holding 17 judgeable surfaces. That is the defect's whole shape, and it is the campaign's own first failure mode occurring INSIDE a gate written to prevent it: a denominator built from what was captured rather than from what was enumerated reads 100% precisely when a surface was never photographed. The direction is the dangerous one — an uncaptured surface raises the percentage instead of lowering it. Nothing is concealed in this campaign's own record: SURF-009 carries a shotNote naming the constraint, its three cases (CASE-0004, CASE-0006, CASE-0109) are n/a with the reason, and evidence/shots/pairs.json carries shot:null. The defect is that a reader of the gate line alone would not know to look for any of it. Remains open-detector: the fix is in the skill's scripts, which are not edited from this repo.
subject.note: DETECTOR DEFECT, recorded so its number is not published as a product finding. `witness-worklist.py:90` is `judgeable = [p for p in pairs if p.get("reference")]` -- it tests the reference half and never the shot half. SURF-009 (Mac menu-bar popover) has `shot: null` and an explicit `reason: build half uncaptured` in pairs.json, and is still counted, so the script reported `pairs=20 judgeable=17 comparable fraction: 85%` where the honest figure is 16 of 20, 80%. The script already defends the mirror-image failure and its own comment says why: a campaign reported 20 judgeable pairs whose references were all unrendered .html paths, and it now demotes those to unjudgeable with a named reason. The shot side has no equivalent test. Consequence here is one point of over-report and no false verdict, because capture-lineage.py computes judgeable from captures that exist and reported JUDGED 16 of 16 -- the two gates disagree by exactly this surface, and the disagreement is what found it. A campaign relying on the worklist alone would carry an uncompared surface inside a comparable fraction. Filed against the skill's script rather than this repo, so it is not fixed here.
subject.text: witness-worklist.py counts a pair as judgeable on the reference alone, so a surface with no build capture inflates the comparable fraction.

The 3 that do appear are there by accident of prose: DEF-001 in two failing case notes and one passing one, DEF-033 and DEF-049 each inside a single PASSING case's note, rendered by the per-case table rather than by the Defects section. This is the skill's own first-named failure mode -- covering a subset and reporting it as the whole -- arriving in its publisher: the gated half of the campaign is sound and the ungated half is the half people look at. subject.detail: Measured 2026-08-21, test-campaign 0.9.2. `ledger.md`'s header line reads `80 cases` and `73 pass · 3 fail · 0 skip · 4 n/a`; its table carries 72 rows. The eight absent cases are CASE-0145, 0146, 0147, 0148 (lane router-daemon) and CASE-0151, 0152, 0153, 0154 (lane swiftui). All eight pass. MECHANISM, exact. The writer at campaign.py:1218-1241 buckets every case with `by_surface.setdefault(c.get('surface', '—'), [])`, so a case whose `surface` is absent lands under the literal key `'—'`. It then emits rows with `for s in inventory['surface']: for c in by_surface.get(s['id'], [])`. `'—'` is not a surface id, so that bucket is never visited and its contents are never printed. Nothing warns; the count in the header comes from a different code path than the rows beneath it, which is why the two disagree without either being flagged. WHAT IS LOST. CASE-0145 through CASE-0148 are this campaign's four `effect-witness` cases — the rung that required building a recorder outside the product, and the most expensive evidence in the run. They are absent from the ledger entirely. A reader of ledger.md cannot learn that the campaign has an effect-witness rung at all. DIRECTION. The eight dropped are all passes, so the table under-states the work rather than over-stating it. That makes it the safer direction, and it does not make it safe: a reader counting 72 rows against a stated 80 meets an unexplained gap of exactly the kind this campaign is written to make impossible, and the campaign's own rule is that every sweep prints its denominator. SCOPE. Ledger-specific. evidence.html renders all eight (5 to 11 references each, measured by grep), so the HTML page is correct and only the markdown artifact is affected. Distinct from DEF-052, which is about the defect registry being absent from BOTH artifacts; this one is about cases, in one artifact, via a different mechanism. NOT FIXED FROM HERE: campaign.py lives in the installed skill cache, not this repo.
subject.title: campaign.py's ledger writer prints only cases filed under a surface, silently dropping 8 of 80 — including all four effect-witness cases

subject.detail: Measured 2026-08-21. `.gitmodules` vendors `.claude/plugins/fledgeling-plugins` at `main`, and `planning/features-to-triage/LEDGER.md`'s allocation notes state the reason: 'a runner reads mockup-fidelity, mac-craft, design-craft and ux-craft at a repo-relative path rather than depending on the machine.' For test-campaign that is not what happens. The submodule (HEAD baaf79a, branch main, clean) carries `plugins/test-campaign` at version 0.5.0, whose `skills/test-campaign/scripts` holds five files: attach-shots.py, campaign.py, evidence-page.py, strict-check.py, witness-worklist.py. It has no `vacuity-check.py` and no `capture-lineage.py`; `grep effect-witness strict-check.py` returns nothing and `grep -c blindVocabulary vacuity-check.py` cannot run because the file is absent. Every gate this campaign reports ran from `~/.claude/plugins/cache/fledgeling-plugins/test-campaign/0.9.2/`, on the machine. The vacuity census, the effect-witness rung, the blind-mutation pass, the capture-lineage ratchet and the strict score of 65 all come from code the submodule does not contain, four minor versions ahead of it. CONSEQUENCE FOR THE PIPELINE, and it is the reason this is filed rather than noted: DEF-051, DEF-052, DEF-054, DEF-055 and DEF-056 are defects in 0.9.2's scripts. None of that code is in this repo at any path, so no ship-feature runner working in an mcp-router worktree can fix them. They are upstream work in github.com/fledgeling-co/fledgeling-plugins, and closing them requires a change pushed to that repo plus a submodule bump here — a different repo and an outward-facing action. Separately, a fresh clone that follows the documented `git submodule update --init --recursive` gets 0.5.0 and would reproduce none of this campaign's numbers. Not fixed here: which version the submodule should track, and whether the campaign should run from it rather than the cache, is the owner's call.

subject.text: Found while building R22's redactor, filed rather than fixed. `Describe.row` emits `command` and `args` RAW, and `ControlHandler.gate` reads the token only for POST/DELETE/PATCH, so the complete command line of every stdio upstream is readable by anything that can open the loopback port. The same function is careful in the adjacent case — it emits `envKeys` and `headerKeys` and never a value, with B10's reasoning attached — so argv is the one credential-carrying position on that route that is published whole. It matters because argv IS a credential channel: `--token=`, `--api-key=` and a connection string with an inline password are ordinary MCP server invocations, and R22 scrubs args for exactly that reason. The exposure predates R22 and is not made worse by it: the bundle's args go through the value scrub, and this route's do not. NOT FIXED HERE, and the reason is a parity decision rather than effort. `GET /servers` is reference-diffed — `control-servers-get` in planning/parity/surface.tsv, verdict `proven` — so redacting args moves a surface R4 compares byte for byte, and the ungated GET is itself a ported defect this repository records rather than silently repairs. Closing it means changing both routers or declaring a divergence, and that is the owner's call. 2026-10-19 — FIXED IN BOTH ROUTERS by merge 74d15306 (Merge ai/argv-redact), whose subject records that GET /servers stops publishing secret-bearing argv. Unit evidence: ArgvRedactionTests (app/Tests/RouterCoreTests/ArgvRedactionTests.swift) and test/argv-redact.test.ts, with parity vectors in argv-redact.json. Verified 2026-10-19: the `ArgvRedactionTests` suite passed under `swift test`, and `node --test` on test/argv-redact.test.ts passed. Status is fixed · in-test. No campaign re-run is recorded against this row.
subject.title: GET /servers discloses every stdio upstream's full argv to an unauthenticated local caller

subject.text: FOUND BY ARMING, not by reading. The status remap on this branch first synced `defects.in.json` to `inventory.json` wholesale, and the sync moved three rows that have nothing to do with vocabulary: DEF-002 `open` -> `closed`, DEF-040 `open-instrument` -> `fixed · in-campaign`, DEF-063 `open · measured` -> `open`. Those are adjudications, not spellings, so the sync was reverted and only the six unclassifiable SHAPES were rewritten in place. THE STANDING FACT: `reckon.read_campaign` reads defects from `inventory.json` and from nowhere else, so `defects.in.json` is a hand-edited source that no reckoning reads. Three of its 24 rows say something different from the file that is read, and nothing compares them. A reader who opens the source file gets a different answer about DEF-002, DEF-040 and DEF-063 than the ledger gives. WHAT IS NOT SETTLED, and why this is open rather than fixed: which of the two files is right about each of the three is an adjudication somebody has to make by reading the defect, and a runner remapping words is the wrong person to make it. `defect-status-vocabulary-gate.py` reads both files, so a NEW unclassifiable word is caught in either; it has no opinion on whether two files that both classify agree with each other.

subject.detail: Measured 2026-08-27 by G16 while enumerating SURF-026, and independently by G15. M15 made Settings a Scene and removed the case from `Destination`, and capture-mac-glass.sh still ran `axkit select Settings`. That select fails — `axkit: no sidebar row starting 'Settings'` — the app stays on whichever board the loop visited last, and the shutter filed THAT board's pixels under SURF-011: byte-identical to the Cleanup board on one loop ordering and to the Insights board on another. THE CAMPAIGN'S OWN INSTRUMENTS CAUGHT IT FROM TWO DIRECTIONS, which is the part worth keeping. glass-assert.py's raster uniqueness check went red because two cases shared a sha256; `--discriminate` reported the neighbouring board's predicate wrongly accepting SURF-011's dump, because that dump IS the neighbouring board; and the capture manifest's readback recorded the picture's target as the neighbour's route under subject SURF-011, contradicting its own filename. FIXED HERE, NARROWLY: the capture script now refuses to photograph a select that did not take, and says which board the window is actually showing. That is the script's own standing rule rather than a new one — it already declines to substitute a picture for the pairing sheet and the status item, and its header records the run that filed the Inbox board as SURF-010. The title and the dump are still written from what the app is really showing, so the failure stays visible downstream; what is withheld is the photograph, because a misattributed picture is the one artefact nothing downstream can correct. STILL OPEN, and deliberately not fixed here: 1. SURF-011 has no route to the Settings SCENE. It needs Cmd-comma or the app menu, not a sidebar select that cannot succeed. CASE-0016 and CASE-0111 fail until it does. 2. THE MENU MAP IS PRE-M22. Committed SURF-001.menu.txt binds Cmd-4 to `Discover`; the running app binds Cmd-4 to `Harnesses`, exactly as Destination.selectionDigit declares (activity 1, servers 2, skills 3, harnesses 4, discover 5, inbox 6, evals 7, cleanup 8, insights 9). glass-assert.py's SURF-001 `menu` dict is the old map, so CASE-0001 asserts five bindings this build does not have. Correcting it is editing an assertion to restore a green, which this campaign forbids — it is owed as its own item, from Destination.selectionDigit rather than by hand. WHY IT IS THE SAME FINDING AS G14'S, ONE LAYER DOWN. G14 found the surface LIST had stopped growing while the product did. This is the EVIDENCE not having been re-taken since the build moved: the committed glass artefacts were last written on 20 Aug by cef3729, before M22 added two destinations and renumbered four accelerators. In both cases a completeness gate reported clean because what it measured was a stale artefact rather than the product. CLOSED ON THE EVIDENCE SIDE, 2026-08-27 (G21/G29). The frame this defect produced was still published: `inventory.json` gave SURF-011 the shot `evidence/shots/SURF-011.build.png`, and at `519aebc` those bytes were the Insights board. `capture-lineage.py --gate` reported it UNTIED because the capture step's own row said `target: app://mac/insights` while the filename said SURF-011 -- the manifest was right and the wall was wrong. Two moves, both provable from git. The Insights frame is renamed `evidence/shots/DEF-059.insights-filed-as-SURF-011.png`, keeping every capture-time field, so the defect keeps its exhibit and no filename match can offer it to SURF-011 again. The Settings capture it overwrote is restored to `SURF-011.build.png` from `cef3729`, TOGETHER WITH ITS MANIFEST ROW from the same commit -- the last commit where those bytes and that row agreed (sha 3b5a26ef, `target: app://mac/settings`, readback `Settings`, 2026-08-20T11:32:58Z). Restoring the pair from one commit is a recovery of a capture-time record; restamping the row against the new bytes would have been the manifest-after-the-fact defect. What is NOT closed is the cause: `axkit select Settings` still fails, so the campaign still has no Settings capture newer than 2026-08-20 and the glass script still declines to take one. THE CAUSE NOW HAS A READER, 2026-09-02 (wa5). `axkit select Settings` still fails, and the campaign still has no Settings capture newer than 2026-08-20 -- unchanged. What has changed is that the age is no longer invisible: `bin/glass-build-gate.py` reports `evidence/shots/SURF-011.build.png` and `evidence/ax/SURF-011.*` as STALE against the build this tree would produce, so the lane cannot be green over them again without somebody re-taking them. `bin/capture-mac-glass.sh`'s refusal to photograph a select that did not take is the other half and is unchanged. Both halves of the remaining work -- a route to the Settings SCENE, and the re-capture -- are macOS work and are not attempted here. CLOSED 2026-10-19 on glass. capture-mac-glass.sh opens Settings with ⌘, (backgrounded), selects the Router pane in the Settings window's own source list, photographs that window as SURF-011 (target app://mac/settings), dumps the Security pane as a second dump of the same surface, and closes the window. glass-assert at the current build: checked=435 failures=0; --decoy SURF-011 reddens 6.
subject.title: `Settings` is no longer a sidebar row, so the glass capture filed a neighbouring board's pixels under SURF-011 — and the committed glass evidence predates M22

subject.detail: Measured 2026-08-27 by G15, while enumerating SURF-025. The committed glass evidence under planning/test-campaign/evidence/ax was last written by commit cef3729 on 20 Aug. M22 then added two destinations and RENUMBERED four accelerators, and nothing re-took the pictures. Running bin/capture-mac-glass.sh against the current build turns four previously-passing cases red, and in every one of them the PRODUCT is right and the recorded evidence is stale: 1. THE MENU MAP. Committed SURF-001.menu.txt binds Cmd-4 to `Discover`; the running app binds Cmd-4 to `Harnesses`, exactly as Destination.swift's selectionDigit declares (activity 1, servers 2, skills 3, harnesses 4, discover 5, inbox 6, evals 7, cleanup 8, insights 9). glass-assert.py's SURF-001 `menu` dict is the pre-M22 map, so CASE-0001 asserts five bindings the shipped build does not have. 2. SETTINGS IS NOT A SIDEBAR ROW. M15 made Settings a Scene and removed the case from Destination, and capture-mac-glass.sh still does `axkit select Settings`. That select now fails — `axkit: no sidebar row starting 'Settings'` — the app stays on Cleanup, and the script photographs the CLEANUP board and files it as SURF-011. CASE-0016 and CASE-0111 fail against it. THE CAMPAIGN'S OWN INSTRUMENTS CAUGHT BOTH, WHICH IS THE ONE GOOD PART. The capture manifest's readback records that picture as target `app://mac/cleanup` under subject SURF-011, contradicting its own filename — the exact mechanism the script was rebuilt around. Independently, glass-assert.py --discriminate reports LEAK SURF-007 wrongly accepted 1 of 8 foreign board dumps: SURF-011 — because SURF-011's dump IS the Cleanup board. Two instruments, one cause. WHY THIS IS THE SAME FINDING AS G14'S, ONE LAYER DOWN. G14 found the surface LIST had not grown since it was written. This is the EVIDENCE not having been re-taken since the build moved. In both cases a completeness gate reported clean because the thing it measured was a stale artefact rather than the product. NOT FIXED HERE, DELIBERATELY. G15's remit is the Harnesses enumeration, and correcting glass-assert.py's menu map or the Settings navigation would be editing an assertion to restore a green — even though the product is right, that is the move this campaign forbids, and the stale assertion is the instrument that found this. The four cases are set to `fail` with this id in their notes. Owed: re-map SURF-001's menu dict from Destination.selectionDigit, and give SURF-011 a route to the Settings SCENE (Cmd-comma or the app menu) instead of a sidebar select that cannot succeed. INSTRUMENTED 2026-09-02 (wa5), NOT CLOSED. The cause this row names -- a committed capture carrying no tie to the build it came from -- is now measurable. `planning/test-campaign/bin/glass-build-gate.py` binds every artifact the macos-glass lane cites to the git blob identity of the Mac app's build inputs (the set `scripts/acceptance/build-freshness.sh` compiles from) and exits 2 when that identity is not the one the lane is being read against. It is RED on this tree over all 56 artifacts, in 7 capture groups spanning 20-29 Aug: `evidence/runs/glass-build-gate.log`. The stamps it reads are marked `reconstructed-from-git` and are deliberately the weaker claim -- git can prove which commit last wrote each artifact, so the record establishes the build the evidence CANNOT BE NEWER THAN rather than the build it was taken from. `bin/capture-mac-glass.sh` now calls `glass-build-gate.py --emit` in the run that takes the pictures, stamping from the bundle's own CFBundleShortVersionString/CFBundleVersion and the `.mcprouter-build-stamp` the Makefile writes after `xcodebuild` exits 0, so a re-capture replaces each reconstructed row with a capture-time one. Watched both ways: `evidence/runs/glass-build-gate.selftest.log`, four arms, green over a current capture and red over a stale one, an uncovered one and an undatable row. Case CASE-0342. WHAT IS NOT SETTLED. The re-capture itself, which is the whole of what this defect asks for. It needs a macOS host with Xcode and a display server; the work above was done on Windows, where there is no Swift toolchain, no xcodebuild and no way to open the app's window. The four cases stay `fail` with `owed` recording the re-capture and its owner. The second half of the row -- SURF-001's menu map, to be re-read from `Destination.selectionDigit` rather than by hand -- is equally macOS work and equally untouched. Nothing here edits an assertion, a stamp or a recorded identity to restore a green.
subject.title: the macos-glass lane is green over window evidence captured from a pre-M22 build, and four of its cases assert a shell that no longer ships

subject.detail: DETECTOR DEFECT in test-campaign 0.9.2, found 21 Aug 2026. attach-shots.py iterates every image under evidence/shots and assigns `hit['shot'] = rel` on each match, last write wins, with no preference for a build capture over a design render. This campaign keeps six directories under evidence/shots (16 root, 8 design-size, 16 fidelity, 9 ios, 17 mock, 11 mock-hidpi), so for SURF-001 the candidates in iteration order are SURF-001.build.png, SURF-001.shell.png, mock/SURF-001.png, mock-hidpi/SURF-001.full.png -- and the last one wins. MEASURED for SURF-001, SURF-002 and SURF-006: `--apply` would repoint each surface's `shot` from its build capture to `evidence/shots/mock-hidpi/SURF-00N.full.png`, which is the render of the DESIGN, not the build. That is the skill's own headline failure mode -- publishing a picture of one thing under the name of another -- arriving in a sibling of the plane built to prevent it, and it would do so while every other gate stayed green, because capture-lineage.py gates the 16 captures cited by CASES and the surface wall is a different population. The report compounds it: the UNCORROBORATED block prints surface ids (SURF-001 ... SURF-011) rather than the file each verdict is about, so a reader sees eleven surfaces apparently lacking provenance when in fact each surface's ACTUAL `shot` field points at a corroborated build capture and the complaint is about a mock render nobody intended to attach. Distinguishing the two costs a re-derivation of the matcher by hand. Recorded rather than patched, precedent DEF-048, DEF-051, DEF-052 and DEF-053. The campaign's standing refusal to run `--apply` here predates this and was based on the DEF-006 mis-wire; it now has a measured mechanism behind it. Separately closed while investigating: this campaign's design-size captures carried their provenance in a second manifest, evidence/shots/design-size/captures.json, in a different schema ({captures:[...]} against the root's bare list) that no gate reads. Its 8 entries were merged into the root manifest with `target` derived from the root's declared target for the same subject and corroborated by each capture's own windowTitleReadback -- Servers, Activity, Skills, Discover, Inbox, Checks, Cleanup, Settings, every one matching -- recorded at capture time, and each carries `targetDerivedFrom` saying so. That was the campaign's own inconsistency and is fixed here; it was not the cause of the 11. RE-MEASURED 2026-08-27 (G21) after `evidence/shots/captures.json` was made a derived file. The uncorroborated count is 12 and stays 12: SURF-001..011 and SURF-022. Eleven of them are this defect -- `mock-hidpi/` sorts last, so it is the row that decides each surface's `shotProvenance`. The mock rows in the manifest deliberately carry NO `target`; the address the channel was pointed at is recorded in full as `renderedFrom`, with an `attachHazard` field naming this defect. Measured both ways on this tree: writing that address as `target` instead drops the uncorroborated count from 12 to 1 and DISARMS `--apply`'s refusal, because `attach-shots.py` only checks the field is present and never compares it to the subject's route -- which is item 5 of X8's work order. So the report going quiet would have been this defect getting worse while looking fixed. The twelfth, SURF-022, is not this defect: see DEF-061.
subject.title: attach-shots --apply would attach the design mock render as the build's surface shot for 11 surfaces, and its report names the surface rather than the file

subject.detail: Measured 2026-08-21 against test-campaign 0.9.2 on app/Tests. The pass reports examined=1661 mutating=320 blind=88. Two structural errors and two idiom errors inflate that number. STRUCTURAL. (1) It scans every `func`, not every test. Restricted to swift-testing's own discriminator (a func whose nearest preceding annotation is @Test) the denominator is 1531, not 1661: 130 of the examined functions are not tests. (2) Its helper exclusion at vacuity-check.py:162 is file-scoped — a name is a helper only if called more than once in the file that declares it. A shared stub declared in TestSupport.swift and called from other files therefore reads as a test, so MemoryFileSystem's `write`, `removeItem` and `moveItem`, HTTPStub's `stop` and WatchTestSupport's `remove` are each counted as a blind test. 21 of the 88 are support-file functions. IDIOM, on the mutator side. (3) The lookbehind `(?<![A-Za-z0-9_])` cannot exclude a dot, so a Swift enum case constructor matches a mutator verb: `ServerRowAction.forServer(s, pendingAuth: nil) == .reset(.clearPlacard)` reports ServerPresentationTests::trippedOutranksHeld as mutating via 'reset', where `.reset` is the expected VALUE inside the assertion. 41 of 72 re-measured findings are dot-prefixed. (4) It takes the last mutator by source POSITION and calls everything after it the tail, which misreads three Swift constructs: a mutator inside the assertion (`await #expect(throws: Never.self) { try await store.delete() }` — nothing can follow it by construction), a mutator in a `defer` block (source-early, execution-last, so the whole test body reads as 'after'), and a mutator as the last statement of a loop body whose observation is the next iteration (CallbackLifecycleTests::stopReleasesTheSocket rebinds the port ten times; the read of cycle N is the start() of cycle N+1). SAMPLE. Of the 15 findings with zero assertions after the last mutator — the highest-yield stratum — 9 were read in full. Two (DiscoveryTests::servers, CapabilityPlateTests::install) are helpers. All 7 remaining are real tests that do observe after mutating, through idioms no reader verb names: `client.calls.last?.operation`, `seen.filter { ... }`, a rebind that throws. Precision on that stratum is 0 of 7. ARMED, two ways, evidence/arming/blind-mutation.arming.log. A probe @Test that mutates and never observes was added and removed: blind moved 88 -> 89 -> 88 and examined/mutating moved by exactly 1 each time. The check does bite; it is the false-positive rate that is at issue, not the sensitivity. NOT REMEDIED BY VOCABULARY. The reader side is deliberately loose because a false reader match suppresses a finding. Adding this codebase's read idioms (`calls`, `operation`, `filter`) would lower the number without improving what the pass knows, and the terms are generic enough to suppress true findings too. The 88 stands recorded as a worklist with its measured precision beside it rather than tuned to look better. RE-MEASURED 2026-08-27 by G22, which declared `testRoot` and gave this pass a corpus for the first time. THE 88 DOES NOT REPRODUCE. Vendored 0.9.2 over `app/Tests` today reports examined=2133 mutating=3 blind=3, against the 1661/320/88 above. The denominator moving up while `mutating` collapses 320 → 3 is not tree churn: 0.9.1 and 0.9.2 ship IDENTICAL DEFAULT_MUTATORS and DEFAULT_READERS, and neither list holds `reset`, `write`, `removeItem`, `moveItem` or `remove` — the verbs this entry's idiom argument turns on. So the 2026-08-21 sitting ran an expanded vocabulary passed on the command line, and `campaign.json` declares none, which makes 88 a figure no documented invocation returns. Its cited evidence, `evidence/arming/blind-mutation.arming.log`, has never existed on any branch of this repository (`git log --all -- '*blind-mutation*'` is empty), so the arming claim above is not checkable from the tree. The measured structural and idiom errors are not withdrawn; what is withdrawn is the population they were measured over. TODAY'S POPULATION, AND ITS PRECISION. With `testRoot: app` the pass reports examined=2179 mutating=3 re-read-after=0 blind=3, and 0.15.0 returns the same three findings from the same corpus. All THREE were read in full — 3 of 3, not a sample — and all three are false positives. Precision 0 of 3. A FOURTH CAUSE, NOT IN THE ORIGINAL ENTRY, AND THE ONE THAT PRODUCES TWO OF THE THREE. The body slice is `src[pos:end]` where `pos` is the start of the DECLARATION, so a test whose own name begins with a mutator verb matches itself. `WatchRestartTests::restartIsIssuedBeforeTheStagingWrite` and `::restartIsOwedBeforeTheWriteLands` contain no mutating call at all: the only `restart\w*\(` in each is `func restart…(` on its own declaration line. Both then read — `WatchWorld.read(scratch.logPath)`, `WatchState.load(path:)`, `WatchWorld.serverNames(in:)` — and assert on `state.mcpServersHash` and `state.restartPending`. The third, `PhoneStorageFailureTests::restartRechecksTheCamera`, does call `await model.restart()` and then asserts twice, on `model.step` and on `model.entry.characters`: property reads that no reader verb names, which is cause (4)'s shape rather than a new one. This cause survives into 0.15.0 unchanged. NOT ENROLLED IN A GATE, and `blindVocabulary` still not declared, for the reason the entry already gives. A related gap measured at the same sitting: pointed at `src/` — the TypeScript tree, which has no tests — the pass prints `corpus: … (0 file(s))` and `examined=0 mutating=0 blind=0` and contributes nothing to `--gate`. It reports its empty corpus and does not fail on it, so a mis-declared `testRoot` reads as a clean pass. VOCABULARY DECLARED 2026-08-29 by K4, and the entry's own 'NOT REMEDIED BY VOCABULARY' paragraph is narrowed rather than withdrawn. That paragraph reasons entirely from the READER side, and on the reader side it is still right: adding this codebase's read idioms lowers the count without improving what the pass knows, which is why the declared reader list stops short of `expect` and `require` -- swift-testing's assertion macros, 5781 and 383 occurrences, either of which would mark every test that asserts after mutating as re-reading and collapse the count to near zero while the pass learned nothing. THE MUTATOR SIDE WAS NEVER ARGUED, AND THAT IS WHERE THE PASS WAS BLIND. Measured over the same 2282 test bodies at `83e5380`: the nine snake_case defaults find 3 mutating call sites; a camelCase list derived from this corpus finds 481. So `blind=3` was a reading of 3 of 481, a recall of 0.6%, and the entry's `precision 0 of 3` was a precision over a population the instrument could barely see. `campaign.json` now carries `blindVocabulary` with `only: true`, 19 mutators and 34 readers, derived mechanically -- a verb is kept only where method calls on a receiver are at least half its corpus sites and its own `func` declaration lines at most a quarter, which is causes (3) and (4) of this entry turned into a selection rule. THE THREE FINDINGS ARE ADJUDICATED, and each clears for a different checkable reason rather than all three for one. `restartIsIssuedBeforeTheStagingWrite`: one fitted mutator, `WatchWorld.remove(scratch)` inside a `defer`, and four declared readers after it -- `load`, `read`, `parse`, `servers`. NOT blind, positively. `restartIsOwedBeforeTheWriteLands`: three fitted mutators, the last `WatchState(restartPending: true).save(`, with `load` after it. NOT blind, positively. `restartRechecksTheCamera`: ZERO fitted mutator call sites in its body. It was flagged only because `restart` is a shipped default and this entry's fourth cause -- the body slice beginning at the declaration -- made `func restartRechecksTheCamera(` match itself. `restart` fails the selection rule (1 method call against 3 declaration lines, of 5 sites), so it is not in the vocabulary and the finding is withdrawn. WHAT THAT DOES NOT MEAN: its real mutation `await model.restart()` is now invisible to the pass, and its reads are still the property comparisons `model.step` and `model.entry.characters` that no reader verb names. It is UNEXAMINED by this instrument, not clean, and that is this entry's ceiling stated once more rather than closed. ARMED, AND ENROLLED, which the entry recorded as missing. `planning/test-campaign/bin/blind-vocabulary-arm.py` runs on every `make lint`: two plants identical but for one line, each measured alone and again inside a `shutil.copytree` of the real corpus, requiring examined+1 mutating+1 blind+1 for the blind plant and examined+1 mutating+1 blind+0 for the reading one. The specificity arm is the half a sensitivity arm alone cannot give: a detector that flagged every mutating body would pass the first and say nothing. 6 of 6 as expected on `cache 0.16.0` and again on the `vendor/` pin via `--instrument`. The two disagree only on the denominator -- 2282 against 2277, the five arrow-style `it/test(` blocks 0.9.3 added block detection for -- and agree on blind=111. THE 111 IS A WORKLIST AND THE CAMPAIGN STILL PUBLISHES NO BLIND NUMBER. Nothing above touches the structural causes: the pass still examines every `func` rather than every `@Test`, its helper exclusion is still file-scoped, and a `defer` mutator still reads as source-early -- which is exactly why the first of the three findings above needed reading rather than counting. This entry stays OPEN; what it now carries is a measured recall beside its measured precision.
subject.title: vacuity-check's blind-mutation pass examines non-tests and mis-reads Swift idiom; 7 of 7 sampled findings are false positives

subject.detail: Found 20 Aug 2026 while building R8's gate against both routers. Against a fixture returning `-32603` with the message `Internal error: Authentication required`, the reference records `MCP error -32603: Internal error: Authentication required` and the Swift router records `[-32603] Internal error`. The upstream's own message is gone. CAUSE, cited exactly: modelcontextprotocol/swift-sdk 0.12.1, `Sources/MCP/Base/Error.swift:217-240`. The decoder reads the server's `message`, then maps the code — `-32700`, `-32600`, `-32601` and `-32602` each pass `unwrapDetail(message)`, and `-32603` alone passes `unwrapDetail(nil)`. `unwrapDetail(fallback)` returns `data.detail` when present and the fallback otherwise, so a server that answers -32603 with a message and no `data.detail` has its message discarded, and `Error.swift:91` renders `"Internal error" + (detail.map { ": \($0)" } ?? "")` as the bare canonical name. -32603 is the code servers use for an arbitrary application error, so it is the one that loses the most. TWO consequences: for the whole class of -32603 upstream errors the Swift router tells the user strictly less than the reference does; and R8's Swift half cannot detect a credential refusal at all, because there is no text left to match. This is a coverage gap in the parity suite as much as a defect in the SDK — no parity scenario had ever exercised a JSON-RPC error carrying a detailed message, which is why 82 proven rows never saw it. Remedies, none taken: report upstream and take a fixed release; pin a patched fork; or read the JSON-RPC error before the SDK types it, which needs a seam below the client.
subject.title: the Swift MCP SDK discards an upstream's error message for code -32603, so the router reports less than the reference does

subject.detail: parity-gate.sh, 20 Aug 2026 on main at e5755d0. The suite lane's citation run of scripts/acceptance/parity-oauth.sh exited non-zero and recorded `control-auth-post-http fail — the Swift router never reached the token endpoint`. The dedicated oauth lane, later in the same gate, ran the same script and recorded ok over 21 checks. The gate reported the row DIVERGED and printed 81 of 83. WHY IT IS UNEXPLAINED, established 21 Aug 2026 from disk without re-running anything. The run survives as evidence/runs/parity-gate-2026-08-20-oauth-flake.log, written 20:39:30. Its line 163 is the whole of what the citation run reported: `FAIL scripts/acceptance/parity-oauth.sh the gate reported findings`, and the next line is the following `ok` row. The script itself does not fail that quietly -- its failure branch (parity-oauth.sh:308-329) prints the POST /auth status, the browser hop, the tail of the router log and the first 20 requests the provider saw. Every one of those bytes existed and was discarded by the caller: `parity-suite.sh`'s `run_script` sent both streams to /dev/null at the time. So this defect is not a run that left no diagnostic, it is a run whose diagnostic the harness threw away, and no amount of re-reading the log can recover it. The instrument was repaired in commit 21d559b at 20:41:28 -- one minute and 58 seconds after this log was written, in the same commit that recorded the defect -- so `run_script` now keeps the log and prints its last 20 lines inline. A recurrence would therefore arrive with the cause attached. That is what closes this: the next occurrence, not more thought about this one. It stays open because there is still no cause and no reproduction; what changed is that the reason it could not be diagnosed is now known and no longer true. One candidate mechanism examined and NOT adopted. The R9 lane reported (21 Aug 2026, via uds:/tmp/cc-socks/9881.sock) that a stale $TMPDIR/mcp-router-parity.lock had made a gate fail its manifest-check for a non-real reason. That is a different symptom -- a manifest-check failure before the comparison, against this defect's completed run that reached `control-auth-post-http` and recorded a row -- and parity-oauth.sh takes that same lock at line 126 and preflights every port at 143-145, so the two lanes inside one gate could not have overlapped. Recorded as ruled out rather than left unmentioned, so the next reader does not spend the lead twice.
subject.text: Observed once, in one of two whole-gate runs, and not reproduced by: a standalone run of `parity-oauth.sh`, a second standalone run of it immediately afterwards (which exercised the same port-reuse wait, 9s and 12s), a standalone run of `parity-suite.sh`, or a second whole `parity-gate.sh` on the same tree. The second gate reported 82 of 83, 0 DIVERGED, and its suite lane reported the citation clean. **What it is not.** The lane distinguishes an environment failure from a finding on purpose, and this was the finding branch: `record control-auth-post-http fail` at `parity-oauth.sh:329`, reached only when the reference side completed an authorization and the Swift side did not. An unbindable port exits 2 through `wait_for_ports_bindable` and records `blocked`, not `fail`, so the port-reuse race is ruled out by the code path that fired. **Why it went undiagnosed, and what changed.** `parity-suite.sh`'s `run_script` sent both streams to `/dev/null` and printed `the gate reported findings` — a verdict with no evidence under it. The bytes naming which guard failed had already been thrown away by the time anyone read the gate's summary. `run_script` now keeps the log, prints its last 20 lines inline and names the file it kept, armed 20 Aug 2026 against a deliberately failing citation. A recurrence will say which of the 21 checks went red. **Why the duplicate run stays.** `control-auth-post-http` is proven on the wire by its own lane and also cites the script, so the gate runs it twice. That is now documented in `parity-suite.sh` rather than deduplicated, because the duplicate is what caught this: a single run would have reported a clean 82 of 83 and nobody would have known. Both record under the same row id and a `fail` wins. **Burn-in, 20 Aug 2026: 8 standalone runs of the lane, all green, 21 checks each.** Three immediately after the failure and five consecutively afterwards, plus one clean whole gate. One failure in roughly ten whole-lane executions, cause unrecoverable because that invocation's stdout was discarded. A green burn-in does not close this: the original failure is uninspectable, so the runs measure only that the lane is not reliably broken. What would close it is a captured reproduction, or a stated gate met — several consecutive whole gates including the cold port-reuse path — decided as its own question rather than inferred from a streak, which is the `install-launchd-watch` mistake this repository already paid for once (G1: name a fix per term and fix a bound IN ADVANCE, never a green streak). Not a UI defect and not a blocker on the cutover count — CASE-0036's measurement is the second run — but it is an unexplained non-determinism in the router or the lane, and it is recorded rather than absorbed.

subject.detail: Measured 2026-09-03 (WE3) while adjudicating `an-effect-class-the-census-cannot-name-reads-as-no-effect.md`. That brief cites one requirement. The requirement axis is clean -- all 44 declare a class in `EFFECT_CLASSES` -- and the finding is on the axis nobody counted: 31 of the 49 cases that name a `witness.effect` name a class the vocabulary does not carry, and every one of the 31 is `oracle: effect-witness` at `status: pass`. machine-state 25 CASE-0366..0371, 0420..0426, 0470..0477, 0490..0493 file 2 CASE-0342, CASE-0386 notification 1 CASE-0441 os-record 1 CASE-0387 process 1 CASE-0440 ui-state 1 CASE-0346 WHY NOBODY SAW IT, and this is the half that makes it a defect rather than a chore. `campaign.py:702` DOES check the field, and its blocker line reads `40 effect-witness claim(s) with no recorder, no effect class, or a count of zero`. That 40 is 31 bad classes plus 9 missing recorders and counts, verified by replicating the loop. The report then caps its detail at twelve lines -- which on this campaign are twelve lines about four cases with missing recorders and null counts. **All 31 class findings are inside the 40 and not one of them is printed.** A reader of the campaign report cannot learn from it that any case names an unrecognised class, and the number reads as a recorder problem. WHY THE 31 ARE NOT REMAPPED HERE, deliberately and on the record. Some are a rename: `process` on CASE-0440, whose recorder is `Get-ScheduledTaskInfo`, is `subprocess`. Some are a harder question a rename would bury: `machine-state` on CASE-0423..0426 and CASE-0490..0493 is recorded over *"the router's own /servers listing, read over the control API"*, which is a recorder INSIDE the product -- whether those cases belong at the `effect-witness` rung at all is a judgement about the case, not about a word. Picking the nearest legal spelling for all 31 would turn 31 rows green while answering neither question, and every one of them belongs to the Windows waves rather than to this runner. `references/effect-boundary.md` is what settles them.

subject.note: R26. THE PAIRED ABSENCE, and the load-bearing case. The claim is that the expiry is DERIVED from files the router already wrote rather than asked of the upstream, and half of that claim is an absence: nothing was spawned. An absence asserted alone is satisfied by a feature that does nothing, which is REQ-035's recorded lesson. So the lane never asserts it alone. It reads the daemon's child count off the process table -- zero, and zero running the stdio fixture's own script -- in the same run in which it REWRITES a planted credential record between two requests and requires the reported `expiresAt` and `state` to move with it. Zero children beside a report that follows the file is the claim; zero children alone is not.

subject.note: WHAT THIS ROW SPEAKS FOR, AND WHAT IT DOES NOT. It measures the NODE reference only. `swift` and `xcodebuild` are absent on this machine, so nothing here is a Swift test result and this case must not be read as coverage of `AuthRoutes.promote`; the Swift side of REQ-019 is still carried by `ControlApproveDispatchTests` and this campaign has not run it. Three arms over the shipped `handleControl` out of `dist/`: a writable home answering 200 with `pending` gone from disk; the same call with the save's temp path occupied by a directory, answering 500 with the errno message and `pending` still on disk; and the occupation removed, answering 200 again. The denial is the filesystem's own `EISDIR` at exactly the step that makes the change durable - not a mocked `FileSystem` - and the lock sidecar and the manifest read are left working on purpose, because a denial that also stopped the lock would produce a 500 carrying the LOCK's sentence and prove nothing about the save. ACLs were tried first and are recorded in the lane's header as a control that did not arm: `icacls <file> /deny <user>:(D,WD,AD,WEA,WA)` and `icacls <dir> /deny <user>:(DC)` both apply, read back as DENY aces, and `renameSync` over the target succeeds anyway on this machine. An ACL that is set and does not bite produces a green arm that never armed, which is why the temp-path occupation replaced it. What it found: the reference answers 500, so Swift's pre-R21 200 was a divergence and R21's change closed it (DEF-442), while the error BODIES still differ (DEF-441). `deps.liveReload` and `deps.manifest` are stubs - they are the announcement collaborators the 200 path calls after the write - and the route, the lock, `loadManifest` and `saveManifest` are the shipped ones.

subject.note: NOT A PRODUCT MEASUREMENT. Nothing here is observed on any surface and `surface` is null on purpose: the gate reads the register, and a green means the register's effect claims are accountable, never that the effects happen. Enrolled in `make lint` beside `defect-status-vocabulary-gate.py`, both the check and its selftest. It exists because `vacuity-check.py` REPORTS this state and cannot refuse it - it lives under `vendor/`, pinned by checksum, and this repository may not edit it - so its finding was carried forward run after run. The rule is a disjunction rather than a count, because a gate written to `9 of 9 named` would be satisfied by somebody typing a plausible filename into the field: name a provider that resolves, OR record the claim `vacuous` and say in `providerNote` what is missing. REQ-016 takes the second branch and passes deliberately - the gate holds the absence visible rather than answering DEF-440's question. Blind spots it prints on every clean run: R3 checks that the FILE exists and never that the symbol inside it does, a `:line` is not followed, and a provider field carrying only prose is counted as checked-by-nothing rather than passed quietly. 40 provider path tokens resolve across 16 bound rows at 42aef112; the unreadable-token count is 0.

subject.detail: This is small and it is filed rather than fixed for a reason worth stating: the fix is one line in Swift, and this machine cannot compile Swift, so changing it would trade a measured divergence for an unmeasured edit. `planning/parity/surface.tsv`'s `control-approve-post` row declares that the 200 promotion path is proven Swift-side only and says nothing at all about the failed-write path, so this divergence was in neither the proven set nor the declared set. It is now declared in that row. The remedy is a choice between two one-line edits and it is not obviously the port's: dropping Swift's prefix matches the reference byte for byte, and adding the prefix to node makes both sentences readable at the cost of moving the reference. Whoever takes it should take it on a machine with a Swift toolchain and re-run `scripts/acceptance/r21-approve-write-denied.mjs` on the node side either way. SWIFT WAS NOT COMPILED AND NOT RUN FOR THIS ROW. `swift` and `xcodebuild` are both absent on the machine this was written on (LUKESFF, Windows 11; `Get-Command` found neither), so every statement here about Swift source is READ off the tree at 42aef112 and none of it is a test result. Where a claim is measured, the command that measured it is named.
subject.text: MEASURED on the reference, READ on the port. Node's `POST /servers/:name/approve` against a manifest write the filesystem refuses answers `500` with `{"error":"<the errno message verbatim>"}` - the run recorded `{"error":"EISDIR: illegal operation on a directory, open '...\\manifest.json.tmp-4752'"}` - and leaves `pending` on disk. Swift's `AuthRoutes.promote` catches the same failure at `app/Sources/RouterCore/Auth/AuthRoutes.swift:171-177` and answers `500` with `{"error": "failed to write manifest: <error.localizedDescription>"}`. The STATUS agrees; the BODY does not, because the port prefixes a sentence of its own that the reference does not write.
subject.title: The two approve routes agree on 500 when the manifest write is refused and disagree on what they put in the body
