subject.cell: execution-plane=windows-host - data-shape=package not installed
subject.note: A real MSIX, built, deployed and removed, with a recorder at each step that is not the thing that wrote it. MakeAppx packs and .NET's ZipArchive reads the OPC container back - so the identity assertion is made against the PACKED ARTIFACT rather than against the file on disk that was handed to the packer. `winget validate` is the winget client applying a schema this repository does not own. Add-AppxPackage deploys and Get-AppxPackage reports: Fledgeling.MCPRouter_0.1.0.0_x64__facmrsw33693e. THE INSTALL ARM IS WHAT TURNS A FILE INTO A PACKAGE. A manifest can pack cleanly, validate cleanly, and be refused at deployment for a capability, an architecture or a signature - and every static check in the world passes right up to that point. 'CLEAN UNINSTALL RULES' IS THE HALF WORTH READING TWICE. UninstallGuidance promises that uninstalling preserves %USERPROFILE%\.claude\mcp-router. That is a promise about what SURVIVES, and a promise about survival cannot be checked by any amount of reading - only by an uninstall that actually ran. The lane plants a marker, installs, removes, and requires both that the deployment stack reports the package gone and that the marker is still there. WHAT THE LANE PUTS BACK: a self-signed certificate is added to LocalMachine\TrustedPeople so an unsigned developer package can deploy at all, and removed in a finally block however the run ends. Verified afterwards: zero Fledgeling.* packages, zero witness certificates. A lane that left a trusted publisher behind would have changed what this machine will install, silently and for every future run. NOT SETTLED: that anyone can obtain the package. Nothing publishes it, the winget InstallerUrl is a deliberate example.invalid placeholder, and this lane asserts the placeholder is PRESENT so the manifest cannot be mistaken for a shipping one. DEF-083 carries the publishing step, which needs a signing certificate and a pull request into a third-party repository.

subject.cell: execution-plane=windows-host - data-shape=one capability queued
subject.note: The COM activator the Windows notification platform wrote, read out of the registry by a process that did not write it. The writer is AppNotificationManager.Register() inside the shell; the recorder is HKCU through PowerShell's registry provider, and nothing of this repository's sits between them. Four arms. BASELINE requires the AUMID key to be ABSENT before the shell launches, so what the other three read is this launch. The three EFFECT arms read the key, the CustomActivator CLSID it names, and that CLSID's LocalServer32 - which came back as MCPRouter.Shell.exe carrying the platform's own ----AppNotificationActivated: argument, a string this repository does not write anywhere. THE ACTIVATOR IS THE ARM THAT CARRIES THE ITEM. A toast outlives the process that raised it; when somebody presses Review an hour later, Windows COM-activates the LocalServer32 registered for that CLSID. Without it the toast still appears and pressing it does nothing, which is the failure that looks most like success and exactly what a screenshot of a notification would have certified. WHAT THIS CASE DOES NOT SETTLE: that a toast is drawn, and that a press re-activates the app. Both need UserNotificationListener, whose capability is only grantable to a packaged application; DEF-082 carries them and is downstream of DEF-073. The shell's own report that the platform accepted a Show is carried in the evidence as writerSelfReport and is graded by nothing, because a process reporting its own effect is the shape of claim DEF-072 was about.

subject.evidence: scripts/windows/win22-toast-witness.ps1 witnesses the REGISTRATION and says so in its own notMeasured[]. Enumerating what is in the Action Center requires Windows.UI.Notifications.Management.UserNotificationListener, whose userNotificationListener capability is only grantable to a packaged application; MCPRouter.Shell.csproj is WindowsPackageType=None. Nothing here can press a notification button either. CORRECTED 2026-09-03: the packaging claim above is false on this host. See planning/evidence/WIN22/run/toast-effect.json, whose LISTENER.unpackaged arm asserts packaged=False alongside RequestAccessAsync=Allowed.
subject.title: Nothing on this host can press a toast button, or say which application raised a toast it can see

subject.cell: execution-plane=windows-host - data-shape=a supervised process that dies
subject.note: The half of WIN23's supervision promise that had never been watched: a daemon the Windows task scheduler starts, loses, and starts again. DEF-081 filed it as unmeasurable and named the blocker as a missing Windows daemon binary; the blocker was real and is gone - app/windows/MCPRouter.Witness.Daemon is a harness process that starts, records its own start and waits to be killed, so there is something for the scheduler to supervise. WHAT THE MEASUREMENT FOUND IS NOT WHAT THE ROW EXPECTED. The registration the product wrote carried RestartOnFailure with a 60-second interval and a count of 3, and it did not restart the daemon at all. Killed, watched 150 seconds, on the unified scheduling engine and the legacy one, for a run started by a trigger and one started on demand: four registrations, no restart. The same block DID restart, three times at exactly 60 seconds, a task whose Command named a file that does not exist - so the instrument can see a restart, and RestartOnFailure governs a task that fails to LAUNCH rather than one whose action launched and later died. DEF-320 carries that, and the product now writes a Repetition on the trigger alongside MultipleInstancesPolicy IgnoreNew. THE RECORDERS ARE TWO AND NEITHER WROTE ANYTHING: Get-ScheduledTaskInfo for the scheduler's own account of its runs, and Get-CimInstance Win32_Process for the process identity, which is what makes 'it came back' a different process id rather than a report from the thing that came back. The daemon's own run log is carried and graded by nothing. EIGHT ARMS, THREE OF THEM ABOUT THE INSTRUMENT: BASELINE requires both tasks absent and no daemon running, so nothing below is inherited from an interrupted run; CLAIM.repetition and CLAIM.ignorenew read the product's own unmodified logon registration back through the WMI provider; SILENCE requires both recorders to say no once the tasks are gone. ONE SUBSTITUTION, SAID OUT LOUD: a trigger repetition does not apply to an on-demand start - measured, twice - so the live task carries a TimeTrigger where the product writes a LogonTrigger, because this lane must not log the machine out. Every Setting, the repetition interval, the principal, the action and the instances policy are the product's own document. That the trigger fires AT LOGON is still unwitnessed and DEF-081 keeps it.

subject.cell: execution-plane=daemon · data-shape=a request on a method the ported token gate does not cover
subject.note: ControlAPIRequest.isMutating is POST || DELETE || PATCH, ported from src/control.ts, and PUT is not in it. No route served PUT before this family, so nothing was ever exposed — but this family's write was written as a PUT, and an untokened PUT /profiles/x measured 200 while the rest of the suite was green. The write is a POST instead, because widening a ported gate that parity-manifest-check.sh derives from the reference in both directions is not a thing to do for a verb. The lane asserts the 405 on the wire and ControlProfileRoutesTests C6 holds the invariant over PUT, HEAD, OPTIONS and TRACE for whoever adds the next route here.

F5. The serialised key set of an InvocationEvent is exactly ts, kind, name, harness. Driven from a fixture transcript line that carries a cwd naming a project and an args carrying prompt text; neither may appear in the output. InvocationEvent.wireKeys is asserted alongside, so a fifth member added later reddens this rather than shipping. The privacy claim in spec-F5.md 3 is worth what fails when it stops being true.

F5. The incremental scan. Scanning an unchanged file twice must yield the same events as scanning it once and must not open it the second time; a file that shrank must be re-read from zero and say so in filesReread. The corpus is 59,476 files and 19.5 GB (measured 2026-08-29), so the watermark is what makes the reader answerable inside a request rather than an optimisation.

F5. With no reporter wired, GET /invocations answers 503 naming that the router was never pointed at a transcript corpus, not an empty window. ControlDeps' optional ports have shipped nil in RouterServiceDispatch twice with a green suite (control-registry-search, D-p1-a), which is a 503 on a whole family no unit test could see.

The Insights board is reachable from the sidebar and the window title becomes its destination name — `axkit select Insights` actuated the row, `axkit title` read `Insights` back off the running app, and the capture manifest records target=app://mac/insights from that readback rather than from a filename. The predicates are the sentences that BOUND its figures rather than the figures themselves: that nothing on it is modelled, the provenance line under the memory reading, why a bar can read nothing at all, and the duty cycle's mechanism and window. The §6 search for a saving runs over the rendered window and is non-vacuous by construction — the copy list requires the board to BE discussing memory and duty cycle, so a clean result is a measurement rather than a search over a tree with no numbers in it. The FIGURES are not asserted here and that is deliberate: a Debug shell reads a fixture, so asserting a number in this window would prove the fixture. CASE-0177 traces them against a live router. ADJUDICATED 2026-10-19 (glass-adjudicate): superseded. The session analyst landed in 404d7832 (2026-08-29, `feat(analyst): ... the button that never did anything`). planning/specs/spec-F7.md §3 item 8 states that `Analyse now` is "enabled exactly when the router serves the route", and the populated AX dump draws it enabled (evidence/ax/SURF-026.window.txt, `Analyse now` row, enabled column 1). bin/glass-assert.py now expects enabled. This is a design change, not a product defect.

Raised off `structural` without claiming a feature that does not exist. PRD.md §6 specifies a session analyst and nothing in app/Sources implements one, so `Analyse now` is drawn disabled, nothing presses it, and no case here says the analyst works. What relation `SURF-026/action-tracks-state` asserts is the thing a disabled control can still be wrong about: the board draws exactly ONE action in each of its three readings, and which one is a function of the reading — `Analyse now` disabled where calls were served, `Watch the live log instead` enabled where the log horizon is nil, `Start the router` enabled where the read failed. The three are pairwise distinct and each appears in neither of the other two windows, so the action is chosen rather than drawn. ADJUDICATED 2026-10-19 (glass-adjudicate): the populated reading's expected action is now `Analyse now` enabled, per spec-F7.md §3 item 8 (404d7832). The relation still asserts one action per reading, pairwise distinct and absent from the other two windows; only the enabled bit of the populated expectation changed.

FLOW-006.02. The panel drew a document THE ROUTER SERVED, not M19's fixture: the titlebar names g17-capability, the package's own H1 and prose are on screen, all three tab controls are drawn, and 'trawl' — the fixture capability every previous dump and capture of this panel was a picture of, M23's included — appears nowhere in the tree. Checks G17-P1, G17-P2, G17-P3. Picture: evidence/g17-document/readme.served.png. The server is CONSTRUCTED by the harness and labelled so in three places — the harness header, the package's own read me, and every row of evidence/g17-document/captures.json. 0 of the 21 upstreams on this machine declare a package directory (M30, planning/evidence/M30-reach.txt), so there is no real one to point at. The router, the route, the transport, the parser, the image resolver and the panel are all the product's. --- RUNG CORRECTED by J3, from `raster-visual`. Its three checks are G17-P1, G17-P2 and G17-P3, and all three read `readme.served.dump.json` — a titlebar's text, a heading and a sentence, the three tab labels, and the absence of the string `trawl` from the tree. Not one of them opens the PNG. The claim is true and it is structural, and it was carrying the strongest rung's badge on a frame it never read. The picture stays cited because it is the frame this dump was taken in the same render as, and it stays on the wall as FLOW-006.02's step shot.

FLOW-006.02, and the claim nothing had ever made: an image inside a served document DRAWS. M19's resolver returns bytes precisely so the app never opens a file, and until now the strongest available statement was that four image cards were laid out — `MarkdownBlockView` draws a figure and a refusal placeholder inside the same measured `card`, so the two are one record. This case does not fix that by adding a node: a node would say two views differ, and what needed saying is that bytes arrived and were painted. The pixels answer it. 65.7% of the figure card's own frame in readme.served.png is the constructed band's authored colour, read at the scale derived from the dump's size rather than assumed to be 2, with a 25% floor and a tolerance on the colour because the backing store resolves in the display's space (authored #2F9C9C reads back near #519A9B). Check G17-P4. --- ARTIFACT CORRECTED by J3. This case reads pixels — G17-P4 counts the band's colour over the figure card's own frame — so the rung is right and the picture was not: it cited the whole 1536x1640 frame, byte for byte the same file CASE-0185 and CASE-0187 cited, and that file does not show which card was measured. It now cites the crop of the card itself, written by the check at the moment it counted those pixels, with the parent frame and its sha256 recorded in `capture.derivedFrom` and in verdicts.json.

The 'outside the package' refusal, rendered and distinguishable. A reference climbing out of the package is refused by the router as escapesPackage, and the panel draws its own sentence — 'Not shown — this image points outside the package it came with.' — read back off the `figure-refusal` node G17 added, in a card carrying 0.00% figure colour. Both halves matter: the node says WHICH refusal landed, which no dump could say before, and the pixels say the card really is a placeholder rather than a picture nobody checked. The node costs the readme fidelity census nothing, because it is drawn only when a reference is refused and the M19 fixture's one image resolves. Check G17-P5. --- ARTIFACT CORRECTED by J3, on the same finding as CASE-0186 and from the other side of it. G17-P5 reads the `figure-refusal` node's own frame and requires under 1% figure colour, so the pixels are real and the picture was the whole frame the other two cases also cited. It now cites the crop of the refusal card — 708x28 of drawn sentence and no picture, which is exactly what the check asserts.

Refusal 1 of 3 — nothing served. A server declaring no cwd is refused noPackageDirectory on the wire, and the panel draws the designed state: 'g17-no-package has no package to read', and no figure. This is the state EVERY ONE of the 21 upstreams on this machine is in today, so the frame is a picture of the product as configured rather than of an edge case. Checks G17-W4, G17-R1. Picture: evidence/g17-document/refusal.nopackage.png. --- RUNG CORRECTED by J3, from `raster-visual`. Its checks are G17-W4 — `reason == "noPackageDirectory"` read off the router's own response — and G17-R1, which reads the state title out of `refusal.nopackage.dump.json` and asserts no `figure` node. The wire read is a real outcome and this case is the only home of it; the drawn half is structural. Neither opens `refusal.nopackage.png`, which stays cited as the frame the dump came from and is claimed as evidence of nothing.

Refusal 2 of 3 — too large. A read me of 600,012 bytes is over the 524,288-byte transport cap for one document; the route refuses `documentTooLarge` naming the file and the limit, and the panel draws 'README.md is too large to show here' with the 512 KB cap in its advice. Note the wire spelling: `documentTooLarge`, not `tooLarge` — the latter is the IMAGE refusal one level in, and a check written against the Swift enum's case name rather than against the wire would have passed on a router that refused nothing. Checks G17-W5, G17-R2. This frame is also DEF-060: it never names the capability it refuses. --- RUNG CORRECTED by J3, from `raster-visual`. Its checks are G17-W5 — `reason`, `file` and `limit` read off the router's own response — and G17-R2, which reads the state title and the `512 KB` string out of `refusal.toolarge.dump.json`. The wire read is a real outcome and this case is its only home; the drawn half is structural. Neither opens `refusal.toolarge.png`, which stays cited as the frame the dump came from.

STRUCTURAL AND PERMANENTLY SO, and the reason is not a missing instrument. Its subject is the correspondence between the capture manifest and the artifacts on disk — a property of the EVIDENCE RECORD rather than of the product, so there is no product state a change could move and no rung on the ladder it could climb to. It is counted against the strict total rather than dropped from it, because a campaign that hid its own record-keeping checks from the denominator would be scoring itself on a smaller suite than it runs. Capture lineage over this flow's own wall of pictures. Each of the five rows in evidence/g17-document/captures.json names the campaign surface and the flow step it is of, carries the sha256 of the file on disk, and — for four of the five — names a string the PANEL draws which the assertion pass then reads back out of that frame's own dump. So a picture is tied to the package it is of independently of its filename. The fifth, refusal.toolarge, cannot do this and is NAMED rather than counted as corroborated: G17-L2 fails if that set is ever anything other than exactly it. DEF-060. Checks G17-L1, G17-L2.

subject.evidence: vacuous
subject.note: HISTORICAL FINDING (2026-08-29, source revision 83e5380): the following absence finding describes that revision, not the current production transport. I5 measured neither side implements a transport; the phone stores a paired-Mac record for a Mac it never contacted. RE-CLASSED `contradicted` -> `vacuous` on 2026-08-29 by K4, per references/effect-boundary.md SS2: contradicted means the product does the thing and does it differently from the document; vacuous means the product does not do the thing at all, so there is nothing for the constraint to be true or false about. The two want different remedies and reading them as one sends a missing subsystem to the place that fixes a wrong one. SS3 names this row's exact shape -- a requirement whose declared effect class has no provider in production source is vacuous at phase 1, before any test is written. MEASURED AT `83e5380`, and the narrow true thing rather than the general one (SS7: absence is a fact about this commit). `PairingService` has exactly ONE conformance in production source, `public struct FixturePairingService: PairingService`, `app/Sources/MCPRouterKit/Pairing/PairingService.swift:31`; the shipped shell wires it by default, `pairing: any PairingService = FixturePairingService()`, `app/Sources/MCPRouterUI/Phone/PhoneShell.swift:63`. No `URLSession`, `NWConnection`, `NWListener` or `Network.NW` symbol appears anywhere under `app/Sources/MCPRouterKit/Pairing/` (9 files); the fourteen files in `app/Sources` that do hold one are OAuth, control-plane, registry and loopback-server code, none of it reachable from the pairing path. The protocol's own docstring states the decision rather than leaving it inferred: 'No live implementation ships in this item, and that is a decision rather than a gap.' SO THE CLAIM IS NOT BOUND, AND THE `provider` FIELD STAYS EMPTY DELIBERATELY. There is no symbol that opens the socket to bind it to. `vacuity-check.py --gate` therefore continues to report REQ-016 as uncensused, correctly, and that finding is a dispositioned expectation rather than a silence: it is the vacuity, visible. What the re-class buys is that `campaign.py check` stops counting REQ-016 as an effect somebody failed to witness -- `unwitnessed_effects` excludes `vacuous` (campaign.py:1099) -- and starts reporting it as the product gap it is. The remedy is to build the transport (I5, DEF-001) or to withdraw the requirement; neither is K4's.

subject.note: J2. The four Servers segments are pressed one at a time and the effect is read on THE ROWS THE TABLE DRAWS, not on the segment. `board.filter == .running` after `board.filter = .running` is the property the assignment just made — the same tautology as a button whose proof is that it now looks pressed. Both directions, on a population chosen so no two segments have the same answer: one plain running server, one plain idle, one running-and-placarded (which `Needs you` claims and `Idle` must not) and one idle-and-placarded (which both claim). The rows that survive are exactly the ones that match and the rows that vanished are exactly the ones that do not — a one-directional check passes on a filter returning nothing and on one returning everything. The four expected row sets are additionally asserted to be four DISTINCT sets, so a bar whose segments all led to one row set fails on the cardinality however green each individual check looked.

NO NUMBER THE ROUTER DOES NOT OBSERVE, CHECKED ON THREE BOARDS RATHER THAN ONE. The `no-memory-figure` and `no-saving-claim` checks are run per state precisely so a guardrail that held on one board and not another cannot pass on a single instance, but three boards are not nine.

K3. `Install` is driven at `DiscoverBoardModel.install` and the effect is read as the DECLARATION THE CLIENT RECORDED — name, command and args, checked against the row that was pressed rather than against the function that built them. N8. The inertness guard on the untrusted-input boundary, made capable of failing. M19 shipped `MarkdownSecurityTests.htmlIsInert` with four spellings that named `javascript:`, no scheme, or nothing, and two assertions -- no link, no `imageURL` -- that `MarkdownInline.sanitized` makes true of every input it touches. It could not go red. M30 wired `ControlAPICapabilityDocumentSource` into the shipped UI, so router-served third-party text now reaches this renderer in a Release build, and the guard on it measured nothing. MEASURED, not assumed: the platform parser does keep inline HTML inert -- under `MarkdownInline`'s own options it hands each tag back as characters and marks it `.inlineHTML`, an intent naming no destination, and it does so under all four combinations of `allowsExtendedAttributes` and `interpretedSyntax`. Swift 6.2, macOS 26.6.2 (25G83), Debug, `swift test`. So this was an evidence defect and not a live vulnerability, and the fix is the assertion rather than new sanitisation. Two `https` spellings were added, because `https` is the one scheme the allowlist keeps and therefore the only one that can carry an interpreted `<a>` through to the assertion; a presence control runs the same reader over the markdown twin of the same destination first; and two clauses were added that the old body did not have -- handed back verbatim, and no attribute beyond the `.inlineHTML` marker. That last clause also corrects the test's own claim: the parser DOES attach one attribute to inline HTML and `sanitized` carries it, so the old name -- `inline HTML acquires no attribute of any kind` -- was false as written as well as unfailable, which is why nobody found out.

ManifestIO.save(...)`. R10's brief declares it out of scope in those words - it has no output to contradict itself with - and that is still true. subject.note: SURF-029's two SecondaryCommands, 'Export log' and 'Reset router', were enumerated and unreached: a CommandBar does not realise its overflow items while the overflow is shut, so the at-rest lane could only record an absence with its reason, and planning/registry-drop-gate.py reported the surface as uncovered for exactly that. This case opens the overflow through ExpandCollapsePattern.Expand and reads both commands back with their names and ControlType.Button, between a BASELINE and a SILENCE that both find them absent from the control view AND the raw view. The writer is not the reader: overflow-actuate.ps1 expands in its own process and writes only the ExpandCollapseState it saw, while every element reading comes from uia-dump.ps1 started separately. TWO FINDINGS FROM THE FIRST RUN, neither planted, both corrected in the manifest rather than in the assertion. (1) probe-expectation.json predicted that opening the overflow would cost the never-activated guarantee, and IT WAS RIGHT: the probe held the foreground at none of the three baseline samples and at all six effect and silence samples, so Expand activates the window and Collapse does not hand the foreground back. That cost is now DECLARED as `overflow.activationCost` and compared both ways, so the day WinUI stops activating, this arm reddens rather than quietly acquiring a guarantee nobody re-checked. Baseline stays a hard assertion. (2) each command resolves to TWO tree paths with the overflow open, because WinUI publishes the OverflowPopup subtree once through a Microsoft.UI.Content.PopupWindowSiteBridge child and once in place beneath the ApplicationBar. Both copies agree on name, controlType, className, isEnabled, isOffscreen, accessKey, patterns and bounding rectangle, so it is one control on two routes; the assertion now permits several matches only while they agree on everything a caller would act on, and plant (H) watches that a genuinely different control under one id still fails. WHAT THIS DOES NOT BUY. It is not at-rest coverage and does not close DESIGN.md section 11 rule 9 for these two commands. The product fix is a surface that realises them without an actuation, and that is DEF-340. Neither command is INVOKED, so both stay outside the actuation census with a stated reason on SURF-029; this arm's subject is realisation and vocabulary, not effect. Re-rated from `structural-visual` to `source-analysis`: it reads source text and runs nothing, so it was never one rung below an effect — it is off the product ladder entirely, and `structural-visual` put it on that ladder where it read as movable. The rendered half of this claim is not missing: CASE-0011 (outcome, macos-glass) carries `Reset history…` in the predicate it asserts over the running Activity window, and evidence/ax/SURF-003.window.txt draws it. What is left here is the part no rendered assertion reaches — that the control is declared in `header` and not inside the rows conditional, which is a property of where the source puts it. A render proves the state it was taken in; this is the claim about the other eight, and the campaign has no empty-Activity dump to relate it against. PREVIOUSLY: DEF-016's affordance half and DEF-012's first rename, at the rung they honestly reach. `theResetActionIsInTheHeader` slices `ActivityBoard.header` from its declaration to `content`'s and asserts the slice carries `CleanupPresentation.resetLabel` and opens `model.sheet = .resetHistory`; `theHeaderLabelIsTheDesigns` asserts that constant is `Reset history…` per `prototype.html:716` and `:930`, not the Settings-Danger wording at `:999` the build had shipped. Recorded as `structural-visual` rather than `outcome` and counted against the strict total on purpose: both read source text, and no assertion here proves a header rendered. It is written that way because the claim is about the header in **all nine** DESIGN.md §5 states — the design puts the control outside the rows conditional precisely so the empty state has it — and a rendered assertion over one state would leave the other eight unchecked while buying effect credit. Watched to fail for real rather than by a staged arm: an earlier script aborted before writing the header change, and this assertion reported `the header draws no reset action` against the tree that was genuinely missing it. Reverting `resetLabel` reads `the header action is called Reset call history…`.

subject.note: DEF-011's affordance half, re-expressed against the running window rather than against `CleanupBoardRow.swift`. The source read asserted that the row declares `accessibilityElement(children: .contain)` and not `.combine`; what that modifier decides is whether each row's buttons are separately addressable, and relation `SURF-007/row-actions` in bin/glass-assert.py reads THAT off two dumps of a real window. Measured: 3 candidate rows in evidence/ax/SURF-007.window.txt and 5 in evidence/ax/SURF-007.cleanup-skills.window.txt, and all 8 own their own AXButtons one level below their own group — which a combined row cannot do, because combining flattens them into the group's label and publishes none. The action set is a function of the row and not of the board: exactly [Inspect, Remove…] on the 7 rows carrying no provenance note and exactly [Read first…] on the 1 that does. `metamorphic` rather than `structural` because the claim spans two different row populations: a column drawn at a fixed size fails the count and a combined row fails the ownership, and a single-window presence check can see neither. The Swift suite it replaces (app/Tests/MCPRouterUITests/CleanupRowActionsTests.swift) is kept and still runs — it is the faster signal — but it is no longer what this case stands on.

DEF-015's closed half — the shell's overflow treatment, which DESIGN.md §5 names and the build got wrong in a way no assertion could see. Every board's `AXSplitGroup` width is read back out of the running app and compared against its own `AXWindow` width, board by board, through the channel that already writes those dumps beside the pictures. It read 3 of 8 overflowing — Checks 988, Skills 1044, Discover 1119 inside a 980pt window, each origin moved left by exactly half its excess — and reads 0 of 8 after `.frame(minWidth: 0, maxWidth: .infinity, alignment: .leading)` on `ContentZone`. `outcome` rather than `raster-visual` on purpose: the claim is a measured relation between two frames the app publishes, not a comparison of pixels, and the pictures are what made the defect *visible* rather than what proves it fixed. Armed 20 Aug 2026, three ways on the gate and two on the test. The gate exits 1 against the pre-fix dumps, 0 against the post-fix ones, and 1 with no dumps at all — `examined=0` is a check that never ran and is never a pass. Removing the modifier reddens `ShellDetailWidthTests` with `passes its boards' minimum width up to the split view`, and dropping just `alignment: .leading` reddens the second half alone. That test's first version did NOT bite: it searched the raw source and matched the doc comment naming the modifier, so deleting the modifier left it green. Comments are stripped before matching now — a predicate satisfied by the prose explaining it is not a predicate. What this case does not cover, because `overflowing=0` reads like `nothing is clipped` and is not that claim: content that overflows the detail PANE stays inside the window and is invisible to this oracle. That half is CASE-0134, measured with a second probe against every leaf's right edge — and that probe was wrong on its first run, reading the frame's y where it meant x and reporting clipping on seven of eight boards. The Settings capture is whole, and looking at it is what caught it.

subject.note: REQ-019 on the one control that has to refuse: the skill row's `Remove…`. The control API is read-only for skills — removing one means writing files the client applications hold open — and the row does not hide the button or offer it and fail. It draws it disabled (AX enabled 0) and states that reason in its help text, which is the shape REQ-019 asks for: no success affordance for work that cannot happen, and the refusal is the server's own. Pixels: `SURF-007.cleanup-skills.png`, 519568 bytes, sha 94dd9d06f87d, window-scoped off CGWindowID 103249 owned by the launched pid, recorded in `evidence/shots/captures.json` with the scenario that produced it. Byte-identical across two consecutive capture runs. It does NOT claim agreement with the design of record: the reference is an HTML mock rasterised at another size, and no macOS API exposes a cross-process computed style.

CASE-0137's claim, rendered. That case reads `CleanupSheets.swift` and states in its own note that no assertion in it proves a sheet was drawn; this one presses `Read first…` on a running build and reads the sheet that opens. `axkit press` is background-safe on a SwiftUI Button — AXPress runs the action on the element and needs no focused scene — and it exits non-zero when the press does not take, so the sheet is photographed or reported uncaptured, never assumed. The AXSheet subtree carries the three observations `SkillProvenance` actually holds (`Where the router first saw it`, `Where it resolves now`, `The router first saw it`, each with its value), and the sentence that bounds them: `The router records where a marketplace resolves, never who owns it and never what changed inside it`. It states none of the four figures `prototype.html:1249` invents — `@jbailey`, `force-pushed`, `no longer in history`, `evals fail` — each checked by name. Frontmost was Ghostty before and after; the app was never activated.

The sheet's pixels: `SURF-007.provenance-sheet.png`, 633476 bytes, sha d48520a1a99d, window-scoped off the CGWindowID the launched pid owns, recorded in `evidence/shots/captures.json` with the `cleanupSkills` scenario that produced it and the title read back off the running app. The claim is that this surface exists as drawn output rather than as a view struct: an AXSheet at 512×416 inside the window, with the copy the case above enumerates. It does NOT claim agreement with the design of record, and here that is the point rather than a caveat — the design's version of this sheet states four things the router cannot observe, so agreement with it would be the defect.

REQ-019 where DEF-001 makes it matter: this build ships no pairing transport, and the sheet says so instead of drawing a code it cannot complete a pairing with. The AXSheet carries `Pair iPhone`, `Pairing is not available in this build`, and the sentence that keeps the reader from debugging their own network — `this build ships no way to listen for one. Nothing is wrong with your phone or your network.` The negative half is the one that would catch a regression: nothing in the window matches Crockford base-32 at the length REQ-015 specifies, checked by pattern rather than against a literal, so a code this predicate's author never saw would still trip it. This case does NOT make REQ-015 pass — CASE-0010 and CASE-0110 fail against it and keep failing. The sheet is honest about a capability that is missing; the capability is still missing.

The refusal's pixels: `SURF-010.build.png`, window-scoped off the CGWindowID the launched pid owns, an AXSheet at 512×173 over the Inbox window. Recorded in `evidence/shots/captures.json` with the title read back as Inbox — the sheet does not change the window title, so the manifest carries both the readback and the `app://mac/pairing` target rather than letting one stand for the other. This surface had no picture at all for three runs: the capture script pressed for a pairing control while the app was on the Servers board, where none exists, and recorded the surface unreachable for a reason that was its own navigation. Selecting Inbox first opened it on the first attempt.

The fixture half of CASE-0138/CASE-0139, checked in the harness rather than on glass. Those two photograph the Cleanup board drawing `Read first…` on one row and a disabled `Remove…` on the other; this asserts the fixture behind them actually contains one moved skill and one unmoved one, which is what makes the photograph a discrimination rather than a picture of whatever the fixture happened to hold. It also guards the reason the scenario is separate: `cleanupSkills` extends `populated` rather than editing it, because SURF-004's on-glass copy asserts the count `populated` publishes (`6 skills from 4 marketplaces · 1 held for review`) and a seventh row there would have broken an existing predicate. The test additionally asserts the servers half of the board survives the scenario, so a fixture that drew skills by losing servers would fail.

subject.cell: execution-plane=daemon · data-shape=one stdio upstream declared
subject.note: The router spawning a child process, seen by two parties that are not the router. `bin/witness-effects.sh` runs `MCPRouterCLI index --force` against a scratch home holding one stdio server, and records the pid the shell launched (`$!`) beside the pid the CHILD reports for its own parent through `getppid()`. The child writes that into a file whose path arrives in its environment and which the router never reads back, so neither record passes through the product. They agree: shell launched 30913, child 30920 names 30913. A ps(1) sample runs alongside and usually misses, because the index verb spawns, handshakes and exits inside one scheduling quantum; two earlier versions of this witness depended on ps alone and could report only that the child had A parent, not whose child it was. Armed: against a config declaring no servers the same recorder reports count=0, and against the populated one count=1 with the parents agreeing.

The half of REQ-028 the app's own menu will answer for. `scripts/acceptance/menu-reason-plane.sh` launches the Debug build with `open -g`, never activates it, and reads its real menu bar off the accessibility plane: 220 menu items, 11 of them carrying a reason ShellMenuReasons wrote, and every sentence one MenuCommandAvailability declares — the vocabulary is derived from the source file at run time rather than copied, so the two cannot drift. WHAT THIS DOES NOT CLAIM: it does not read the badge. SwiftUI does not publish an NSMenuItem's badge to this plane and this app's menu bar is SwiftUI's, which the same lane asserts and `menu-badge-lane.sh` measured first on a fixture. The badge's CONTENT follows from the reason through MenuReasonBadgePairingTests, which proves one reason never appears beside two badges; the badge as DRAWN is CASE-0197 and is unoracled. Armed: `menu-reason-plane-selftest.sh` hands each of the five assertions a doctored dump and requires it to fire, then requires none of them to fire on the dump today's platform produces.

THE OTHER HALF OF REQ-005: the router is not running, and it never has been. Arranged by NOT starting it, over a port the harness proved free first — a cold state cannot be arranged while something is listening, so `bin/forced-state.sh` refuses to run at all if http://127.0.0.1:8955 answers before it begins. Nothing has ever loaded, so `ServerStateTracker` is `.failed` rather than `.stale`, and the board may claim nothing at all. Five checks, four of them absences: the board draws `The router isn't running` — `ControlAPIError`'s own wording, not a paraphrase; it states no tools/servers total; it states no running count; the sidebar readout states nothing; and no server name is drawn for a router that has never answered. The last one is the one a fabricated zero would survive: `0 tools from 0 servers` is a figure nobody measured, and the header's three-case `Reading` exists precisely because a boolean once rendered it on every cold start. THIS CASE IS IN THE AX PLANE ONLY. The cold frame was refused by `bin/paint-check.py` for the reason CASE-0198 records in full, so there is no photograph of this state and none is claimed.

subject.cell: execution-plane=daemon · data-shape=a projection asked for over a harness tree the router must not touch
subject.note: NOTHING IS APPLIED, and it is measured on the filesystem rather than read off the reply. After the projection is requested the lane asserts that the deleted target is still absent, the live link is still present, `design-craft` is still a broken symlink, and the root still holds exactly two entries. A body carrying `applies: false` proves only what the router said about itself; these four assertions are what the harness tree says. The refusal is held mechanically as well: scripts/lint/no-harness-skill-writes.sh refuses a mutating call anywhere in the read-only seam, whatever the path was.

subject.cell: execution-plane=daemon · data-shape=the bundle path asked three ways: untokened POST, GET, tokened POST
subject.note: The verb IS the gate, and it is not describing a mutation. The bundle changes nothing. It is a POST because stage 2 of `ControlHandler.handle` gates the token on POST/DELETE/PATCH only, so the verb is the only thing deciding whether this router hands its whole diagnostic corpus — log lines included — to any unauthenticated caller that can open the loopback port, which per `ControlToken` includes a web page the user merely visits. All three answers are pinned — 401 untokened, 405 on GET, 200 on a tokened POST — so a later tidy-up that makes the verb 'correct' goes red rather than silently opening the route. The 200 is asserted beside the other two so they read as refusals rather than as an absent route.

Can every published glass capture be shown to have been written AT THE SHUTTER rather than afterwards? A manifest that post-dates its capture records what somebody believed, not what the channel did, so it is not lineage -- which is the finding `capture-lineage.py`'s RECONSTRUCTED pass raised against SURF-028 and which `bin/capture-manifest.py` closed on the derivation side. This is the ordering side: the gate requires each published row to carry `capturedAt`, `conditions.windowTitleReadback` and `conditions.cgWindowID`, none of which can be recovered after the fact, or an explicit `provenanceGap` saying that it cannot. WHAT IT DOES NOT PROVE, stated rather than folded in: it establishes that the row COULD only have been written by something standing at the shutter, not that it was. Only the capture channel writing its own row does that, which `bin/capture-mac-glass.sh` does and which no reader can verify from the artifact alone.

Written from the control census in scripts/windows/uia/shell-lane.ps1 section 3b, which runs out of process against the real shell binary in the interactive session. The ids and labels it asserts are READ OUT OF THE PRODUCT'S OWN SOURCE (SettingsPresentation.cs) rather than restated in the harness, so a rename moves the expectation with it instead of leaving the lane measuring a product that does not ship. Controls are addressed by AutomationId, never by name: a UIA name search returns the first element carrying that name anywhere in the tree, and this shell's menu bar already holds a 'Router' and a 'Help'. The lane recorded: Get-ScheduledTask reports no task at '\MCPRouter\WIN-SHELL Settings Witness (transient)' before the switch is driven, so the arms below measure THIS run's registration. THE RECORDER IS NOT THE WRITER, and on this row it is not even the shell: Get-ScheduledTask (ScheduledTasks module over the Task Scheduler WMI provider). That is what makes this row a claim about the MACHINE rather than about the application's own report of itself, which is the whole of DEF-087. WHAT IT DOES NOT SETTLE: that the registration fires at a real logon, and that a daemon executable resolves on an operator's machine - the lane points the shipped resolution at a witness task name and a witness executable of its own so it cannot disturb the operator's real registration. Both limits stay on DEF-087's resolution rather than being folded into this green. THE CALL THIS LANE MADE, which is what `actuates` is NOT for: the row was driven through System.Windows.Automation's TogglePattern.Toggle() from shell-lane.ps1. `actuates` carries the control the surface declares - DEF-080.

subject.cell: execution-plane=windows-host - modality=operating-system crash record - data-shape=one deliberate fail-fast
subject.note: A REAL STATUS_STOWED_EXCEPTION, raised on demand, and what the XAML handler did about it - DEF-086. That row said this repository had no way to raise one: the original Skills crash was removed by DEF-077 and DEF-078, and a cross-ABI fault was not something product code could ask for. It turned out the lane already raised one without recognising it. An UNGUARDED throw from a DispatcherQueue callback - `--fault dispatcher --fault-unregister dispatcher`, which is DEF-085 as found - terminates MCPRouter.Shell.exe with WER Application Error 1000, exception code 0xc000027b, faulting module CoreMessagingXP.dll, fault offset 0x0000000000093b76. WHAT IT MEASURES: on that same run the region of shell-startup.log ends at `fault: injecting dispatcher` with nothing appended, so Microsoft.UI.Xaml.Application.UnhandledException does not see this class. DEF-079's mechanism field guessed exactly that and recorded it as unestablished; it is established now. THE RECORDER IS NOT THE WRITER, twice over: WER is written by the operating system after the process is gone, and it is read here through Get-WinEvent over the Windows Application log, which is a different API from the file the shell appends to. THE CONTROL: the guarded run of the same fault leaves no Application Error at all, so the record is the injection's rather than something this machine produces anyway. WHAT IT DOES NOT SETTLE, and this is the narrower thing rather than the wider claim: what matches the Skills crash of 2026-09-02 is the exception code, the faulting module and the fault offset - identical to the Application Error entries this machine still holds from 18:57:35 and 19:03:30 that day - and NOT a stack. This case says this host raises the same stowed-exception fail-fast and that the XAML handler does not catch it. It does not say the original throw took the identical path; DEF-077 named that throw and fixed it.

The 3 that remain: fixture-registry-search is a STANDING EXCLUSION nobody is working on; control-auth-post-http needs D-p1-a; install-launchd-watch is held blocked deliberately, because its `reran` term reads yes on 2 of 6 decoy trials where no stimulus can reach the watched path, so agreement on it is not evidence of parity. Two real-work rows therefore stood between 80 and the owner's 82/83 cutover target. Not a product UI defect. **CLOSED 20 Aug 2026.** Both closed the same day and both were merged into main: `install-launchd-watch` by ai/p8, which replaced the `reran` term with one a lane was shown able to fail on, and `control-auth-post-http` by ai/p7, which built a real OAuth client and agrees with the reference across the discovery cascade, the registration bytes, the PKCE parameters, the token exchange, the callback page, the credential file and the re-authorization branch — 21 checks, examined=21 failures=0. `parity-gate.sh` on main at e5755d0 then read 82 of 83 proven, 0 DIVERGED, 1 blocked, and that one is `fixture-registry-search`, the standing exclusion REQ-014 names. The gate still exits 1, because it exits 1 while any row is blocked and it says so: `82 proven is at or past the target of 82. That is a count, not a licence.` Flipping the installer is the owner's call on R4-C's evidence and is not this defect. subject.detail: prototype.html routes ?pane=evals and titles the board Evals; the running app's window title reads back Checks. Found by capture-lineage's tie pass, which refused a capture whose recorded target did not resolve to the surface's route. The rename went one way and the design of record was not followed.
subject.text: WITHDRAWN 20 Aug 2026 — this was not a product defect. It was recorded as "prototype.html routes ?pane=evals and titles the board Evals; the running app's window title reads back Checks". The second half is false. `prototype.html:600` declares the sidebar entry as `{id:'evals',t:'Checks',ic:'evals'}` — the route **id** is `evals` and the **title** is `Checks` — and the board's own header draws the selected suite (`pr-summariser · 8 cases`) rather than a board name at all. So the design of record titles this board Checks, the app titles it Checks, and there was never a rename to follow. WHAT ACTUALLY HAPPENED is a detector artefact, and it is worth keeping for that: capture-lineage's tie pass refused a capture whose recorded target did not resolve to the surface's title, and the target it held was the route id. An id and a title are different fields that the design is entitled to disagree on, so a tie pass that compares one to the other reports a rename wherever a route is not named after its board. Checked against the other seven boards: no second instance, because every other route id matches its title. Closed rather than deleted, so the next reader meets the artefact rather than rediscovering it.
subject.title: a route id was compared against a board title, and they differ in the design itself

subject.text: Measured 20 Aug 2026. `make test` failed with 4 issues at a one-minute load average of ~700 and passed all 1473 tests in 179 suites at load 46, on the same source, minutes apart. The four were `ActivityReconnectTests` (`a reconnect over a feed that stays live releases its guard`), `DiscoverBoardTests` (`client.searchQueries.count` reading 1 where the baseline said 2), and `SettingsAndMenuBarTests` twice (`model.trackerState` still nil). An earlier run at the same load failed only the first, so the set was not stable either — which is what separated this from a product defect. A suite that reports a defect the product does not have is the failure this campaign has already paid for once, in DEF-029, where a dead instrument read as a dead product for ten consecutive runs. CLOSED by making each wait a condition rather than a deadline, at three sites: 1. `ShellTestSupport.waitUntil` — ceiling 5s → 30s. It returns the moment the condition holds, so a passing test pays nothing for the larger bound; the bound exists only so a condition that never arrives fails instead of hanging. Five seconds was inside the scheduling noise of a contended host, which is the whole finding. 2. `ActivityReconnectTests.completes` — 2s → 30s, same argument. The defect it bounds is a call that *never* returns, so it exhausts any budget and a generous one costs only the time a genuine hang takes to report. 3. `DiscoverBoardTests.searchIsDebounced` — a fixed sleep replaced by two waits, because the claim has two halves and one sleep proved neither on a slow host. First a bounded wait for the debounce to fire at all; then a full debounce window of quiet with the count still at one, which is what rules out one request per keystroke. The second is a real quiet period rather than a deadline, so load cannot shorten it into a false pass — the wait on its own is satisfied by the *first* request and would pass against exactly the defect this test exists to catch. Armed 20 Aug 2026, all three, each watched to fail with its own message: `waitUntil` at `.seconds(0)` reads `no poll ran at all`, `the poll died with the scene that started it` and `five keystrokes issued 0 requests`; `completes` at `.milliseconds(1)` reads `reconnect did not return while the feed stayed live`; and a `queryChanged()` inserted inside the quiet period reads `a later request arrived: five keystrokes issued 2 requests in total`. The original trigger is not reproducible on demand from here — the load came from another project's Rust test binary, two node processes and `lsdiagnose` — so the fix is proven by the arms rather than by reproducing the contention.
subject.title: four async package tests asserted on a deadline the machine could miss

subject.text: Measured 20 Aug 2026 on two different worktrees the same afternoon. A fresh `git worktree` has no `node_modules` and no `dist`; `parity-selftest` is the last target `make all` runs, and its own environment check therefore fires only after lint, both builds, 1483 package tests, the iOS lane and the on-glass lane have all passed. Both runs came back `exit=2` on a tree where nothing was wrong with the code — roughly forty minutes each, twice. It is a lane defect rather than a product one, and the shape is familiar: the gate was honest (it said `the MCP SDK is not installed. Run npm install.` rather than skipping) and it was honest at the wrong moment. A check that can only fail on the environment belongs where the environment is checked. CLOSED by moving both checks into the `tools` target, which `all` runs first: `node_modules` must exist, and `dist/index.js` must exist because without it `parity-lane-selftest` SKIPS, and a skip is not a pass. Each names the command that fixes it. Armed 20 Aug 2026 in a bare directory holding nothing but the Makefile: with no `node_modules` it exits 1 naming `npm install && npm run build`, and with `node_modules` present but no `dist` it exits 1 naming `npm run build` and saying why a skip is not a pass. Costs a millisecond on a tree that has both.
subject.title: the whole-repo gate discovered a missing environment forty minutes in, twice

subject.text: CleanupBoardRow carries three treatments for a skill row — the `Read first…` substitution when SkillChecks.originUnchanged fails, the skill-kind `Remove…` drawn disabled because the router removes servers and never files on disk, and the candidacy reason — and none of them had a rendered path in any configuration of the product. A skill is proposed for cleanup only when every readable client lacks it, and all six skills in SkillFixtures.populated are installed somewhere, so the Debug Cleanup board drew three servers and zero skills. Release reaches the branch only if a real user happens to hold an orphaned skill. CASE-0136 asserted the branch exists by reading CleanupBoardRow and said in its own note why it stopped there; what nobody could say was that a build had ever drawn it. Fixed in-campaign by adding a Debug-only `cleanupSkills` scenario and two SkillFixtures.uninstalled rows, kept separate from `populated` because SURF-004's on-glass predicate asserts the count populated publishes. No view code was touched and no assertion was weakened. Now photographed by CASE-0138/CASE-0139 and guarded in the harness by CASE-0144.

subject.source: app/Sources/MCPRouterKit/Control/Scenario.swift; evidence/runs/make-test-3.log (clean build, 1512 tests in 188 suites); app/Scripts/enum-layout-stamp.py; Makefile target enum-layout-stamp; evidence/runs/make-test-4.log
subject.text: Adding a 14th case to `Scenario` made `make test` fail with 31 issues, two of which cannot be true of the source: `Expectation failed: (… → .live) == (.live → .fixture(…cleanupSkills))` in ShellClientFactoryTests and TriageSourceGuardTests, both asserting a Release-posture guard that returns .live unconditionally. `git stash` of the two changed source files → 19 tests pass; unstash → the same failures return, which reads as a real regression. It is not. `Choice.live` is encoded in the spare inhabitants of `Scenario`'s tag, so a new Scenario case shifts that encoding, and stale MCPRouterUI object files compiled against the old layout compare a value that no longer means what they think. `rm -rf app/.build` then rebuild: 5/5 pass, then 1512/1512. The hazard for this campaign is the mirror case — a stale build can as easily produce a green — so any test evidence taken across an enum change is taken from a clean build. MITIGATED 2026-08-20: `app/Scripts/enum-layout-stamp.py` hashes the ordered case list of every enum in the package (212 of them) and removes `app/.build` when that hash moves; `make test` now depends on it. The stamp is the case lists rather than the source, so it holds still for an ordinary edit and for a `switch` over the enum — the false positive a naive grep for `^\s*case` would hit — and moves for an added or renamed case. Armed on all four: comment SAME, switch statement SAME, added Scenario case MOVED, renamed Scenario case MOVED, restore back to baseline. The SwiftPM behaviour itself is unchanged and still upstream; what is fixed is this repo's exposure to it.
subject.title: an incremental Swift build after adding an enum case reports impossible test failures

subject.detail: `campaign.py` keeps defects in `inventory.json` under a `defect` list, and `add` assigns the next id from that list. `defects.in.json` is an input file. Twelve defects found in the sittings of 19 and 20 Aug were written straight into the input file with hand-written ids taken from that file's own length, which had stopped tracking the registry at DEF-006. The result: DEF-007 through DEF-018 each named one defect in the registry and a different one in the staging file, and neither file said so. Visible symptom, and the only reason it was caught: `RUN-2026-08-20.md` contains 'DEF-011 is the finding worth acting on ... Cleanup's' at line 96 and 'DEF-011 - the rendered-quality gate has never been able to run' at line 481, in one document, meaning two unrelated things. This is `capture-lineage`'s failure mode moved from pictures to identifiers: a name binding to two subjects with nothing checking the binding. Fixed by renumbering the twelve staged defects to DEF-034..DEF-045, merging them into the registry, and rewriting the fifteen references that meant the staged numbering. Every renumbered record carries `stagedAs` naming its old local id, so a reader meeting the old number in an untouched artifact can resolve it. The remaining 74 references were checked one at a time and meant the registry defect they already named. A fourth lesson, from the third instance's cleanup rather than from the collision itself. Reconstructing the concurrent session's two entries welded `text: ""` and `note: ""` onto both, and the first renumbering pass then used `"text" in d` to tell the two writers' entries apart -- so the artifact defeated the discriminator that would have caught it. Both authors independently read the empty values as harmless because they carried no content. The hazard is shape, not content: a membership test reads a key's PRESENCE, and an empty string defeats `"text" in d` exactly as thoroughly as a populated one would. `campaign.py add` injects only `id`, `status`, `evidence` and `armed`, so that key-shape occurred on exactly the two reconstructed entries and was traceable; the keys were stripped and the pass re-run discriminating on `title`. Recorded because "empty therefore harmless" is a reasonable-sounding wrong answer that both sessions gave.
subject.note: SECOND INSTANCE, 20 Aug 2026, in the case registry rather than the defect registry, and it landed the same way. A helper reported `next case id: CASE-0145` while cases.json already held CASE-0149 and CASE-0150; campaign.py's own `next_id` is max+1 and would have said CASE-0151, so the number that was trusted did not come from it. `add` takes an explicit id through `setdefault` and therefore appends a second entry rather than refusing, so CASE-0149 and CASE-0150 each came to name two cases -- an iOS Settings structural case against REQ-005 and a RouterCore write-failure case against REQ-019 -- and the `set` calls that followed wrote onto the pre-existing pair. Caught by an evidence-existence audit rather than by any gate: the new cases printed `3 evidence` where two were supplied. Restored from `git show HEAD:` (both pre-existing entries are byte-identical to HEAD again, verified by dict comparison) and the new pair renumbered to CASE-0153 and CASE-0154. The registry is sparse -- 74 gaps between 1 and 152 -- so a free-looking number is not evidence that it is free, and only max+1 is. THIRD INSTANCE, the same evening, and this one had two writers rather than one. A second Claude session working the same campaign allocated DEF-047 and DEF-048 at about 23:30 (the SDK -32603 message discard, and a detector defect in vacuity-check.py's blind pass) and committed planning/test-campaign as a directory in 6bdeea4, which also swept up this session's in-progress registry edits. This session allocated DEF-047 and DEF-048 for different defects minutes later, from a read taken before that commit landed. Resolved by renumbering THIS session's pair to DEF-049 and DEF-050 -- the later allocation moves, and the session that moves is the one that can enumerate its own references, which is the only reason the choice is safe rather than arbitrary. The peer's entries were not edited. Note for anyone reading the mechanism: `add` assigns from the registry list, so two writers holding a stale read get the same number, and no gate in the campaign detects it. The detection here was a peer message, and before that an evidence-existence audit; neither is a gate. campaign.py could refuse an explicit id that already exists -- `add` currently takes one through `setdefault` and appends a duplicate instead.
subject.title: the campaign's own defect ids named two different defects each, because the staging file numbered from its own length

subject.detail: DETECTOR DEFECT, recorded so its numbers are not published as product findings. `vacuity-check.py`'s `blind` pass asks whether any READER appears after the last MUTATING call in a test body, both matched by name prefix. Run with the shipped defaults it reports `examined=1820 mutating=3 blind=3` — and all three are false: DEFAULT_READERS is snake_case (`load_`, `get_`, `read_`, `list_`) while this is a camelCase Swift codebase, so NO Swift reader can ever match, and the three `mutating` hits matched the token `restart` in their own function names. Both flagged WatchRestartTests cases read extensively after the mutation. Run with a hand-derived camelCase verb list it reports `examined=1834 mutating=258 re-read-after=158 blind=100`. Two of the flagged real tests were read in full and BOTH re-read: `undoRestoresTheItem` calls `queue.all()` three times after `model.remove(...)`, and `resetReindexesAnIndexFailure` reads `client.calls` after `board.reset(...)`. Neither `all` nor `calls` was in the list. Of the 20 findings the script prints, only 6 are `@Test` functions at all; the other 14 are test doubles and helpers, because the population is every `func` in any file with `test` in its path. CONCLUSION: on this codebase the pass measures the verb list rather than the suite, and no verb list derived by hand is evidence of anything. It is recorded, not published, and the campaign claims no blind-mutation number. The pass's other two arms — `unclassed` and `uncensused` — are exact and are kept. ADDRESSED UPSTREAM in 0.9.2, confirmed by running it 21 Aug 2026. Commit 28ecd67 (`the blind-mutation check was measuring itself`) fixes four detector defects that each RAISED the blind count, and the pass now prints the vocabulary it used above its findings -- `vocabulary: defaults + campaign.blindVocabulary — 22 mutator(s), 20 reader(s)` followed by the reader list -- which was this defect's complaint: a number published without saying what configuration produced it. The denominator also moved, 1841 to 1657, because fixture helpers are no longer counted as tests. Left open rather than closed: the residual named on DEF-040 sits in the same pass. SUPERSEDED 21 Aug 2026 by DEF-055. The specific claim here — snake_case DEFAULT_READERS against a camelCase Swift codebase, giving examined=1820 mutating=3 blind=3 with all three false — was resolved by declaring campaign.json's blindVocabulary, which 0.9.2 reads. The general claim, that no hand-derived verb list is evidence of anything, is not resolved; it is now MEASURED rather than asserted. DEF-055 carries that measurement (7 of 7 sampled findings false, four named mechanisms, a two-way arm) and is the entry to read. Recorded as superseded rather than closed: the finding was real and its successor is open.
subject.title: test-campaign 0.9.1's blind-mutation pass is dominated by its own verb configuration on this codebase, in both directions

subject.note: `#expect(result.tools != nil, ...)` at ShellTests.swift:133. `ReindexResult.tools` is a non-optional `Int` (MCPRouterKit/Control/Models.swift:263), so the comparison could not fail. The Swift compiler emitted `comparing non-optional value of type 'Int' to 'nil' always returns true` on every build of the test target; it was the only such warning in the suite. The intent was stated in the comment directly above it -- `.success` is distinguished from `.populated` by `a reindex that comes back with no error and a tool count` -- so the assertion was one character from doing its job. Repaired to `result.tools == 14`, the value FixtureControlAPIClient+Writes.swift:33 overrides for `.success`, which discriminates against the base `reindex-failure.json` fixture it starts from (`{"tools":0,"error":"fetch failed"}`). Armed in evidence/arming/CASE-0152.arming.log: with the override changed to 0 the assertion goes red (`(result.tools -> 0) == 14`), and the log records that the pre-repair form would have stayed green under the same mutation.
subject.text: A ShellTests assertion on the `.success` reindex scenario compared a non-optional Int to nil, so it was always true and read nothing.

subject.detail:
DETECTOR DEFECT in test-campaign 0.9.1, found 20 Aug 2026 by the concurrent session at uds:/tmp/cc-socks/9881.sock and confirmed here against the artifact rather than against a model of it. The string `defect` does not appear as a registry key anywhere in evidence-page.py; measured with grep, zero occurrences. Its `

Defects

` at line 521 renders `[c for c in cases if state_of(c.get('status')) == 'fail']` -- failing CASES -- and the nav counter at line 305 is `counts['fail']`, the same population. So the page's Defects section counts 3 (the failing cases CASE-0010, CASE-0040, CASE-0110) while inventory.json holds 11 open defects, and the two numbers are about different things. MEASURED against the regenerated 124100-byte evidence.html: of the 11 open defects, 8 appear ZERO times -- DEF-008, DEF-040, DEF-041, DEF-042, DEF-043, DEF-047, DEF-048, DEF-051. The 3 that do appear are there by accident of prose: DEF-001 in two failing case notes and one passing one, DEF-033 and DEF-049 each inside a single PASSING case's note, rendered by the per-case table rather than by the Defects section. The peer reported 11 invisible; the true figure is 8, because writing a defect id into a case note is a convention doing a gate's job and it happened to fire three times. `campaign.py check` also exits 0 with all 11 open, so no gate holds on the registry either. This is the skill's own first-named failure mode -- covering a subset and reporting it as the whole -- arriving in its publisher: the gated half of the campaign is sound and the ungated half is the half people look at. The fix belongs in the installed skill (render inv['defect'], and count open defects in the nav), not in this repo; recorded rather than patched, precedent DEF-048 and DEF-051. SECOND PUBLISHER, same root cause, measured here: `campaign.py`'s own ledger writer (campaign.py:1210-1240) loads `inventory` and never reads `inventory['defect']` either, so ledger.md names zero defects across its 83 lines. Its header line is sharper than an omission -- it prints `73 pass . 3 fail . 0 skip . 4 n/a . 0 open . armed 73/73`, where `0 open` is the count of open CASES, on a campaign holding 12 open defects. A reader who takes that line at face value reads a campaign with nothing outstanding. ledger.md is generated rather than hand-kept, so it cannot be corrected in this repo: a fix that patched only evidence-page.py would leave the ledger short, and both publishers need to read the registry.
subject.title: evidence-page.py and campaign.py's ledger writer both skip the defect registry, so no published artifact lists a defect

subject.text: Measured by R27 on 2026-08-29 against the daemon on a scratch home. A server whose command exists and exits immediately (a shell that returns 17) is acquired for the full startupTimeoutMs and then reported as 'did not initialize within Nms': with the budget at 3000ms the probe took 3.15s wall clock. A server whose command does NOT exist fails in 0.01s, because the spawn itself throws. So the cost is specific to a child that spawns and dies, and the reason is that the handshake races connect() against a timer with no third branch for 'the process exited' - nothing watches the child's termination during startup. NOT FIXED HERE, and the reason is a boundary rather than effort. The race lives in StdioUpstreamTransport, which is the reference-diffed startup path R2 owns and R4 compares; adding an exit branch would change how this router reports a failure the reference reports differently, which is a parity decision and not a health-check one. R27's own bound is deliberately narrower - probeTimeoutMs covers the tools/list request so that 'the child never started' and 'the child answered too slowly' stay different answers - which means the budget that governs this arm is the upstream's startupTimeoutMs, and that is stated on the record rather than hidden. WHAT IT COSTS TODAY: a manual probe of a crash-looping stdio upstream blocks for the default 60s, and the caller has no way to shorten it except by setting that server's startupTimeoutMs. scripts/acceptance/r27-health.sh sets 1500 on its flaky fixture for exactly this reason, and says so. 2026-10-19 — FIXED IN BOTH ROUTERS by merge 02d764b0 (Merge ai/stdio-exit). A child that exits before initializing now fails at once, naming its status, instead of waiting out startupTimeoutMs. Unit evidence: RealProcessStartupTests (app/Tests/RouterCoreTests/RealProcessStartupTests.swift) and test/stdio-exit.test.ts. Verified 2026-10-19: the `Real child processes — startup` suite passed under `swift test`, and `node --test` on test/stdio-exit.test.ts passed. Status is fixed · in-test. No campaign re-run is recorded against this row, and the R27 wall-clock probe has not been run again against it.

subject.text: Found while building R22's redactor, filed rather than fixed. `Describe.row` emits `command` and `args` RAW, and `ControlHandler.gate` reads the token only for POST/DELETE/PATCH, so the complete command line of every stdio upstream is readable by anything that can open the loopback port. The same function is careful in the adjacent case — it emits `envKeys` and `headerKeys` and never a value, with B10's reasoning attached — so argv is the one credential-carrying position on that route that is published whole. It matters because argv IS a credential channel: `--token=`, `--api-key=` and a connection string with an inline password are ordinary MCP server invocations, and R22 scrubs args for exactly that reason. The exposure predates R22 and is not made worse by it: the bundle's args go through the value scrub, and this route's do not. NOT FIXED HERE, and the reason is a parity decision rather than effort. `GET /servers` is reference-diffed — `control-servers-get` in planning/parity/surface.tsv, verdict `proven` — so redacting args moves a surface R4 compares byte for byte, and the ungated GET is itself a ported defect this repository records rather than silently repairs. Closing it means changing both routers or declaring a divergence, and that is the owner's call. 2026-10-19 — FIXED IN BOTH ROUTERS by merge 74d15306 (Merge ai/argv-redact), whose subject records that GET /servers stops publishing secret-bearing argv. Unit evidence: ArgvRedactionTests (app/Tests/RouterCoreTests/ArgvRedactionTests.swift) and test/argv-redact.test.ts, with parity vectors in argv-redact.json. Verified 2026-10-19: the `ArgvRedactionTests` suite passed under `swift test`, and `node --test` on test/argv-redact.test.ts passed. Status is fixed · in-test. No campaign re-run is recorded against this row.
subject.title: GET /servers discloses every stdio upstream's full argv to an unauthenticated local caller

subject.evidence: `PREVIOUS = "HEAD:planning/test-campaign/bin/control-census.py"`. The arm's whole claim is a DIFFERENCE - six plants that redden this branch's census and are silent on the one it replaced, and two DECLARED SILENCES where the old census is red and the new one is deliberately not. That holds while the new census is UNCOMMITTED, which is the state wd3 wrote and watched it in, and it reported 8/8 correctly. Once the commit that earns it lands, `HEAD:` resolves to the NEW census and the arm compares the file with itself. Measured on the merged tree at 07d347c7 before the fix: all six EFFECT plants read `previous census exit 1 red`, the three that were the point - DEF-131's own exhibit among them - stopped being differences, DEF-420's given-up coverage read as no loss, and the arm exited 1 reporting its own collapse.

subject.evidence: `discover()` reads the git INDEX through `git ls-files` and separately walks the DISK through `os.walk` + `os.path.relpath`, then names the difference as briefs the gate did not read. `git ls-files` prints POSIX separators on every platform; `os.path.relpath` prints the platform's. On Windows the two sets therefore never intersect and the difference is the WHOLE corpus. Measured before the fix on this branch: the same run printed `brief discovery read 226 items of the git index ...; kept 219` and, four lines later, `219 brief(s) on disk are NOT in the index and are outside this verdict`, listing ten of them and `... and 209 more`. Both sentences cannot be true. The verdict and the partition were correct throughout - it is the accounting sentence above them that was false.
subject.title: brief-target-gate reported every tracked brief as one it had not read, so a genuinely untracked brief was one line inside a list of 219

subject.detail: Measured 2026-08-27 by G16 while enumerating SURF-026, and independently by G15. M15 made Settings a Scene and removed the case from `Destination`, and capture-mac-glass.sh still ran `axkit select Settings`. That select fails — `axkit: no sidebar row starting 'Settings'` — the app stays on whichever board the loop visited last, and the shutter filed THAT board's pixels under SURF-011: byte-identical to the Cleanup board on one loop ordering and to the Insights board on another. THE CAMPAIGN'S OWN INSTRUMENTS CAUGHT IT FROM TWO DIRECTIONS, which is the part worth keeping. glass-assert.py's raster uniqueness check went red because two cases shared a sha256; `--discriminate` reported the neighbouring board's predicate wrongly accepting SURF-011's dump, because that dump IS the neighbouring board; and the capture manifest's readback recorded the picture's target as the neighbour's route under subject SURF-011, contradicting its own filename. FIXED HERE, NARROWLY: the capture script now refuses to photograph a select that did not take, and says which board the window is actually showing. That is the script's own standing rule rather than a new one — it already declines to substitute a picture for the pairing sheet and the status item, and its header records the run that filed the Inbox board as SURF-010. The title and the dump are still written from what the app is really showing, so the failure stays visible downstream; what is withheld is the photograph, because a misattributed picture is the one artefact nothing downstream can correct. STILL OPEN, and deliberately not fixed here: 1. SURF-011 has no route to the Settings SCENE. It needs Cmd-comma or the app menu, not a sidebar select that cannot succeed. CASE-0016 and CASE-0111 fail until it does. 2. THE MENU MAP IS PRE-M22. Committed SURF-001.menu.txt binds Cmd-4 to `Discover`; the running app binds Cmd-4 to `Harnesses`, exactly as Destination.selectionDigit declares (activity 1, servers 2, skills 3, harnesses 4, discover 5, inbox 6, evals 7, cleanup 8, insights 9). glass-assert.py's SURF-001 `menu` dict is the old map, so CASE-0001 asserts five bindings this build does not have. Correcting it is editing an assertion to restore a green, which this campaign forbids — it is owed as its own item, from Destination.selectionDigit rather than by hand. WHY IT IS THE SAME FINDING AS G14'S, ONE LAYER DOWN. G14 found the surface LIST had stopped growing while the product did. This is the EVIDENCE not having been re-taken since the build moved: the committed glass artefacts were last written on 20 Aug by cef3729, before M22 added two destinations and renumbered four accelerators. In both cases a completeness gate reported clean because what it measured was a stale artefact rather than the product. CLOSED ON THE EVIDENCE SIDE, 2026-08-27 (G21/G29). The frame this defect produced was still published: `inventory.json` gave SURF-011 the shot `evidence/shots/SURF-011.build.png`, and at `519aebc` those bytes were the Insights board. `capture-lineage.py --gate` reported it UNTIED because the capture step's own row said `target: app://mac/insights` while the filename said SURF-011 -- the manifest was right and the wall was wrong. Two moves, both provable from git. The Insights frame is renamed `evidence/shots/DEF-059.insights-filed-as-SURF-011.png`, keeping every capture-time field, so the defect keeps its exhibit and no filename match can offer it to SURF-011 again. The Settings capture it overwrote is restored to `SURF-011.build.png` from `cef3729`, TOGETHER WITH ITS MANIFEST ROW from the same commit -- the last commit where those bytes and that row agreed (sha 3b5a26ef, `target: app://mac/settings`, readback `Settings`, 2026-08-20T11:32:58Z). Restoring the pair from one commit is a recovery of a capture-time record; restamping the row against the new bytes would have been the manifest-after-the-fact defect. What is NOT closed is the cause: `axkit select Settings` still fails, so the campaign still has no Settings capture newer than 2026-08-20 and the glass script still declines to take one. THE CAUSE NOW HAS A READER, 2026-09-02 (wa5). `axkit select Settings` still fails, and the campaign still has no Settings capture newer than 2026-08-20 -- unchanged. What has changed is that the age is no longer invisible: `bin/glass-build-gate.py` reports `evidence/shots/SURF-011.build.png` and `evidence/ax/SURF-011.*` as STALE against the build this tree would produce, so the lane cannot be green over them again without somebody re-taking them. `bin/capture-mac-glass.sh`'s refusal to photograph a select that did not take is the other half and is unchanged. Both halves of the remaining work -- a route to the Settings SCENE, and the re-capture -- are macOS work and are not attempted here. CLOSED 2026-10-19 on glass. capture-mac-glass.sh opens Settings with ⌘, (backgrounded), selects the Router pane in the Settings window's own source list, photographs that window as SURF-011 (target app://mac/settings), dumps the Security pane as a second dump of the same surface, and closes the window. glass-assert at the current build: checked=435 failures=0; --decoy SURF-011 reddens 6.
