subject.detail: Measured 2026-08-27 by G15, while enumerating SURF-025. The committed glass evidence under planning/test-campaign/evidence/ax was last written by commit cef3729 on 20 Aug. M22 then added two destinations and RENUMBERED four accelerators, and nothing re-took the pictures. Running bin/capture-mac-glass.sh against the current build turns four previously-passing cases red, and in every one of them the PRODUCT is right and the recorded evidence is stale: 1. THE MENU MAP. Committed SURF-001.menu.txt binds Cmd-4 to `Discover`; the running app binds Cmd-4 to `Harnesses`, exactly as Destination.swift's selectionDigit declares (activity 1, servers 2, skills 3, harnesses 4, discover 5, inbox 6, evals 7, cleanup 8, insights 9). glass-assert.py's SURF-001 `menu` dict is the pre-M22 map, so CASE-0001 asserts five bindings the shipped build does not have. 2. SETTINGS IS NOT A SIDEBAR ROW. M15 made Settings a Scene and removed the case from Destination, and capture-mac-glass.sh still does `axkit select Settings`. That select now fails — `axkit: no sidebar row starting 'Settings'` — the app stays on Cleanup, and the script photographs the CLEANUP board and files it as SURF-011. CASE-0016 and CASE-0111 fail against it. THE CAMPAIGN'S OWN INSTRUMENTS CAUGHT BOTH, WHICH IS THE ONE GOOD PART. The capture manifest's readback records that picture as target `app://mac/cleanup` under subject SURF-011, contradicting its own filename — the exact mechanism the script was rebuilt around. Independently, glass-assert.py --discriminate reports LEAK SURF-007 wrongly accepted 1 of 8 foreign board dumps: SURF-011 — because SURF-011's dump IS the Cleanup board. Two instruments, one cause. WHY THIS IS THE SAME FINDING AS G14'S, ONE LAYER DOWN. G14 found the surface LIST had not grown since it was written. This is the EVIDENCE not having been re-taken since the build moved. In both cases a completeness gate reported clean because the thing it measured was a stale artefact rather than the product. NOT FIXED HERE, DELIBERATELY. G15's remit is the Harnesses enumeration, and correcting glass-assert.py's menu map or the Settings navigation would be editing an assertion to restore a green — even though the product is right, that is the move this campaign forbids, and the stale assertion is the instrument that found this. The four cases are set to `fail` with this id in their notes. Owed: re-map SURF-001's menu dict from Destination.selectionDigit, and give SURF-011 a route to the Settings SCENE (Cmd-comma or the app menu) instead of a sidebar select that cannot succeed. INSTRUMENTED 2026-09-02 (wa5), NOT CLOSED. The cause this row names -- a committed capture carrying no tie to the build it came from -- is now measurable. `planning/test-campaign/bin/glass-build-gate.py` binds every artifact the macos-glass lane cites to the git blob identity of the Mac app's build inputs (the set `scripts/acceptance/build-freshness.sh` compiles from) and exits 2 when that identity is not the one the lane is being read against. It is RED on this tree over all 56 artifacts, in 7 capture groups spanning 20-29 Aug: `evidence/runs/glass-build-gate.log`. The stamps it reads are marked `reconstructed-from-git` and are deliberately the weaker claim -- git can prove which commit last wrote each artifact, so the record establishes the build the evidence CANNOT BE NEWER THAN rather than the build it was taken from. `bin/capture-mac-glass.sh` now calls `glass-build-gate.py --emit` in the run that takes the pictures, stamping from the bundle's own CFBundleShortVersionString/CFBundleVersion and the `.mcprouter-build-stamp` the Makefile writes after `xcodebuild` exits 0, so a re-capture replaces each reconstructed row with a capture-time one. Watched both ways: `evidence/runs/glass-build-gate.selftest.log`, four arms, green over a current capture and red over a stale one, an uncovered one and an undatable row. Case CASE-0342. WHAT IS NOT SETTLED. The re-capture itself, which is the whole of what this defect asks for. It needs a macOS host with Xcode and a display server; the work above was done on Windows, where there is no Swift toolchain, no xcodebuild and no way to open the app's window. The four cases stay `fail` with `owed` recording the re-capture and its owner. The second half of the row -- SURF-001's menu map, to be re-read from `Destination.selectionDigit` rather than by hand -- is equally macOS work and equally untouched. Nothing here edits an assertion, a stamp or a recorded identity to restore a green.

subject.detail: DETECTOR DEFECT in test-campaign 0.9.2, found 21 Aug 2026. attach-shots.py iterates every image under evidence/shots and assigns `hit['shot'] = rel` on each match, last write wins, with no preference for a build capture over a design render. This campaign keeps six directories under evidence/shots (16 root, 8 design-size, 16 fidelity, 9 ios, 17 mock, 11 mock-hidpi), so for SURF-001 the candidates in iteration order are SURF-001.build.png, SURF-001.shell.png, mock/SURF-001.png, mock-hidpi/SURF-001.full.png -- and the last one wins. MEASURED for SURF-001, SURF-002 and SURF-006: `--apply` would repoint each surface's `shot` from its build capture to `evidence/shots/mock-hidpi/SURF-00N.full.png`, which is the render of the DESIGN, not the build. That is the skill's own headline failure mode -- publishing a picture of one thing under the name of another -- arriving in a sibling of the plane built to prevent it, and it would do so while every other gate stayed green, because capture-lineage.py gates the 16 captures cited by CASES and the surface wall is a different population. The report compounds it: the UNCORROBORATED block prints surface ids (SURF-001 ... SURF-011) rather than the file each verdict is about, so a reader sees eleven surfaces apparently lacking provenance when in fact each surface's ACTUAL `shot` field points at a corroborated build capture and the complaint is about a mock render nobody intended to attach. Distinguishing the two costs a re-derivation of the matcher by hand. Recorded rather than patched, precedent DEF-048, DEF-051, DEF-052 and DEF-053. The campaign's standing refusal to run `--apply` here predates this and was based on the DEF-006 mis-wire; it now has a measured mechanism behind it. Separately closed while investigating: this campaign's design-size captures carried their provenance in a second manifest, evidence/shots/design-size/captures.json, in a different schema ({captures:[...]} against the root's bare list) that no gate reads. Its 8 entries were merged into the root manifest with `target` derived from the root's declared target for the same subject and corroborated by each capture's own windowTitleReadback -- Servers, Activity, Skills, Discover, Inbox, Checks, Cleanup, Settings, every one matching -- recorded at capture time, and each carries `targetDerivedFrom` saying so. That was the campaign's own inconsistency and is fixed here; it was not the cause of the 11. RE-MEASURED 2026-08-27 (G21) after `evidence/shots/captures.json` was made a derived file. The uncorroborated count is 12 and stays 12: SURF-001..011 and SURF-022. Eleven of them are this defect -- `mock-hidpi/` sorts last, so it is the row that decides each surface's `shotProvenance`. The mock rows in the manifest deliberately carry NO `target`; the address the channel was pointed at is recorded in full as `renderedFrom`, with an `attachHazard` field naming this defect. Measured both ways on this tree: writing that address as `target` instead drops the uncorroborated count from 12 to 1 and DISARMS `--apply`'s refusal, because `attach-shots.py` only checks the field is present and never compares it to the subject's route -- which is item 5 of X8's work order. So the report going quiet would have been this defect getting worse while looking fixed. The twelfth, SURF-022, is not this defect: see DEF-061.
subject.title: attach-shots --apply would attach the design mock render as the build's surface shot for 11 surfaces, and its report names the surface rather than the file

subject.detail: Measured 2026-08-21 against test-campaign 0.9.2 on app/Tests. The pass reports examined=1661 mutating=320 blind=88. Two structural errors and two idiom errors inflate that number. STRUCTURAL. (1) It scans every `func`, not every test. Restricted to swift-testing's own discriminator (a func whose nearest preceding annotation is @Test) the denominator is 1531, not 1661: 130 of the examined functions are not tests. (2) Its helper exclusion at vacuity-check.py:162 is file-scoped — a name is a helper only if called more than once in the file that declares it. A shared stub declared in TestSupport.swift and called from other files therefore reads as a test, so MemoryFileSystem's `write`, `removeItem` and `moveItem`, HTTPStub's `stop` and WatchTestSupport's `remove` are each counted as a blind test. 21 of the 88 are support-file functions. IDIOM, on the mutator side. (3) The lookbehind `(?<![A-Za-z0-9_])` cannot exclude a dot, so a Swift enum case constructor matches a mutator verb: `ServerRowAction.forServer(s, pendingAuth: nil) == .reset(.clearPlacard)` reports ServerPresentationTests::trippedOutranksHeld as mutating via 'reset', where `.reset` is the expected VALUE inside the assertion. 41 of 72 re-measured findings are dot-prefixed. (4) It takes the last mutator by source POSITION and calls everything after it the tail, which misreads three Swift constructs: a mutator inside the assertion (`await #expect(throws: Never.self) { try await store.delete() }` — nothing can follow it by construction), a mutator in a `defer` block (source-early, execution-last, so the whole test body reads as 'after'), and a mutator as the last statement of a loop body whose observation is the next iteration (CallbackLifecycleTests::stopReleasesTheSocket rebinds the port ten times; the read of cycle N is the start() of cycle N+1). SAMPLE. Of the 15 findings with zero assertions after the last mutator — the highest-yield stratum — 9 were read in full. Two (DiscoveryTests::servers, CapabilityPlateTests::install) are helpers. All 7 remaining are real tests that do observe after mutating, through idioms no reader verb names: `client.calls.last?.operation`, `seen.filter { ... }`, a rebind that throws. Precision on that stratum is 0 of 7. ARMED, two ways, evidence/arming/blind-mutation.arming.log. A probe @Test that mutates and never observes was added and removed: blind moved 88 -> 89 -> 88 and examined/mutating moved by exactly 1 each time. The check does bite; it is the false-positive rate that is at issue, not the sensitivity. NOT REMEDIED BY VOCABULARY. The reader side is deliberately loose because a false reader match suppresses a finding. Adding this codebase's read idioms (`calls`, `operation`, `filter`) would lower the number without improving what the pass knows, and the terms are generic enough to suppress true findings too. The 88 stands recorded as a worklist with its measured precision beside it rather than tuned to look better. RE-MEASURED 2026-08-27 by G22, which declared `testRoot` and gave this pass a corpus for the first time. THE 88 DOES NOT REPRODUCE. Vendored 0.9.2 over `app/Tests` today reports examined=2133 mutating=3 blind=3, against the 1661/320/88 above. The denominator moving up while `mutating` collapses 320 → 3 is not tree churn: 0.9.1 and 0.9.2 ship IDENTICAL DEFAULT_MUTATORS and DEFAULT_READERS, and neither list holds `reset`, `write`, `removeItem`, `moveItem` or `remove` — the verbs this entry's idiom argument turns on. So the 2026-08-21 sitting ran an expanded vocabulary passed on the command line, and `campaign.json` declares none, which makes 88 a figure no documented invocation returns. Its cited evidence, `evidence/arming/blind-mutation.arming.log`, has never existed on any branch of this repository (`git log --all -- '*blind-mutation*'` is empty), so the arming claim above is not checkable from the tree. The measured structural and idiom errors are not withdrawn; what is withdrawn is the population they were measured over. TODAY'S POPULATION, AND ITS PRECISION. With `testRoot: app` the pass reports examined=2179 mutating=3 re-read-after=0 blind=3, and 0.15.0 returns the same three findings from the same corpus. All THREE were read in full — 3 of 3, not a sample — and all three are false positives. Precision 0 of 3. A FOURTH CAUSE, NOT IN THE ORIGINAL ENTRY, AND THE ONE THAT PRODUCES TWO OF THE THREE. The body slice is `src[pos:end]` where `pos` is the start of the DECLARATION, so a test whose own name begins with a mutator verb matches itself. `WatchRestartTests::restartIsIssuedBeforeTheStagingWrite` and `::restartIsOwedBeforeTheWriteLands` contain no mutating call at all: the only `restart\w*\(` in each is `func restart…(` on its own declaration line. Both then read — `WatchWorld.read(scratch.logPath)`, `WatchState.load(path:)`, `WatchWorld.serverNames(in:)` — and assert on `state.mcpServersHash` and `state.restartPending`. The third, `PhoneStorageFailureTests::restartRechecksTheCamera`, does call `await model.restart()` and then asserts twice, on `model.step` and on `model.entry.characters`: property reads that no reader verb names, which is cause (4)'s shape rather than a new one. This cause survives into 0.15.0 unchanged. NOT ENROLLED IN A GATE, and `blindVocabulary` still not declared, for the reason the entry already gives. A related gap measured at the same sitting: pointed at `src/` — the TypeScript tree, which has no tests — the pass prints `corpus: … (0 file(s))` and `examined=0 mutating=0 blind=0` and contributes nothing to `--gate`. It reports its empty corpus and does not fail on it, so a mis-declared `testRoot` reads as a clean pass. VOCABULARY DECLARED 2026-08-29 by K4, and the entry's own 'NOT REMEDIED BY VOCABULARY' paragraph is narrowed rather than withdrawn. That paragraph reasons entirely from the READER side, and on the reader side it is still right: adding this codebase's read idioms lowers the count without improving what the pass knows, which is why the declared reader list stops short of `expect` and `require` -- swift-testing's assertion macros, 5781 and 383 occurrences, either of which would mark every test that asserts after mutating as re-reading and collapse the count to near zero while the pass learned nothing. THE MUTATOR SIDE WAS NEVER ARGUED, AND THAT IS WHERE THE PASS WAS BLIND. Measured over the same 2282 test bodies at `83e5380`: the nine snake_case defaults find 3 mutating call sites; a camelCase list derived from this corpus finds 481. So `blind=3` was a reading of 3 of 481, a recall of 0.6%, and the entry's `precision 0 of 3` was a precision over a population the instrument could barely see. `campaign.json` now carries `blindVocabulary` with `only: true`, 19 mutators and 34 readers, derived mechanically -- a verb is kept only where method calls on a receiver are at least half its corpus sites and its own `func` declaration lines at most a quarter, which is causes (3) and (4) of this entry turned into a selection rule. THE THREE FINDINGS ARE ADJUDICATED, and each clears for a different checkable reason rather than all three for one. `restartIsIssuedBeforeTheStagingWrite`: one fitted mutator, `WatchWorld.remove(scratch)` inside a `defer`, and four declared readers after it -- `load`, `read`, `parse`, `servers`. NOT blind, positively. `restartIsOwedBeforeTheWriteLands`: three fitted mutators, the last `WatchState(restartPending: true).save(`, with `load` after it. NOT blind, positively. `restartRechecksTheCamera`: ZERO fitted mutator call sites in its body. It was flagged only because `restart` is a shipped default and this entry's fourth cause -- the body slice beginning at the declaration -- made `func restartRechecksTheCamera(` match itself. `restart` fails the selection rule (1 method call against 3 declaration lines, of 5 sites), so it is not in the vocabulary and the finding is withdrawn. WHAT THAT DOES NOT MEAN: its real mutation `await model.restart()` is now invisible to the pass, and its reads are still the property comparisons `model.step` and `model.entry.characters` that no reader verb names. It is UNEXAMINED by this instrument, not clean, and that is this entry's ceiling stated once more rather than closed. ARMED, AND ENROLLED, which the entry recorded as missing. `planning/test-campaign/bin/blind-vocabulary-arm.py` runs on every `make lint`: two plants identical but for one line, each measured alone and again inside a `shutil.copytree` of the real corpus, requiring examined+1 mutating+1 blind+1 for the blind plant and examined+1 mutating+1 blind+0 for the reading one. The specificity arm is the half a sensitivity arm alone cannot give: a detector that flagged every mutating body would pass the first and say nothing. 6 of 6 as expected on `cache 0.16.0` and again on the `vendor/` pin via `--instrument`. The two disagree only on the denominator -- 2282 against 2277, the five arrow-style `it/test(` blocks 0.9.3 added block detection for -- and agree on blind=111. THE 111 IS A WORKLIST AND THE CAMPAIGN STILL PUBLISHES NO BLIND NUMBER. Nothing above touches the structural causes: the pass still examines every `func` rather than every `@Test`, its helper exclusion is still file-scoped, and a `defer` mutator still reads as source-early -- which is exactly why the first of the three findings above needed reading rather than counting. This entry stays OPEN; what it now carries is a measured recall beside its measured precision.

subject.detail: Found 20 Aug 2026 while building R8's gate against both routers. Against a fixture returning `-32603` with the message `Internal error: Authentication required`, the reference records `MCP error -32603: Internal error: Authentication required` and the Swift router records `[-32603] Internal error`. The upstream's own message is gone. CAUSE, cited exactly: modelcontextprotocol/swift-sdk 0.12.1, `Sources/MCP/Base/Error.swift:217-240`. The decoder reads the server's `message`, then maps the code — `-32700`, `-32600`, `-32601` and `-32602` each pass `unwrapDetail(message)`, and `-32603` alone passes `unwrapDetail(nil)`. `unwrapDetail(fallback)` returns `data.detail` when present and the fallback otherwise, so a server that answers -32603 with a message and no `data.detail` has its message discarded, and `Error.swift:91` renders `"Internal error" + (detail.map { ": \($0)" } ?? "")` as the bare canonical name. -32603 is the code servers use for an arbitrary application error, so it is the one that loses the most. TWO consequences: for the whole class of -32603 upstream errors the Swift router tells the user strictly less than the reference does; and R8's Swift half cannot detect a credential refusal at all, because there is no text left to match. This is a coverage gap in the parity suite as much as a defect in the SDK — no parity scenario had ever exercised a JSON-RPC error carrying a detailed message, which is why 82 proven rows never saw it. Remedies, none taken: report upstream and take a fixed release; pin a patched fork; or read the JSON-RPC error before the SDK types it, which needs a seam below the client.
subject.title: the Swift MCP SDK discards an upstream's error message for code -32603, so the router reports less than the reference does

subject.detail: parity-gate.sh, 20 Aug 2026 on main at e5755d0. The suite lane's citation run of scripts/acceptance/parity-oauth.sh exited non-zero and recorded `control-auth-post-http fail — the Swift router never reached the token endpoint`. The dedicated oauth lane, later in the same gate, ran the same script and recorded ok over 21 checks. The gate reported the row DIVERGED and printed 81 of 83. WHY IT IS UNEXPLAINED, established 21 Aug 2026 from disk without re-running anything. The run survives as evidence/runs/parity-gate-2026-08-20-oauth-flake.log, written 20:39:30. Its line 163 is the whole of what the citation run reported: `FAIL scripts/acceptance/parity-oauth.sh the gate reported findings`, and the next line is the following `ok` row. The script itself does not fail that quietly -- its failure branch (parity-oauth.sh:308-329) prints the POST /auth status, the browser hop, the tail of the router log and the first 20 requests the provider saw. Every one of those bytes existed and was discarded by the caller: `parity-suite.sh`'s `run_script` sent both streams to /dev/null at the time. So this defect is not a run that left no diagnostic, it is a run whose diagnostic the harness threw away, and no amount of re-reading the log can recover it. The instrument was repaired in commit 21d559b at 20:41:28 -- one minute and 58 seconds after this log was written, in the same commit that recorded the defect -- so `run_script` now keeps the log and prints its last 20 lines inline. A recurrence would therefore arrive with the cause attached. That is what closes this: the next occurrence, not more thought about this one. It stays open because there is still no cause and no reproduction; what changed is that the reason it could not be diagnosed is now known and no longer true. One candidate mechanism examined and NOT adopted. The R9 lane reported (21 Aug 2026, via uds:/tmp/cc-socks/9881.sock) that a stale $TMPDIR/mcp-router-parity.lock had made a gate fail its manifest-check for a non-real reason. That is a different symptom -- a manifest-check failure before the comparison, against this defect's completed run that reached `control-auth-post-http` and recorded a row -- and parity-oauth.sh takes that same lock at line 126 and preflights every port at 143-145, so the two lanes inside one gate could not have overlapped. subject.text: Observed once, in one of two whole-gate runs, and not reproduced by: a standalone run of `parity-oauth.sh`, a second standalone run of it immediately afterwards (which exercised the same port-reuse wait, 9s and 12s), a standalone run of `parity-suite.sh`, or a second whole `parity-gate.sh` on the same tree. The second gate reported 82 of 83, 0 DIVERGED, and its suite lane reported the citation clean. **What it is not.** The lane distinguishes an environment failure from a finding on purpose, and this was the finding branch: `record control-auth-post-http fail` at `parity-oauth.sh:329`, reached only when the reference side completed an authorization and the Swift side did not. An unbindable port exits 2 through `wait_for_ports_bindable` and records `blocked`, not `fail`, so the port-reuse race is ruled out by the code path that fired. **Why it went undiagnosed, and what changed.** `parity-suite.sh`'s `run_script` sent both streams to `/dev/null` and printed `the gate reported findings` — a verdict with no evidence under it. The bytes naming which guard failed had already been thrown away by the time anyone read the gate's summary. `run_script` now keeps the log, prints its last 20 lines inline and names the file it kept, armed 20 Aug 2026 against a deliberately failing citation. A recurrence will say which of the 21 checks went red. **Why the duplicate run stays.** `control-auth-post-http` is proven on the wire by its own lane and also cites the script, so the gate runs it twice. That is now documented in `parity-suite.sh` rather than deduplicated, because the duplicate is what caught this: a single run would have reported a clean 82 of 83 and nobody would have known. Both record under the same row id and a `fail` wins. **Burn-in, 20 Aug 2026: 8 standalone runs of the lane, all green, 21 checks each.** Three immediately after the failure and five consecutively afterwards, plus one clean whole gate. One failure in roughly ten whole-lane executions, cause unrecoverable because that invocation's stdout was discarded. A green burn-in does not close this: the original failure is uninspectable, so the runs measure only that the lane is not reliably broken. What would close it is a captured reproduction, or a stated gate met — several consecutive whole gates including the cold port-reuse path — decided as its own question rather than inferred from a streak, which is the `install-launchd-watch` mistake this repository already paid for once (G1: name a fix per term and fix a bound IN ADVANCE, never a green streak). Not a UI defect and not a blocker on the cutover count — CASE-0036's measurement is the second run — but it is an unexplained non-determinism in the router or the lane, and it is recorded rather than absorbed.

subject.note: A real MSIX, built, deployed and removed, with a recorder at each step that is not the thing that wrote it. MakeAppx packs and .NET's ZipArchive reads the OPC container back - so the identity assertion is made against the PACKED ARTIFACT rather than against the file on disk that was handed to the packer. `winget validate` is the winget client applying a schema this repository does not own. Add-AppxPackage deploys and Get-AppxPackage reports: Fledgeling.MCPRouter_0.1.0.0_x64__facmrsw33693e. THE INSTALL ARM IS WHAT TURNS A FILE INTO A PACKAGE. A manifest can pack cleanly, validate cleanly, and be refused at deployment for a capability, an architecture or a signature - and every static check in the world passes right up to that point. 'CLEAN UNINSTALL RULES' IS THE HALF WORTH READING TWICE. UninstallGuidance promises that uninstalling preserves %USERPROFILE%\.claude\mcp-router. That is a promise about what SURVIVES, and a promise about survival cannot be checked by any amount of reading - only by an uninstall that actually ran. The lane plants a marker, installs, removes, and requires both that the deployment stack reports the package gone and that the marker is still there. WHAT THE LANE PUTS BACK: a self-signed certificate is added to LocalMachine\TrustedPeople so an unsigned developer package can deploy at all, and removed in a finally block however the run ends. Verified afterwards: zero Fledgeling.* packages, zero witness certificates. A lane that left a trusted publisher behind would have changed what this machine will install, silently and for every future run. NOT SETTLED: that anyone can obtain the package. Nothing publishes it, the winget InstallerUrl is a deliberate example.invalid placeholder, and this lane asserts the placeholder is PRESENT so the manifest cannot be mistaken for a shipping one. subject.cell: execution-plane=windows-host - data-shape=one capability queued
subject.note: The COM activator the Windows notification platform wrote, read out of the registry by a process that did not write it. The writer is AppNotificationManager.Register() inside the shell; the recorder is HKCU through PowerShell's registry provider, and nothing of this repository's sits between them. Four arms. BASELINE requires the AUMID key to be ABSENT before the shell launches, so what the other three read is this launch. The three EFFECT arms read the key, the CustomActivator CLSID it names, and that CLSID's LocalServer32 - which came back as MCPRouter.Shell.exe carrying the platform's own ----AppNotificationActivated: argument, a string this repository does not write anywhere. THE ACTIVATOR IS THE ARM THAT CARRIES THE ITEM. A toast outlives the process that raised it; when somebody presses Review an hour later, Windows COM-activates the LocalServer32 registered for that CLSID. Without it the toast still appears and pressing it does nothing, which is the failure that looks most like success and exactly what a screenshot of a notification would have certified. WHAT THIS CASE DOES NOT SETTLE: that a toast is drawn, and that a press re-activates the app. Both need UserNotificationListener, whose capability is only grantable to a packaged application; DEF-082 carries them and is downstream of DEF-073. The shell's own report that the platform accepted a Show is carried in the evidence as writerSelfReport and is graded by nothing, because a process reporting its own effect is the shape of claim DEF-072 was about.

subject.evidence: scripts/windows/win22-toast-witness.ps1 witnesses the REGISTRATION and says so in its own notMeasured[]. Nothing here can press a notification button either. CORRECTED 2026-09-03: the packaging claim above is false on this host. subject.cell: execution-plane=windows-host - data-shape=a supervised process that dies
subject.note: The half of WIN23's supervision promise that had never been watched: a daemon the Windows task scheduler starts, loses, and starts again. DEF-081 filed it as unmeasurable and named the blocker as a missing Windows daemon binary; the blocker was real and is gone - app/windows/MCPRouter.Witness.Daemon is a harness process that starts, records its own start and waits to be killed, so there is something for the scheduler to supervise. WHAT THE MEASUREMENT FOUND IS NOT WHAT THE ROW EXPECTED. The registration the product wrote carried RestartOnFailure with a 60-second interval and a count of 3, and it did not restart the daemon at all. Killed, watched 150 seconds, on the unified scheduling engine and the legacy one, for a run started by a trigger and one started on demand: four registrations, no restart. The same block DID restart, three times at exactly 60 seconds, a task whose Command named a file that does not exist - so the instrument can see a restart, and RestartOnFailure governs a task that fails to LAUNCH rather than one whose action launched and later died. DEF-320 carries that, and the product now writes a Repetition on the trigger alongside MultipleInstancesPolicy IgnoreNew. THE RECORDERS ARE TWO AND NEITHER WROTE ANYTHING: Get-ScheduledTaskInfo for the scheduler's own account of its runs, and Get-CimInstance Win32_Process for the process identity, which is what makes 'it came back' a different process id rather than a report from the thing that came back. The daemon's own run log is carried and graded by nothing. EIGHT ARMS, THREE OF THEM ABOUT THE INSTRUMENT: BASELINE requires both tasks absent and no daemon running, so nothing below is inherited from an interrupted run; CLAIM.repetition and CLAIM.ignorenew read the product's own unmodified logon registration back through the WMI provider; SILENCE requires both recorders to say no once the tasks are gone. ONE SUBSTITUTION, SAID OUT LOUD: a trigger repetition does not apply to an on-demand start - measured, twice - so the live task carries a TimeTrigger where the product writes a LogonTrigger, because this lane must not log the machine out. Every Setting, the repetition interval, the principal, the action and the instances policy are the product's own document. That the trigger fires AT LOGON is still unwitnessed and DEF-081 keeps it.

subject.note: ControlAPIRequest.isMutating is POST || DELETE || PATCH, ported from src/control.ts, and PUT is not in it. The Insights board is reachable from the sidebar and the window title becomes its destination name — `axkit select Insights` actuated the row, `axkit title` read `Insights` back off the running app, and the capture manifest records target=app://mac/insights from that readback rather than from a filename. ADJUDICATED 2026-10-19 (glass-adjudicate): superseded. subject.note: HISTORICAL FINDING (2026-08-29, source revision 83e5380): the following absence finding describes that revision, not the current production transport. I5 measured neither side implements a transport; the phone stores a paired-Mac record for a Mac it never contacted. RE-CLASSED `contradicted` -> `vacuous` on 2026-08-29 by K4, per references/effect-boundary.md SS2: contradicted means the product does the thing and does it differently from the document; vacuous means the product does not do the thing at all, so there is nothing for the constraint to be true or false about. The two want different remedies and reading them as one sends a missing subsystem to the place that fixes a wrong one. SS3 names this row's exact shape -- a requirement whose declared effect class has no provider in production source is vacuous at phase 1, before any test is written. MEASURED AT `83e5380`, and the narrow true thing rather than the general one (SS7: absence is a fact about this commit). `PairingService` has exactly ONE conformance in production source, `public struct FixturePairingService: PairingService`, `app/Sources/MCPRouterKit/Pairing/PairingService.swift:31`; the shipped shell wires it by default, `pairing: any PairingService = FixturePairingService()`, `app/Sources/MCPRouterUI/Phone/PhoneShell.swift:63`. No `URLSession`, `NWConnection`, `NWListener` or `Network.NW` symbol appears anywhere under `app/Sources/MCPRouterKit/Pairing/` (9 files); the fourteen files in `app/Sources` that do hold one are OAuth, control-plane, registry and loopback-server code, none of it reachable from the pairing path. The protocol's own docstring states the decision rather than leaving it inferred: 'No live implementation ships in this item, and that is a decision rather than a gap.' SO THE CLAIM IS NOT BOUND, AND THE `provider` FIELD STAYS EMPTY DELIBERATELY. There is no symbol that opens the socket to bind it to. `vacuity-check.py --gate` therefore continues to report REQ-016 as uncensused, correctly, and that finding is a dispositioned expectation rather than a silence: it is the vacuity, visible. What the re-class buys is that `campaign.py check` stops counting REQ-016 as an effect somebody failed to witness -- `unwitnessed_effects` excludes `vacuous` (campaign.py:1099) -- and starts reporting it as the product gap it is. The remedy is to build the transport (I5, DEF-001) or to withdraw the requirement; neither is K4's.

subject.note: J2. The four Servers segments are pressed one at a time and the effect is read on THE ROWS THE TABLE DRAWS, not on the segment. `board.filter == .running` after `board.filter = .running` is the property the assignment just made — the same tautology as a button whose proof is that it now looks pressed. Both directions, on a population chosen so no two segments have the same answer: one plain running server, one plain idle, one running-and-placarded (which `Needs you` claims and `Idle` must not) and one idle-and-placarded (which both claim). The rows that survive are exactly the ones that match and the rows that vanished are exactly the ones that do not — a one-directional check passes on a filter returning nothing and on one returning everything. The four expected row sets are additionally asserted to be four DISTINCT sets, so a bar whose segments all led to one row set fails on the cardinality however green each individual check looked.

NO NUMBER THE ROUTER DOES NOT OBSERVE, CHECKED ON THREE BOARDS RATHER THAN ONE. CASE-0008 and CASE-0137/0140/0141 hold this requirement over fixtures and over the Cleanup board's provenance sheet; what they cannot reach is a board with a real router behind it, because until J5 no Debug build had one. Two claims. First, every figure the Servers board states while the router is answering resolves to that router's own response — `3 tools from 3 servers · 1 running` and `1 of 3 declared servers running` against tools 3, servers 3, running 1 read independently over HTTP. Second, and on all three arranged states rather than the flattering one, no memory figure and no saving is displayed anywhere: `DESIGN.md` §6 names the fabricated memory saving by hand, because the router never runs the world it would have to be subtracted from, and a claim of that shape would be the easiest one to add without anybody noticing. WHAT THIS DOES NOT REACH, stated rather than left to be inferred: the sweep is over the accessibility tree of one board in three states. A figure drawn on a board this run did not visit, or painted without reaching the AX plane, is outside it. The `no-memory-figure` and `no-saving-claim` checks are run per state precisely so a guardrail that held on one board and not another cannot pass on a single instance, but three boards are not nine.

K3. `Install` is driven at `DiscoverBoardModel.install` and the effect is read as the DECLARATION THE CLIENT RECORDED — name, command and args, checked against the row that was pressed rather than against the function that built them. Two entries are staged with different install blocks and both are pressed, so a handler that declares a fixed payload, or the row it happened to have selected, fails on the second press; one press and one assertion cannot tell those apart. The read refused is `board.rows[0].installed == true`. `markInstalled` writes that from the board's own copy of the response, so it is true whether or not anything reached the router — the app's report that it worked, which is what the arm leaves standing.

N8. The inertness guard on the untrusted-input boundary, made capable of failing. M19 shipped `MarkdownSecurityTests.htmlIsInert` with four spellings that named `javascript:`, no scheme, or nothing, and two assertions -- no link, no `imageURL` -- that `MarkdownInline.sanitized` makes true of every input it touches. It could not go red. M30 wired `ControlAPICapabilityDocumentSource` into the shipped UI, so router-served third-party text now reaches this renderer in a Release build, and the guard on it measured nothing. MEASURED, not assumed: the platform parser does keep inline HTML inert -- under `MarkdownInline`'s own options it hands each tag back as characters and marks it `.inlineHTML`, an intent naming no destination, and it does so under all four combinations of `allowsExtendedAttributes` and `interpretedSyntax`. Swift 6.2, macOS 26.6.2 (25G83), Debug, `swift test`. So this was an evidence defect and not a live vulnerability, and the fix is the assertion rather than new sanitisation. Two `https` spellings were added, because `https` is the one scheme the allowlist keeps and therefore the only one that can carry an interpreted `<a>` through to the assertion; a presence control runs the same reader over the markdown twin of the same destination first; and two clauses were added that the old body did not have -- handed back verbatim, and no attribute beyond the `.inlineHTML` marker. That last clause also corrects the test's own claim: the parser DOES attach one attribute to inline HTML and `sanitized` carries it, so the old name -- `inline HTML acquires no attribute of any kind` -- was false as written as well as unfailable, which is why nobody found out.

subject.note: A served document returns its content, and the response carries NO filesystem path. Eleven assertions: 200; the read me carries the fixture's sentinel; changelog and capabilities both present; exactly one image travelled; its reference is the string the document spelled (`docs/figure.png`) rather than a resolved path; media `image/png`; the base64 decodes to the file's own bytes; nothing refused; the package root appears NOWHERE in the raw body; and no absolute path of any shape (/private/tmp, /Users, /tmp) appears in it either. This case opens the overflow through ExpandCollapsePattern.Expand and reads both commands back with their names and ControlType.Button, between a BASELINE and a SILENCE that both find them absent from the control view AND the raw view. The writer is not the reader: overflow-actuate.ps1 expands in its own process and writes only the ExpandCollapseState it saw, while every element reading comes from uia-dump.ps1 started separately. TWO FINDINGS FROM THE FIRST RUN, neither planted, both corrected in the manifest rather than in the assertion. (1) probe-expectation.json predicted that opening the overflow would cost the never-activated guarantee, and IT WAS RIGHT: the probe held the foreground at none of the three baseline samples and at all six effect and silence samples, so Expand activates the window and Collapse does not hand the foreground back. That cost is now DECLARED as `overflow.activationCost` and compared both ways, so the day WinUI stops activating, this arm reddens rather than quietly acquiring a guarantee nobody re-checked. Baseline stays a hard assertion. (2) each command resolves to TWO tree paths with the overflow open, because WinUI publishes the OverflowPopup subtree once through a Microsoft.UI.Content.PopupWindowSiteBridge child and once in place beneath the ApplicationBar. Both copies agree on name, controlType, className, isEnabled, isOffscreen, accessKey, patterns and bounding rectangle, so it is one control on two routes; the assertion now permits several matches only while they agree on everything a caller would act on, and plant (H) watches that a genuinely different control under one id still fails. WHAT THIS DOES NOT BUY. It is not at-rest coverage and does not close DESIGN.md section 11 rule 9 for these two commands. The product fix is a surface that realises them without an actuation, and that is DEF-340. Neither command is INVOKED, so both stay outside the actuation census with a stated reason on SURF-029; this arm's subject is realisation and vocabulary, not effect. DEF-015's closed half — the shell's overflow treatment, which DESIGN.md §5 names and the build got wrong in a way no assertion could see. Every board's `AXSplitGroup` width is read back out of the running app and compared against its own `AXWindow` width, board by board, through the channel that already writes those dumps beside the pictures. It read 3 of 8 overflowing — Checks 988, Skills 1044, Discover 1119 inside a 980pt window, each origin moved left by exactly half its excess — and reads 0 of 8 after `.frame(minWidth: 0, maxWidth: .infinity, alignment: .leading)` on `ContentZone`. `outcome` rather than `raster-visual` on purpose: the claim is a measured relation between two frames the app publishes, not a comparison of pixels, and the pictures are what made the defect *visible* rather than what proves it fixed. Armed 20 Aug 2026, three ways on the gate and two on the test. The gate exits 1 against the pre-fix dumps, 0 against the post-fix ones, and 1 with no dumps at all — `examined=0` is a check that never ran and is never a pass. Removing the modifier reddens `ShellDetailWidthTests` with `passes its boards' minimum width up to the split view`, and dropping just `alignment: .leading` reddens the second half alone. That test's first version did NOT bite: it searched the raw source and matched the doc comment naming the modifier, so deleting the modifier left it green. Comments are stripped before matching now — a predicate satisfied by the prose explaining it is not a predicate. What this case does not cover, because `overflowing=0` reads like `nothing is clipped` and is not that claim: content that overflows the detail PANE stays inside the window and is invisible to this oracle. That half is CASE-0134, measured with a second probe against every leaf's right edge — and that probe was wrong on its first run, reading the frame's y where it meant x and reporting clipping on seven of eight boards. Re-rated to `source-analysis`: it reads source text and renders nothing. CASE-0137's claim, rendered. Nothing is wrong with your phone or your network.` The negative half is the one that would catch a regression: nothing in the window matches Crockford base-32 at the length REQ-015 specifies, checked by pattern rather than against a literal, so a code this predicate's author never saw would still trip it. subject.cell: execution-plane=daemon · data-shape=one stdio upstream declared
subject.note: The router spawning a child process, seen by two parties that are not the router. `bin/witness-effects.sh` runs `MCPRouterCLI index --force` against a scratch home holding one stdio server, and records the pid the shell launched (`$!`) beside the pid the CHILD reports for its own parent through `getppid()`. A ps(1) sample runs alongside and usually misses, because the index verb spawns, handshakes and exits inside one scheduling quantum; two earlier versions of this witness depended on ps alone and could report only that the child had A parent, not whose child it was. Armed: against a config declaring no servers the same recorder reports count=0, and against the populated one count=1 with the parents agreeing.

subject.cell: execution-plane=daemon · data-shape=the bundle path asked three ways: untokened POST, GET, tokened POST
subject.note: The verb IS the gate, and it is not describing a mutation. The bundle changes nothing. It is a POST because stage 2 of `ControlHandler.handle` gates the token on POST/DELETE/PATCH only, so the verb is the only thing deciding whether this router hands its whole diagnostic corpus — log lines included — to any unauthenticated caller that can open the loopback port, which per `ControlToken` includes a web page the user merely visits. All three answers are pinned — 401 untokened, 405 on GET, 200 on a tokened POST — so a later tidy-up that makes the verb 'correct' goes red rather than silently opening the route. The 200 is asserted beside the other two so they read as refusals rather than as an absent route.

Can every published glass capture be shown to have been written AT THE SHUTTER rather than afterwards? A manifest that post-dates its capture records what somebody believed, not what the channel did, so it is not lineage -- which is the finding `capture-lineage.py`'s RECONSTRUCTED pass raised against SURF-028 and which `bin/capture-manifest.py` closed on the derivation side. This is the ordering side: the gate requires each published row to carry `capturedAt`, `conditions.windowTitleReadback` and `conditions.cgWindowID`, none of which can be recovered after the fact, or an explicit `provenanceGap` saying that it cannot. WHAT IT DOES NOT PROVE, stated rather than folded in: it establishes that the row COULD only have been written by something standing at the shutter, not that it was. Only the capture channel writing its own row does that, which `bin/capture-mac-glass.sh` does and which no reader can verify from the artifact alone.

subject.cell: execution-plane=windows-host - modality=operating-system crash record - data-shape=one deliberate fail-fast
subject.note: A REAL STATUS_STOWED_EXCEPTION, raised on demand, and what the XAML handler did about it - DEF-086. That row said this repository had no way to raise one: the original Skills crash was removed by DEF-077 and DEF-078, and a cross-ABI fault was not something product code could ask for. It turned out the lane already raised one without recognising it. An UNGUARDED throw from a DispatcherQueue callback - `--fault dispatcher --fault-unregister dispatcher`, which is DEF-085 as found - terminates MCPRouter.Shell.exe with WER Application Error 1000, exception code 0xc000027b, faulting module CoreMessagingXP.dll, fault offset 0x0000000000093b76. WHAT IT MEASURES: on that same run the region of shell-startup.log ends at `fault: injecting dispatcher` with nothing appended, so Microsoft.UI.Xaml.Application.UnhandledException does not see this class. DEF-079's mechanism field guessed exactly that and recorded it as unestablished; it is established now. THE RECORDER IS NOT THE WRITER, twice over: WER is written by the operating system after the process is gone, and it is read here through Get-WinEvent over the Windows Application log, which is a different API from the file the shell appends to. THE CONTROL: the guarded run of the same fault leaves no Application Error at all, so the record is the injection's rather than something this machine produces anyway. WHAT IT DOES NOT SETTLE, and this is the narrower thing rather than the wider claim: what matches the Skills crash of 2026-09-02 is the exception code, the faulting module and the fault offset - identical to the Application Error entries this machine still holds from 18:57:35 and 19:03:30 that day - and NOT a stack. This case says this host raises the same stowed-exception fail-fast and that the XAML handler does not catch it. It does not say the original throw took the identical path; DEF-077 named that throw and fixed it.

subject.detail: prototype.html routes ?pane=evals and titles the board Evals; the running app's window title reads back Checks. Found by capture-lineage's tie pass, which refused a capture whose recorded target did not resolve to the surface's route. The rename went one way and the design of record was not followed.
subject.text: WITHDRAWN 20 Aug 2026 — this was not a product defect. It was recorded as "prototype.html routes ?pane=evals and titles the board Evals; the running app's window title reads back Checks". The second half is false. `prototype.html:600` declares the sidebar entry as `{id:'evals',t:'Checks',ic:'evals'}` — the route **id** is `evals` and the **title** is `Checks` — and the board's own header draws the selected suite (`pr-summariser · 8 cases`) rather than a board name at all. So the design of record titles this board Checks, the app titles it Checks, and there was never a rename to follow. WHAT ACTUALLY HAPPENED is a detector artefact, and it is worth keeping for that: capture-lineage's tie pass refused a capture whose recorded target did not resolve to the surface's title, and the target it held was the route id. An id and a title are different fields that the design is entitled to disagree on, so a tie pass that compares one to the other reports a rename wherever a route is not named after its board. Checked against the other seven boards: no second instance, because every other route id matches its title. Closed rather than deleted, so the next reader meets the artefact rather than rediscovering it.
subject.title: a route id was compared against a board title, and they differ in the design itself

subject.detail: MCPROUTER_SCENARIO=empty launched the app and Discover still rendered the populated catalogue — GitHub 2,984 sessions, DeepWiki 2,332 — so the surface is not reading the router's answer. Measured on glass by PhoneGlassTests.testDiscoverTracksWhatTheRouterReturned, iPhone 16 Pro, iOS 26.5. CLOSED 20 Aug 2026. Mechanism: `FixtureControlAPIClient.searchRegistry` ignored the scenario entirely and decoded the same `registry-search` recording for all fourteen, so MCPROUTER_SCENARIO=empty reached the client and the client answered with a populated catalogue. Discover was reading its data correctly from the wrong answer. `.empty` is now built in code beside `skills()` and `marketplaces()` rather than added as a second file under Control/Fixtures, which parity-fixture.sh would replay against a reference that cannot reproduce it. `sources` is zeroed with `results`. testDiscoverTracksWhatTheRouterReturned passes.
subject.title: the empty scenario does not reach Discover on the phone

Neither was visible because the filename was the only thing binding a picture to a surface. subject.text: Measured 20 Aug 2026. `make test` failed with 4 issues at a one-minute load average of ~700 and passed all 1473 tests in 179 suites at load 46, on the same source, minutes apart. The four were `ActivityReconnectTests` (`a reconnect over a feed that stays live releases its guard`), `DiscoverBoardTests` (`client.searchQueries.count` reading 1 where the baseline said 2), and `SettingsAndMenuBarTests` twice (`model.trackerState` still nil). An earlier run at the same load failed only the first, so the set was not stable either — which is what separated this from a product defect. A suite that reports a defect the product does not have is the failure this campaign has already paid for once, in DEF-029, where a dead instrument read as a dead product for ten consecutive runs. CLOSED by making each wait a condition rather than a deadline, at three sites: 1. `ShellTestSupport.waitUntil` — ceiling 5s → 30s. It returns the moment the condition holds, so a passing test pays nothing for the larger bound; the bound exists only so a condition that never arrives fails instead of hanging. Five seconds was inside the scheduling noise of a contended host, which is the whole finding. 2. `ActivityReconnectTests.completes` — 2s → 30s, same argument. The defect it bounds is a call that *never* returns, so it exhausts any budget and a generous one costs only the time a genuine hang takes to report. 3. `DiscoverBoardTests.searchIsDebounced` — a fixed sleep replaced by two waits, because the claim has two halves and one sleep proved neither on a slow host. First a bounded wait for the debounce to fire at all; then a full debounce window of quiet with the count still at one, which is what rules out one request per keystroke. The second is a real quiet period rather than a deadline, so load cannot shorten it into a false pass — the wait on its own is satisfied by the *first* request and would pass against exactly the defect this test exists to catch. Armed 20 Aug 2026, all three, each watched to fail with its own message: `waitUntil` at `.seconds(0)` reads `no poll ran at all`, `the poll died with the scene that started it` and `five keystrokes issued 0 requests`; `completes` at `.milliseconds(1)` reads `reconnect did not return while the feed stayed live`; and a `queryChanged()` inserted inside the quiet period reads `a later request arrived: five keystrokes issued 2 requests in total`. The original trigger is not reproducible on demand from here — the load came from another project's Rust test binary, two node processes and `lsdiagnose` — so the fix is proven by the arms rather than by reproducing the contention.

subject.text: Measured 20 Aug 2026 on two different worktrees the same afternoon. A fresh `git worktree` has no `node_modules` and no `dist`; `parity-selftest` is the last target `make all` runs, and its own environment check therefore fires only after lint, both builds, 1483 package tests, the iOS lane and the on-glass lane have all passed. Both runs came back `exit=2` on a tree where nothing was wrong with the code — roughly forty minutes each, twice. It is a lane defect rather than a product one, and the shape is familiar: the gate was honest (it said `the MCP SDK is not installed. Run npm install.` rather than skipping) and it was honest at the wrong moment. A check that can only fail on the environment belongs where the environment is checked. CLOSED by moving both checks into the `tools` target, which `all` runs first: `node_modules` must exist, and `dist/index.js` must exist because without it `parity-lane-selftest` SKIPS, and a skip is not a pass. Each names the command that fixes it. Armed 20 Aug 2026 in a bare directory holding nothing but the Makefile: with no `node_modules` it exits 1 naming `npm install && npm run build`, and with `node_modules` present but no `dist` it exits 1 naming `npm run build` and saying why a skip is not a pass. Costs a millisecond on a tree that has both.
subject.title: the whole-repo gate discovered a missing environment forty minutes in, twice

subject.text: CleanupBoardRow carries three treatments for a skill row — the `Read first…` substitution when SkillChecks.originUnchanged fails, the skill-kind `Remove…` drawn disabled because the router removes servers and never files on disk, and the candidacy reason — and none of them had a rendered path in any configuration of the product. A skill is proposed for cleanup only when every readable client lacks it, and all six skills in SkillFixtures.populated are installed somewhere, so the Debug Cleanup board drew three servers and zero skills. Release reaches the branch only if a real user happens to hold an orphaned skill. CASE-0136 asserted the branch exists by reading CleanupBoardRow and said in its own note why it stopped there; what nobody could say was that a build had ever drawn it. Fixed in-campaign by adding a Debug-only `cleanupSkills` scenario and two SkillFixtures.uninstalled rows, kept separate from `populated` because SURF-004's on-glass predicate asserts the count populated publishes. No view code was touched and no assertion was weakened. Now photographed by CASE-0138/CASE-0139 and guarded in the harness by CASE-0144.

subject.source: app/Sources/MCPRouterKit/Control/Scenario.swift; evidence/runs/make-test-3.log (clean build, 1512 tests in 188 suites); app/Scripts/enum-layout-stamp.py; Makefile target enum-layout-stamp; evidence/runs/make-test-4.log
subject.text: Adding a 14th case to `Scenario` made `make test` fail with 31 issues, two of which cannot be true of the source: `Expectation failed: (… → .live) == (.live → .fixture(…cleanupSkills))` in ShellClientFactoryTests and TriageSourceGuardTests, both asserting a Release-posture guard that returns .live unconditionally. `git stash` of the two changed source files → 19 tests pass; unstash → the same failures return, which reads as a real regression. It is not. `Choice.live` is encoded in the spare inhabitants of `Scenario`'s tag, so a new Scenario case shifts that encoding, and stale MCPRouterUI object files compiled against the old layout compare a value that no longer means what they think. `rm -rf app/.build` then rebuild: 5/5 pass, then 1512/1512. The hazard for this campaign is the mirror case — a stale build can as easily produce a green — so any test evidence taken across an enum change is taken from a clean build. MITIGATED 2026-08-20: `app/Scripts/enum-layout-stamp.py` hashes the ordered case list of every enum in the package (212 of them) and removes `app/.build` when that hash moves; `make test` now depends on it. The stamp is the case lists rather than the source, so it holds still for an ordinary edit and for a `switch` over the enum — the false positive a naive grep for `^\s*case` would hit — and moves for an added or renamed case. Armed on all four: comment SAME, switch statement SAME, added Scenario case MOVED, renamed Scenario case MOVED, restore back to baseline. The SwiftPM behaviour itself is unchanged and still upstream; what is fixed is this repo's exposure to it.
subject.title: an incremental Swift build after adding an enum case reports impossible test failures

subject.detail: `evidence/shots/captures.json` is the only manifest `capture-lineage.py --gate` reads, and two lanes write it: `capture-mac-glass.sh`, and `scripts/acceptance/name-glass-attachments.py`, which merges the iOS lane's rows up from `evidence/shots/ios/captures.json`. The Mac script wrote `json.dumps(rows)` — its own rows, whole file — so whichever lane captured last erased the other's lineage without saying anything. Measured 2026-08-20 on v0.9.1's new lineage plane: the parent held 16 Mac rows and none of the 9 iOS ones, and the gate reported 6 iOS captures UNSOURCED — 'the only thing binding this picture to SURF-012 is its filename', which is the correct verdict on a manifest that had been overwritten. The pictures were always right and their provenance was always recorded; it was recorded into a file that was then replaced. Fixed by merging on `path` in both writers, and the 9 rows were restored from the lane's own capture-time record rather than reconstructed.
subject.title: two capture lanes wrote one manifest and the last one deleted the other's provenance

subject.detail: `campaign.py` keeps defects in `inventory.json` under a `defect` list, and `add` assigns the next id from that list. `defects.in.json` is an input file. Twelve defects found in the sittings of 19 and 20 Aug were written straight into the input file with hand-written ids taken from that file's own length, which had stopped tracking the registry at DEF-006. The result: DEF-007 through DEF-018 each named one defect in the registry and a different one in the staging file, and neither file said so. Visible symptom, and the only reason it was caught: `RUN-2026-08-20.md` contains 'DEF-011 is the finding worth acting on ... Cleanup's' at line 96 and 'DEF-011 - the rendered-quality gate has never been able to run' at line 481, in one document, meaning two unrelated things. This is `capture-lineage`'s failure mode moved from pictures to identifiers: a name binding to two subjects with nothing checking the binding. Fixed by renumbering the twelve staged defects to DEF-034..DEF-045, merging them into the registry, and rewriting the fifteen references that meant the staged numbering. Every renumbered record carries `stagedAs` naming its old local id, so a reader meeting the old number in an untouched artifact can resolve it. The remaining 74 references were checked one at a time and meant the registry defect they already named. A fourth lesson, from the third instance's cleanup rather than from the collision itself. Reconstructing the concurrent session's two entries welded `text: ""` and `note: ""` onto both, and the first renumbering pass then used `"text" in d` to tell the two writers' entries apart -- so the artifact defeated the discriminator that would have caught it. Both authors independently read the empty values as harmless because they carried no content. The hazard is shape, not content: a membership test reads a key's PRESENCE, and an empty string defeats `"text" in d` exactly as thoroughly as a populated one would. `campaign.py add` injects only `id`, `status`, `evidence` and `armed`, so that key-shape occurred on exactly the two reconstructed entries and was traceable; the keys were stripped and the pass re-run discriminating on `title`. Recorded because "empty therefore harmless" is a reasonable-sounding wrong answer that both sessions gave.
subject.note: SECOND INSTANCE, 20 Aug 2026, in the case registry rather than the defect registry, and it landed the same way. A helper reported `next case id: CASE-0145` while cases.json already held CASE-0149 and CASE-0150; campaign.py's own `next_id` is max+1 and would have said CASE-0151, so the number that was trusted did not come from it. `add` takes an explicit id through `setdefault` and therefore appends a second entry rather than refusing, so CASE-0149 and CASE-0150 each came to name two cases -- an iOS Settings structural case against REQ-005 and a RouterCore write-failure case against REQ-019 -- and the `set` calls that followed wrote onto the pre-existing pair. Caught by an evidence-existence audit rather than by any gate: the new cases printed `3 evidence` where two were supplied. Restored from `git show HEAD:` (both pre-existing entries are byte-identical to HEAD again, verified by dict comparison) and the new pair renumbered to CASE-0153 and CASE-0154. The registry is sparse -- 74 gaps between 1 and 152 -- so a free-looking number is not evidence that it is free, and only max+1 is. THIRD INSTANCE, the same evening, and this one had two writers rather than one. A second Claude session working the same campaign allocated DEF-047 and DEF-048 at about 23:30 (the SDK -32603 message discard, and a detector defect in vacuity-check.py's blind pass) and committed planning/test-campaign as a directory in 6bdeea4, which also swept up this session's in-progress registry edits. This session allocated DEF-047 and DEF-048 for different defects minutes later, from a read taken before that commit landed. Resolved by renumbering THIS session's pair to DEF-049 and DEF-050 -- the later allocation moves, and the session that moves is the one that can enumerate its own references, which is the only reason the choice is safe rather than arbitrary. The peer's entries were not edited. Note for anyone reading the mechanism: `add` assigns from the registry list, so two writers holding a stale read get the same number, and no gate in the campaign detects it. The detection here was a peer message, and before that an evidence-existence audit; neither is a gate. campaign.py could refuse an explicit id that already exists -- `add` currently takes one through `setdefault` and appends a duplicate instead.
subject.title: the campaign's own defect ids named two different defects each, because the staging file numbered from its own length

subject.detail: DETECTOR DEFECT, recorded so its numbers are not published as product findings. `vacuity-check.py`'s `blind` pass asks whether any READER appears after the last MUTATING call in a test body, both matched by name prefix. Run with the shipped defaults it reports `examined=1820 mutating=3 blind=3` — and all three are false: DEFAULT_READERS is snake_case (`load_`, `get_`, `read_`, `list_`) while this is a camelCase Swift codebase, so NO Swift reader can ever match, and the three `mutating` hits matched the token `restart` in their own function names. Both flagged WatchRestartTests cases read extensively after the mutation. Run with a hand-derived camelCase verb list it reports `examined=1834 mutating=258 re-read-after=158 blind=100`. Two of the flagged real tests were read in full and BOTH re-read: `undoRestoresTheItem` calls `queue.all()` three times after `model.remove(...)`, and `resetReindexesAnIndexFailure` reads `client.calls` after `board.reset(...)`. Neither `all` nor `calls` was in the list. Of the 20 findings the script prints, only 6 are `@Test` functions at all; the other 14 are test doubles and helpers, because the population is every `func` in any file with `test` in its path. CONCLUSION: on this codebase the pass measures the verb list rather than the suite, and no verb list derived by hand is evidence of anything. It is recorded, not published, and the campaign claims no blind-mutation number. The pass's other two arms — `unclassed` and `uncensused` — are exact and are kept. ADDRESSED UPSTREAM in 0.9.2, confirmed by running it 21 Aug 2026. Commit 28ecd67 (`the blind-mutation check was measuring itself`) fixes four detector defects that each RAISED the blind count, and the pass now prints the vocabulary it used above its findings -- `vocabulary: defaults + campaign.blindVocabulary — 22 mutator(s), 20 reader(s)` followed by the reader list -- which was this defect's complaint: a number published without saying what configuration produced it. The denominator also moved, 1841 to 1657, because fixture helpers are no longer counted as tests. Left open rather than closed: the residual named on DEF-040 sits in the same pass. SUPERSEDED 21 Aug 2026 by DEF-055. The specific claim here — snake_case DEFAULT_READERS against a camelCase Swift codebase, giving examined=1820 mutating=3 blind=3 with all three false — was resolved by declaring campaign.json's blindVocabulary, which 0.9.2 reads. The general claim, that no hand-derived verb list is evidence of anything, is not resolved; it is now MEASURED rather than asserted. DEF-055 carries that measurement (7 of 7 sampled findings false, four named mechanisms, a two-way arm) and is the entry to read. Recorded as superseded rather than closed: the finding was real and its successor is open.
subject.title: test-campaign 0.9.1's blind-mutation pass is dominated by its own verb configuration on this codebase, in both directions

subject.note: `#expect(result.tools != nil, ...)` at ShellTests.swift:133. `ReindexResult.tools` is a non-optional `Int` (MCPRouterKit/Control/Models.swift:263), so the comparison could not fail. The Swift compiler emitted `comparing non-optional value of type 'Int' to 'nil' always returns true` on every build of the test target; it was the only such warning in the suite. The intent was stated in the comment directly above it -- `.success` is distinguished from `.populated` by `a reindex that comes back with no error and a tool count` -- so the assertion was one character from doing its job. Repaired to `result.tools == 14`, the value FixtureControlAPIClient+Writes.swift:33 overrides for `.success`, which discriminates against the base `reindex-failure.json` fixture it starts from (`{"tools":0,"error":"fetch failed"}`). Armed in evidence/arming/CASE-0152.arming.log: with the override changed to 0 the assertion goes red (`(result.tools -> 0) == 14`), and the log records that the pre-repair form would have stayed green under the same mutation.
subject.text: A ShellTests assertion on the `.success` reindex scenario compared a non-optional Int to nil, so it was always true and read nothing.

subject.detail:
DETECTOR DEFECT in test-campaign 0.9.1, found 20 Aug 2026 by the concurrent session at uds:/tmp/cc-socks/9881.sock and confirmed here against the artifact rather than against a model of it. The string `defect` does not appear as a registry key anywhere in evidence-page.py; measured with grep, zero occurrences. Its `

Defects

` at line 521 renders `[c for c in cases if state_of(c.get('status')) == 'fail']` -- failing CASES -- and the nav counter at line 305 is `counts['fail']`, the same population. So the page's Defects section counts 3 (the failing cases CASE-0010, CASE-0040, CASE-0110) while inventory.json holds 11 open defects, and the two numbers are about different things. MEASURED against the regenerated 124100-byte evidence.html: of the 11 open defects, 8 appear ZERO times -- DEF-008, DEF-040, DEF-041, DEF-042, DEF-043, DEF-047, DEF-048, DEF-051. The 3 that do appear are there by accident of prose: DEF-001 in two failing case notes and one passing one, DEF-033 and DEF-049 each inside a single PASSING case's note, rendered by the per-case table rather than by the Defects section. The peer reported 11 invisible; the true figure is 8, because writing a defect id into a case note is a convention doing a gate's job and it happened to fire three times. `campaign.py check` also exits 0 with all 11 open, so no gate holds on the registry either. This is the skill's own first-named failure mode -- covering a subset and reporting it as the whole -- arriving in its publisher: the gated half of the campaign is sound and the ungated half is the half people look at. The fix belongs in the installed skill (render inv['defect'], and count open defects in the nav), not in this repo; recorded rather than patched, precedent DEF-048 and DEF-051. SECOND PUBLISHER, same root cause, measured here: `campaign.py`'s own ledger writer (campaign.py:1210-1240) loads `inventory` and never reads `inventory['defect']` either, so ledger.md names zero defects across its 83 lines. Its header line is sharper than an omission -- it prints `73 pass . 3 fail . 0 skip . 4 n/a . 0 open . armed 73/73`, where `0 open` is the count of open CASES, on a campaign holding 12 open defects. A reader who takes that line at face value reads a campaign with nothing outstanding. ledger.md is generated rather than hand-kept, so it cannot be corrected in this repo: a fix that patched only evidence-page.py would leave the ledger short, and both publishers need to read the registry.
subject.title: evidence-page.py and campaign.py's ledger writer both skip the defect registry, so no published artifact lists a defect

subject.text: Measured by R27 on 2026-08-29 against the daemon on a scratch home. A server whose command exists and exits immediately (a shell that returns 17) is acquired for the full startupTimeoutMs and then reported as 'did not initialize within Nms': with the budget at 3000ms the probe took 3.15s wall clock. A server whose command does NOT exist fails in 0.01s, because the spawn itself throws. So the cost is specific to a child that spawns and dies, and the reason is that the handshake races connect() against a timer with no third branch for 'the process exited' - nothing watches the child's termination during startup. NOT FIXED HERE, and the reason is a boundary rather than effort. The race lives in StdioUpstreamTransport, which is the reference-diffed startup path R2 owns and R4 compares; adding an exit branch would change how this router reports a failure the reference reports differently, which is a parity decision and not a health-check one. R27's own bound is deliberately narrower - probeTimeoutMs covers the tools/list request so that 'the child never started' and 'the child answered too slowly' stay different answers - which means the budget that governs this arm is the upstream's startupTimeoutMs, and that is stated on the record rather than hidden. WHAT IT COSTS TODAY: a manual probe of a crash-looping stdio upstream blocks for the default 60s, and the caller has no way to shorten it except by setting that server's startupTimeoutMs. scripts/acceptance/r27-health.sh sets 1500 on its flaky fixture for exactly this reason, and says so. 2026-10-19 — FIXED IN BOTH ROUTERS by merge 02d764b0 (Merge ai/stdio-exit). A child that exits before initializing now fails at once, naming its status, instead of waiting out startupTimeoutMs. Unit evidence: RealProcessStartupTests (app/Tests/RouterCoreTests/RealProcessStartupTests.swift) and test/stdio-exit.test.ts. Verified 2026-10-19: the `Real child processes — startup` suite passed under `swift test`, and `node --test` on test/stdio-exit.test.ts passed. Status is fixed · in-test. No campaign re-run is recorded against this row, and the R27 wall-clock probe has not been run again against it.
subject.title: A stdio child that starts and then exits is not noticed, so acquisition waits out the whole startup budget

subject.source: app/Sources/RouterCore/Control/Describe.swift transportMembers; app/Sources/RouterCore/Control/ControlHandler.swift gate; src/control.ts is the reference half
subject.text: Found while building R22's redactor, filed rather than fixed. `Describe.row` emits `command` and `args` RAW, and `ControlHandler.gate` reads the token only for POST/DELETE/PATCH, so the complete command line of every stdio upstream is readable by anything that can open the loopback port. The same function is careful in the adjacent case — it emits `envKeys` and `headerKeys` and never a value, with B10's reasoning attached — so argv is the one credential-carrying position on that route that is published whole. It matters because argv IS a credential channel: `--token=`, `--api-key=` and a connection string with an inline password are ordinary MCP server invocations, and R22 scrubs args for exactly that reason. The exposure predates R22 and is not made worse by it: the bundle's args go through the value scrub, and this route's do not. NOT FIXED HERE, and the reason is a parity decision rather than effort. `GET /servers` is reference-diffed — `control-servers-get` in planning/parity/surface.tsv, verdict `proven` — so redacting args moves a surface R4 compares byte for byte, and the ungated GET is itself a ported defect this repository records rather than silently repairs. Closing it means changing both routers or declaring a divergence, and that is the owner's call. 2026-10-19 — FIXED IN BOTH ROUTERS by merge 74d15306 (Merge ai/argv-redact), whose subject records that GET /servers stops publishing secret-bearing argv. Unit evidence: ArgvRedactionTests (app/Tests/RouterCoreTests/ArgvRedactionTests.swift) and test/argv-redact.test.ts, with parity vectors in argv-redact.json. Verified 2026-10-19: the `ArgvRedactionTests` suite passed under `swift test`, and `node --test` on test/argv-redact.test.ts passed. Status is fixed · in-test. No campaign re-run is recorded against this row.
subject.title: GET /servers discloses every stdio upstream's full argv to an unauthenticated local caller

subject.evidence: `PREVIOUS = "HEAD:planning/test-campaign/bin/control-census.py"`. The arm's whole claim is a DIFFERENCE - six plants that redden this branch's census and are silent on the one it replaced, and two DECLARED SILENCES where the old census is red and the new one is deliberately not. That holds while the new census is UNCOMMITTED, which is the state wd3 wrote and watched it in, and it reported 8/8 correctly. Once the commit that earns it lands, `HEAD:` resolves to the NEW census and the arm compares the file with itself. subject.evidence: `discover()` reads the git INDEX through `git ls-files` and separately walks the DISK through `os.walk` + `os.path.relpath`, then names the difference as briefs the gate did not read. `git ls-files` prints POSIX separators on every platform; `os.path.relpath` prints the platform's. On Windows the two sets therefore never intersect and the difference is the WHOLE corpus. Measured before the fix on this branch: the same run printed `brief discovery read 226 items of the git index ...; kept 219` and, four lines later, `219 brief(s) on disk are NOT in the index and are outside this verdict`, listing ten of them and `... and 209 more`. Both sentences cannot be true. The verdict and the partition were correct throughout - it is the accounting sentence above them that was false.
