subject.detail: Measured 2026-08-27 by G16 while enumerating SURF-026, and independently by G15. M15 made Settings a Scene and removed the case from `Destination`, and capture-mac-glass.sh still ran `axkit select Settings`. That select fails — `axkit: no sidebar row starting 'Settings'` — the app stays on whichever board the loop visited last, and the shutter filed THAT board's pixels under SURF-011: byte-identical to the Cleanup board on one loop ordering and to the Insights board on another. THE CAMPAIGN'S OWN INSTRUMENTS CAUGHT IT FROM TWO DIRECTIONS, which is the part worth keeping. glass-assert.py's raster uniqueness check went red because two cases shared a sha256; `--discriminate` reported the neighbouring board's predicate wrongly accepting SURF-011's dump, because that dump IS the neighbouring board; and the capture manifest's readback recorded the picture's target as the neighbour's route under subject SURF-011, contradicting its own filename. FIXED HERE, NARROWLY: the capture script now refuses to photograph a select that did not take, and says which board the window is actually showing. That is the script's own standing rule rather than a new one — it already declines to substitute a picture for the pairing sheet and the status item, and its header records the run that filed the Inbox board as SURF-010. The title and the dump are still written from what the app is really showing, so the failure stays visible downstream; what is withheld is the photograph, because a misattributed picture is the one artefact nothing downstream can correct. STILL OPEN, and deliberately not fixed here: 1. SURF-011 has no route to the Settings SCENE. It needs Cmd-comma or the app menu, not a sidebar select that cannot succeed. CASE-0016 and CASE-0111 fail until it does. 2. THE MENU MAP IS PRE-M22. Committed SURF-001.menu.txt binds Cmd-4 to `Discover`; the running app binds Cmd-4 to `Harnesses`, exactly as Destination.selectionDigit declares (activity 1, servers 2, skills 3, harnesses 4, discover 5, inbox 6, evals 7, cleanup 8, insights 9). glass-assert.py's SURF-001 `menu` dict is the old map, so CASE-0001 asserts five bindings this build does not have. Correcting it is editing an assertion to restore a green, which this campaign forbids — it is owed as its own item, from Destination.selectionDigit rather than by hand. WHY IT IS THE SAME FINDING AS G14'S, ONE LAYER DOWN. G14 found the surface LIST had stopped growing while the product did. This is the EVIDENCE not having been re-taken since the build moved: the committed glass artefacts were last written on 20 Aug by cef3729, before M22 added two destinations and renumbered four accelerators. In both cases a completeness gate reported clean because what it measured was a stale artefact rather than the product. CLOSED ON THE EVIDENCE SIDE, 2026-08-27 (G21/G29). The frame this defect produced was still published: `inventory.json` gave SURF-011 the shot `evidence/shots/SURF-011.build.png`, and at `519aebc` those bytes were the Insights board. `capture-lineage.py --gate` reported it UNTIED because the capture step's own row said `target: app://mac/insights` while the filename said SURF-011 -- the manifest was right and the wall was wrong. Two moves, both provable from git. The Insights frame is renamed `evidence/shots/DEF-059.insights-filed-as-SURF-011.png`, keeping every capture-time field, so the defect keeps its exhibit and no filename match can offer it to SURF-011 again. The Settings capture it overwrote is restored to `SURF-011.build.png` from `cef3729`, TOGETHER WITH ITS MANIFEST ROW from the same commit -- the last commit where those bytes and that row agreed (sha 3b5a26ef, `target: app://mac/settings`, readback `Settings`, 2026-08-20T11:32:58Z). Restoring the pair from one commit is a recovery of a capture-time record; restamping the row against the new bytes would have been the manifest-after-the-fact defect. What is NOT closed is the cause: `axkit select Settings` still fails, so the campaign still has no Settings capture newer than 2026-08-20 and the glass script still declines to take one. THE CAUSE NOW HAS A READER, 2026-09-02 (wa5). `axkit select Settings` still fails, and the campaign still has no Settings capture newer than 2026-08-20 -- unchanged. What has changed is that the age is no longer invisible: `bin/glass-build-gate.py` reports `evidence/shots/SURF-011.build.png` and `evidence/ax/SURF-011.*` as STALE against the build this tree would produce, so the lane cannot be green over them again without somebody re-taking them. `bin/capture-mac-glass.sh`'s refusal to photograph a select that did not take is the other half and is unchanged. Both halves of the remaining work -- a route to the Settings SCENE, and the re-capture -- are macOS work and are not attempted here. CLOSED 2026-10-19 on glass. capture-mac-glass.sh opens Settings with ⌘, (backgrounded), selects the Router pane in the Settings window's own source list, photographs that window as SURF-011 (target app://mac/settings), dumps the Security pane as a second dump of the same surface, and closes the window. glass-assert at the current build: checked=435 failures=0; --decoy SURF-011 reddens 6.

subject.detail: Measured 2026-08-27 by G15, while enumerating SURF-025. The committed glass evidence under planning/test-campaign/evidence/ax was last written by commit cef3729 on 20 Aug. M22 then added two destinations and RENUMBERED four accelerators, and nothing re-took the pictures. Running bin/capture-mac-glass.sh against the current build turns four previously-passing cases red, and in every one of them the PRODUCT is right and the recorded evidence is stale: 1. THE MENU MAP. Committed SURF-001.menu.txt binds Cmd-4 to `Discover`; the running app binds Cmd-4 to `Harnesses`, exactly as Destination.swift's selectionDigit declares (activity 1, servers 2, skills 3, harnesses 4, discover 5, inbox 6, evals 7, cleanup 8, insights 9). glass-assert.py's SURF-001 `menu` dict is the pre-M22 map, so CASE-0001 asserts five bindings the shipped build does not have. 2. SETTINGS IS NOT A SIDEBAR ROW. M15 made Settings a Scene and removed the case from Destination, and capture-mac-glass.sh still does `axkit select Settings`. That select now fails — `axkit: no sidebar row starting 'Settings'` — the app stays on Cleanup, and the script photographs the CLEANUP board and files it as SURF-011. CASE-0016 and CASE-0111 fail against it. THE CAMPAIGN'S OWN INSTRUMENTS CAUGHT BOTH, WHICH IS THE ONE GOOD PART. The capture manifest's readback records that picture as target `app://mac/cleanup` under subject SURF-011, contradicting its own filename — the exact mechanism the script was rebuilt around. Independently, glass-assert.py --discriminate reports LEAK SURF-007 wrongly accepted 1 of 8 foreign board dumps: SURF-011 — because SURF-011's dump IS the Cleanup board. Two instruments, one cause. WHY THIS IS THE SAME FINDING AS G14'S, ONE LAYER DOWN. G14 found the surface LIST had not grown since it was written. This is the EVIDENCE not having been re-taken since the build moved. In both cases a completeness gate reported clean because the thing it measured was a stale artefact rather than the product. NOT FIXED HERE, DELIBERATELY. G15's remit is the Harnesses enumeration, and correcting glass-assert.py's menu map or the Settings navigation would be editing an assertion to restore a green — even though the product is right, that is the move this campaign forbids, and the stale assertion is the instrument that found this. The four cases are set to `fail` with this id in their notes. Owed: re-map SURF-001's menu dict from Destination.selectionDigit, and give SURF-011 a route to the Settings SCENE (Cmd-comma or the app menu) instead of a sidebar select that cannot succeed. INSTRUMENTED 2026-09-02 (wa5), NOT CLOSED. The cause this row names -- a committed capture carrying no tie to the build it came from -- is now measurable. `planning/test-campaign/bin/glass-build-gate.py` binds every artifact the macos-glass lane cites to the git blob identity of the Mac app's build inputs (the set `scripts/acceptance/build-freshness.sh` compiles from) and exits 2 when that identity is not the one the lane is being read against. It is RED on this tree over all 56 artifacts, in 7 capture groups spanning 20-29 Aug: `evidence/runs/glass-build-gate.log`. The stamps it reads are marked `reconstructed-from-git` and are deliberately the weaker claim -- git can prove which commit last wrote each artifact, so the record establishes the build the evidence CANNOT BE NEWER THAN rather than the build it was taken from. `bin/capture-mac-glass.sh` now calls `glass-build-gate.py --emit` in the run that takes the pictures, stamping from the bundle's own CFBundleShortVersionString/CFBundleVersion and the `.mcprouter-build-stamp` the Makefile writes after `xcodebuild` exits 0, so a re-capture replaces each reconstructed row with a capture-time one. Watched both ways: `evidence/runs/glass-build-gate.selftest.log`, four arms, green over a current capture and red over a stale one, an uncovered one and an undatable row. Case CASE-0342. WHAT IS NOT SETTLED. The re-capture itself, which is the whole of what this defect asks for. It needs a macOS host with Xcode and a display server; the work above was done on Windows, where there is no Swift toolchain, no xcodebuild and no way to open the app's window. The four cases stay `fail` with `owed` recording the re-capture and its owner. The second half of the row -- SURF-001's menu map, to be re-read from `Destination.selectionDigit` rather than by hand -- is equally macOS work and equally untouched. Nothing here edits an assertion, a stamp or a recorded identity to restore a green.

subject.detail: DETECTOR DEFECT in test-campaign 0.9.2, found 21 Aug 2026. attach-shots.py iterates every image under evidence/shots and assigns `hit['shot'] = rel` on each match, last write wins, with no preference for a build capture over a design render. This campaign keeps six directories under evidence/shots (16 root, 8 design-size, 16 fidelity, 9 ios, 17 mock, 11 mock-hidpi), so for SURF-001 the candidates in iteration order are SURF-001.build.png, SURF-001.shell.png, mock/SURF-001.png, mock-hidpi/SURF-001.full.png -- and the last one wins. MEASURED for SURF-001, SURF-002 and SURF-006: `--apply` would repoint each surface's `shot` from its build capture to `evidence/shots/mock-hidpi/SURF-00N.full.png`, which is the render of the DESIGN, not the build. That is the skill's own headline failure mode -- publishing a picture of one thing under the name of another -- arriving in a sibling of the plane built to prevent it, and it would do so while every other gate stayed green, because capture-lineage.py gates the 16 captures cited by CASES and the surface wall is a different population. The report compounds it: the UNCORROBORATED block prints surface ids (SURF-001 ... SURF-011) rather than the file each verdict is about, so a reader sees eleven surfaces apparently lacking provenance when in fact each surface's ACTUAL `shot` field points at a corroborated build capture and the complaint is about a mock render nobody intended to attach. Distinguishing the two costs a re-derivation of the matcher by hand. Recorded rather than patched, precedent DEF-048, DEF-051, DEF-052 and DEF-053. The campaign's standing refusal to run `--apply` here predates this and was based on the DEF-006 mis-wire; it now has a measured mechanism behind it. Separately closed while investigating: this campaign's design-size captures carried their provenance in a second manifest, evidence/shots/design-size/captures.json, in a different schema ({captures:[...]} against the root's bare list) that no gate reads. Its 8 entries were merged into the root manifest with `target` derived from the root's declared target for the same subject and corroborated by each capture's own windowTitleReadback -- Servers, Activity, Skills, Discover, Inbox, Checks, Cleanup, Settings, every one matching -- recorded at capture time, and each carries `targetDerivedFrom` saying so. That was the campaign's own inconsistency and is fixed here; it was not the cause of the 11. RE-MEASURED 2026-08-27 (G21) after `evidence/shots/captures.json` was made a derived file. The uncorroborated count is 12 and stays 12: SURF-001..011 and SURF-022. Eleven of them are this defect -- `mock-hidpi/` sorts last, so it is the row that decides each surface's `shotProvenance`. The mock rows in the manifest deliberately carry NO `target`; the address the channel was pointed at is recorded in full as `renderedFrom`, with an `attachHazard` field naming this defect. Measured both ways on this tree: writing that address as `target` instead drops the uncorroborated count from 12 to 1 and DISARMS `--apply`'s refusal, because `attach-shots.py` only checks the field is present and never compares it to the subject's route -- which is item 5 of X8's work order. So the report going quiet would have been this defect getting worse while looking fixed. The twelfth, SURF-022, is not this defect: see DEF-061.

subject.detail: Measured 2026-08-21 against test-campaign 0.9.2 on app/Tests. The pass reports examined=1661 mutating=320 blind=88. Two structural errors and two idiom errors inflate that number. STRUCTURAL. (1) It scans every `func`, not every test. Restricted to swift-testing's own discriminator (a func whose nearest preceding annotation is @Test) the denominator is 1531, not 1661: 130 of the examined functions are not tests. (2) Its helper exclusion at vacuity-check.py:162 is file-scoped — a name is a helper only if called more than once in the file that declares it. A shared stub declared in TestSupport.swift and called from other files therefore reads as a test, so MemoryFileSystem's `write`, `removeItem` and `moveItem`, HTTPStub's `stop` and WatchTestSupport's `remove` are each counted as a blind test. 21 of the 88 are support-file functions. IDIOM, on the mutator side. (3) The lookbehind `(?<![A-Za-z0-9_])` cannot exclude a dot, so a Swift enum case constructor matches a mutator verb: `ServerRowAction.forServer(s, pendingAuth: nil) == .reset(.clearPlacard)` reports ServerPresentationTests::trippedOutranksHeld as mutating via 'reset', where `.reset` is the expected VALUE inside the assertion. 41 of 72 re-measured findings are dot-prefixed. (4) It takes the last mutator by source POSITION and calls everything after it the tail, which misreads three Swift constructs: a mutator inside the assertion (`await #expect(throws: Never.self) { try await store.delete() }` — nothing can follow it by construction), a mutator in a `defer` block (source-early, execution-last, so the whole test body reads as 'after'), and a mutator as the last statement of a loop body whose observation is the next iteration (CallbackLifecycleTests::stopReleasesTheSocket rebinds the port ten times; the read of cycle N is the start() of cycle N+1). SAMPLE. Of the 15 findings with zero assertions after the last mutator — the highest-yield stratum — 9 were read in full. Two (DiscoveryTests::servers, CapabilityPlateTests::install) are helpers. All 7 remaining are real tests that do observe after mutating, through idioms no reader verb names: `client.calls.last?.operation`, `seen.filter { ... }`, a rebind that throws. Precision on that stratum is 0 of 7. ARMED, two ways, evidence/arming/blind-mutation.arming.log. A probe @Test that mutates and never observes was added and removed: blind moved 88 -> 89 -> 88 and examined/mutating moved by exactly 1 each time. The check does bite; it is the false-positive rate that is at issue, not the sensitivity. NOT REMEDIED BY VOCABULARY. The reader side is deliberately loose because a false reader match suppresses a finding. Adding this codebase's read idioms (`calls`, `operation`, `filter`) would lower the number without improving what the pass knows, and the terms are generic enough to suppress true findings too. The 88 stands recorded as a worklist with its measured precision beside it rather than tuned to look better. RE-MEASURED 2026-08-27 by G22, which declared `testRoot` and gave this pass a corpus for the first time. THE 88 DOES NOT REPRODUCE. Vendored 0.9.2 over `app/Tests` today reports examined=2133 mutating=3 blind=3, against the 1661/320/88 above. The denominator moving up while `mutating` collapses 320 → 3 is not tree churn: 0.9.1 and 0.9.2 ship IDENTICAL DEFAULT_MUTATORS and DEFAULT_READERS, and neither list holds `reset`, `write`, `removeItem`, `moveItem` or `remove` — the verbs this entry's idiom argument turns on. So the 2026-08-21 sitting ran an expanded vocabulary passed on the command line, and `campaign.json` declares none, which makes 88 a figure no documented invocation returns. Its cited evidence, `evidence/arming/blind-mutation.arming.log`, has never existed on any branch of this repository (`git log --all -- '*blind-mutation*'` is empty), so the arming claim above is not checkable from the tree. The measured structural and idiom errors are not withdrawn; what is withdrawn is the population they were measured over. TODAY'S POPULATION, AND ITS PRECISION. With `testRoot: app` the pass reports examined=2179 mutating=3 re-read-after=0 blind=3, and 0.15.0 returns the same three findings from the same corpus. All THREE were read in full — 3 of 3, not a sample — and all three are false positives. Precision 0 of 3. A FOURTH CAUSE, NOT IN THE ORIGINAL ENTRY, AND THE ONE THAT PRODUCES TWO OF THE THREE. The body slice is `src[pos:end]` where `pos` is the start of the DECLARATION, so a test whose own name begins with a mutator verb matches itself. `WatchRestartTests::restartIsIssuedBeforeTheStagingWrite` and `::restartIsOwedBeforeTheWriteLands` contain no mutating call at all: the only `restart\w*\(` in each is `func restart…(` on its own declaration line. Both then read — `WatchWorld.read(scratch.logPath)`, `WatchState.load(path:)`, `WatchWorld.serverNames(in:)` — and assert on `state.mcpServersHash` and `state.restartPending`. The third, `PhoneStorageFailureTests::restartRechecksTheCamera`, does call `await model.restart()` and then asserts twice, on `model.step` and on `model.entry.characters`: property reads that no reader verb names, which is cause (4)'s shape rather than a new one. This cause survives into 0.15.0 unchanged. NOT ENROLLED IN A GATE, and `blindVocabulary` still not declared, for the reason the entry already gives. A related gap measured at the same sitting: pointed at `src/` — the TypeScript tree, which has no tests — the pass prints `corpus: … (0 file(s))` and `examined=0 mutating=0 blind=0` and contributes nothing to `--gate`. It reports its empty corpus and does not fail on it, so a mis-declared `testRoot` reads as a clean pass. VOCABULARY DECLARED 2026-08-29 by K4, and the entry's own 'NOT REMEDIED BY VOCABULARY' paragraph is narrowed rather than withdrawn. That paragraph reasons entirely from the READER side, and on the reader side it is still right: adding this codebase's read idioms lowers the count without improving what the pass knows, which is why the declared reader list stops short of `expect` and `require` -- swift-testing's assertion macros, 5781 and 383 occurrences, either of which would mark every test that asserts after mutating as re-reading and collapse the count to near zero while the pass learned nothing. THE MUTATOR SIDE WAS NEVER ARGUED, AND THAT IS WHERE THE PASS WAS BLIND. Measured over the same 2282 test bodies at `83e5380`: the nine snake_case defaults find 3 mutating call sites; a camelCase list derived from this corpus finds 481. So `blind=3` was a reading of 3 of 481, a recall of 0.6%, and the entry's `precision 0 of 3` was a precision over a population the instrument could barely see. `campaign.json` now carries `blindVocabulary` with `only: true`, 19 mutators and 34 readers, derived mechanically -- a verb is kept only where method calls on a receiver are at least half its corpus sites and its own `func` declaration lines at most a quarter, which is causes (3) and (4) of this entry turned into a selection rule. THE THREE FINDINGS ARE ADJUDICATED, and each clears for a different checkable reason rather than all three for one. `restartIsIssuedBeforeTheStagingWrite`: one fitted mutator, `WatchWorld.remove(scratch)` inside a `defer`, and four declared readers after it -- `load`, `read`, `parse`, `servers`. NOT blind, positively. `restartIsOwedBeforeTheWriteLands`: three fitted mutators, the last `WatchState(restartPending: true).save(`, with `load` after it. NOT blind, positively. `restartRechecksTheCamera`: ZERO fitted mutator call sites in its body. It was flagged only because `restart` is a shipped default and this entry's fourth cause -- the body slice beginning at the declaration -- made `func restartRechecksTheCamera(` match itself. `restart` fails the selection rule (1 method call against 3 declaration lines, of 5 sites), so it is not in the vocabulary and the finding is withdrawn. WHAT THAT DOES NOT MEAN: its real mutation `await model.restart()` is now invisible to the pass, and its reads are still the property comparisons `model.step` and `model.entry.characters` that no reader verb names. It is UNEXAMINED by this instrument, not clean, and that is this entry's ceiling stated once more rather than closed. ARMED, AND ENROLLED, which the entry recorded as missing. `planning/test-campaign/bin/blind-vocabulary-arm.py` runs on every `make lint`: two plants identical but for one line, each measured alone and again inside a `shutil.copytree` of the real corpus, requiring examined+1 mutating+1 blind+1 for the blind plant and examined+1 mutating+1 blind+0 for the reading one. The specificity arm is the half a sensitivity arm alone cannot give: a detector that flagged every mutating body would pass the first and say nothing. 6 of 6 as expected on `cache 0.16.0` and again on the `vendor/` pin via `--instrument`. The two disagree only on the denominator -- 2282 against 2277, the five arrow-style `it/test(` blocks 0.9.3 added block detection for -- and agree on blind=111. THE 111 IS A WORKLIST AND THE CAMPAIGN STILL PUBLISHES NO BLIND NUMBER. Nothing above touches the structural causes: the pass still examines every `func` rather than every `@Test`, its helper exclusion is still file-scoped, and a `defer` mutator still reads as source-early -- which is exactly why the first of the three findings above needed reading rather than counting. This entry stays OPEN; what it now carries is a measured recall beside its measured precision.
subject.title: vacuity-check's blind-mutation pass examines non-tests and mis-reads Swift idiom; 7 of 7 sampled findings are false positives

subject.detail: THE FACT, RE-MEASURED AT 42aef112 rather than inherited from the 83e5380 note. `PairingService` still has exactly ONE conformance in production source, `public struct FixturePairingService: PairingService`, `app/Sources/MCPRouterKit/Pairing/PairingService.swift:31` - measured by `grep -rn "PairingService" app/ --include=*.swift` excluding `app/Tests`, which returns that one declaration and no other. The shipped phone shell still wires it by default, `pairing: any PairingService = FixturePairingService()`, `app/Sources/MCPRouterUI/Phone/PhoneShell.swift:63` and again at `:183`. All nine files under `app/Sources/MCPRouterKit/Pairing/` import `Foundation` and nothing else; a grep for `NWConnection`, `URLSession`, `URLRequest` and `connect(` over that directory returns zero lines. Twenty-two files elsewhere under `app/Sources` do hold one of those symbols and they are OAuth, the control plane, the registry client, the loopback server, the stdio pool and the CLI - none of them takes a `PairedMac` or is reachable from `PairingService.pair`. WHY THIS IS NOT A RUNNER'S CALL. The two remedies differ on what the product IS, not on how to say it. Building the transport is I5/DEF-001 - a subsystem, a wire contract, and a Mac endpoint to match; `PairingService.swift`'s own docstring records that not shipping one was a decision taken so that the consumer would not invent a contract the producer has to match late. Withdrawing the claim deletes a promise from the requirement set, and `spec-I5.md` and `ORCHESTRATOR.md`'s I5 row are where it was made. A runner who picked either would be deciding what the product does while calling it a defect fix - the same move `R10`'s brief refused over the CLI exit code. subject.detail: Found 20 Aug 2026 while building R8's gate against both routers. Against a fixture returning `-32603` with the message `Internal error: Authentication required`, the reference records `MCP error -32603: Internal error: Authentication required` and the Swift router records `[-32603] Internal error`. The upstream's own message is gone. CAUSE, cited exactly: modelcontextprotocol/swift-sdk 0.12.1, `Sources/MCP/Base/Error.swift:217-240`. The decoder reads the server's `message`, then maps the code — `-32700`, `-32600`, `-32601` and `-32602` each pass `unwrapDetail(message)`, and `-32603` alone passes `unwrapDetail(nil)`. `unwrapDetail(fallback)` returns `data.detail` when present and the fallback otherwise, so a server that answers -32603 with a message and no `data.detail` has its message discarded, and `Error.swift:91` renders `"Internal error" + (detail.map { ": \($0)" } ?? "")` as the bare canonical name. -32603 is the code servers use for an arbitrary application error, so it is the one that loses the most. TWO consequences: for the whole class of -32603 upstream errors the Swift router tells the user strictly less than the reference does; and R8's Swift half cannot detect a credential refusal at all, because there is no text left to match. This is a coverage gap in the parity suite as much as a defect in the SDK — no parity scenario had ever exercised a JSON-RPC error carrying a detailed message, which is why 82 proven rows never saw it. Remedies, none taken: report upstream and take a fixed release; pin a patched fork; or read the JSON-RPC error before the SDK types it, which needs a seam below the client.
subject.title: the Swift MCP SDK discards an upstream's error message for code -32603, so the router reports less than the reference does

subject.detail: parity-gate.sh, 20 Aug 2026 on main at e5755d0. Its line 163 is the whole of what the citation run reported: `FAIL scripts/acceptance/parity-oauth.sh the gate reported findings`, and the next line is the following `ok` row. Every one of those bytes existed and was discarded by the caller: `parity-suite.sh`'s `run_script` sent both streams to /dev/null at the time. The instrument was repaired in commit 21d559b at 20:41:28 -- one minute and 58 seconds after this log was written, in the same commit that recorded the defect -- so `run_script` now keeps the log and prints its last 20 lines inline. A recurrence would therefore arrive with the cause attached. That is what closes this: the next occurrence, not more thought about this one. It stays open because there is still no cause and no reproduction; what changed is that the reason it could not be diagnosed is now known and no longer true. One candidate mechanism examined and NOT adopted. The R9 lane reported (21 Aug 2026, via uds:/tmp/cc-socks/9881.sock) that a stale $TMPDIR/mcp-router-parity.lock had made a gate fail its manifest-check for a non-real reason. That is a different symptom -- a manifest-check failure before the comparison, against this defect's completed run that reached `control-auth-post-http` and recorded a row -- and parity-oauth.sh takes that same lock at line 126 and preflights every port at 143-145, so the two lanes inside one gate could not have overlapped. subject.text: Observed once, in one of two whole-gate runs, and not reproduced by: a standalone run of `parity-oauth.sh`, a second standalone run of it immediately afterwards (which exercised the same port-reuse wait, 9s and 12s), a standalone run of `parity-suite.sh`, or a second whole `parity-gate.sh` on the same tree. The second gate reported 82 of 83, 0 DIVERGED, and its suite lane reported the citation clean. **What it is not.** The lane distinguishes an environment failure from a finding on purpose, and this was the finding branch: `record control-auth-post-http fail` at `parity-oauth.sh:329`, reached only when the reference side completed an authorization and the Swift side did not. An unbindable port exits 2 through `wait_for_ports_bindable` and records `blocked`, not `fail`, so the port-reuse race is ruled out by the code path that fired. **Why it went undiagnosed, and what changed.** `parity-suite.sh`'s `run_script` sent both streams to `/dev/null` and printed `the gate reported findings` — a verdict with no evidence under it. The bytes naming which guard failed had already been thrown away by the time anyone read the gate's summary. `run_script` now keeps the log, prints its last 20 lines inline and names the file it kept, armed 20 Aug 2026 against a deliberately failing citation. A recurrence will say which of the 21 checks went red. **Why the duplicate run stays.** `control-auth-post-http` is proven on the wire by its own lane and also cites the script, so the gate runs it twice. That is now documented in `parity-suite.sh` rather than deduplicated, because the duplicate is what caught this: a single run would have reported a clean 82 of 83 and nobody would have known. Both record under the same row id and a `fail` wins. **Burn-in, 20 Aug 2026: 8 standalone runs of the lane, all green, 21 checks each.** Three immediately after the failure and five consecutively afterwards, plus one clean whole gate. One failure in roughly ten whole-lane executions, cause unrecoverable because that invocation's stdout was discarded. A green burn-in does not close this: the original failure is uninspectable, so the runs measure only that the lane is not reliably broken. What would close it is a captured reproduction, or a stated gate met — several consecutive whole gates including the cold port-reuse path — decided as its own question rather than inferred from a streak, which is the `install-launchd-watch` mistake this repository already paid for once (G1: name a fix per term and fix a bound IN ADVANCE, never a green streak). Not a UI defect and not a blocker on the cutover count — CASE-0036's measurement is the second run — but it is an unexplained non-determinism in the router or the lane, and it is recorded rather than absorbed.

subject.note: A real MSIX, built, deployed and removed, with a recorder at each step that is not the thing that wrote it. MakeAppx packs and .NET's ZipArchive reads the OPC container back - so the identity assertion is made against the PACKED ARTIFACT rather than against the file on disk that was handed to the packer. `winget validate` is the winget client applying a schema this repository does not own. Add-AppxPackage deploys and Get-AppxPackage reports: Fledgeling.MCPRouter_0.1.0.0_x64__facmrsw33693e. THE INSTALL ARM IS WHAT TURNS A FILE INTO A PACKAGE. A manifest can pack cleanly, validate cleanly, and be refused at deployment for a capability, an architecture or a signature - and every static check in the world passes right up to that point. 'CLEAN UNINSTALL RULES' IS THE HALF WORTH READING TWICE. UninstallGuidance promises that uninstalling preserves %USERPROFILE%\.claude\mcp-router. That is a promise about what SURVIVES, and a promise about survival cannot be checked by any amount of reading - only by an uninstall that actually ran. The lane plants a marker, installs, removes, and requires both that the deployment stack reports the package gone and that the marker is still there. WHAT THE LANE PUTS BACK: a self-signed certificate is added to LocalMachine\TrustedPeople so an unsigned developer package can deploy at all, and removed in a finally block however the run ends. Verified afterwards: zero Fledgeling.* packages, zero witness certificates. A lane that left a trusted publisher behind would have changed what this machine will install, silently and for every future run. NOT SETTLED: that anyone can obtain the package. Nothing publishes it, the winget InstallerUrl is a deliberate example.invalid placeholder, and this lane asserts the placeholder is PRESENT so the manifest cannot be mistaken for a shipping one. subject.note: The COM activator the Windows notification platform wrote, read out of the registry by a process that did not write it. The writer is AppNotificationManager.Register() inside the shell; the recorder is HKCU through PowerShell's registry provider, and nothing of this repository's sits between them. Four arms. BASELINE requires the AUMID key to be ABSENT before the shell launches, so what the other three read is this launch. The three EFFECT arms read the key, the CustomActivator CLSID it names, and that CLSID's LocalServer32 - which came back as MCPRouter.Shell.exe carrying the platform's own ----AppNotificationActivated: argument, a string this repository does not write anywhere. THE ACTIVATOR IS THE ARM THAT CARRIES THE ITEM. A toast outlives the process that raised it; when somebody presses Review an hour later, Windows COM-activates the LocalServer32 registered for that CLSID. Without it the toast still appears and pressing it does nothing, which is the failure that looks most like success and exactly what a screenshot of a notification would have certified. WHAT THIS CASE DOES NOT SETTLE: that a toast is drawn, and that a press re-activates the app. Both need UserNotificationListener, whose capability is only grantable to a packaged application; DEF-082 carries them and is downstream of DEF-073. The shell's own report that the platform accepted a Show is carried in the evidence as writerSelfReport and is graded by nothing, because a process reporting its own effect is the shape of claim DEF-072 was about.

subject.cell: execution-plane=windows-host - data-shape=a supervised process that dies
subject.note: The half of WIN23's supervision promise that had never been watched: a daemon the Windows task scheduler starts, loses, and starts again. DEF-081 filed it as unmeasurable and named the blocker as a missing Windows daemon binary; the blocker was real and is gone - app/windows/MCPRouter.Witness.Daemon is a harness process that starts, records its own start and waits to be killed, so there is something for the scheduler to supervise. WHAT THE MEASUREMENT FOUND IS NOT WHAT THE ROW EXPECTED. The registration the product wrote carried RestartOnFailure with a 60-second interval and a count of 3, and it did not restart the daemon at all. Killed, watched 150 seconds, on the unified scheduling engine and the legacy one, for a run started by a trigger and one started on demand: four registrations, no restart. The same block DID restart, three times at exactly 60 seconds, a task whose Command named a file that does not exist - so the instrument can see a restart, and RestartOnFailure governs a task that fails to LAUNCH rather than one whose action launched and later died. DEF-320 carries that, and the product now writes a Repetition on the trigger alongside MultipleInstancesPolicy IgnoreNew. THE RECORDERS ARE TWO AND NEITHER WROTE ANYTHING: Get-ScheduledTaskInfo for the scheduler's own account of its runs, and Get-CimInstance Win32_Process for the process identity, which is what makes 'it came back' a different process id rather than a report from the thing that came back. The daemon's own run log is carried and graded by nothing. EIGHT ARMS, THREE OF THEM ABOUT THE INSTRUMENT: BASELINE requires both tasks absent and no daemon running, so nothing below is inherited from an interrupted run; CLAIM.repetition and CLAIM.ignorenew read the product's own unmodified logon registration back through the WMI provider; SILENCE requires both recorders to say no once the tasks are gone. ONE SUBSTITUTION, SAID OUT LOUD: a trigger repetition does not apply to an on-demand start - measured, twice - so the live task carries a TimeTrigger where the product writes a LogonTrigger, because this lane must not log the machine out. Every Setting, the repetition interval, the principal, the action and the instances policy are the product's own document. That the trigger fires AT LOGON is still unwitnessed and DEF-081 keeps it.

The four Servers segments are pressed one at a time and the effect is read on THE ROWS THE TABLE DRAWS, not on the segment. `board.filter == .running` after `board.filter = .running` is the property the assignment just made — the same tautology as a button whose proof is that it now looks pressed. Both directions, on a population chosen so no two segments have the same answer: one plain running server, one plain idle, one running-and-placarded (which `Needs you` claims and `Idle` must not) and one idle-and-placarded (which both claim). The rows that survive are exactly the ones that match and the rows that vanished are exactly the ones that do not — a one-directional check passes on a filter returning nothing and on one returning everything. The four expected row sets are additionally asserted to be four DISTINCT sets, so a bar whose segments all led to one row set fails on the cardinality however green each individual check looked.

NO NUMBER THE ROUTER DOES NOT OBSERVE, CHECKED ON THREE BOARDS RATHER THAN ONE. CASE-0008 and CASE-0137/0140/0141 hold this requirement over fixtures and over the Cleanup board's provenance sheet; what they cannot reach is a board with a real router behind it, because until J5 no Debug build had one. Two claims. First, every figure the Servers board states while the router is answering resolves to that router's own response — `3 tools from 3 servers · 1 running` and `1 of 3 declared servers running` against tools 3, servers 3, running 1 read independently over HTTP. Second, and on all three arranged states rather than the flattering one, no memory figure and no saving is displayed anywhere: `DESIGN.md` §6 names the fabricated memory saving by hand, because the router never runs the world it would have to be subtracted from, and a claim of that shape would be the easiest one to add without anybody noticing. WHAT THIS DOES NOT REACH, stated rather than left to be inferred: the sweep is over the accessibility tree of one board in three states. A figure drawn on a board this run did not visit, or painted without reaching the AX plane, is outside it. The `no-memory-figure` and `no-saving-claim` checks are run per state precisely so a guardrail that held on one board and not another cannot pass on a single instance, but three boards are not nine.

K3. `Install` is driven at `DiscoverBoardModel.install` and the effect is read as the DECLARATION THE CLIENT RECORDED — name, command and args, checked against the row that was pressed rather than against the function that built them. Two entries are staged with different install blocks and both are pressed, so a handler that declares a fixed payload, or the row it happened to have selected, fails on the second press; one press and one assertion cannot tell those apart. The read refused is `board.rows[0].installed == true`. `markInstalled` writes that from the board's own copy of the response, so it is true whether or not anything reached the router — the app's report that it worked, which is what the arm leaves standing.

N8. The inertness guard on the untrusted-input boundary, made capable of failing. M19 shipped `MarkdownSecurityTests.htmlIsInert` with four spellings that named `javascript:`, no scheme, or nothing, and two assertions -- no link, no `imageURL` -- that `MarkdownInline.sanitized` makes true of every input it touches. It could not go red. M30 wired `ControlAPICapabilityDocumentSource` into the shipped UI, so router-served third-party text now reaches this renderer in a Release build, and the guard on it measured nothing. MEASURED, not assumed: the platform parser does keep inline HTML inert -- under `MarkdownInline`'s own options it hands each tag back as characters and marks it `.inlineHTML`, an intent naming no destination, and it does so under all four combinations of `allowsExtendedAttributes` and `interpretedSyntax`. Swift 6.2, macOS 26.6.2 (25G83), Debug, `swift test`. So this was an evidence defect and not a live vulnerability, and the fix is the assertion rather than new sanitisation. Two `https` spellings were added, because `https` is the one scheme the allowlist keeps and therefore the only one that can carry an interpreted `<a>` through to the assertion; a presence control runs the same reader over the markdown twin of the same destination first; and two clauses were added that the old body did not have -- handed back verbatim, and no attribute beyond the `.inlineHTML` marker. That last clause also corrects the test's own claim: the parser DOES attach one attribute to inline HTML and `sanitized` carries it, so the old name -- `inline HTML acquires no attribute of any kind` -- was false as written as well as unfailable, which is why nobody found out.

subject.note: An oversized image is refused ON ITS OWN TERMS and does NOT spend the shared budget. Ten assertions. The document names `oversize.png` (over the 2 MiB imageBytes cap) first, then a.png..d.png at exactly 2 MiB each — which together spend the 8 MiB imageBudgetBytes exactly — then tail.png. The discriminator is d.png: it travels only if the oversized figure spent nothing, because had it spent its own 2 MiB + 1 the budget would be gone before d.png was reached and d.png would come back budgetExhausted. tail.png is budgetExhausted either way and so proves nothing on its own, which is why the case does not rest on it. Also asserted: oversize.png is refused `tooLarge` naming the 2,097,152-byte per-image limit rather than `budgetExhausted`, and the budget was spent to exactly 8,388,608 bytes. Run against BOTH implementations over a real socket: `dist/index.js serve` and the shipped `app/.build/debug/MCPRouterCLI serve`, each on 127.0.0.1:8981 with a scratch MCP_ROUTER_HOME. M30 already proves this route in process — `ControlDocumentRouteTests.swift` calls the handler and asserts on the string it returns — which is a different claim from this one: this lets the kernel carry the bytes and reads what a client actually receives, which is what the campaign asks of every other route on this lane. Observing only the TypeScript half would leave the SHIPPED router unobserved, so both are run and both pass.

M38. A refused manifest write leaves the served catalog exactly where it was AND leaves the change pending, so the decision is still available to be taken. R21 fixed the status code; this reads the same refusal at the catalog, which is where the user's question actually lives. The failure is injected on the FileSystem method names (writeFile, moveItem) — a key naming an operation nothing performs would let the case pass by writing successfully.

M38. A held tool surface is not served, and approving it is what starts serving it. The strike is POST /servers/:name/approve through the real ControlHandler; the read-back is MCPEndpoint.listTools() over a ManifestStore built before the strike and never handed to the handler — the two lines a client's tools/list runs. Never the approve response, which is the writer's account of its own write. An untouched sibling server in the same manifest is the control: every assertion about the promoted server is also passed by a route that promoted the whole file.

M38. Over a real router and the MCP SDK's own client: approving a held surface announces notifications/tools/list_changed, the announcement is ATTRIBUTED to the approval in the router's log rather than to the three-second poller's 'rebuilt outside this process', and the client's re-fetch carries the text the user accepted. The notification COUNT is not the oracle — the poller supplies one either way — so the log line is what the case stands on. scripts/e2e-live-reload.mjs.

M38. The negative control for CASE-0265: an approve that promoted nothing (409) announces nothing — no notification and no new live-reload log line. Without it the arm above is satisfied by a route that announces on every approve, which would send every attached session to re-fetch a list that did not move.

M39's honesty control, and the reason it is filed against REQ-016 rather than REQ-015. REQ-016 is vacuous: no symbol in production source opens a connection to a paired device (DEF-001), so a guarantee about what happens after contact cannot be violated by a build that never contacts anything. M39 adds presentation on top of that and must not be readable as progress against it. What this case asserts is the frame: ShellPairingFactory.choice returns .noTransport for every scenario name in a Release build, so Phase.live -- the only phase drawing a ring or a fallback line -- is unreachable outside a Debug build with MCPROUTER_PAIRING set. No effect-witness case exists in this item because the item claims no effect: no recorder, no effect class, no count.

Found by a denial control in the effect-witness pass rather than by reading code: `bin/witness-arm-denial.sh` points the CLI at a router home with mode dr-x------, which the process may read and traverse but not write. `index --force` then prints `ok witness-fixture (1 tools)`, prints `0 tools cached -> /tmp/.../manifest.json` eight lines later, and exits 0 over a manifest.json that does not exist. Cause: ManifestIndexer.record at RouterCore/Service/ServicePorts.swift:341 calls `try? ManifestIO.save(...)`. ManifestIO.save throws correctly and its own doc comment is careful about the disk-full case -- it deliberately leaves the temp file behind as evidence -- but all three call sites discard the error (AuthRoutes.swift:120, WatchIndexing.swift:150, ServicePorts.swift:341). The verb's closing count is honest, because MCPRouterCLI.swift:167-173 re-reads the manifest from disk to compute it; nothing compares that count against the per-server line above it. The same `try?` on the control-API path is already characterised and deliberate -- ControlApproveDispatchTests.approveWithARefusingFileSystem pins the 200, registered in spec-P1 section 8, as R5's shipped behaviour that P1 does not move. This is the second call site, and until CASE-0153, CASE-0154 and CASE-0151 no test in the repo named ManifestIndexer at all, which is why the swallow survived here after being characterised there. The iOS side of the same requirement was found and fixed -- PhoneStorageFailureTests covers `try? await store.save(mac)` letting a success surface render over a refused write. Left open-owner rather than fixed in campaign: propagating the error changes the CLI's exit code, which is a shipped-contract decision, and the project has already taken the opposite decision once on a sibling path. CASE-0153, CASE-0154 and CASE-0151 characterise today's behaviour so the day someone changes it, the change is deliberate. RE-READ AT 42aef112 ON 2026-09-03, BECAUSE THIS NOTE HAD GONE STALE IN THE DIRECTION THAT MATTERS. It says all three call sites discard the error and cites `ServicePorts.swift:341`. Two of the three no longer discard it and the file it names no longer holds the indexer. * The indexer moved to `app/Sources/RouterCore/Service/ManifestIndexer.swift`. Its `record` is a `do`/`catch` at `:193-223` that returns a `cacheFailure`, which reaches the CLI's `IndexReport.add` (`MCPRouterCLI.swift:331-334`) and prints a `not cached <server> ...` line deliberately kept out of the ordinary pass/fail pair, plus a closing sentence about what was not recorded (`MCPRouterCLIIndex.swift:99-135`). A server whose row was lost no longer gets an `ok` line. That is R10, merged at `8241e0f`. * The approve route is a `do`/`catch` at `app/Sources/RouterCore/Auth/AuthRoutes.swift:171-177` returning `(500, {"error": "failed to write manifest: ..."})`. That is R21, merged at `5a51776`, and it CHANGED THE WIRE STATUS this note records as deliberate - see DEF-442, and note that the change agrees with the reference, measured at DEF-441. * `app/Sources/RouterCore/Watch/WatchIndexing.swift:209` is still `try? ManifestIO.save(...)`. R10's brief declares it out of scope in those words - it has no output to contradict itself with - and that is still true. WHAT KEEPS THIS ROW OPEN is unchanged and is the half neither brief would take: `index` still EXITS 0 when every write was refused, and moving that is a shipped-contract decision the owner has not taken. SWIFT WAS NOT COMPILED FOR THIS RE-READ - `swift` and `xcodebuild` are absent on the machine it was written on - so every line above is read off the tree and none of it is a test result. `app/Tests/RouterCoreTests/CLIIndexWriteDeniedTests.swift` and `ManifestIndexerWriteFailureTests.swift` exist and pin this behaviour; whether they pass at 42aef112 is not known here and must not be assumed.

subject.note: R22. The verb IS the gate, and it is not describing a mutation. The bundle changes nothing. It is a POST because stage 2 of `ControlHandler.handle` gates the token on POST/DELETE/PATCH only, so the verb is the only thing deciding whether this router hands its whole diagnostic corpus — log lines included — to any unauthenticated caller that can open the loopback port, which per `ControlToken` includes a web page the user merely visits.

WHERE THE AMBIENT STATE IS ACTUALLY ON SCREEN. SURF-041, the notification-area flyout, is the surface WIN11 describes and nothing in the build mounts it (DEF-380). This one is the pane footer the shell draws on every destination: two lines, ambient.status.title and ambient.status.detail, painted from the reading RouterStatusReader takes off the router's own /status every two seconds. It is in the pane rather than on a board because an ambient claim that appears on one destination is not ambient. It declares NO controls, and that is not an omission: it is a readout. Nothing on it can be pressed, so nothing on it belongs in an actuation denominator - the cases that read it carry no `actuates` for the same reason.

subject.note: SURF-029's two SecondaryCommands, 'Export log' and 'Reset router', were enumerated and unreached: a CommandBar does not realise its overflow items while the overflow is shut, so the at-rest lane could only record an absence with its reason, and planning/registry-drop-gate.py reported the surface as uncovered for exactly that. This case opens the overflow through ExpandCollapsePattern.Expand and reads both commands back with their names and ControlType.Button, between a BASELINE and a SILENCE that both find them absent from the control view AND the raw view. The writer is not the reader: overflow-actuate.ps1 expands in its own process and writes only the ExpandCollapseState it saw, while every element reading comes from uia-dump.ps1 started separately. TWO FINDINGS FROM THE FIRST RUN, neither planted, both corrected in the manifest rather than in the assertion. (1) probe-expectation.json predicted that opening the overflow would cost the never-activated guarantee, and IT WAS RIGHT: the probe held the foreground at none of the three baseline samples and at all six effect and silence samples, so Expand activates the window and Collapse does not hand the foreground back. That cost is now DECLARED as `overflow.activationCost` and compared both ways, so the day WinUI stops activating, this arm reddens rather than quietly acquiring a guarantee nobody re-checked. Baseline stays a hard assertion. (2) each command resolves to TWO tree paths with the overflow open, because WinUI publishes the OverflowPopup subtree once through a Microsoft.UI.Content.PopupWindowSiteBridge child and once in place beneath the ApplicationBar. Both copies agree on name, controlType, className, isEnabled, isOffscreen, accessKey, patterns and bounding rectangle, so it is one control on two routes; the assertion now permits several matches only while they agree on everything a caller would act on, and plant (H) watches that a genuinely different control under one id still fails. WHAT THIS DOES NOT BUY. It is not at-rest coverage and does not close DESIGN.md section 11 rule 9 for these two commands. The product fix is a surface that realises them without an actuation, and that is DEF-340. Neither command is INVOKED, so both stay outside the actuation census with a stated reason on SURF-029; this arm's subject is realisation and vocabulary, not effect. And the subject is WIN20's probe rather than the MCP Router Windows client: it measures WinUI 3's automation behaviour on this machine.

Re-rated from `structural-visual` to `source-analysis`: it reads source text and runs nothing, so it was never one rung below an effect — it is off the product ladder entirely, and `structural-visual` put it on that ladder where it read as movable. The rendered half of this claim is not missing: CASE-0011 (outcome, macos-glass) carries `Reset history…` in the predicate it asserts over the running Activity window, and evidence/ax/SURF-003.window.txt draws it. What is left here is the part no rendered assertion reaches — that the control is declared in `header` and not inside the rows conditional, which is a property of where the source puts it. A render proves the state it was taken in; this is the claim about the other eight, and the campaign has no empty-Activity dump to relate it against. PREVIOUSLY: DEF-016's affordance half and DEF-012's first rename, at the rung they honestly reach. `theResetActionIsInTheHeader` slices `ActivityBoard.header` from its declaration to `content`'s and asserts the slice carries `CleanupPresentation.resetLabel` and opens `model.sheet = .resetHistory`; `theHeaderLabelIsTheDesigns` asserts that constant is `Reset history…` per `prototype.html:716` and `:930`, not the Settings-Danger wording at `:999` the build had shipped. Recorded as `structural-visual` rather than `outcome` and counted against the strict total on purpose: both read source text, and no assertion here proves a header rendered. It is written that way because the claim is about the header in **all nine** DESIGN.md §5 states — the design puts the control outside the rows conditional precisely so the empty state has it — and a rendered assertion over one state would leave the other eight unchecked while buying effect credit. Watched to fail for real rather than by a staged arm: an earlier script aborted before writing the header change, and this assertion reported `the header draws no reset action` against the tree that was genuinely missing it. Reverting `resetLabel` reads `the header action is called Reset call history…`.

subject.note: DEF-011's affordance half, re-expressed against the running window rather than against `CleanupBoardRow.swift`. The source read asserted that the row declares `accessibilityElement(children: .contain)` and not `.combine`; what that modifier decides is whether each row's buttons are separately addressable, and relation `SURF-007/row-actions` in bin/glass-assert.py reads THAT off two dumps of a real window. Measured: 3 candidate rows in evidence/ax/SURF-007.window.txt and 5 in evidence/ax/SURF-007.cleanup-skills.window.txt, and all 8 own their own AXButtons one level below their own group — which a combined row cannot do, because combining flattens them into the group's label and publishes none. The action set is a function of the row and not of the board: exactly [Inspect, Remove…] on the 7 rows carrying no provenance note and exactly [Read first…] on the 1 that does. `metamorphic` rather than `structural` because the claim spans two different row populations: a column drawn at a fixed size fails the count and a combined row fails the ownership, and a single-window presence check can see neither. The Swift suite it replaces (app/Tests/MCPRouterUITests/CleanupRowActionsTests.swift) is kept and still runs — it is the faster signal — but it is no longer what this case stands on.

DEF-015's closed half — the shell's overflow treatment, which DESIGN.md §5 names and the build got wrong in a way no assertion could see. Every board's `AXSplitGroup` width is read back out of the running app and compared against its own `AXWindow` width, board by board, through the channel that already writes those dumps beside the pictures. It read 3 of 8 overflowing — Checks 988, Skills 1044, Discover 1119 inside a 980pt window, each origin moved left by exactly half its excess — and reads 0 of 8 after `.frame(minWidth: 0, maxWidth: .infinity, alignment: .leading)` on `ContentZone`. `outcome` rather than `raster-visual` on purpose: the claim is a measured relation between two frames the app publishes, not a comparison of pixels, and the pictures are what made the defect *visible* rather than what proves it fixed. Armed 20 Aug 2026, three ways on the gate and two on the test. The gate exits 1 against the pre-fix dumps, 0 against the post-fix ones, and 1 with no dumps at all — `examined=0` is a check that never ran and is never a pass. Removing the modifier reddens `ShellDetailWidthTests` with `passes its boards' minimum width up to the split view`, and dropping just `alignment: .leading` reddens the second half alone. That test's first version did NOT bite: it searched the raw source and matched the doc comment naming the modifier, so deleting the modifier left it green. Comments are stripped before matching now — a predicate satisfied by the prose explaining it is not a predicate. What this case does not cover, because `overflowing=0` reads like `nothing is clipped` and is not that claim: content that overflows the detail PANE stays inside the window and is invisible to this oracle. That half is CASE-0134, measured with a second probe against every leaf's right edge — and that probe was wrong on its first run, reading the frame's y where it meant x and reporting clipping on seven of eight boards. The Settings capture is whole, and looking at it is what caught it.

Re-rated to `source-analysis`: it reads source text and renders nothing. The behaviour it names is covered at an effect rung by CASE-0138 (outcome, macos-glass), which reads the substitution off a running build, and by CASE-0131's relation, which reads it off two windows and requires the action set to be a function of the row. This case is kept rather than retired because its predicate is the one that fires in seconds on a source change, and it is counted against the strict total rather than disappearing from it — but its rung now says it reads text, so no future reader takes it for a rendered assertion one step from an effect. PREVIOUSLY: `prototype.html:961` puts `Read first…` **in place of** Inspect and Remove rather than beside them, and the substitution is the requirement rather than a layout preference: a removal left on that row is one click from a fact nobody has read yet. `theRowSwapsItsActions` takes the `CleanupBoardRow` declaration, finds the `if candidate.provenance != nil {` branch, and asserts Inspect and `Remove…` appear nowhere inside it. It reads the declaration with every `//` line stripped, because the first `ShellDetailWidthTests` searched raw source for a modifier its own doc comment three lines above also named, and deleting the modifier left the assertion green: a predicate satisfied by the prose explaining it is not a predicate. `structural-visual`, and counted against the strict total, for CASE-0128's reason. Armed 20 Aug 2026 twice: renaming the button reads `draws no Read first…` plus the Inspect predicate firing, and adding `Remove…` back into the flagged branch reads `a flagged row still draws Inspect or Remove`.

subject.note: REQ-019 on the one control that has to refuse: the skill row's `Remove…`. The control API is read-only for skills — removing one means writing files the client applications hold open — and the row does not hide the button or offer it and fail. It draws it disabled (AX enabled 0) and states that reason in its help text, which is the shape REQ-019 asks for: no success affordance for work that cannot happen, and the refusal is the server's own. Pixels: `SURF-007.cleanup-skills.png`, 519568 bytes, sha 94dd9d06f87d, window-scoped off CGWindowID 103249 owned by the launched pid, recorded in `evidence/shots/captures.json` with the scenario that produced it. Byte-identical across two consecutive capture runs. It does NOT claim agreement with the design of record: the reference is an HTML mock rasterised at another size, and no macOS API exposes a cross-process computed style.

CASE-0137's claim, rendered. That case reads `CleanupSheets.swift` and states in its own note that no assertion in it proves a sheet was drawn; this one presses `Read first…` on a running build and reads the sheet that opens. `axkit press` is background-safe on a SwiftUI Button — AXPress runs the action on the element and needs no focused scene — and it exits non-zero when the press does not take, so the sheet is photographed or reported uncaptured, never assumed. The AXSheet subtree carries the three observations `SkillProvenance` actually holds (`Where the router first saw it`, `Where it resolves now`, `The router first saw it`, each with its value), and the sentence that bounds them: `The router records where a marketplace resolves, never who owns it and never what changed inside it`. subject.cell: execution-plane=daemon · data-shape=the bundle path asked three ways: untokened POST, GET, tokened POST
subject.note: The verb IS the gate, and it is not describing a mutation. The bundle changes nothing. It is a POST because stage 2 of `ControlHandler.handle` gates the token on POST/DELETE/PATCH only, so the verb is the only thing deciding whether this router hands its whole diagnostic corpus — log lines included — to any unauthenticated caller that can open the loopback port, which per `ControlToken` includes a web page the user merely visits. All three answers are pinned — 401 untokened, 405 on GET, 200 on a tokened POST — so a later tidy-up that makes the verb 'correct' goes red rather than silently opening the route. The 200 is asserted beside the other two so they read as refusals rather than as an absent route.

Can every published glass capture be shown to have been written AT THE SHUTTER rather than afterwards? A manifest that post-dates its capture records what somebody believed, not what the channel did, so it is not lineage -- which is the finding `capture-lineage.py`'s RECONSTRUCTED pass raised against SURF-028 and which `bin/capture-manifest.py` closed on the derivation side. This is the ordering side: the gate requires each published row to carry `capturedAt`, `conditions.windowTitleReadback` and `conditions.cgWindowID`, none of which can be recovered after the fact, or an explicit `provenanceGap` saying that it cannot. WHAT IT DOES NOT PROVE, stated rather than folded in: it establishes that the row COULD only have been written by something standing at the shutter, not that it was. Only the capture channel writing its own row does that, which `bin/capture-mac-glass.sh` does and which no reader can verify from the artifact alone.

subject.cell: execution-plane=windows-host - modality=operating-system crash record - data-shape=one deliberate fail-fast
subject.note: A REAL STATUS_STOWED_EXCEPTION, raised on demand, and what the XAML handler did about it - DEF-086. That row said this repository had no way to raise one: the original Skills crash was removed by DEF-077 and DEF-078, and a cross-ABI fault was not something product code could ask for. It turned out the lane already raised one without recognising it. An UNGUARDED throw from a DispatcherQueue callback - `--fault dispatcher --fault-unregister dispatcher`, which is DEF-085 as found - terminates MCPRouter.Shell.exe with WER Application Error 1000, exception code 0xc000027b, faulting module CoreMessagingXP.dll, fault offset 0x0000000000093b76. WHAT IT MEASURES: on that same run the region of shell-startup.log ends at `fault: injecting dispatcher` with nothing appended, so Microsoft.UI.Xaml.Application.UnhandledException does not see this class. DEF-079's mechanism field guessed exactly that and recorded it as unestablished; it is established now. THE RECORDER IS NOT THE WRITER, twice over: WER is written by the operating system after the process is gone, and it is read here through Get-WinEvent over the Windows Application log, which is a different API from the file the shell appends to. THE CONTROL: the guarded run of the same fault leaves no Application Error at all, so the record is the injection's rather than something this machine produces anyway. WHAT IT DOES NOT SETTLE, and this is the narrower thing rather than the wider claim: what matches the Skills crash of 2026-09-02 is the exception code, the faulting module and the fault offset - identical to the Application Error entries this machine still holds from 18:57:35 and 19:03:30 that day - and NOT a stack. This case says this host raises the same stowed-exception fail-fast and that the XAML handler does not catch it. It does not say the original throw took the identical path; DEF-077 named that throw and fixed it.

subject.detail: prototype.html routes ?pane=evals and titles the board Evals; the running app's window title reads back Checks. Found by capture-lineage's tie pass, which refused a capture whose recorded target did not resolve to the surface's route. The rename went one way and the design of record was not followed.
subject.text: WITHDRAWN 20 Aug 2026 — this was not a product defect. It was recorded as "prototype.html routes ?pane=evals and titles the board Evals; the running app's window title reads back Checks". The second half is false. `prototype.html:600` declares the sidebar entry as `{id:'evals',t:'Checks',ic:'evals'}` — the route **id** is `evals` and the **title** is `Checks` — and the board's own header draws the selected suite (`pr-summariser · 8 cases`) rather than a board name at all. So the design of record titles this board Checks, the app titles it Checks, and there was never a rename to follow. WHAT ACTUALLY HAPPENED is a detector artefact, and it is worth keeping for that: capture-lineage's tie pass refused a capture whose recorded target did not resolve to the surface's title, and the target it held was the route id. An id and a title are different fields that the design is entitled to disagree on, so a tie pass that compares one to the other reports a rename wherever a route is not named after its board. Checked against the other seven boards: no second instance, because every other route id matches its title. Closed rather than deleted, so the next reader meets the artefact rather than rediscovering it.
subject.title: a route id was compared against a board title, and they differ in the design itself

subject.detail: MCPROUTER_SCENARIO=empty launched the app and Discover still rendered the populated catalogue — GitHub 2,984 sessions, DeepWiki 2,332 — so the surface is not reading the router's answer. Measured on glass by PhoneGlassTests.testDiscoverTracksWhatTheRouterReturned, iPhone 16 Pro, iOS 26.5. CLOSED 20 Aug 2026. Mechanism: `FixtureControlAPIClient.searchRegistry` ignored the scenario entirely and decoded the same `registry-search` recording for all fourteen, so MCPROUTER_SCENARIO=empty reached the client and the client answered with a populated catalogue. Discover was reading its data correctly from the wrong answer. `.empty` is now built in code beside `skills()` and `marketplaces()` rather than added as a second file under Control/Fixtures, which parity-fixture.sh would replay against a reference that cannot reproduce it. `sources` is zeroed with `results`. testDiscoverTracksWhatTheRouterReturned passes.
subject.title: the empty scenario does not reach Discover on the phone

subject.text: Measured 20 Aug 2026. `make test` failed with 4 issues at a one-minute load average of ~700 and passed all 1473 tests in 179 suites at load 46, on the same source, minutes apart. The four were `ActivityReconnectTests` (`a reconnect over a feed that stays live releases its guard`), `DiscoverBoardTests` (`client.searchQueries.count` reading 1 where the baseline said 2), and `SettingsAndMenuBarTests` twice (`model.trackerState` still nil). An earlier run at the same load failed only the first, so the set was not stable either — which is what separated this from a product defect. A suite that reports a defect the product does not have is the failure this campaign has already paid for once, in DEF-029, where a dead instrument read as a dead product for ten consecutive runs. CLOSED by making each wait a condition rather than a deadline, at three sites: 1. `ShellTestSupport.waitUntil` — ceiling 5s → 30s. It returns the moment the condition holds, so a passing test pays nothing for the larger bound; the bound exists only so a condition that never arrives fails instead of hanging. Five seconds was inside the scheduling noise of a contended host, which is the whole finding. 2. `ActivityReconnectTests.completes` — 2s → 30s, same argument. The defect it bounds is a call that *never* returns, so it exhausts any budget and a generous one costs only the time a genuine hang takes to report. 3. `DiscoverBoardTests.searchIsDebounced` — a fixed sleep replaced by two waits, because the claim has two halves and one sleep proved neither on a slow host. First a bounded wait for the debounce to fire at all; then a full debounce window of quiet with the count still at one, which is what rules out one request per keystroke. The second is a real quiet period rather than a deadline, so load cannot shorten it into a false pass — the wait on its own is satisfied by the *first* request and would pass against exactly the defect this test exists to catch. Armed 20 Aug 2026, all three, each watched to fail with its own message: `waitUntil` at `.seconds(0)` reads `no poll ran at all`, `the poll died with the scene that started it` and `five keystrokes issued 0 requests`; `completes` at `.milliseconds(1)` reads `reconnect did not return while the feed stayed live`; and a `queryChanged()` inserted inside the quiet period reads `a later request arrived: five keystrokes issued 2 requests in total`. The original trigger is not reproducible on demand from here — the load came from another project's Rust test binary, two node processes and `lsdiagnose` — so the fix is proven by the arms rather than by reproducing the contention.
subject.title: four async package tests asserted on a deadline the machine could miss

subject.text: Measured 20 Aug 2026 on two different worktrees the same afternoon. A fresh `git worktree` has no `node_modules` and no `dist`; `parity-selftest` is the last target `make all` runs, and its own environment check therefore fires only after lint, both builds, 1483 package tests, the iOS lane and the on-glass lane have all passed. Both runs came back `exit=2` on a tree where nothing was wrong with the code — roughly forty minutes each, twice. It is a lane defect rather than a product one, and the shape is familiar: the gate was honest (it said `the MCP SDK is not installed. Run npm install.` rather than skipping) and it was honest at the wrong moment. A check that can only fail on the environment belongs where the environment is checked. CLOSED by moving both checks into the `tools` target, which `all` runs first: `node_modules` must exist, and `dist/index.js` must exist because without it `parity-lane-selftest` SKIPS, and a skip is not a pass. Each names the command that fixes it. Armed 20 Aug 2026 in a bare directory holding nothing but the Makefile: with no `node_modules` it exits 1 naming `npm install && npm run build`, and with `node_modules` present but no `dist` it exits 1 naming `npm run build` and saying why a skip is not a pass. Costs a millisecond on a tree that has both.
subject.title: the whole-repo gate discovered a missing environment forty minutes in, twice

subject.text: CleanupBoardRow carries three treatments for a skill row — the `Read first…` substitution when SkillChecks.originUnchanged fails, the skill-kind `Remove…` drawn disabled because the router removes servers and never files on disk, and the candidacy reason — and none of them had a rendered path in any configuration of the product. A skill is proposed for cleanup only when every readable client lacks it, and all six skills in SkillFixtures.populated are installed somewhere, so the Debug Cleanup board drew three servers and zero skills. Release reaches the branch only if a real user happens to hold an orphaned skill. CASE-0136 asserted the branch exists by reading CleanupBoardRow and said in its own note why it stopped there; what nobody could say was that a build had ever drawn it. Fixed in-campaign by adding a Debug-only `cleanupSkills` scenario and two SkillFixtures.uninstalled rows, kept separate from `populated` because SURF-004's on-glass predicate asserts the count populated publishes. No view code was touched and no assertion was weakened. Now photographed by CASE-0138/CASE-0139 and guarded in the harness by CASE-0144.
subject.title: the Cleanup board's skill half could not be drawn by any build

subject.source: app/Sources/MCPRouterKit/Control/Scenario.swift; evidence/runs/make-test-3.log (clean build, 1512 tests in 188 suites); app/Scripts/enum-layout-stamp.py; Makefile target enum-layout-stamp; evidence/runs/make-test-4.log
subject.text: Adding a 14th case to `Scenario` made `make test` fail with 31 issues, two of which cannot be true of the source: `Expectation failed: (… → .live) == (.live → .fixture(…cleanupSkills))` in ShellClientFactoryTests and TriageSourceGuardTests, both asserting a Release-posture guard that returns .live unconditionally. `git stash` of the two changed source files → 19 tests pass; unstash → the same failures return, which reads as a real regression. It is not. `Choice.live` is encoded in the spare inhabitants of `Scenario`'s tag, so a new Scenario case shifts that encoding, and stale MCPRouterUI object files compiled against the old layout compare a value that no longer means what they think. `rm -rf app/.build` then rebuild: 5/5 pass, then 1512/1512. The hazard for this campaign is the mirror case — a stale build can as easily produce a green — so any test evidence taken across an enum change is taken from a clean build. MITIGATED 2026-08-20: `app/Scripts/enum-layout-stamp.py` hashes the ordered case list of every enum in the package (212 of them) and removes `app/.build` when that hash moves; `make test` now depends on it. The stamp is the case lists rather than the source, so it holds still for an ordinary edit and for a `switch` over the enum — the false positive a naive grep for `^\s*case` would hit — and moves for an added or renamed case. Armed on all four: comment SAME, switch statement SAME, added Scenario case MOVED, renamed Scenario case MOVED, restore back to baseline. The SwiftPM behaviour itself is unchanged and still upstream; what is fixed is this repo's exposure to it.

subject.detail: `evidence/shots/captures.json` is the only manifest `capture-lineage.py --gate` reads, and two lanes write it: `capture-mac-glass.sh`, and `scripts/acceptance/name-glass-attachments.py`, which merges the iOS lane's rows up from `evidence/shots/ios/captures.json`. subject.detail: `campaign.py` keeps defects in `inventory.json` under a `defect` list, and `add` assigns the next id from that list. `defects.in.json` is an input file. Twelve defects found in the sittings of 19 and 20 Aug were written straight into the input file with hand-written ids taken from that file's own length, which had stopped tracking the registry at DEF-006. The result: DEF-007 through DEF-018 each named one defect in the registry and a different one in the staging file, and neither file said so. Visible symptom, and the only reason it was caught: `RUN-2026-08-20.md` contains 'DEF-011 is the finding worth acting on ... Cleanup's' at line 96 and 'DEF-011 - the rendered-quality gate has never been able to run' at line 481, in one document, meaning two unrelated things. This is `capture-lineage`'s failure mode moved from pictures to identifiers: a name binding to two subjects with nothing checking the binding. Fixed by renumbering the twelve staged defects to DEF-034..DEF-045, merging them into the registry, and rewriting the fifteen references that meant the staged numbering. Every renumbered record carries `stagedAs` naming its old local id, so a reader meeting the old number in an untouched artifact can resolve it. The remaining 74 references were checked one at a time and meant the registry defect they already named. A fourth lesson, from the third instance's cleanup rather than from the collision itself. Reconstructing the concurrent session's two entries welded `text: ""` and `note: ""` onto both, and the first renumbering pass then used `"text" in d` to tell the two writers' entries apart -- so the artifact defeated the discriminator that would have caught it. Both authors independently read the empty values as harmless because they carried no content. The hazard is shape, not content: a membership test reads a key's PRESENCE, and an empty string defeats `"text" in d` exactly as thoroughly as a populated one would. `campaign.py add` injects only `id`, `status`, `evidence` and `armed`, so that key-shape occurred on exactly the two reconstructed entries and was traceable; the keys were stripped and the pass re-run discriminating on `title`. Recorded because "empty therefore harmless" is a reasonable-sounding wrong answer that both sessions gave.
subject.note: SECOND INSTANCE, 20 Aug 2026, in the case registry rather than the defect registry, and it landed the same way. A helper reported `next case id: CASE-0145` while cases.json already held CASE-0149 and CASE-0150; campaign.py's own `next_id` is max+1 and would have said CASE-0151, so the number that was trusted did not come from it. `add` takes an explicit id through `setdefault` and therefore appends a second entry rather than refusing, so CASE-0149 and CASE-0150 each came to name two cases -- an iOS Settings structural case against REQ-005 and a RouterCore write-failure case against REQ-019 -- and the `set` calls that followed wrote onto the pre-existing pair. Caught by an evidence-existence audit rather than by any gate: the new cases printed `3 evidence` where two were supplied. Restored from `git show HEAD:` (both pre-existing entries are byte-identical to HEAD again, verified by dict comparison) and the new pair renumbered to CASE-0153 and CASE-0154. The registry is sparse -- 74 gaps between 1 and 152 -- so a free-looking number is not evidence that it is free, and only max+1 is. THIRD INSTANCE, the same evening, and this one had two writers rather than one. A second Claude session working the same campaign allocated DEF-047 and DEF-048 at about 23:30 (the SDK -32603 message discard, and a detector defect in vacuity-check.py's blind pass) and committed planning/test-campaign as a directory in 6bdeea4, which also swept up this session's in-progress registry edits. This session allocated DEF-047 and DEF-048 for different defects minutes later, from a read taken before that commit landed. Resolved by renumbering THIS session's pair to DEF-049 and DEF-050 -- the later allocation moves, and the session that moves is the one that can enumerate its own references, which is the only reason the choice is safe rather than arbitrary. The peer's entries were not edited. Note for anyone reading the mechanism: `add` assigns from the registry list, so two writers holding a stale read get the same number, and no gate in the campaign detects it. The detection here was a peer message, and before that an evidence-existence audit; neither is a gate. campaign.py could refuse an explicit id that already exists -- `add` currently takes one through `setdefault` and appends a duplicate instead.
