subject.detail: Measured 2026-08-21 against test-campaign 0.9.2 on app/Tests. The pass reports examined=1661 mutating=320 blind=88. Two structural errors and two idiom errors inflate that number. STRUCTURAL. (1) It scans every `func`, not every test. Restricted to swift-testing's own discriminator (a func whose nearest preceding annotation is @Test) the denominator is 1531, not 1661: 130 of the examined functions are not tests. (2) Its helper exclusion at vacuity-check.py:162 is file-scoped — a name is a helper only if called more than once in the file that declares it. A shared stub declared in TestSupport.swift and called from other files therefore reads as a test, so MemoryFileSystem's `write`, `removeItem` and `moveItem`, HTTPStub's `stop` and WatchTestSupport's `remove` are each counted as a blind test. 21 of the 88 are support-file functions. IDIOM, on the mutator side. (3) The lookbehind `(?<![A-Za-z0-9_])` cannot exclude a dot, so a Swift enum case constructor matches a mutator verb: `ServerRowAction.forServer(s, pendingAuth: nil) == .reset(.clearPlacard)` reports ServerPresentationTests::trippedOutranksHeld as mutating via 'reset', where `.reset` is the expected VALUE inside the assertion. 41 of 72 re-measured findings are dot-prefixed. (4) It takes the last mutator by source POSITION and calls everything after it the tail, which misreads three Swift constructs: a mutator inside the assertion (`await #expect(throws: Never.self) { try await store.delete() }` — nothing can follow it by construction), a mutator in a `defer` block (source-early, execution-last, so the whole test body reads as 'after'), and a mutator as the last statement of a loop body whose observation is the next iteration (CallbackLifecycleTests::stopReleasesTheSocket rebinds the port ten times; the read of cycle N is the start() of cycle N+1). SAMPLE. Of the 15 findings with zero assertions after the last mutator — the highest-yield stratum — 9 were read in full. Two (DiscoveryTests::servers, CapabilityPlateTests::install) are helpers. All 7 remaining are real tests that do observe after mutating, through idioms no reader verb names: `client.calls.last?.operation`, `seen.filter { ... }`, a rebind that throws. Precision on that stratum is 0 of 7. ARMED, two ways, evidence/arming/blind-mutation.arming.log. A probe @Test that mutates and never observes was added and removed: blind moved 88 -> 89 -> 88 and examined/mutating moved by exactly 1 each time. The check does bite; it is the false-positive rate that is at issue, not the sensitivity. NOT REMEDIED BY VOCABULARY. The reader side is deliberately loose because a false reader match suppresses a finding. Adding this codebase's read idioms (`calls`, `operation`, `filter`) would lower the number without improving what the pass knows, and the terms are generic enough to suppress true findings too. The 88 stands recorded as a worklist with its measured precision beside it rather than tuned to look better. RE-MEASURED 2026-08-27 by G22, which declared `testRoot` and gave this pass a corpus for the first time. THE 88 DOES NOT REPRODUCE. Vendored 0.9.2 over `app/Tests` today reports examined=2133 mutating=3 blind=3, against the 1661/320/88 above. The denominator moving up while `mutating` collapses 320 → 3 is not tree churn: 0.9.1 and 0.9.2 ship IDENTICAL DEFAULT_MUTATORS and DEFAULT_READERS, and neither list holds `reset`, `write`, `removeItem`, `moveItem` or `remove` — the verbs this entry's idiom argument turns on. So the 2026-08-21 sitting ran an expanded vocabulary passed on the command line, and `campaign.json` declares none, which makes 88 a figure no documented invocation returns. Its cited evidence, `evidence/arming/blind-mutation.arming.log`, has never existed on any branch of this repository (`git log --all -- '*blind-mutation*'` is empty), so the arming claim above is not checkable from the tree. The measured structural and idiom errors are not withdrawn; what is withdrawn is the population they were measured over. TODAY'S POPULATION, AND ITS PRECISION. With `testRoot: app` the pass reports examined=2179 mutating=3 re-read-after=0 blind=3, and 0.15.0 returns the same three findings from the same corpus. All THREE were read in full — 3 of 3, not a sample — and all three are false positives. Precision 0 of 3. A FOURTH CAUSE, NOT IN THE ORIGINAL ENTRY, AND THE ONE THAT PRODUCES TWO OF THE THREE. The body slice is `src[pos:end]` where `pos` is the start of the DECLARATION, so a test whose own name begins with a mutator verb matches itself. `WatchRestartTests::restartIsIssuedBeforeTheStagingWrite` and `::restartIsOwedBeforeTheWriteLands` contain no mutating call at all: the only `restart\w*\(` in each is `func restart…(` on its own declaration line. Both then read — `WatchWorld.read(scratch.logPath)`, `WatchState.load(path:)`, `WatchWorld.serverNames(in:)` — and assert on `state.mcpServersHash` and `state.restartPending`. The third, `PhoneStorageFailureTests::restartRechecksTheCamera`, does call `await model.restart()` and then asserts twice, on `model.step` and on `model.entry.characters`: property reads that no reader verb names, which is cause (4)'s shape rather than a new one. This cause survives into 0.15.0 unchanged. NOT ENROLLED IN A GATE, and `blindVocabulary` still not declared, for the reason the entry already gives. A related gap measured at the same sitting: pointed at `src/` — the TypeScript tree, which has no tests — the pass prints `corpus: … (0 file(s))` and `examined=0 mutating=0 blind=0` and contributes nothing to `--gate`. It reports its empty corpus and does not fail on it, so a mis-declared `testRoot` reads as a clean pass. VOCABULARY DECLARED 2026-08-29 by K4, and the entry's own 'NOT REMEDIED BY VOCABULARY' paragraph is narrowed rather than withdrawn. That paragraph reasons entirely from the READER side, and on the reader side it is still right: adding this codebase's read idioms lowers the count without improving what the pass knows, which is why the declared reader list stops short of `expect` and `require` -- swift-testing's assertion macros, 5781 and 383 occurrences, either of which would mark every test that asserts after mutating as re-reading and collapse the count to near zero while the pass learned nothing. THE MUTATOR SIDE WAS NEVER ARGUED, AND THAT IS WHERE THE PASS WAS BLIND. Measured over the same 2282 test bodies at `83e5380`: the nine snake_case defaults find 3 mutating call sites; a camelCase list derived from this corpus finds 481. So `blind=3` was a reading of 3 of 481, a recall of 0.6%, and the entry's `precision 0 of 3` was a precision over a population the instrument could barely see. `campaign.json` now carries `blindVocabulary` with `only: true`, 19 mutators and 34 readers, derived mechanically -- a verb is kept only where method calls on a receiver are at least half its corpus sites and its own `func` declaration lines at most a quarter, which is causes (3) and (4) of this entry turned into a selection rule. THE THREE FINDINGS ARE ADJUDICATED, and each clears for a different checkable reason rather than all three for one. `restartIsIssuedBeforeTheStagingWrite`: one fitted mutator, `WatchWorld.remove(scratch)` inside a `defer`, and four declared readers after it -- `load`, `read`, `parse`, `servers`. NOT blind, positively. `restartIsOwedBeforeTheWriteLands`: three fitted mutators, the last `WatchState(restartPending: true).save(`, with `load` after it. NOT blind, positively. `restartRechecksTheCamera`: ZERO fitted mutator call sites in its body. It was flagged only because `restart` is a shipped default and this entry's fourth cause -- the body slice beginning at the declaration -- made `func restartRechecksTheCamera(` match itself. `restart` fails the selection rule (1 method call against 3 declaration lines, of 5 sites), so it is not in the vocabulary and the finding is withdrawn. WHAT THAT DOES NOT MEAN: its real mutation `await model.restart()` is now invisible to the pass, and its reads are still the property comparisons `model.step` and `model.entry.characters` that no reader verb names. It is UNEXAMINED by this instrument, not clean, and that is this entry's ceiling stated once more rather than closed. ARMED, AND ENROLLED, which the entry recorded as missing. `planning/test-campaign/bin/blind-vocabulary-arm.py` runs on every `make lint`: two plants identical but for one line, each measured alone and again inside a `shutil.copytree` of the real corpus, requiring examined+1 mutating+1 blind+1 for the blind plant and examined+1 mutating+1 blind+0 for the reading one. The specificity arm is the half a sensitivity arm alone cannot give: a detector that flagged every mutating body would pass the first and say nothing. 6 of 6 as expected on `cache 0.16.0` and again on the `vendor/` pin via `--instrument`. The two disagree only on the denominator -- 2282 against 2277, the five arrow-style `it/test(` blocks 0.9.3 added block detection for -- and agree on blind=111. THE 111 IS A WORKLIST AND THE CAMPAIGN STILL PUBLISHES NO BLIND NUMBER. Nothing above touches the structural causes: the pass still examines every `func` rather than every `@Test`, its helper exclusion is still file-scoped, and a `defer` mutator still reads as source-early -- which is exactly why the first of the three findings above needed reading rather than counting. This entry stays OPEN; what it now carries is a measured recall beside its measured precision.

cell.role: whoever asks whether DEF-043's two elements are still missing

subject.note: SOURCE-ANALYSIS, AND THAT IS THE CEILING. This case reads Swift. It does not run the Mac app and does not photograph a board, and it cannot on this host: the shell is a SwiftPM target with no Windows build and `swift` is not on LUKESFF. A green means the code that draws DEF-043's two elements is present and composed the way DESIGN.md section 2 requires. It does NOT mean either element reached a screen, and it must not be read as closing DEF-043. M27 asked for on-glass coverage and that is still owed, on a Mac, through the campaign's own capture lane. WHAT IT ESTABLISHES. SidebarFoot renders the address on its `.address` case; the reading comes from LoopbackAddress.hostPort while the Settings endpoint row comes from LoopbackAddress.controlEndpoint, so the two cannot drift; no literal host:port appears in any of the four files that DISPLAY an address; and ReadoutCopy.childProcessesLabel is "Child processes" and Readout draws it - the string DEF-043 measured in 0 of 9 accessibility dumps. THE FIRST RUN FAILED AND THE INSTRUMENT WAS THE ONE AT FAULT. The honesty arm originally refused a literal host:port anywhere in either shell tree and reported `ShellClientFactory.shippingEndpoint`. Every reference to that symbol was then read: it is consumed by Choice.live, LiveControlAPIClient, ControlEventStream and the Release guard, and reaches no view. It is a dialled endpoint, not a displayed one, and the honesty rule governs what a user is told. The scope was corrected rather than the finding suppressed, and the sweep was NOT narrowed: it still covers both trees, and a literal outside the display files fails unless its symbol is declared with a reason - which plant Q6 watches. PLATFORM. macOS, and DEF-043 never said so, which is what the row cost to establish. M27-sidebar-foot-readout.md reads `Category: mac`, the evidence is nine accessibility dumps at 1156x680 against the Mac design of record, and the sidebar-foot specification is in DESIGN.md section 2 rather than in the Windows floor. The Windows shell's NavigationView declares no pane footer content at all and the Windows floor's own owed list names no sidebar foot, so the absence there is not a defect - Windows was never promised it. This case asserts nothing about Windows, because a check demanding Windows never grow a sidebar foot would redden on somebody adding a good thing.

subject.cell: execution-plane=static-source-read - data-shape=one registry fact removed per arm
subject.note: Seven arms, each removing exactly one fact and requiring the exit code to move: the Harnesses surface row deleted (R1 red), `Insights` removed from the shell's controls (R2 red), CASE-0341 stripped of its surface link (R3 red), SURF-036's controlsSource removed (R4 red), SURF-031's source path misspelt (R4 red), a control invented on SURF-039 (R4 red), and DestinationCatalog.cs emptied - which must exit 2 and REFUSE a verdict rather than reporting a clean registry, because a reader that finds nothing must not report a pass. 7/7 moved. The arm restores every file in a finally, and its last act is to re-run the reader and require green, so a half-applied mutation cannot be left behind as a passing run.

subject.cell: execution-plane=windows-host - data-shape=package not installed
subject.note: A real MSIX, built, deployed and removed, with a recorder at each step that is not the thing that wrote it. MakeAppx packs and .NET's ZipArchive reads the OPC container back - so the identity assertion is made against the PACKED ARTIFACT rather than against the file on disk that was handed to the packer. `winget validate` is the winget client applying a schema this repository does not own. Add-AppxPackage deploys and Get-AppxPackage reports: Fledgeling.MCPRouter_0.1.0.0_x64__facmrsw33693e. THE INSTALL ARM IS WHAT TURNS A FILE INTO A PACKAGE. A manifest can pack cleanly, validate cleanly, and be refused at deployment for a capability, an architecture or a signature - and every static check in the world passes right up to that point. 'CLEAN UNINSTALL RULES' IS THE HALF WORTH READING TWICE. UninstallGuidance promises that uninstalling preserves %USERPROFILE%\.claude\mcp-router. That is a promise about what SURVIVES, and a promise about survival cannot be checked by any amount of reading - only by an uninstall that actually ran. The lane plants a marker, installs, removes, and requires both that the deployment stack reports the package gone and that the marker is still there. WHAT THE LANE PUTS BACK: a self-signed certificate is added to LocalMachine\TrustedPeople so an unsigned developer package can deploy at all, and removed in a finally block however the run ends. Verified afterwards: zero Fledgeling.* packages, zero witness certificates. A lane that left a trusted publisher behind would have changed what this machine will install, silently and for every future run. NOT SETTLED: that anyone can obtain the package. Nothing publishes it, the winget InstallerUrl is a deliberate example.invalid placeholder, and this lane asserts the placeholder is PRESENT so the manifest cannot be mistaken for a shipping one. DEF-083 carries the publishing step, which needs a signing certificate and a pull request into a third-party repository.

subject.cell: execution-plane=windows-host - data-shape=no task registered
subject.note: The Windows task scheduler holding a task the product registered, read by an API that did not write it. The writer is MCPRouter.Shell.Live's LogonTaskSupervisor driving schtasks.exe with the Task Scheduler XML it builds; the recorder is Get-ScheduledTask, the ScheduledTasks module over the scheduler's WMI provider - a different API, a different process and a different vocabulary for the same facts. The XML says RunLevel LeastPrivilege and the recorder answers RunLevel Limited, and nothing in this repository translates between them. The scheduler also normalised the interval this run asked for, PT60S, into PT1M, which is the plainest available evidence that the read did not come back through anything this code wrote. EIGHT ARMS, AND TWO ARE ABOUT THE INSTRUMENT. BASELINE requires the recorder to report the task ABSENT before registration - without it, a task left behind by an interrupted run makes every other arm pass over a run that registered nothing. SILENCE requires it to report absence again after removal, which is what separates a reader from an echo: a recorder that always answered yes would satisfy the six product arms by construction. The other six read the three claims LifecyclePresentation prints to the operator - triggered at logon, un-elevated, restarting on failure - plus the executable and port this run asked for, plus presence and removal. WHAT IT DOES NOT SETTLE, and the reason it is one case rather than the whole of REQ-035: nothing here logs the user out, so the trigger has never been watched to fire, and nothing here starts or kills a daemon, so the restart has never been watched to happen. DEF-081 carries those two. This case settles that the registration the product performs produces, in the Windows task scheduler, a task carrying the properties the product's own UI describes - which before 2026-09-02 was unmeasured entirely, and which DEF-074 recorded as a supervision model nothing performed.

subject.cell: execution-plane=windows-host - data-shape=a supervised process that dies
subject.note: The half of WIN23's supervision promise that had never been watched: a daemon the Windows task scheduler starts, loses, and starts again. DEF-081 filed it as unmeasurable and named the blocker as a missing Windows daemon binary; the blocker was real and is gone - app/windows/MCPRouter.Witness.Daemon is a harness process that starts, records its own start and waits to be killed, so there is something for the scheduler to supervise. WHAT THE MEASUREMENT FOUND IS NOT WHAT THE ROW EXPECTED. The registration the product wrote carried RestartOnFailure with a 60-second interval and a count of 3, and it did not restart the daemon at all. Killed, watched 150 seconds, on the unified scheduling engine and the legacy one, for a run started by a trigger and one started on demand: four registrations, no restart. The same block DID restart, three times at exactly 60 seconds, a task whose Command named a file that does not exist - so the instrument can see a restart, and RestartOnFailure governs a task that fails to LAUNCH rather than one whose action launched and later died. DEF-320 carries that, and the product now writes a Repetition on the trigger alongside MultipleInstancesPolicy IgnoreNew. THE RECORDERS ARE TWO AND NEITHER WROTE ANYTHING: Get-ScheduledTaskInfo for the scheduler's own account of its runs, and Get-CimInstance Win32_Process for the process identity, which is what makes 'it came back' a different process id rather than a report from the thing that came back. The daemon's own run log is carried and graded by nothing. EIGHT ARMS, THREE OF THEM ABOUT THE INSTRUMENT: BASELINE requires both tasks absent and no daemon running, so nothing below is inherited from an interrupted run; CLAIM.repetition and CLAIM.ignorenew read the product's own unmodified logon registration back through the WMI provider; SILENCE requires both recorders to say no once the tasks are gone. ONE SUBSTITUTION, SAID OUT LOUD: a trigger repetition does not apply to an on-demand start - measured, twice - so the live task carries a TimeTrigger where the product writes a LogonTrigger, because this lane must not log the machine out. Every Setting, the repetition interval, the principal, the action and the instances policy are the product's own document. That the trigger fires AT LOGON is still unwitnessed and DEF-081 keeps it.

subject.evidence: scripts/windows/win23-logon-task-witness.ps1 measures the REGISTRATION and says so in its own notMeasured[]: it does not log the user out and it does not start or kill a daemon. So the two behaviours the operator is actually promised - that the daemon comes up at logon, and that a crashed one comes back - rest on the Windows task scheduler honouring a LogonTrigger and a RestartOnFailure block that this repository has confirmed are present and has never confirmed are honoured. UPDATED 2026-09-03: planning/evidence/WIN23/run/restart-witness.json (all 8 arms held) and restart-witness-armed.json (exactly LIVE.restarted broke).

Every sidebar row is selected in turn and the effect is read in the RESTORATION STORE, which is a different channel from the one that struck: `ShellModel.selection`'s `didSet` calls `store.save(destination:)`, so a real selection leaves a value in a scratch `UserDefaults` suite that nothing in the test wrote, and that a relaunch reads. `model.selection == .servers` after `model.select(.servers)` was deliberately NOT used — it reads the property the call just wrote, which is the actuation side of the vacuous assertion (`references/inert-ui.md`, `detector-defects.md` §11). Each row is approached from a DIFFERENT destination, because `didSet` guards on `oldValue != selection` and a loop starting where the model boots would have the first row write nothing at all. The destination-collapse relation is asserted as a count rather than as seven separate greens: seven presses, seven DISTINCT persisted values, so a shell whose rows all led to one place fails on the cardinality. A second model built on the same store comes up where the last row left it, which is the read-back a relaunch actually performs. `Settings` is the eighth control and is not a destination: M15 moved it to a scene of its own, so the effect read is the installed opener firing exactly once AND the console's persisted destination not moving. Both halves, because an implementation that opened the scene and also selected a board would pass the first alone. LIMIT, stated rather than left implicit: a persisted destination proves the selection took. It does not prove a different board was DRAWN — SwiftUI's view tree is opaque to a SwiftPM test and `ContentZone`'s switch is unreachable from here. That half is CASE-0001's, on glass, and it is FAILING (DEF-058, DEF-059), so it counts nothing. This is the in-process half and says which half it is.

J2. `Held` and `All` are the two filter chips SURF-004 declares, driven off one loaded reading of the fixture. `Held` is asserted in both directions against `Skill.held?.wantsMore` — every row it draws has an update held, and every row it hid does not — and `All` is asserted as the RESTORATION, which is the assertion that fails if a segment latches. SURF-004 reaches 2 of 21 and the remaining four state-changing controls are recorded in `inventory.json` under `controlsUnactuatable` rather than left in the denominator unexplained: the build draws none of them. That is DEF-062, and it is the finding this case produced — `references/inert-ui.md`'s own stated limit is that no amount of testing the build reveals what the build lacks, and giving the surface a denominator is what made the four visible.

N8. The inertness guard on the untrusted-input boundary, made capable of failing. M19 shipped `MarkdownSecurityTests.htmlIsInert` with four spellings that named `javascript:`, no scheme, or nothing, and two assertions -- no link, no `imageURL` -- that `MarkdownInline.sanitized` makes true of every input it touches. It could not go red. M30 wired `ControlAPICapabilityDocumentSource` into the shipped UI, so router-served third-party text now reaches this renderer in a Release build, and the guard on it measured nothing. MEASURED, not assumed: the platform parser does keep inline HTML inert -- under `MarkdownInline`'s own options it hands each tag back as characters and marks it `.inlineHTML`, an intent naming no destination, and it does so under all four combinations of `allowsExtendedAttributes` and `interpretedSyntax`. Swift 6.2, macOS 26.6.2 (25G83), Debug, `swift test`. So this was an evidence defect and not a live vulnerability, and the fix is the assertion rather than new sanitisation. Two `https` spellings were added, because `https` is the one scheme the allowlist keeps and therefore the only one that can carry an interpreted `<a>` through to the assertion; a presence control runs the same reader over the markdown twin of the same destination first; and two clauses were added that the old body did not have -- handed back verbatim, and no attribute beyond the `.inlineHTML` marker. That last clause also corrects the test's own claim: the parser DOES attach one attribute to inline HTML and `sanitized` carries it, so the old name -- `inline HTML acquires no attribute of any kind` -- was false as written as well as unfailable, which is why nobody found out.

subject.note: SURF-029's two SecondaryCommands, 'Export log' and 'Reset router', were enumerated and unreached: a CommandBar does not realise its overflow items while the overflow is shut, so the at-rest lane could only record an absence with its reason, and planning/registry-drop-gate.py reported the surface as uncovered for exactly that. This case opens the overflow through ExpandCollapsePattern.Expand and reads both commands back with their names and ControlType.Button, between a BASELINE and a SILENCE that both find them absent from the control view AND the raw view. The writer is not the reader: overflow-actuate.ps1 expands in its own process and writes only the ExpandCollapseState it saw, while every element reading comes from uia-dump.ps1 started separately. TWO FINDINGS FROM THE FIRST RUN, neither planted, both corrected in the manifest rather than in the assertion. (1) probe-expectation.json predicted that opening the overflow would cost the never-activated guarantee, and IT WAS RIGHT: the probe held the foreground at none of the three baseline samples and at all six effect and silence samples, so Expand activates the window and Collapse does not hand the foreground back. That cost is now DECLARED as `overflow.activationCost` and compared both ways, so the day WinUI stops activating, this arm reddens rather than quietly acquiring a guarantee nobody re-checked. Baseline stays a hard assertion. (2) each command resolves to TWO tree paths with the overflow open, because WinUI publishes the OverflowPopup subtree once through a Microsoft.UI.Content.PopupWindowSiteBridge child and once in place beneath the ApplicationBar. Both copies agree on name, controlType, className, isEnabled, isOffscreen, accessKey, patterns and bounding rectangle, so it is one control on two routes; the assertion now permits several matches only while they agree on everything a caller would act on, and plant (H) watches that a genuinely different control under one id still fails. WHAT THIS DOES NOT BUY. It is not at-rest coverage and does not close DESIGN.md section 11 rule 9 for these two commands. The product fix is a surface that realises them without an actuation, and that is DEF-340. Neither command is INVOKED, so both stay outside the actuation census with a stated reason on SURF-029; this arm's subject is realisation and vocabulary, not effect. And the subject is WIN20's probe rather than the MCP Router Windows client: it measures WinUI 3's automation behaviour on this machine.

subject.note: The verb IS the gate, and it is not describing a mutation. The bundle changes nothing. It is a POST because stage 2 of `ControlHandler.handle` gates the token on POST/DELETE/PATCH only, so the verb is the only thing deciding whether this router hands its whole diagnostic corpus — log lines included — to any unauthenticated caller that can open the loopback port, which per `ControlToken` includes a web page the user merely visits. All three answers are pinned — 401 untokened, 405 on GET, 200 on a tokened POST — so a later tidy-up that makes the verb 'correct' goes red rather than silently opening the route. The 200 is asserted beside the other two so they read as refusals rather than as an absent route.

Written from the ambient section of scripts/windows/uia/shell-lane.ps1, which runs out of process against the real shell binary in the interactive session and DRIVES THE ROUTER FROM OUTSIDE THE APPLICATION: the lane owns the router the shell is pointed at - its own node process, on its own port, over its own MCP_ROUTER_HOME - and these rows stop it, put a stand-in on that port and start it again while the shell is told nothing at all. What is read back is the pane footer, addressed by AutomationId, never by name. The lane recorded: the router was stopped from outside the application - this script killed the process and then confirmed, over the loopback port, that nothing answers http://127.0.0.1:62755/status - and the shell's pane moved to 'Cannot reach router' / 'The router daemon is not responding on 127.0.0.1:62755.'. It does not say 'Router ready' over a router that is not running, which is DEF-301 exactly. THE RECORDER IS NOT THE WRITER, and on this row it is not even the shell: UI Automation read of the shell pane, over a router state driven by starting and stopping processes outside the application. That is what makes this row a claim about the MACHINE rather than about the application's own report of itself, which is the whole of DEF-087. WHAT IT DOES NOT SETTLE: that the registration fires at a real logon, and that a daemon executable resolves on an operator's machine - the lane points the shipped resolution at a witness task name and a witness executable of its own so it cannot disturb the operator's real registration. Both limits stay on DEF-087's resolution rather than being folded into this green. THE CALL THIS LANE MADE, which is what `actuates` is NOT for: the row was driven through System.Windows.Automation's TogglePattern.Toggle() from shell-lane.ps1. `actuates` carries the control the surface declares - DEF-080.

subject.text: PARTLY CLOSED 20 Aug 2026, and the part that is not closed is named rather than left as a silent gap. The vocabulary differential compared accessible names of AXButton/AXCheckBox/AXPopUpButton/AXTextField against their DOM counterparts board by board, with the shell and the fixture rows subtracted, and reported examined=8 boards, in-design-not-build=20, in-build-not-design=16. Cleanup's design specifies Inspect, Read first… and Remove on each row and the running board published none of them. FIXED: `CleanupBoardRow` now draws a trailing action column — `prototype.html:950` gives it `width:150px` — carrying `Inspect` and `Remove…`, wired by `CleanupBoard` to the selection and to the removal dialog. Removal opens the dialog rather than removing, because the one destructive act on this board is never one click. It is dimmed in place for a skill with `CheckCopy.skillRemoveDisabled` as both tooltip and accessibility hint, exactly as `CleanupInspector.actions` already does it — a reason only a mouse can reach is not a reason. The row's accessibility element moved from `children: .combine` to `.contain`, because combining flattens the buttons into the label and leaves nothing to press: the same failure this campaign already recorded for a time-limited undo inside a live region. FIXED 20 Aug 2026, and it was the half this row was held open for: (a) `Read first…`. `CleanupBoardModel.Candidate` now carries `provenance: String?`, read through `SkillChecks.originUnchanged` rather than off `skill.provenance` directly so this board and the Checks board cannot disagree about what counts as moved, and a server's call site passes `nil` because a server has no marketplace to have moved from. The row draws `Read first…` **in place of** Inspect and Remove rather than beside them — `prototype.html:961` is making the same argument this pane makes everywhere else, and a removal left on that row is one click from a fact nobody has read yet — plus the three other things the design keys on the same field: the fail-coloured leading tile standing in for `dot f`, the warn icon, and the provenance note substituted for the candidacy reason in the `why it is here` column. The tint is painted **behind** the selection fill rather than in front of it, which is a deliberate divergence: the mock sets it as an inline style, which in CSS beats the selected class, so a selected flagged row there reads as unselected. The sheet behind the button states the three fields `SkillProvenance` carries and none of the four the prototype invents — an owner at install, a force-pushed branch, a hash no longer in history, and an eval score — one of which is not computable at all, and it says on screen that its date is the router's own first sighting rather than an install date. Its dismiss reads `Leave it` because there is nothing to cancel, and removal is dimmed in place with `CheckCopy.skillRemoveDisabled` rather than offered, because the control API is read-only for skills and the prototype's `Remove it` would have been a control that does nothing. Guarded by CASE-0135, CASE-0136 and CASE-0137, nine assertions across five tests, all armed — nine mutation arms, each red for its own stated reason. STILL NOT FIXED: (b) the reason column still truncates where the design shows the whole sentence; (c) Checks' `Edit cases` and `Run again`, a different board; (d) Settings' `Pair another device` and `Unpair`, which is DEF-001 reaching this instrument through the design rather than through a failing assertion. Guarded by `CleanupRowActionsTests`, four assertions, all armed 20 Aug 2026: blanking the Inspect label, switching `.contain` back to `.combine`, dropping the board's `inspect:` wiring, and performing a real removal to prove the write-guard predicate is live rather than vacuously true. Measured on the fixed build before it was reported: adding a 156pt action column to every row does **not** push this board into DEF-015's overflow. `AXSplitGroup` reads 980pt inside a 980pt window on Cleanup, unchanged, while Checks, Skills and Discover still read 988, 1044 and 1119 — the same three as before. subject.text: CAUSE FOUND AND FIXED 20 Aug 2026; this record replaces one that said the cause was unknown and named machine saturation as a candidate. The candidate was wrong. The process-wide accessibility engine was OFF, so SwiftUI's `_UIHostingView` built its accessibility container and vended an EMPTY element array — `accessibilityElements == []`, not nil — and every label assertion in the target read empty and reported its own honest verdict, `nothing was measured, so this proved nothing`. That is indistinguishable, from inside the suite, from a product that renders no copy. A probe settled it: calling `_AXSSetAutomationEnabled(true)` took the same hosted view's published element count from 0 to 1. THE ENGINE HAD BEEN ON BY ACCIDENT — something else on this machine had switched it on — which is why this suite was green for months while depending on ambient host state no file in this repo controls, and why it went red with no change to the branch. THREE CHANGES ARE THE FIX, and the third was found only because the first two were not enough. (1) `PhoneSurfaceTests` resolves `_AXSSetAutomationEnabled` out of `/usr/lib/libAccessibility.dylib` (falling back to `AccessibilityUtilities.framework`) via dlopen/dlsym and calls it once per process, before the first `host()`. (2) The walker reads `accessibilityElements` first, because SwiftUI publishes through the array and leaves `accessibilityElementCount()` at 0 — measured on iOS 26.5, where one hosted `Text` reported `accessibilityElements.count == 1` and `accessibilityElementCount() == 0` in the same breath, so reading only the indexed API walked past every element SwiftUI had. Those two took `make test-ios` from 52 failures to 0 — and then `make all`, run immediately afterwards on the same device, came back with 39. (3) THE STATE IS DEVICE-SCOPED AND THE CALL LANDS ON THE NEXT PROCESS, NOT THIS ONE. On a device left in the disabled state, the run that re-enables it fails a DETERMINISTIC set of 15 test cases — identical set, measured three times, verified with `comm` in both directions — and the run after it, with no change to anything, is clean. The 15 are exactly the cases that host a `ScrollView`; the tests that pass alongside them are geometry, counts and negative assertions, all of which an empty tree satisfies, so the green half of that run was vacuous too. `test-ios` therefore runs a throwaway single-test process before the graded one and discards its exit code. MEASURED END TO END: three consecutive runs with the call mutated to `(false)` drive `MCPRouter-Unit` into the disabled state (54 failures each, the whole suite red, which is correct for a dead engine); the very next `make test-ios`, with the warm-up in the recipe, is 36 tests and 0 failures in 1.4s. THE INSTRUMENT CHECK IS ITSELF INSTRUMENTED. `testTheAccessibilityEngineCanBeSwitchedOn` blocks on a probe that hosts `ScrollView { Text }` and reads it back through the same walk every other assertion uses, with a 20s deadline. Two narrower probes were built first and both were wrong in opposite directions, which is why the shape is stated rather than assumed: a bare `Text` read either way reports the engine live at t=0 of a run in which 15 cases went on to read empty, and a `ScrollView` read through the accessibility-container path alone reports the engine dead on a device where all 35 other tests pass. A probe that answers differently from the thing it stands for answers a different question. On a dead engine the deadline fires and the case fails with `no hosted Text published a label within 20s`, measured. ARMED THREE WAYS. (a) Renaming the symbol to `_AXSSetAutomationEnabledXXX` on a device whose engine is already live fails exactly one test — the instrument check — and leaves the other 35 green, which is correct for that arm and proves only the resolution assertion. (b) With the call mutated to `(false)`, the first run on `MCPRouter-Arm`, a device created for the arm, recorded 53 failures across 36 tests: that is what proves the other 35 depend on the engine. (c) The first run ever taken on `MCPRouter-Arm2`, a device whose engine had never been live, is 36 tests and 0 failures, so a fresh device needs no warm-up and only an explicitly disabled one does. Both arm devices were deleted afterwards; `make test-ios IOS_UNIT_DEVICE=<name>` recreates either. TWO HARDENING CHANGES from the investigation are kept and neither is the fix: `test-ios` creates and owns `MCPRouter-Unit` instead of sorting booted devices first — the exact picker DEF-020 condemned, still live in this recipe — and the walk retains every element it visits so `ObjectIdentifier` is unique among live objects as its use assumes. A third, waiting on a product surface's tree over a two-second deadline, was written, measured to change nothing, and removed: it cost 130 seconds a run and bought no measurement. The wait that IS kept differs from it in the one way that matters — it waits on a probe whose answer is known, so a timeout is a fact about the instrument rather than about the view. THE DEPENDENCY IS ON A PRIVATE SYMBOL, in the test target only, never linked into the app; the instrument check fails loudly if a future runtime renames it, so this target goes red rather than quietly empty. Carried as CASE-0126.
subject.title: the iOS unit lane read an empty accessibility tree because the engine was off

subject.source: app/Sources/MCPRouterKit/Control/Scenario.swift; evidence/runs/make-test-3.log (clean build, 1512 tests in 188 suites); app/Scripts/enum-layout-stamp.py; Makefile target enum-layout-stamp; evidence/runs/make-test-4.log
subject.text: Adding a 14th case to `Scenario` made `make test` fail with 31 issues, two of which cannot be true of the source: `Expectation failed: (… → .live) == (.live → .fixture(…cleanupSkills))` in ShellClientFactoryTests and TriageSourceGuardTests, both asserting a Release-posture guard that returns .live unconditionally. `git stash` of the two changed source files → 19 tests pass; unstash → the same failures return, which reads as a real regression. It is not. `Choice.live` is encoded in the spare inhabitants of `Scenario`'s tag, so a new Scenario case shifts that encoding, and stale MCPRouterUI object files compiled against the old layout compare a value that no longer means what they think. `rm -rf app/.build` then rebuild: 5/5 pass, then 1512/1512. The hazard for this campaign is the mirror case — a stale build can as easily produce a green — so any test evidence taken across an enum change is taken from a clean build. MITIGATED 2026-08-20: `app/Scripts/enum-layout-stamp.py` hashes the ordered case list of every enum in the package (212 of them) and removes `app/.build` when that hash moves; `make test` now depends on it. The stamp is the case lists rather than the source, so it holds still for an ordinary edit and for a `switch` over the enum — the false positive a naive grep for `^\s*case` would hit — and moves for an added or renamed case. Armed on all four: comment SAME, switch statement SAME, added Scenario case MOVED, renamed Scenario case MOVED, restore back to baseline. The SwiftPM behaviour itself is unchanged and still upstream; what is fixed is this repo's exposure to it.

subject.detail: `vacuity-check.py`'s blind pass reports `examined=1820 mutating=3 re-read-after=0 blind=3` over this test tree. All three read after the mutation: `restartIsIssuedBeforeTheStagingWrite` reads `WatchWorld.serverNames`, the log, `kicks.issued` and `WatchState.load`; `restartIsOwedBeforeTheWriteLands` reads `WatchState.load` inside the lock and `WatchWorld.serverNames` on both sides of the rename; `restartRechecksTheCamera` reads `model.entry.characters`. The heuristic looks for a read AFTER the last occurrence of a mutating verb, and in this product the verb `restart` is also the name of the thing being observed — `restartPending`, `restarted scratch-label` — so the last `restart` in the file sits inside the final assertion and nothing is textually after it. Recorded rather than acted on: the tests are correct as written, and rewording an assertion to satisfy a text heuristic would make the suite worse. The pass is still worth running; 3 of 1820 is a reviewable rate, and it is the check that would have caught 26 of 32 on the campaign it was built from. CAUSE CORRECTED 21 Aug 2026; the diagnosis recorded above was wrong. It said the mutator's name is the observable's name (`restart` inside `restartPending`). Measured against 0.9.2's actual patterns, that cannot happen: the mutator scan at vacuity-check.py:180 requires `(?<![A-Za-z0-9_])` + verb + `\w*\s*\(`, so `state.restartPending == false` never matches for want of the call parenthesis. The real cause is that the seven default readers are all snake_case -- list_, get_, read_, fetch_, sample_, count_, load_ -- and the nine default mutators mostly are too (stop_all, stop_runner, clear_, cancel_). This is a camelCase Swift codebase, so NEITHER side could fire. The pass examined 1657 test bodies and found 3 mutating, 0 re-reading and 3 blind: `blind=3` reads as almost nothing wrong, and meant almost nothing looked at. The denominator was printed and nobody read 3-of-1657 as the alarm it was. Fixed by declaring the project's own vocabulary, which 0.9.2 added for exactly this: campaign.json now carries `blindVocabulary` with 14 camelCase mutators and 13 readers, and the pass reports examined=1657 mutating=320 re-read-after=232 blind=88, with the vocabulary it used printed above the findings. Two of the three original findings resolved on their real reads (`WatchState.load(`, `WatchWorld.read(`). The third, restartRechecksTheCamera, stays flagged and correctly so for a verb heuristic: its only reads are property comparisons -- `model.step`, `model.entry.characters` -- which carry no verb at all. That is the ceiling of this instrument rather than a defect in the test, and it is why the 88 is a worklist and not a verdict: the vocabulary is hand-declared and unvalidated. Of the 21 findings the tool prints, 15 carry a @Test attribute and 5 are fixture helpers in dedicated client files that 0.9.2's per-file helper heuristic does not exclude, because it keys on a function being called more than once in its OWN file and these are called from their importers.
subject.title: the blind-test pass flags three tests that do read after mutating, because the mutator's name is the observable's name

subject.detail: DETECTOR DEFECT, recorded so its numbers are not published as product findings. `vacuity-check.py`'s `blind` pass asks whether any READER appears after the last MUTATING call in a test body, both matched by name prefix. Run with the shipped defaults it reports `examined=1820 mutating=3 blind=3` — and all three are false: DEFAULT_READERS is snake_case (`load_`, `get_`, `read_`, `list_`) while this is a camelCase Swift codebase, so NO Swift reader can ever match, and the three `mutating` hits matched the token `restart` in their own function names. Both flagged WatchRestartTests cases read extensively after the mutation. Run with a hand-derived camelCase verb list it reports `examined=1834 mutating=258 re-read-after=158 blind=100`. Two of the flagged real tests were read in full and BOTH re-read: `undoRestoresTheItem` calls `queue.all()` three times after `model.remove(...)`, and `resetReindexesAnIndexFailure` reads `client.calls` after `board.reset(...)`. Neither `all` nor `calls` was in the list. Of the 20 findings the script prints, only 6 are `@Test` functions at all; the other 14 are test doubles and helpers, because the population is every `func` in any file with `test` in its path. CONCLUSION: on this codebase the pass measures the verb list rather than the suite, and no verb list derived by hand is evidence of anything. It is recorded, not published, and the campaign claims no blind-mutation number. The pass's other two arms — `unclassed` and `uncensused` — are exact and are kept. ADDRESSED UPSTREAM in 0.9.2, confirmed by running it 21 Aug 2026. Commit 28ecd67 (`the blind-mutation check was measuring itself`) fixes four detector defects that each RAISED the blind count, and the pass now prints the vocabulary it used above its findings -- `vocabulary: defaults + campaign.blindVocabulary — 22 mutator(s), 20 reader(s)` followed by the reader list -- which was this defect's complaint: a number published without saying what configuration produced it. The denominator also moved, 1841 to 1657, because fixture helpers are no longer counted as tests. Left open rather than closed: the residual named on DEF-040 sits in the same pass. SUPERSEDED 21 Aug 2026 by DEF-055. The specific claim here — snake_case DEFAULT_READERS against a camelCase Swift codebase, giving examined=1820 mutating=3 blind=3 with all three false — was resolved by declaring campaign.json's blindVocabulary, which 0.9.2 reads. The general claim, that no hand-derived verb list is evidence of anything, is not resolved; it is now MEASURED rather than asserted. DEF-055 carries that measurement (7 of 7 sampled findings false, four named mechanisms, a two-way arm) and is the entry to read. Recorded as superseded rather than closed: the finding was real and its successor is open.
subject.title: test-campaign 0.9.1's blind-mutation pass is dominated by its own verb configuration on this codebase, in both directions

subject.note: `#expect(result.tools != nil, ...)` at ShellTests.swift:133. `ReindexResult.tools` is a non-optional `Int` (MCPRouterKit/Control/Models.swift:263), so the comparison could not fail. The Swift compiler emitted `comparing non-optional value of type 'Int' to 'nil' always returns true` on every build of the test target; it was the only such warning in the suite. The intent was stated in the comment directly above it -- `.success` is distinguished from `.populated` by `a reindex that comes back with no error and a tool count` -- so the assertion was one character from doing its job. Repaired to `result.tools == 14`, the value FixtureControlAPIClient+Writes.swift:33 overrides for `.success`, which discriminates against the base `reindex-failure.json` fixture it starts from (`{"tools":0,"error":"fetch failed"}`). Armed in evidence/arming/CASE-0152.arming.log: with the override changed to 0 the assertion goes red (`(result.tools -> 0) == 14`), and the log records that the pre-repair form would have stayed green under the same mutation.
subject.text: A ShellTests assertion on the `.success` reindex scenario compared a non-optional Int to nil, so it was always true and read nothing.

subject.detail: Measured 2026-08-21. `.gitmodules` vendors `.claude/plugins/fledgeling-plugins` at `main`, and `planning/features-to-triage/LEDGER.md`'s allocation notes state the reason: 'a runner reads mockup-fidelity, mac-craft, design-craft and ux-craft at a repo-relative path rather than depending on the machine.' For test-campaign that is not what happens. The submodule (HEAD baaf79a, branch main, clean) carries `plugins/test-campaign` at version 0.5.0, whose `skills/test-campaign/scripts` holds five files: attach-shots.py, campaign.py, evidence-page.py, strict-check.py, witness-worklist.py. It has no `vacuity-check.py` and no `capture-lineage.py`; `grep effect-witness strict-check.py` returns nothing and `grep -c blindVocabulary vacuity-check.py` cannot run because the file is absent. Every gate this campaign reports ran from `~/.claude/plugins/cache/fledgeling-plugins/test-campaign/0.9.2/`, on the machine. The vacuity census, the effect-witness rung, the blind-mutation pass, the capture-lineage ratchet and the strict score of 65 all come from code the submodule does not contain, four minor versions ahead of it. CONSEQUENCE FOR THE PIPELINE, and it is the reason this is filed rather than noted: DEF-051, DEF-052, DEF-054, DEF-055 and DEF-056 are defects in 0.9.2's scripts. None of that code is in this repo at any path, so no ship-feature runner working in an mcp-router worktree can fix them. They are upstream work in github.com/fledgeling-co/fledgeling-plugins, and closing them requires a change pushed to that repo plus a submodule bump here — a different repo and an outward-facing action. Separately, a fresh clone that follows the documented `git submodule update --init --recursive` gets 0.5.0 and would reproduce none of this campaign's numbers. Not fixed here: which version the submodule should track, and whether the campaign should run from it rather than the cache, is the owner's call.
subject.title: the vendored fledgeling-plugins submodule is test-campaign 0.5.0 while every gate in this campaign ran from the machine's 0.9.2 cache

subject.evidence: TWO COMMENTS IN THIS REPOSITORY ALREADY NAME THIS AND NEITHER REMOVED IT. sweep-control-gate.py's own note on CONTROL_TIMEOUT says 'a timeout there answered nothing about whether the control is rotted'. scripts/windows/verify.ps1, declaring SWEEP_CONTROL_TIMEOUT=600, says the 120s default 'produced two findings reading its declared control does not pass, which is the gate reporting the host's shell as a rotted control - a false finding, and the direction that gets a gate switched off'. Both diagnose it exactly. The remedy taken was to raise the budget, which removes the symptom on this host and leaves the conflation in place: `run_control` returned False on TimeoutExpired, indistinguishable from a control that ran and exited non-zero. HOW IT SURFACED, AND IT WAS NOT A RED IN THE LANE. The gate was invoked bare during Wave C integration - outside verify.ps1, so without the 600s declaration - and reported six to eight controls as not passing. That red was the invocation's, not the tree's. What the investigation did establish is a measurement: planning/hooks/prove-pre-commit.sh exits 0 with 8 assertions over 6 directions in 258s on LUKESFF, so under the 120s default a control that fully holds is reported as one that does not.
subject.title: sweep-control-gate reported a control that timed out as a control that does not pass, which is the unmeasured-read-as-failed conflation arriving inside one of the campaign's own gates

subject.detail: Measured 2026-08-27 by G16 while enumerating SURF-026, and independently by G15. M15 made Settings a Scene and removed the case from `Destination`, and capture-mac-glass.sh still ran `axkit select Settings`. That select fails — `axkit: no sidebar row starting 'Settings'` — the app stays on whichever board the loop visited last, and the shutter filed THAT board's pixels under SURF-011: byte-identical to the Cleanup board on one loop ordering and to the Insights board on another. THE CAMPAIGN'S OWN INSTRUMENTS CAUGHT IT FROM TWO DIRECTIONS, which is the part worth keeping. glass-assert.py's raster uniqueness check went red because two cases shared a sha256; `--discriminate` reported the neighbouring board's predicate wrongly accepting SURF-011's dump, because that dump IS the neighbouring board; and the capture manifest's readback recorded the picture's target as the neighbour's route under subject SURF-011, contradicting its own filename. FIXED HERE, NARROWLY: the capture script now refuses to photograph a select that did not take, and says which board the window is actually showing. That is the script's own standing rule rather than a new one — it already declines to substitute a picture for the pairing sheet and the status item, and its header records the run that filed the Inbox board as SURF-010. The title and the dump are still written from what the app is really showing, so the failure stays visible downstream; what is withheld is the photograph, because a misattributed picture is the one artefact nothing downstream can correct. STILL OPEN, and deliberately not fixed here: 1. SURF-011 has no route to the Settings SCENE. It needs Cmd-comma or the app menu, not a sidebar select that cannot succeed. CASE-0016 and CASE-0111 fail until it does. 2. THE MENU MAP IS PRE-M22. Committed SURF-001.menu.txt binds Cmd-4 to `Discover`; the running app binds Cmd-4 to `Harnesses`, exactly as Destination.selectionDigit declares (activity 1, servers 2, skills 3, harnesses 4, discover 5, inbox 6, evals 7, cleanup 8, insights 9). glass-assert.py's SURF-001 `menu` dict is the old map, so CASE-0001 asserts five bindings this build does not have. Correcting it is editing an assertion to restore a green, which this campaign forbids — it is owed as its own item, from Destination.selectionDigit rather than by hand. WHY IT IS THE SAME FINDING AS G14'S, ONE LAYER DOWN. G14 found the surface LIST had stopped growing while the product did. This is the EVIDENCE not having been re-taken since the build moved: the committed glass artefacts were last written on 20 Aug by cef3729, before M22 added two destinations and renumbered four accelerators. In both cases a completeness gate reported clean because what it measured was a stale artefact rather than the product. CLOSED ON THE EVIDENCE SIDE, 2026-08-27 (G21/G29). The frame this defect produced was still published: `inventory.json` gave SURF-011 the shot `evidence/shots/SURF-011.build.png`, and at `519aebc` those bytes were the Insights board. `capture-lineage.py --gate` reported it UNTIED because the capture step's own row said `target: app://mac/insights` while the filename said SURF-011 -- the manifest was right and the wall was wrong. Two moves, both provable from git. The Insights frame is renamed `evidence/shots/DEF-059.insights-filed-as-SURF-011.png`, keeping every capture-time field, so the defect keeps its exhibit and no filename match can offer it to SURF-011 again. The Settings capture it overwrote is restored to `SURF-011.build.png` from `cef3729`, TOGETHER WITH ITS MANIFEST ROW from the same commit -- the last commit where those bytes and that row agreed (sha 3b5a26ef, `target: app://mac/settings`, readback `Settings`, 2026-08-20T11:32:58Z). Restoring the pair from one commit is a recovery of a capture-time record; restamping the row against the new bytes would have been the manifest-after-the-fact defect. What is NOT closed is the cause: `axkit select Settings` still fails, so the campaign still has no Settings capture newer than 2026-08-20 and the glass script still declines to take one. THE CAUSE NOW HAS A READER, 2026-09-02 (wa5). `axkit select Settings` still fails, and the campaign still has no Settings capture newer than 2026-08-20 -- unchanged. What has changed is that the age is no longer invisible: `bin/glass-build-gate.py` reports `evidence/shots/SURF-011.build.png` and `evidence/ax/SURF-011.*` as STALE against the build this tree would produce, so the lane cannot be green over them again without somebody re-taking them. `bin/capture-mac-glass.sh`'s refusal to photograph a select that did not take is the other half and is unchanged. Both halves of the remaining work -- a route to the Settings SCENE, and the re-capture -- are macOS work and are not attempted here. CLOSED 2026-10-19 on glass. capture-mac-glass.sh opens Settings with ⌘, (backgrounded), selects the Router pane in the Settings window's own source list, photographs that window as SURF-011 (target app://mac/settings), dumps the Security pane as a second dump of the same surface, and closes the window. glass-assert at the current build: checked=435 failures=0; --decoy SURF-011 reddens 6.

subject.detail: Measured 2026-08-27 by G15, while enumerating SURF-025. The committed glass evidence under planning/test-campaign/evidence/ax was last written by commit cef3729 on 20 Aug. M22 then added two destinations and RENUMBERED four accelerators, and nothing re-took the pictures. Running bin/capture-mac-glass.sh against the current build turns four previously-passing cases red, and in every one of them the PRODUCT is right and the recorded evidence is stale: 1. THE MENU MAP. Committed SURF-001.menu.txt binds Cmd-4 to `Discover`; the running app binds Cmd-4 to `Harnesses`, exactly as Destination.swift's selectionDigit declares (activity 1, servers 2, skills 3, harnesses 4, discover 5, inbox 6, evals 7, cleanup 8, insights 9). glass-assert.py's SURF-001 `menu` dict is the pre-M22 map, so CASE-0001 asserts five bindings the shipped build does not have. 2. SETTINGS IS NOT A SIDEBAR ROW. M15 made Settings a Scene and removed the case from Destination, and capture-mac-glass.sh still does `axkit select Settings`. That select now fails — `axkit: no sidebar row starting 'Settings'` — the app stays on Cleanup, and the script photographs the CLEANUP board and files it as SURF-011. CASE-0016 and CASE-0111 fail against it. THE CAMPAIGN'S OWN INSTRUMENTS CAUGHT BOTH, WHICH IS THE ONE GOOD PART. The capture manifest's readback records that picture as target `app://mac/cleanup` under subject SURF-011, contradicting its own filename — the exact mechanism the script was rebuilt around. Independently, glass-assert.py --discriminate reports LEAK SURF-007 wrongly accepted 1 of 8 foreign board dumps: SURF-011 — because SURF-011's dump IS the Cleanup board. Two instruments, one cause. WHY THIS IS THE SAME FINDING AS G14'S, ONE LAYER DOWN. G14 found the surface LIST had not grown since it was written. This is the EVIDENCE not having been re-taken since the build moved. In both cases a completeness gate reported clean because the thing it measured was a stale artefact rather than the product. NOT FIXED HERE, DELIBERATELY. G15's remit is the Harnesses enumeration, and correcting glass-assert.py's menu map or the Settings navigation would be editing an assertion to restore a green — even though the product is right, that is the move this campaign forbids, and the stale assertion is the instrument that found this. The four cases are set to `fail` with this id in their notes. Owed: re-map SURF-001's menu dict from Destination.selectionDigit, and give SURF-011 a route to the Settings SCENE (Cmd-comma or the app menu) instead of a sidebar select that cannot succeed. INSTRUMENTED 2026-09-02 (wa5), NOT CLOSED. The cause this row names -- a committed capture carrying no tie to the build it came from -- is now measurable. `planning/test-campaign/bin/glass-build-gate.py` binds every artifact the macos-glass lane cites to the git blob identity of the Mac app's build inputs (the set `scripts/acceptance/build-freshness.sh` compiles from) and exits 2 when that identity is not the one the lane is being read against. It is RED on this tree over all 56 artifacts, in 7 capture groups spanning 20-29 Aug: `evidence/runs/glass-build-gate.log`. The stamps it reads are marked `reconstructed-from-git` and are deliberately the weaker claim -- git can prove which commit last wrote each artifact, so the record establishes the build the evidence CANNOT BE NEWER THAN rather than the build it was taken from. `bin/capture-mac-glass.sh` now calls `glass-build-gate.py --emit` in the run that takes the pictures, stamping from the bundle's own CFBundleShortVersionString/CFBundleVersion and the `.mcprouter-build-stamp` the Makefile writes after `xcodebuild` exits 0, so a re-capture replaces each reconstructed row with a capture-time one. Watched both ways: `evidence/runs/glass-build-gate.selftest.log`, four arms, green over a current capture and red over a stale one, an uncovered one and an undatable row. Case CASE-0342. WHAT IS NOT SETTLED. The re-capture itself, which is the whole of what this defect asks for. It needs a macOS host with Xcode and a display server; the work above was done on Windows, where there is no Swift toolchain, no xcodebuild and no way to open the app's window. The four cases stay `fail` with `owed` recording the re-capture and its owner. The second half of the row -- SURF-001's menu map, to be re-read from `Destination.selectionDigit` rather than by hand -- is equally macOS work and equally untouched. Nothing here edits an assertion, a stamp or a recorded identity to restore a green.

subject.detail: Measured 2026-08-21 against test-campaign 0.9.2 on app/Tests. The pass reports examined=1661 mutating=320 blind=88. Two structural errors and two idiom errors inflate that number. STRUCTURAL. (1) It scans every `func`, not every test. Restricted to swift-testing's own discriminator (a func whose nearest preceding annotation is @Test) the denominator is 1531, not 1661: 130 of the examined functions are not tests. (2) Its helper exclusion at vacuity-check.py:162 is file-scoped — a name is a helper only if called more than once in the file that declares it. A shared stub declared in TestSupport.swift and called from other files therefore reads as a test, so MemoryFileSystem's `write`, `removeItem` and `moveItem`, HTTPStub's `stop` and WatchTestSupport's `remove` are each counted as a blind test. 21 of the 88 are support-file functions. IDIOM, on the mutator side. (3) The lookbehind `(?<![A-Za-z0-9_])` cannot exclude a dot, so a Swift enum case constructor matches a mutator verb: `ServerRowAction.forServer(s, pendingAuth: nil) == .reset(.clearPlacard)` reports ServerPresentationTests::trippedOutranksHeld as mutating via 'reset', where `.reset` is the expected VALUE inside the assertion. 41 of 72 re-measured findings are dot-prefixed. (4) It takes the last mutator by source POSITION and calls everything after it the tail, which misreads three Swift constructs: a mutator inside the assertion (`await #expect(throws: Never.self) { try await store.delete() }` — nothing can follow it by construction), a mutator in a `defer` block (source-early, execution-last, so the whole test body reads as 'after'), and a mutator as the last statement of a loop body whose observation is the next iteration (CallbackLifecycleTests::stopReleasesTheSocket rebinds the port ten times; the read of cycle N is the start() of cycle N+1). SAMPLE. Of the 15 findings with zero assertions after the last mutator — the highest-yield stratum — 9 were read in full. Two (DiscoveryTests::servers, CapabilityPlateTests::install) are helpers. All 7 remaining are real tests that do observe after mutating, through idioms no reader verb names: `client.calls.last?.operation`, `seen.filter { ... }`, a rebind that throws. Precision on that stratum is 0 of 7. ARMED, two ways, evidence/arming/blind-mutation.arming.log. A probe @Test that mutates and never observes was added and removed: blind moved 88 -> 89 -> 88 and examined/mutating moved by exactly 1 each time. The check does bite; it is the false-positive rate that is at issue, not the sensitivity. NOT REMEDIED BY VOCABULARY. The reader side is deliberately loose because a false reader match suppresses a finding. Adding this codebase's read idioms (`calls`, `operation`, `filter`) would lower the number without improving what the pass knows, and the terms are generic enough to suppress true findings too. The 88 stands recorded as a worklist with its measured precision beside it rather than tuned to look better. RE-MEASURED 2026-08-27 by G22, which declared `testRoot` and gave this pass a corpus for the first time. THE 88 DOES NOT REPRODUCE. Vendored 0.9.2 over `app/Tests` today reports examined=2133 mutating=3 blind=3, against the 1661/320/88 above. The denominator moving up while `mutating` collapses 320 → 3 is not tree churn: 0.9.1 and 0.9.2 ship IDENTICAL DEFAULT_MUTATORS and DEFAULT_READERS, and neither list holds `reset`, `write`, `removeItem`, `moveItem` or `remove` — the verbs this entry's idiom argument turns on. So the 2026-08-21 sitting ran an expanded vocabulary passed on the command line, and `campaign.json` declares none, which makes 88 a figure no documented invocation returns. Its cited evidence, `evidence/arming/blind-mutation.arming.log`, has never existed on any branch of this repository (`git log --all -- '*blind-mutation*'` is empty), so the arming claim above is not checkable from the tree. The measured structural and idiom errors are not withdrawn; what is withdrawn is the population they were measured over. TODAY'S POPULATION, AND ITS PRECISION. With `testRoot: app` the pass reports examined=2179 mutating=3 re-read-after=0 blind=3, and 0.15.0 returns the same three findings from the same corpus. All THREE were read in full — 3 of 3, not a sample — and all three are false positives. Precision 0 of 3. A FOURTH CAUSE, NOT IN THE ORIGINAL ENTRY, AND THE ONE THAT PRODUCES TWO OF THE THREE. The body slice is `src[pos:end]` where `pos` is the start of the DECLARATION, so a test whose own name begins with a mutator verb matches itself. `WatchRestartTests::restartIsIssuedBeforeTheStagingWrite` and `::restartIsOwedBeforeTheWriteLands` contain no mutating call at all: the only `restart\w*\(` in each is `func restart…(` on its own declaration line. Both then read — `WatchWorld.read(scratch.logPath)`, `WatchState.load(path:)`, `WatchWorld.serverNames(in:)` — and assert on `state.mcpServersHash` and `state.restartPending`. The third, `PhoneStorageFailureTests::restartRechecksTheCamera`, does call `await model.restart()` and then asserts twice, on `model.step` and on `model.entry.characters`: property reads that no reader verb names, which is cause (4)'s shape rather than a new one. This cause survives into 0.15.0 unchanged. NOT ENROLLED IN A GATE, and `blindVocabulary` still not declared, for the reason the entry already gives. A related gap measured at the same sitting: pointed at `src/` — the TypeScript tree, which has no tests — the pass prints `corpus: … (0 file(s))` and `examined=0 mutating=0 blind=0` and contributes nothing to `--gate`. It reports its empty corpus and does not fail on it, so a mis-declared `testRoot` reads as a clean pass. VOCABULARY DECLARED 2026-08-29 by K4, and the entry's own 'NOT REMEDIED BY VOCABULARY' paragraph is narrowed rather than withdrawn. That paragraph reasons entirely from the READER side, and on the reader side it is still right: adding this codebase's read idioms lowers the count without improving what the pass knows, which is why the declared reader list stops short of `expect` and `require` -- swift-testing's assertion macros, 5781 and 383 occurrences, either of which would mark every test that asserts after mutating as re-reading and collapse the count to near zero while the pass learned nothing. THE MUTATOR SIDE WAS NEVER ARGUED, AND THAT IS WHERE THE PASS WAS BLIND. Measured over the same 2282 test bodies at `83e5380`: the nine snake_case defaults find 3 mutating call sites; a camelCase list derived from this corpus finds 481. So `blind=3` was a reading of 3 of 481, a recall of 0.6%, and the entry's `precision 0 of 3` was a precision over a population the instrument could barely see. `campaign.json` now carries `blindVocabulary` with `only: true`, 19 mutators and 34 readers, derived mechanically -- a verb is kept only where method calls on a receiver are at least half its corpus sites and its own `func` declaration lines at most a quarter, which is causes (3) and (4) of this entry turned into a selection rule. THE THREE FINDINGS ARE ADJUDICATED, and each clears for a different checkable reason rather than all three for one. `restartIsIssuedBeforeTheStagingWrite`: one fitted mutator, `WatchWorld.remove(scratch)` inside a `defer`, and four declared readers after it -- `load`, `read`, `parse`, `servers`. NOT blind, positively. `restartIsOwedBeforeTheWriteLands`: three fitted mutators, the last `WatchState(restartPending: true).save(`, with `load` after it. NOT blind, positively. `restartRechecksTheCamera`: ZERO fitted mutator call sites in its body. It was flagged only because `restart` is a shipped default and this entry's fourth cause -- the body slice beginning at the declaration -- made `func restartRechecksTheCamera(` match itself. `restart` fails the selection rule (1 method call against 3 declaration lines, of 5 sites), so it is not in the vocabulary and the finding is withdrawn. WHAT THAT DOES NOT MEAN: its real mutation `await model.restart()` is now invisible to the pass, and its reads are still the property comparisons `model.step` and `model.entry.characters` that no reader verb names. It is UNEXAMINED by this instrument, not clean, and that is this entry's ceiling stated once more rather than closed. ARMED, AND ENROLLED, which the entry recorded as missing. `planning/test-campaign/bin/blind-vocabulary-arm.py` runs on every `make lint`: two plants identical but for one line, each measured alone and again inside a `shutil.copytree` of the real corpus, requiring examined+1 mutating+1 blind+1 for the blind plant and examined+1 mutating+1 blind+0 for the reading one. The specificity arm is the half a sensitivity arm alone cannot give: a detector that flagged every mutating body would pass the first and say nothing. 6 of 6 as expected on `cache 0.16.0` and again on the `vendor/` pin via `--instrument`. The two disagree only on the denominator -- 2282 against 2277, the five arrow-style `it/test(` blocks 0.9.3 added block detection for -- and agree on blind=111. THE 111 IS A WORKLIST AND THE CAMPAIGN STILL PUBLISHES NO BLIND NUMBER. Nothing above touches the structural causes: the pass still examines every `func` rather than every `@Test`, its helper exclusion is still file-scoped, and a `defer` mutator still reads as source-early -- which is exactly why the first of the three findings above needed reading rather than counting. This entry stays OPEN; what it now carries is a measured recall beside its measured precision.

subject.note: SOURCE-ANALYSIS, AND THAT IS THE CEILING. This case reads Swift. It does not run the Mac app and does not photograph a board, and it cannot on this host: the shell is a SwiftPM target with no Windows build and `swift` is not on LUKESFF. A green means the code that draws DEF-043's two elements is present and composed the way DESIGN.md section 2 requires. It does NOT mean either element reached a screen, and it must not be read as closing DEF-043. M27 asked for on-glass coverage and that is still owed, on a Mac, through the campaign's own capture lane. WHAT IT ESTABLISHES. SidebarFoot renders the address on its `.address` case; the reading comes from LoopbackAddress.hostPort while the Settings endpoint row comes from LoopbackAddress.controlEndpoint, so the two cannot drift; no literal host:port appears in any of the four files that DISPLAY an address; and ReadoutCopy.childProcessesLabel is "Child processes" and Readout draws it - the string DEF-043 measured in 0 of 9 accessibility dumps. THE FIRST RUN FAILED AND THE INSTRUMENT WAS THE ONE AT FAULT. The honesty arm originally refused a literal host:port anywhere in either shell tree and reported `ShellClientFactory.shippingEndpoint`. Every reference to that symbol was then read: it is consumed by Choice.live, LiveControlAPIClient, ControlEventStream and the Release guard, and reaches no view. It is a dialled endpoint, not a displayed one, and the honesty rule governs what a user is told. The scope was corrected rather than the finding suppressed, and the sweep was NOT narrowed: it still covers both trees, and a literal outside the display files fails unless its symbol is declared with a reason - which plant Q6 watches. PLATFORM. macOS, and DEF-043 never said so, which is what the row cost to establish. M27-sidebar-foot-readout.md reads `Category: mac`, the evidence is nine accessibility dumps at 1156x680 against the Mac design of record, and the sidebar-foot specification is in DESIGN.md section 2 rather than in the Windows floor. The Windows shell's NavigationView declares no pane footer content at all and the Windows floor's own owed list names no sidebar foot, so the absence there is not a defect - Windows was never promised it. This case asserts nothing about Windows, because a check demanding Windows never grow a sidebar foot would redden on somebody adding a good thing.

subject.cell: execution-plane=static-source-read - data-shape=one registry fact removed per arm
subject.note: Seven arms, each removing exactly one fact and requiring the exit code to move: the Harnesses surface row deleted (R1 red), `Insights` removed from the shell's controls (R2 red), CASE-0341 stripped of its surface link (R3 red), SURF-036's controlsSource removed (R4 red), SURF-031's source path misspelt (R4 red), a control invented on SURF-039 (R4 red), and DestinationCatalog.cs emptied - which must exit 2 and REFUSE a verdict rather than reporting a clean registry, because a reader that finds nothing must not report a pass. 7/7 moved.
