subject.cell: execution-plane=daemon · data-shape=the same credential quoted back inside a router log line
subject.note: Layer 2, and the channel layer 1 structurally cannot reach. A credential arrives in a diagnostics export by more routes than the field it was configured in: an upstream that rejects a call and quotes the token back in its error text, a command line carrying `--token=`, a log line somebody wrote by hand. Those are strings the bundle has every reason to carry, and the only thing distinguishing the secret inside one is its VALUE. The scrub runs over the value tree ONCE, as the last step, so every string goes through it by construction rather than because each site remembered to call it — the property that survives the next person adding a section. Object keys are scrubbed as well as values. `occurrencesRemoved` is asserted non-zero, because a scrubber that ran and a scrubber that had something to do read as the same clean bundle and only one of them is evidence.

subject.cell: execution-plane=daemon · data-shape=an env value of three characters beside a log line containing it
subject.note: The needle floor, which is a correctness rule rather than a performance one. An env value of `1`, `true` or `dev` used as a scrub needle deletes every occurrence of that text from every log line in the bundle — the timestamps, the ports, the word `device`. The result READS as thorough redaction and is a corrupted document, and nobody looking at it can tell which. So a value below 8 characters is not used as a needle, is named in `unscrubbable` with the reason, and is still withheld by layer 1. The assertion that bites is the positive one: `dev-server on port 3000` must survive intact. BOTH out-of-family reviewers proposed an entropy filter on top of the floor, to stop a value like `production` scrubbing that word out of the logs. Declined, and the reason is the direction of the error: an over-redaction announces itself in place as `<redacted:MODE>` and a reader can see exactly what happened; an under-redaction is silent. A second exclusion tuned by entropy moves values from the first class to the second on a judgement nobody can audit from the bundle.

subject.cell: execution-plane=daemon · data-shape=the same credential percent-encoded and base64-encoded in log lines
subject.note: A secret does not always reach a log line as itself. It reaches it percent-encoded when it travelled in a URL and base64-encoded when it travelled in a `Basic` credential, and a scrubber that knows only the literal reports a clean bundle over both. Both out-of-family lanes raised this independently and it is the one addition of theirs taken wholesale. JSON escaping is DELIBERATELY NOT a third variant, and that is where this departs from both reviews. They are right that a token containing a quote appears in the SERIALISED document as `\"` and would survive a needle search over the finished bytes. The scrub does not search the finished bytes: it walks the value tree before serialisation, where every string is still unescaped. Scrubbing earlier removes the whole class rather than enumerating its members.

subject.cell: execution-plane=daemon · data-shape=an untokened GET against a router holding a planted secret
subject.note: The preview is a GET and GET is UNGATED in this router — `ControlHandler.gate` reads the token only for POST/DELETE/PATCH, matching the reference, recorded there as a ported defect rather than quietly fixed. So the preview is written to one rule: it discloses nothing `GET /servers` does not already disclose. Category names, counts, key names, and the redaction plan. The assertion that makes this a real constraint rather than a restatement of `no secret leaked` is the canary one: the preview must NOT contain the public log canary either. A preview carrying no secret is satisfied by a preview that carries the whole log with the secret scrubbed out; a preview carrying no log LINE is not.

subject.cell: execution-plane=daemon · data-shape=the bundle path asked three ways: untokened POST, GET, tokened POST
subject.note: The verb IS the gate, and it is not describing a mutation. The bundle changes nothing. It is a POST because stage 2 of `ControlHandler.handle` gates the token on POST/DELETE/PATCH only, so the verb is the only thing deciding whether this router hands its whole diagnostic corpus — log lines included — to any unauthenticated caller that can open the loopback port, which per `ControlToken` includes a web page the user merely visits. All three answers are pinned — 401 untokened, 405 on GET, 200 on a tokened POST — so a later tidy-up that makes the verb 'correct' goes red rather than silently opening the route. The 200 is asserted beside the other two so they read as refusals rather than as an absent route.

subject.cell: execution-plane=windows-host - modality=process diagnostics - data-shape=one injected fault per launch
subject.note: Each of the shell's three top-level unhandled-exception handlers made to fire on purpose, and the line it wrote read back out of shell-startup.log by a process that did not write it, after the process that did had exited. THIS CASE EXISTS BECAUSE REGISTRATION IS NOT FIRING. DEF-079 was raised on sixteen launches that wrote no `unhandled:` line including eight that terminated at 0xC000027B, and it stayed open through the fix - two more handlers registered - because none of the three had been observed catching anything. App.xaml.cs takes `--fault <ui|appdomain|task|dispatcher>`, compiled out outside DEBUG and inert unless passed; win-shell-unhandled-witness.ps1 launches the shell once per kind. FOUR ARMS. BASELINE is a launch with NO --fault and requires its region of the log to hold `launched` and no `unhandled:` line, which is what makes the three EFFECT lines the injection's rather than startup's; and every arm reads only the bytes appended after its own launch, so a line an earlier run left behind cannot satisfy one. The three EFFECT arms then require, each after its own fault, `unhandled: [xaml]` for a throw on the UI thread inside XAML's dispatch of OnLaunched, `unhandled: [appdomain terminating=True]` for a throw on a non-UI foreground thread, and `unhandled: [unobserved-task]` for a faulted task nobody awaits after a collection and WaitForPendingFinalizers. All four held. WHAT THIS CASE DOES NOT SETTLE, and what has since moved. The DispatcherQueue route ran here as an UNGRADED probe while DEF-085 was open. DEF-085 is fixed, the probe is a graded fifth arm of the same script, and it is carried by CASE-0386 rather than by this case: what this one grades is still the three top-level handlers, and folding a guard this repository owns into a case about framework handlers would make one verdict answer two questions. Whether any of these three would have caught the 0xC000027B Skills crash was unmeasured when this case was written; it is measured now, and the answer is no - CASE-0387 and DEF-086 carry it. And the injection is compiled out outside DEBUG, so this grades the Debug binary only. The shell's own `handlers:` line saying which handlers it attached is carried in runs[] as writerSelfReport and is graded by nothing. ACTUATES VOCABULARY, corrected at merge: `actuates` is read by planning/test-campaign/bin/control-census.py as a control the surface DECLARES, which is what gives the actuation census its denominator. This case originally listed the command the lane ran instead - App.UnhandledException, AppDomain.CurrentDomain.UnhandledException and TaskScheduler.UnobservedTaskException (handlers, not controls, and this case names no surface) - and that is DEF-080, two meanings sharing one field. The command is here in the note where it can be read; the field now carries nothing, because the case drives no declared control.

subject.cell: execution-plane=host - oracle-rung=structural - data-shape=the view as declared
subject.note: The structural rung under DEF-076, and the arm that runs on a host with no interactive session - which is most of them, since the live census needs WinSta0. ViewAutomationSurfaceTests parses SettingsBoard.xaml as XML and requires one addressable section container per section SettingsPresentation.SectionOrder declares, each with an accessible name; one ToggleSwitch per SettingsPresentation.ToggleKeys entry, each tagged with its key and each carrying a Toggled handler; and no literal IsOn, because a switch seeded from markup can start out disagreeing with the model it claims to show. It also requires the state readout to carry an automation id and NO AutomationProperties.Name - that absence is load-bearing, because a name would override the TextBlock's own text and the out-of-process effect check would then read a constant forever. WHAT IT CANNOT SAY: that any of it reaches the live tree, or that a toggle is bound to anything. Markup and a running control are different claims; CASE-0342 to CASE-0346 make the second one. ACTUATES VOCABULARY, corrected at merge: `actuates` is read by planning/test-campaign/bin/control-census.py as a control the surface DECLARES, which is what gives the actuation census its denominator. This case originally listed the command the lane ran instead - dotnet test app/windows/MCPRouter.Shell.Tests - and that is DEF-080, two meanings sharing one field. The command is here in the note where it can be read; the field now carries nothing, because a source-analysis rung drives no control at all.

subject.cell: execution-plane=windows-host - modality=process diagnostics - data-shape=one injected fault per launch
subject.note: DEF-085's guard: a throw inside a DispatcherQueue callback made to happen on purpose, and the line the guard wrote read back out of shell-startup.log by a process that did not write it, after the process that did had exited. WHY IT IS A CASE OF ITS OWN. CASE-0342 grades the shell's three top-level unhandled-exception handlers, which are the framework's. This route reaches none of them - a callback posted to a DispatcherQueue runs below XAML's own dispatch - so what catches it is code this repository owns: DispatcherGuard, applied at every posting site through GuardedDispatch.TryEnqueueGuarded. It ran in the same script as an UNGRADED PROBE while DEF-085 was open, because there was nothing yet to grade. THE ARM. win-shell-unhandled-witness.ps1 launches the shell with `--fault dispatcher` and requires `unhandled: [dispatcher` in the region of the log appended after that launch - so no earlier run's line can satisfy it - on a run whose BASELINE arm proved an ordinary launch writes no `unhandled:` line at all. Held: `unhandled: [dispatcher site=App.InjectFault] System.InvalidOperationException: DEF-085 fault injection: unhandled in a DispatcherQueue callback`. A SECOND EFFECT is recorded beside it and graded by nothing here: the guarded run leaves NO WER Application Error, where the unguarded one fails fast at 0xC000027B - see CASE-0387. WHAT IT DOES NOT SETTLE. GuardedDispatch is a convention and not a wall: nothing in the compiler stops a future caller from writing DispatcherQueue.TryEnqueue directly, and this arm would not notice a new unguarded site. The neighbouring `async void` XAML event-handler route is not covered here either. And the injection is compiled out outside DEBUG, so this grades the Debug binary only. ACTUATES: empty, because this case drives no control the surface declares - the command it ran is `--fault dispatcher` and it is in this note, which is where DEF-080 says it belongs. THE DEBUG-ONLY GRADING WAS A DECISION, not an oversight, and it is recorded here because DEF-079 left it open. The injection stays compiled out outside DEBUG: turning it on in Release would ship a code path whose whole purpose is to terminate the process, gated by nothing but a command-line flag, which is a worse risk than the observation is worth. What is Debug-only is the INJECTION and not the remedy - DispatcherGuard and GuardedDispatch compile into Release unchanged, and so do the three top-level handlers - so what goes unobserved in a Release build is whether the fault can be raised there, not whether the guard exists. The cheaper way to close it, if somebody wants it closed, is a third build configuration that defines the injection symbol without being the shipping one; that needs a new configuration and a lane re-run and was out of this item's scope.

subject.cell: execution-plane=windows-host - modality=operating-system crash record - data-shape=one deliberate fail-fast
subject.note: A REAL STATUS_STOWED_EXCEPTION, raised on demand, and what the XAML handler did about it - DEF-086. That row said this repository had no way to raise one: the original Skills crash was removed by DEF-077 and DEF-078, and a cross-ABI fault was not something product code could ask for. It turned out the lane already raised one without recognising it. An UNGUARDED throw from a DispatcherQueue callback - `--fault dispatcher --fault-unregister dispatcher`, which is DEF-085 as found - terminates MCPRouter.Shell.exe with WER Application Error 1000, exception code 0xc000027b, faulting module CoreMessagingXP.dll, fault offset 0x0000000000093b76. WHAT IT MEASURES: on that same run the region of shell-startup.log ends at `fault: injecting dispatcher` with nothing appended, so Microsoft.UI.Xaml.Application.UnhandledException does not see this class. DEF-079's mechanism field guessed exactly that and recorded it as unestablished; it is established now. THE RECORDER IS NOT THE WRITER, twice over: WER is written by the operating system after the process is gone, and it is read here through Get-WinEvent over the Windows Application log, which is a different API from the file the shell appends to. THE CONTROL: the guarded run of the same fault leaves no Application Error at all, so the record is the injection's rather than something this machine produces anyway. WHAT IT DOES NOT SETTLE, and this is the narrower thing rather than the wider claim: what matches the Skills crash of 2026-09-02 is the exception code, the faulting module and the fault offset - identical to the Application Error entries this machine still holds from 18:57:35 and 19:03:30 that day - and NOT a stack. This case says this host raises the same stowed-exception fail-fast and that the XAML handler does not catch it. It does not say the original throw took the identical path; DEF-077 named that throw and fixed it.

subject.text: A local `UIWindow` dies when the host function returns, leaving SwiftUI's hosting view without a window: layout numbers already computed survive, so `sizeThatFits` returns a real height while the accessibility tree is EMPTY. The first two iOS runs failed every copy assertion with `in: `. The window is now retained for the test's lifetime. This is the lane's version of a check that could not run reading as a check that ran.

subject.detail: Two instances of one mistake, found together. **The camera adapter** was constructed in `MCPRouterIOSApp.body`; `LiveCameraAuthorization` is a fieldless struct so a fresh one per render cost nothing and hid it, and the moment the lane asked for `FixtureCameraAuthorization` — an actor — the identity changed under the flow on every body pass. Stored once as a `let` beside `storage`, which was already stored for the same reason. **The pairing model** was the real defect. `PhoneSettingsScreen` built `PairingFlowModel(pairing:camera:store:)` inline inside its `navigationDestination` closure, and `PairingFlowView` takes it as `@Bindable` — which observes an object someone else owns rather than owning one. So every re-render of the Settings screen replaced the model, and `step`'s initial value is `.scan`, so each replacement discarded whatever `start()` had decided and put the scanner back. Now held in `@State` on the screen and created in `onPair`, before `isPairing` is set. This is a product defect and not a harness artefact: on a phone whose camera has not been asked for yet, the pre-prompt that explains what the camera is for can be replaced by the scanner it was meant to precede, and that scanner has no permission to show anything. It was invisible for as long as it existed because the simulator reports camera access as `.authorized`, which makes `start()` set `.scan` — the same value the reset produced. Two wrongs agreeing is why no host test could see it: the fault is in view composition, and only the on-glass lane exercises that. Left open as a standing note: `Step`'s default of `.scan` is a second hazard of the same shape, since a slow `current()` shows the scanner and then swaps. Fixing that needs an undecided case and is a design call rather than a repair.
subject.title: the phone rebuilt two owned objects inside body, resetting the pairing flow

subject.detail: `PairingCopy.settingsNeverPaired` carries `carriesNarrowing: true`, so `PhoneMessageBlock` rendered "This app queues items for review on your Mac. It cannot install, update or remove anything…" inside its block — and `PairedMacSettingsView` then rendered an About section that states the same sentence unconditionally. Both appear on the one surface a first-time user meets first, which reads as the app repeating itself rather than as emphasis. i1-phone-pairing.html states it once: §B puts it under the button with no About header, §I puts it under About. Fixed by suppressing the About section for a state whose own block carries it, read off the copy rather than off a case list. `PhoneSurfaceTests.testNarrowingIsRenderedWherePermissionIsDecided` now counts rather than existence-checks; armed 20 Aug 2026 against the pre-fix form, which read 2.
subject.title: the never-paired settings surface stated the narrowing twice

subject.text: CAUSE FOUND AND FIXED 20 Aug 2026; this record replaces one that said the cause was unknown and named machine saturation as a candidate. The candidate was wrong. The process-wide accessibility engine was OFF, so SwiftUI's `_UIHostingView` built its accessibility container and vended an EMPTY element array — `accessibilityElements == []`, not nil — and every label assertion in the target read empty and reported its own honest verdict, `nothing was measured, so this proved nothing`. That is indistinguishable, from inside the suite, from a product that renders no copy. A probe settled it: calling `_AXSSetAutomationEnabled(true)` took the same hosted view's published element count from 0 to 1. THE ENGINE HAD BEEN ON BY ACCIDENT — something else on this machine had switched it on — which is why this suite was green for months while depending on ambient host state no file in this repo controls, and why it went red with no change to the branch. THREE CHANGES ARE THE FIX, and the third was found only because the first two were not enough. (1) `PhoneSurfaceTests` resolves `_AXSSetAutomationEnabled` out of `/usr/lib/libAccessibility.dylib` (falling back to `AccessibilityUtilities.framework`) via dlopen/dlsym and calls it once per process, before the first `host()`. (2) The walker reads `accessibilityElements` first, because SwiftUI publishes through the array and leaves `accessibilityElementCount()` at 0 — measured on iOS 26.5, where one hosted `Text` reported `accessibilityElements.count == 1` and `accessibilityElementCount() == 0` in the same breath, so reading only the indexed API walked past every element SwiftUI had. Those two took `make test-ios` from 52 failures to 0 — and then `make all`, run immediately afterwards on the same device, came back with 39. (3) THE STATE IS DEVICE-SCOPED AND THE CALL LANDS ON THE NEXT PROCESS, NOT THIS ONE. On a device left in the disabled state, the run that re-enables it fails a DETERMINISTIC set of 15 test cases — identical set, measured three times, verified with `comm` in both directions — and the run after it, with no change to anything, is clean. The 15 are exactly the cases that host a `ScrollView`; the tests that pass alongside them are geometry, counts and negative assertions, all of which an empty tree satisfies, so the green half of that run was vacuous too. `test-ios` therefore runs a throwaway single-test process before the graded one and discards its exit code. MEASURED END TO END: three consecutive runs with the call mutated to `(false)` drive `MCPRouter-Unit` into the disabled state (54 failures each, the whole suite red, which is correct for a dead engine); the very next `make test-ios`, with the warm-up in the recipe, is 36 tests and 0 failures in 1.4s. THE INSTRUMENT CHECK IS ITSELF INSTRUMENTED. `testTheAccessibilityEngineCanBeSwitchedOn` blocks on a probe that hosts `ScrollView { Text }` and reads it back through the same walk every other assertion uses, with a 20s deadline. Two narrower probes were built first and both were wrong in opposite directions, which is why the shape is stated rather than assumed: a bare `Text` read either way reports the engine live at t=0 of a run in which 15 cases went on to read empty, and a `ScrollView` read through the accessibility-container path alone reports the engine dead on a device where all 35 other tests pass. A probe that answers differently from the thing it stands for answers a different question. On a dead engine the deadline fires and the case fails with `no hosted Text published a label within 20s`, measured. ARMED THREE WAYS. (a) Renaming the symbol to `_AXSSetAutomationEnabledXXX` on a device whose engine is already live fails exactly one test — the instrument check — and leaves the other 35 green, which is correct for that arm and proves only the resolution assertion. (b) With the call mutated to `(false)`, the first run on `MCPRouter-Arm`, a device created for the arm, recorded 53 failures across 36 tests: that is what proves the other 35 depend on the engine. (c) The first run ever taken on `MCPRouter-Arm2`, a device whose engine had never been live, is 36 tests and 0 failures, so a fresh device needs no warm-up and only an explicitly disabled one does. Both arm devices were deleted afterwards; `make test-ios IOS_UNIT_DEVICE=<name>` recreates either. TWO HARDENING CHANGES from the investigation are kept and neither is the fix: `test-ios` creates and owns `MCPRouter-Unit` instead of sorting booted devices first — the exact picker DEF-020 condemned, still live in this recipe — and the walk retains every element it visits so `ObjectIdentifier` is unique among live objects as its use assumes. A third, waiting on a product surface's tree over a two-second deadline, was written, measured to change nothing, and removed: it cost 130 seconds a run and bought no measurement. The wait that IS kept differs from it in the one way that matters — it waits on a probe whose answer is known, so a timeout is a fact about the instrument rather than about the view. THE DEPENDENCY IS ON A PRIVATE SYMBOL, in the test target only, never linked into the app; the instrument check fails loudly if a future runtime renames it, so this target goes red rather than quietly empty. Carried as CASE-0126.

subject.text: Measured 20 Aug 2026. `make test` failed with 4 issues at a one-minute load average of ~700 and passed all 1473 tests in 179 suites at load 46, on the same source, minutes apart. The four were `ActivityReconnectTests` (`a reconnect over a feed that stays live releases its guard`), `DiscoverBoardTests` (`client.searchQueries.count` reading 1 where the baseline said 2), and `SettingsAndMenuBarTests` twice (`model.trackerState` still nil). An earlier run at the same load failed only the first, so the set was not stable either — which is what separated this from a product defect. A suite that reports a defect the product does not have is the failure this campaign has already paid for once, in DEF-029, where a dead instrument read as a dead product for ten consecutive runs. CLOSED by making each wait a condition rather than a deadline, at three sites: 1. `ShellTestSupport.waitUntil` — ceiling 5s → 30s. It returns the moment the condition holds, so a passing test pays nothing for the larger bound; the bound exists only so a condition that never arrives fails instead of hanging. Five seconds was inside the scheduling noise of a contended host, which is the whole finding. 2. `ActivityReconnectTests.completes` — 2s → 30s, same argument. The defect it bounds is a call that *never* returns, so it exhausts any budget and a generous one costs only the time a genuine hang takes to report. 3. `DiscoverBoardTests.searchIsDebounced` — a fixed sleep replaced by two waits, because the claim has two halves and one sleep proved neither on a slow host. First a bounded wait for the debounce to fire at all; then a full debounce window of quiet with the count still at one, which is what rules out one request per keystroke. The second is a real quiet period rather than a deadline, so load cannot shorten it into a false pass — the wait on its own is satisfied by the *first* request and would pass against exactly the defect this test exists to catch. Armed 20 Aug 2026, all three, each watched to fail with its own message: `waitUntil` at `.seconds(0)` reads `no poll ran at all`, `the poll died with the scene that started it` and `five keystrokes issued 0 requests`; `completes` at `.milliseconds(1)` reads `reconnect did not return while the feed stayed live`; and a `queryChanged()` inserted inside the quiet period reads `a later request arrived: five keystrokes issued 2 requests in total`. The original trigger is not reproducible on demand from here — the load came from another project's Rust test binary, two node processes and `lsdiagnose` — so the fix is proven by the arms rather than by reproducing the contention.

subject.text: Found 20 Aug 2026 by the vocabulary differential, which reported `Edit cases…` and `Run again` in-design-not-build on this board, and recorded here rather than fixed because bolting those two buttons on would be the wrong repair. The design's pane at `prototype.html:885-891` is **one subject's** eval suite: it heads `pr-summariser · 8 cases`, subtitles `Ran 2 minutes ago against 0.4.1 in a scratch checkout`, and lists eight named cases with a verdict each. The built board is **cross-subject**: every server and skill, one row apiece, a reachability verdict per row, a filter, and `CheckCopy.runAllLabel` = `Re-check all…`. Those are two different surfaces wearing one route id, and the actions follow the framing — `Run again` re-runs the one suite on screen, which is what `Re-check all…` already does across all of them, so drawing both would be two names for one act (the failure DEF-012 records). `Edit cases…` opens an editor for a collection the app does not model: there is no eval case anywhere in `EvalsBoardModel`, so the button would offer a reading of something that does not exist — the same reason `Read first…` is a stated gap in DEF-011 rather than a drawn control. The divergence itself is the finding, and it is a scope question rather than a defect fix: the design specifies a per-subject eval board with named cases and an editor, and the app ships a cross-subject reachability board. Which one this product wants is the owner's call, and it is written up as a brief rather than decided here. Not guarded by an assertion, deliberately: there is nothing to assert until that call is made, and a test pinning today's cross-subject board would make the divergence harder to close rather than easier.

subject.detail: CLOSED 2026-08-20. The cause was two independent framing errors, both invisible because the gate could not run to report them. The design references came from `obscura fetch --screenshot`, which captures at a fixed 1280x720 dpr1 viewport with no viewport flag, so every reference was clipped rather than merely small - the bottom row of one carried 578 non-background pixels of 640 sampled. And the build captures were 980x620 against the design's 1156x680 window, aspect 1.581 against 1.700, which no crop reconciles. Fixed by rasterising the design through CDP with `Emulation.setDeviceMetricsOverride` at 1280x900 dpr2 (readback asserted `[1280, 900, 2]` before any capture), re-photographing the eight Mac boards at the design's own 1156x680 with a setframe readback guard, and cropping both halves to the window's own content box. prescan goes from framingComparable 0/16 to 8/8, aspectRatioOfRatios 1.0 and scaleRatio 1.0 on every pair (evidence/runs/prescan-fidelity.json). Eight verdicts written: 2 pass, 5 fail, 1 unoracled.
subject.text: The campaign names design-review and be-my-witness as gates and has never run either, and the reason was never measured — it read as a skip. It is not. be-my-witness 0.2.0's deterministic prescan over all 16 pairs that hold both halves reports isEvidence 16/16, settled 16/16, framingComparable 0/16, proceed 0/16. Not a dead predicate: the scale ratios differ per lane (0.466x on the SURF-001 sidebar crop, 1.64x on the Mac boards, 0.942x on the phone) rather than returning a constant. Every reference was rasterised at a 1280x720 dpr-1 viewport, inside which prototype.html draws a fixed artboard rather than filling the frame, so rendering larger pads rather than enlarges. Re-rendering the reference does not fix it either: the design's Mac window is #win at 1156x680, aspect 1.700, and the build's is 980x620, aspect 1.581. The build half crops exactly — scale=(2096-1376)/(980-620)=2.0, margin=(2096-980*2)/2=68, content rect (68,68,1960,1240), precisely 2x the AX frame — but no crop reconciles two different window shapes. What would make them comparable is re-capturing the app at the design's window size, which means driving the app again and photographing a window shape the product does not use. Left unresolved deliberately: the structural and lexical differential in evidence/differential.md is the comparison that is valid here, and it ran.

subject.detail: `evidence/shots/captures.json` is the only manifest `capture-lineage.py --gate` reads, and two lanes write it: `capture-mac-glass.sh`, and `scripts/acceptance/name-glass-attachments.py`, which merges the iOS lane's rows up from `evidence/shots/ios/captures.json`. The Mac script wrote `json.dumps(rows)` — its own rows, whole file — so whichever lane captured last erased the other's lineage without saying anything. Measured 2026-08-20 on v0.9.1's new lineage plane: the parent held 16 Mac rows and none of the 9 iOS ones, and the gate reported 6 iOS captures UNSOURCED — 'the only thing binding this picture to SURF-012 is its filename', which is the correct verdict on a manifest that had been overwritten. The pictures were always right and their provenance was always recorded; it was recorded into a file that was then replaced. Fixed by merging on `path` in both writers, and the 9 rows were restored from the lane's own capture-time record rather than reconstructed.

subject.detail: `vacuity-check.py`'s blind pass reports `examined=1820 mutating=3 re-read-after=0 blind=3` over this test tree. All three read after the mutation: `restartIsIssuedBeforeTheStagingWrite` reads `WatchWorld.serverNames`, the log, `kicks.issued` and `WatchState.load`; `restartIsOwedBeforeTheWriteLands` reads `WatchState.load` inside the lock and `WatchWorld.serverNames` on both sides of the rename; `restartRechecksTheCamera` reads `model.entry.characters`. The heuristic looks for a read AFTER the last occurrence of a mutating verb, and in this product the verb `restart` is also the name of the thing being observed — `restartPending`, `restarted scratch-label` — so the last `restart` in the file sits inside the final assertion and nothing is textually after it. Recorded rather than acted on: the tests are correct as written, and rewording an assertion to satisfy a text heuristic would make the suite worse. The pass is still worth running; 3 of 1820 is a reviewable rate, and it is the check that would have caught 26 of 32 on the campaign it was built from. CAUSE CORRECTED 21 Aug 2026; the diagnosis recorded above was wrong. It said the mutator's name is the observable's name (`restart` inside `restartPending`). Measured against 0.9.2's actual patterns, that cannot happen: the mutator scan at vacuity-check.py:180 requires `(?<![A-Za-z0-9_])` + verb + `\w*\s*\(`, so `state.restartPending == false` never matches for want of the call parenthesis. The real cause is that the seven default readers are all snake_case -- list_, get_, read_, fetch_, sample_, count_, load_ -- and the nine default mutators mostly are too (stop_all, stop_runner, clear_, cancel_). This is a camelCase Swift codebase, so NEITHER side could fire. The pass examined 1657 test bodies and found 3 mutating, 0 re-reading and 3 blind: `blind=3` reads as almost nothing wrong, and meant almost nothing looked at. The denominator was printed and nobody read 3-of-1657 as the alarm it was. Fixed by declaring the project's own vocabulary, which 0.9.2 added for exactly this: campaign.json now carries `blindVocabulary` with 14 camelCase mutators and 13 readers, and the pass reports examined=1657 mutating=320 re-read-after=232 blind=88, with the vocabulary it used printed above the findings. Two of the three original findings resolved on their real reads (`WatchState.load(`, `WatchWorld.read(`). The third, restartRechecksTheCamera, stays flagged and correctly so for a verb heuristic: its only reads are property comparisons -- `model.step`, `model.entry.characters` -- which carry no verb at all. That is the ceiling of this instrument rather than a defect in the test, and it is why the 88 is a worklist and not a verdict: the vocabulary is hand-declared and unvalidated. Of the 21 findings the tool prints, 15 carry a @Test attribute and 5 are fixture helpers in dedicated client files that 0.9.2's per-file helper heuristic does not exclude, because it keys on a function being called more than once in its OWN file and these are called from their importers.
subject.title: the blind-test pass flags three tests that do read after mutating, because the mutator's name is the observable's name

subject.detail: Four boards diverge from `design/mocks/prototype.html` in one direction and for one reason. Skills: the design has `runs`, `last run` and `eval` columns with graded pills; the build drops all three and prints 'A skill is loaded into an agent's context by the client and never reaches the router, so the router does not see it run.' Discover: the design has install velocity and eval pills; the build prints 'No trend or velocity figure is shown. Measuring one needs a history of these indexes over time, which the router does not keep yet.' Checks: the design shows a graded eval run with per-case verdicts and a failed exchange; the build shows checks the router performed itself and states 'No model-graded evaluation exists in this product.' Servers: every design row carries a trailing evaluation pill; no build row does. The build is the correct half. ORCHESTRATOR.md's rule is that no number is displayed that the router does not observe, and the build obeys it on all four boards while explaining itself on three. The design of record predates the rule. Filed against the design rather than the build, and left open because which artifact gets changed - re-cut the mock, or annotate it as superseded - is the owner's call, not the campaign's.

subject.detail: The SURF-007 verdict of this campaign read 'the built board's rows carry no trailing controls at all' and 'the build also truncates the column that exists to explain'. Photographed at the design's own 1156pt, every Cleanup row carries `Inspect` and `Remove...`. The controls were outside the 980pt capture the verdict was written against. subject.detail: DETECTOR DEFECT, recorded so its numbers are not published as product findings. `vacuity-check.py`'s `blind` pass asks whether any READER appears after the last MUTATING call in a test body, both matched by name prefix. Run with the shipped defaults it reports `examined=1820 mutating=3 blind=3` — and all three are false: DEFAULT_READERS is snake_case (`load_`, `get_`, `read_`, `list_`) while this is a camelCase Swift codebase, so NO Swift reader can ever match, and the three `mutating` hits matched the token `restart` in their own function names. Both flagged WatchRestartTests cases read extensively after the mutation. Run with a hand-derived camelCase verb list it reports `examined=1834 mutating=258 re-read-after=158 blind=100`. Two of the flagged real tests were read in full and BOTH re-read: `undoRestoresTheItem` calls `queue.all()` three times after `model.remove(...)`, and `resetReindexesAnIndexFailure` reads `client.calls` after `board.reset(...)`. Neither `all` nor `calls` was in the list. Of the 20 findings the script prints, only 6 are `@Test` functions at all; the other 14 are test doubles and helpers, because the population is every `func` in any file with `test` in its path. CONCLUSION: on this codebase the pass measures the verb list rather than the suite, and no verb list derived by hand is evidence of anything. It is recorded, not published, and the campaign claims no blind-mutation number. The pass's other two arms — `unclassed` and `uncensused` — are exact and are kept. ADDRESSED UPSTREAM in 0.9.2, confirmed by running it 21 Aug 2026. Commit 28ecd67 (`the blind-mutation check was measuring itself`) fixes four detector defects that each RAISED the blind count, and the pass now prints the vocabulary it used above its findings -- `vocabulary: defaults + campaign.blindVocabulary — 22 mutator(s), 20 reader(s)` followed by the reader list -- which was this defect's complaint: a number published without saying what configuration produced it. The denominator also moved, 1841 to 1657, because fixture helpers are no longer counted as tests. Left open rather than closed: the residual named on DEF-040 sits in the same pass. SUPERSEDED 21 Aug 2026 by DEF-055. The specific claim here — snake_case DEFAULT_READERS against a camelCase Swift codebase, giving examined=1820 mutating=3 blind=3 with all three false — was resolved by declaring campaign.json's blindVocabulary, which 0.9.2 reads. The general claim, that no hand-derived verb list is evidence of anything, is not resolved; it is now MEASURED rather than asserted. DEF-055 carries that measurement (7 of 7 sampled findings false, four named mechanisms, a two-way arm) and is the entry to read. Recorded as superseded rather than closed: the finding was real and its successor is open.
subject.title: test-campaign 0.9.1's blind-mutation pass is dominated by its own verb configuration on this codebase, in both directions

subject.note: `#expect(result.tools != nil, ...)` at ShellTests.swift:133. `ReindexResult.tools` is a non-optional `Int` (MCPRouterKit/Control/Models.swift:263), so the comparison could not fail. The Swift compiler emitted `comparing non-optional value of type 'Int' to 'nil' always returns true` on every build of the test target; it was the only such warning in the suite. The intent was stated in the comment directly above it -- `.success` is distinguished from `.populated` by `a reindex that comes back with no error and a tool count` -- so the assertion was one character from doing its job. Repaired to `result.tools == 14`, the value FixtureControlAPIClient+Writes.swift:33 overrides for `.success`, which discriminates against the base `reindex-failure.json` fixture it starts from (`{"tools":0,"error":"fetch failed"}`). Armed in evidence/arming/CASE-0152.arming.log: with the override changed to 0 the assertion goes red (`(result.tools -> 0) == 14`), and the log records that the pre-repair form would have stayed green under the same mutation.
subject.text: A ShellTests assertion on the `.success` reindex scenario compared a non-optional Int to nil, so it was always true and read nothing.

subject.detail: STILL PRESENT in 0.9.2, re-measured 21 Aug 2026 and the gap widened by one. witness-worklist.py reports `pairs=20 judgeable=17 WITHOUT a reference=3` and a comparable fraction of 85%, while capture-lineage.py --gate on the same registry reports `published captures: 16` and `JUDGED 16 of 16 judgeable (100%)`. Two gates in one skill version disagree about the judgeable denominator, 17 against 16, and neither names the other's population. CAUSE PINNED 21 Aug 2026. The disagreeing member is SURF-009, the Mac menu-bar popover, and it is the only one: witness-worklist's judgeable set and capture-lineage's judged set are identical apart from it. SURF-009 has a rendered design of record on disk (evidence/shots/mock/SURF-009.png), which is the sole condition witness-worklist tests, so it counts as the 17th judgeable pair. It has NO build capture at all — the popover cannot be opened without activating MCPRouter, which this campaign never does — so it never enters capture-lineage's population, which is built from published captures. capture-lineage therefore reports 'JUDGED 16 of 16 judgeable (100%)' on a registry holding 17 judgeable surfaces. That is the defect's whole shape, and it is the campaign's own first failure mode occurring INSIDE a gate written to prevent it: a denominator built from what was captured rather than from what was enumerated reads 100% precisely when a surface was never photographed. The direction is the dangerous one — an uncaptured surface raises the percentage instead of lowering it. Nothing is concealed in this campaign's own record: SURF-009 carries a shotNote naming the constraint, its three cases (CASE-0004, CASE-0006, CASE-0109) are n/a with the reason, and evidence/shots/pairs.json carries shot:null. The defect is that a reader of the gate line alone would not know to look for any of it. Remains open-detector: the fix is in the skill's scripts, which are not edited from this repo.
subject.note: DETECTOR DEFECT, recorded so its number is not published as a product finding. `witness-worklist.py:90` is `judgeable = [p for p in pairs if p.get("reference")]` -- it tests the reference half and never the shot half. SURF-009 (Mac menu-bar popover) has `shot: null` and an explicit `reason: build half uncaptured` in pairs.json, and is still counted, so the script reported `pairs=20 judgeable=17 comparable fraction: 85%` where the honest figure is 16 of 20, 80%. The script already defends the mirror-image failure and its own comment says why: a campaign reported 20 judgeable pairs whose references were all unrendered .html paths, and it now demotes those to unjudgeable with a named reason. The shot side has no equivalent test. Consequence here is one point of over-report and no false verdict, because capture-lineage.py computes judgeable from captures that exist and reported JUDGED 16 of 16 -- the two gates disagree by exactly this surface, and the disagreement is what found it. A campaign relying on the worklist alone would carry an uncompared surface inside a comparable fraction. Filed against the skill's script rather than this repo, so it is not fixed here.
subject.text: witness-worklist.py counts a pair as judgeable on the reference alone, so a surface with no build capture inflates the comparable fraction.

Defects

` at line 521 renders `[c for c in cases if state_of(c.get('status')) == 'fail']` -- failing CASES -- and the nav counter at line 305 is `counts['fail']`, the same population. So the page's Defects section counts 3 (the failing cases CASE-0010, CASE-0040, CASE-0110) while inventory.json holds 11 open defects, and the two numbers are about different things. MEASURED against the regenerated 124100-byte evidence.html: of the 11 open defects, 8 appear ZERO times -- DEF-008, DEF-040, DEF-041, DEF-042, DEF-043, DEF-047, DEF-048, DEF-051. The 3 that do appear are there by accident of prose: DEF-001 in two failing case notes and one passing one, DEF-033 and DEF-049 each inside a single PASSING case's note, rendered by the per-case table rather than by the Defects section. The peer reported 11 invisible; the true figure is 8, because writing a defect id into a case note is a convention doing a gate's job and it happened to fire three times. `campaign.py check` also exits 0 with all 11 open, so no gate holds on the registry either. This is the skill's own first-named failure mode -- covering a subset and reporting it as the whole -- arriving in its publisher: the gated half of the campaign is sound and the ungated half is the half people look at. The fix belongs in the installed skill (render inv['defect'], and count open defects in the nav), not in this repo; recorded rather than patched, precedent DEF-048 and DEF-051. SECOND PUBLISHER, same root cause, measured here: `campaign.py`'s own ledger writer (campaign.py:1210-1240) loads `inventory` and never reads `inventory['defect']` either, so ledger.md names zero defects across its 83 lines. Its header line is sharper than an omission -- it prints `73 pass . 3 fail . 0 skip . 4 n/a . 0 open . armed 73/73`, where `0 open` is the count of open CASES, on a campaign holding 12 open defects. A reader who takes that line at face value reads a campaign with nothing outstanding. ledger.md is generated rather than hand-kept, so it cannot be corrected in this repo: a fix that patched only evidence-page.py would leave the ledger short, and both publishers need to read the registry.
subject.title: evidence-page.py and campaign.py's ledger writer both skip the defect registry, so no published artifact lists a defect

subject.detail: DETECTOR DEFECT in test-campaign 0.9.1, found 21 Aug 2026 while accounting for the 19 unchecked cases. Two scripts in the SAME skill version disagree about what asserts an effect, and both carry a comment claiming to define it. `campaign.py:123` -- `EFFECT_RUNGS = ('outcome', 'metamorphic', 'effect-witness', 'raster-visual', 'interactive-glass')`, under the comment `A critical flow promises an effect. Only these rungs assert one.` `strict-check.py:54` -- `EFFECT_RUNGS = {'outcome', 'metamorphic', 'raster-visual', 'interactive-glass'}`, under `Only these assert an effect`, and its comment ends `See campaign.py` -- pointing at the file it contradicts. MEASURED here: this campaign holds 4 effect-witness cases (CASE-0145 through CASE-0148), all pass, all armed, each carrying an independent kernel recorder (the shell's $! plus the child's own getppid(); lsof(8)'s LISTEN row and the accepted ESTABLISHED half; stat(2) inode and mtime) and each backed by a denial control that flips it. strict-check.py scores all four into the `only proves something rendered` bucket, which is why that bucket reads 12 when only 8 cases sit at a structural rung. The gate therefore reports CHECKED 61 of 80; counting effect-witness as campaign.py does, and as SKILL.md's ladder does, the figure is 65 of 80 (81%). The consequence is worse than an understatement. effect-witness is the most expensive rung in the ladder -- it requires a recorder the product does not control, a non-zero count, and a sabotage control -- and a campaign optimising for the strict number is steered AWAY from it toward `outcome`, which costs less and scores more. A gate that pays less for harder evidence inverts the incentive the whole skill exists to create. The fix is one token in strict-check.py:54. It belongs in the installed skill and is recorded rather than patched from here, precedent DEF-048, DEF-051 and DEF-052. The ratchet is deliberately left at the gate's own 61 rather than raised to the corrected 65: the ratchet is the gate's record of itself, and editing it to a number the gate does not compute would be the campaign marking its own homework. RESOLVED 21 Aug 2026, and the fix predates the finding. test-campaign 0.9.2 is installed at ~/.claude/plugins/cache/fledgeling-plugins/test-campaign/0.9.2 and its strict-check.py:59 already reads `EFFECT_RUNGS = {'outcome', 'metamorphic', 'effect-witness', 'raster-visual', 'interactive-glass'}`, under a comment naming the same incentive inversion independently derived here: `a campaign that built a real witness watched its strict score stay flat, which is precisely the wrong incentive to attach to the most expensive rung.` Confirmed by running it: 0.9.2 reports CHECKED 65 of 80 (81%) with 8 in the rendered-only bucket, against 0.9.1's 61 of 80 and 12 -- exactly the four effect-witness cases and no others. This session had been running 0.9.1's scripts throughout while 0.9.2 sat installed alongside it, which is the reason the defect was visible here at all.
subject.title: strict-check.py omits effect-witness from EFFECT_RUNGS, so the ladder's top rung scores as 'only proves something rendered' and the gate penalises the hardest available work

subject.text: Measured by K3 on 2026-08-29 while trying to fill SURF-010's and SURF-011's denominators. Three declared controls have nothing to press, for three different reasons, and only one of them is a gap in the product. `Can't scan? Type a code` is declared on both the Mac pairing sheet and Settings' pair-another sheet. The copy exists — `InboxCopy.Pairing.typeInstead` — and the only view that draws it is the PHONE's `PairingFlowView`. REQ-015 says the phone can scan or type; the Mac sheet offers `Show a new code` and `Done`, so the typed path is reachable from one device and the design puts the affordance on the other. `Unpair` cannot be built as drawn: the control API has no devices endpoint, so what this Mac knows about a paired phone is the name on the inbox snapshot the shell is already polling. `SecurityPane` states that in its own words and offers `Manage…` — which routes to the Inbox — in its place. A refusal with a reason rather than an omission, but the design still promises a control the surface does not carry. `Reset history` is the confirm button of a sheet the Settings window does not host. The act itself ships and is proven: `ActivityModel.resetHistory()` and `CleanupBoardModel.resetHistory()` reach the same endpoint and `Reset history` is actuated on SURF-003 by a passing case. What is absent is this surface's entry point. M39 DISPOSITION, 2026-08-29, for the FIRST of the three only. The defect stays open because `Unpair` and `Reset history` are untouched. `Can't scan? Type a code` is answered by deciding it should not be a control on the Mac at all, rather than by adding one. The copy is the phone's button and switches `PairingFlowView` from the camera to a keypad; the Mac has no second screen to switch to, already draws the eight characters under the QR, and is not the device that types them. A Mac button would change no state and reveal nothing, which is this defect again rather than its repair. What shipped is the instruction the brief asked for -- `InboxCopy.Pairing.typeInsteadDetail`, drawn by `PairingSheet.typedFallback` in the live state, in the design of record's own wording. CASE-0289 asserts the sentence is drawn and that the action bar did not gain a fourth control; the surface's `controlsUnactuatable` row now records the decision instead of the absence.
subject.title: Three Settings and pairing controls the design draws have no counterpart on the Mac

subject.text: Measured by K3 on 2026-08-29 while trying to fill SURF-026's denominator, and it is the SkillSheets shape (DEF-062) a second time: a button drawn with an empty closure. `Button(InsightsBoardCopy.analyseNow) {}` is the whole of the analyst's action. It is `.disabled(true)` with `analyseUnavailable` as its help and its accessibility hint, which is `DESIGN.md` §3.4's dim-with-a-reason rather than an inert control — the refusal is the product's, not the campaign's — and the reason is that `PRD.md` §6 specifies a session analyst and nothing under `app/Sources` implements one. Three further declared readouts — `Analyst cadence`, `Analyst model`, `Second-opinion model` — have no counterpart at all: the build draws the panel's empty state where the design draws its configuration. The fifth declared control on that panel, `Insights window`, is NOT part of this defect and is recorded separately as a refusal: the window is fixed at 24 hours because the call log rotates and what a router can answer for is whatever survived, so a control offering seven days on a machine holding two would lie about its own range. That reasoning is already in the board's own header comment, which is why it is a stated reason rather than a finding. Recorded rather than trimmed, so five of SURF-026's seven declared controls sit in the denominator with a sentence each.

subject.source: app/Sources/RouterCore/Control/Describe.swift transportMembers; app/Sources/RouterCore/Control/ControlHandler.swift gate; src/control.ts is the reference half
subject.text: Found while building R22's redactor, filed rather than fixed. `Describe.row` emits `command` and `args` RAW, and `ControlHandler.gate` reads the token only for POST/DELETE/PATCH, so the complete command line of every stdio upstream is readable by anything that can open the loopback port. The same function is careful in the adjacent case — it emits `envKeys` and `headerKeys` and never a value, with B10's reasoning attached — so argv is the one credential-carrying position on that route that is published whole. It matters because argv IS a credential channel: `--token=`, `--api-key=` and a connection string with an inline password are ordinary MCP server invocations, and R22 scrubs args for exactly that reason. The exposure predates R22 and is not made worse by it: the bundle's args go through the value scrub, and this route's do not. NOT FIXED HERE, and the reason is a parity decision rather than effort. `GET /servers` is reference-diffed — `control-servers-get` in planning/parity/surface.tsv, verdict `proven` — so redacting args moves a surface R4 compares byte for byte, and the ungated GET is itself a ported defect this repository records rather than silently repairs. Closing it means changing both routers or declaring a divergence, and that is the owner's call. 2026-10-19 — FIXED IN BOTH ROUTERS by merge 74d15306 (Merge ai/argv-redact), whose subject records that GET /servers stops publishing secret-bearing argv. Unit evidence: ArgvRedactionTests (app/Tests/RouterCoreTests/ArgvRedactionTests.swift) and test/argv-redact.test.ts, with parity vectors in argv-redact.json. Verified 2026-10-19: the `ArgvRedactionTests` suite passed under `swift test`, and `node --test` on test/argv-redact.test.ts passed. Status is fixed · in-test. No campaign re-run is recorded against this row.
subject.title: GET /servers discloses every stdio upstream's full argv to an unauthenticated local caller

subject.evidence: Selecting Harnesses, Cleanup or Inbox through SelectionItemPattern.Select() leaves the window title, the caption band and the ENTIRE control-view tree byte-identical to the destination before it - the lane's fingerprint over the tree's accessible names is unchanged, which is why it is recorded as a COLLAPSE rather than as an empty board. The pane item itself does take the selection: SelectionItemPattern.Current.IsSelected reads True on all three. So the highlight moves and nothing behind it does. Order-independent: a reverse sweep, where every destination has a different predecessor, fails on exactly the same three. Six others - Discover, Servers, Activity, Checks, Insights, Settings - pass in both directions, so the harness, the actuation and the oracle all work.

subject.evidence: run-shell-lane.ps1 registered a fixed task name, MCPRouter-WINSHELL-AutomationPlaneLane. Two runners in separate worktrees called it seconds apart; `schtasks /Create /F` overwrote, and the first runner's `schtasks /Run` then printed "ERROR: The system cannot find the file specified" because the winner had already deleted the task on its way out. That wrapper sat for its full 900 s and reported NO VERDICT with an empty lane.log.

subject.evidence: The lane defaulted $ExePath to app\windows\MCPRouter.Shell\bin\x64\Debug\..., which is what `MSBuild -p:Platform=x64` writes. scripts/windows/build-shell.ps1 writes bin\Debug\..., and so does everything that reads it. On a tree built correctly seconds earlier the lane returned NO VERDICT and told the reader to go and build a shell that was already on disk. Its message printed a literal {0} where the path should have been, because the -f bound to the second half of a concatenated string rather than to the whole expression.

subject.evidence: Four claims about the ambient surface have no instrument on this machine. (1) AmbientPresentation.TrayToolTip is carried into the icon through NIM_MODIFY and Shell_NotifyIconGetRect returns a rectangle, never the tip, so the tip's text is the application's own account of itself. (2) A notification-area click is delivered to a window procedure and there is no out-of-process way to press it here - already recorded on DEF-101. (3) settings.ambientIcon.explorerRestart.baseline shows the reader can say no with nothing owning the icon, but nothing distinguishes a restored tray entry that is live from one the tray answers for out of HKCU\Control Panel\NotifyIconSettings, which is why DEF-300's arm passes with the re-add watchdog removed. (4) Nothing in the build constructs AmbientFlyoutView: it renders from the model it is handed rather than from literals now, but no operator can open it and no arm reads it.
subject.title: Nothing on this host can read a notification-area tooltip, press its icon, or tell a restored tray record from a live one - and the ambient flyout is not mounted at all

subject.evidence: `discover()` reads the git INDEX through `git ls-files` and separately walks the DISK through `os.walk` + `os.path.relpath`, then names the difference as briefs the gate did not read. `git ls-files` prints POSIX separators on every platform; `os.path.relpath` prints the platform's. On Windows the two sets therefore never intersect and the difference is the WHOLE corpus. Measured before the fix on this branch: the same run printed `brief discovery read 226 items of the git index ...; kept 219` and, four lines later, `219 brief(s) on disk are NOT in the index and are outside this verdict`, listing ten of them and `... and 209 more`. Both sentences cannot be true. The verdict and the partition were correct throughout - it is the accounting sentence above them that was false.

cell.role: whoever asks whether DEF-043's two elements are still missing

subject.note: SOURCE-ANALYSIS, AND THAT IS THE CEILING. This case reads Swift. It does not run the Mac app and does not photograph a board, and it cannot on this host: the shell is a SwiftPM target with no Windows build and `swift` is not on LUKESFF. A green means the code that draws DEF-043's two elements is present and composed the way DESIGN.md section 2 requires. It does NOT mean either element reached a screen, and it must not be read as closing DEF-043. M27 asked for on-glass coverage and that is still owed, on a Mac, through the campaign's own capture lane. WHAT IT ESTABLISHES. SidebarFoot renders the address on its `.address` case; the reading comes from LoopbackAddress.hostPort while the Settings endpoint row comes from LoopbackAddress.controlEndpoint, so the two cannot drift; no literal host:port appears in any of the four files that DISPLAY an address; and ReadoutCopy.childProcessesLabel is "Child processes" and Readout draws it - the string DEF-043 measured in 0 of 9 accessibility dumps. THE FIRST RUN FAILED AND THE INSTRUMENT WAS THE ONE AT FAULT. The honesty arm originally refused a literal host:port anywhere in either shell tree and reported `ShellClientFactory.shippingEndpoint`. Every reference to that symbol was then read: it is consumed by Choice.live, LiveControlAPIClient, ControlEventStream and the Release guard, and reaches no view. It is a dialled endpoint, not a displayed one, and the honesty rule governs what a user is told. The scope was corrected rather than the finding suppressed, and the sweep was NOT narrowed: it still covers both trees, and a literal outside the display files fails unless its symbol is declared with a reason - which plant Q6 watches. PLATFORM. macOS, and DEF-043 never said so, which is what the row cost to establish. M27-sidebar-foot-readout.md reads `Category: mac`, the evidence is nine accessibility dumps at 1156x680 against the Mac design of record, and the sidebar-foot specification is in DESIGN.md section 2 rather than in the Windows floor. The Windows shell's NavigationView declares no pane footer content at all and the Windows floor's own owed list names no sidebar foot, so the absence there is not a defect - Windows was never promised it. This case asserts nothing about Windows, because a check demanding Windows never grow a sidebar foot would redden on somebody adding a good thing.

J2. Every sidebar row is selected in turn and the effect is read in the RESTORATION STORE, which is a different channel from the one that struck: `ShellModel.selection`'s `didSet` calls `store.save(destination:)`, so a real selection leaves a value in a scratch `UserDefaults` suite that nothing in the test wrote, and that a relaunch reads. `model.selection == .servers` after `model.select(.servers)` was deliberately NOT used — it reads the property the call just wrote, which is the actuation side of the vacuous assertion (`references/inert-ui.md`, `detector-defects.md` §11). Each row is approached from a DIFFERENT destination, because `didSet` guards on `oldValue != selection` and a loop starting where the model boots would have the first row write nothing at all. The destination-collapse relation is asserted as a count rather than as seven separate greens: seven presses, seven DISTINCT persisted values, so a shell whose rows all led to one place fails on the cardinality. A second model built on the same store comes up where the last row left it, which is the read-back a relaunch actually performs. `Settings` is the eighth control and is not a destination: M15 moved it to a scene of its own, so the effect read is the installed opener firing exactly once AND the console's persisted destination not moving. Both halves, because an implementation that opened the scene and also selected a board would pass the first alone. LIMIT, stated rather than left implicit: a persisted destination proves the selection took. It does not prove a different board was DRAWN — SwiftUI's view tree is opaque to a SwiftPM test and `ContentZone`'s switch is unreachable from here. That half is CASE-0001's, on glass, and it is FAILING (DEF-058, DEF-059), so it counts nothing. This is the in-process half and says which half it is.

subject.text: Adding a 14th case to `Scenario` made `make test` fail with 31 issues, two of which cannot be true of the source: `Expectation failed: (… → .live) == (.live → .fixture(…cleanupSkills))` in ShellClientFactoryTests and TriageSourceGuardTests, both asserting a Release-posture guard that returns .live unconditionally. `git stash` of the two changed source files → 19 tests pass; unstash → the same failures return, which reads as a real regression. It is not. `Choice.live` is encoded in the spare inhabitants of `Scenario`'s tag, so a new Scenario case shifts that encoding, and stale MCPRouterUI object files compiled against the old layout compare a value that no longer means what they think. `rm -rf app/.build` then rebuild: 5/5 pass, then 1512/1512. The hazard for this campaign is the mirror case — a stale build can as easily produce a green — so any test evidence taken across an enum change is taken from a clean build. MITIGATED 2026-08-20: `app/Scripts/enum-layout-stamp.py` hashes the ordered case list of every enum in the package (212 of them) and removes `app/.build` when that hash moves; `make test` now depends on it. The stamp is the case lists rather than the source, so it holds still for an ordinary edit and for a `switch` over the enum — the false positive a naive grep for `^\s*case` would hit — and moves for an added or renamed case. Armed on all four: comment SAME, switch statement SAME, added Scenario case MOVED, renamed Scenario case MOVED, restore back to baseline. The SwiftPM behaviour itself is unchanged and still upstream; what is fixed is this repo's exposure to it.

subject.detail: `TypedEntryView` rendered eight styled boxes, a helper line and a submit button, and no input affordance of any kind — no TextField, no keypad, no focus state. `PairingCodeEntry` had carried `append(contentsOf:)` and `deleteBackward()` since it was written and nothing in the UI called either, so `.disabled(!entry.isComplete)` on the submit button could never become false. The typed path is the documented fallback for every camera state — the source cites A16 — and for `.restricted`, where iOS Settings is a dead end the user may not be able to clear, it is the *primary* recovery. So the one surface a user reaches by deliberately choosing it was the one that could not be completed. Fixed with a real `TextField` behind the boxes: it carries the system keyboard, hardware keys on iPad, paste and dictation, and it is what `app.textFields` resolves to on glass. Deliberately NOT `.textContentType(.oneTimeCode)` — that AutoFill reads codes out of Messages and Mail, and this code is read off the Mac's own screen, so it would offer suggestions that are always wrong. The boxes became decoration (`accessibilityHidden`) and the field is the single element labelled 'Pairing code', because `children: .ignore` on a display is right and on an editor strips the trait VoiceOver and XCUITest need. Approach checked against an out-of-family lane (grok-4.6, xhigh) before implementing; it named the same shape and the same reason for avoiding `.oneTimeCode`. Guarded by `PhoneSurfaceTests.testTypedEntryPublishesAFieldToTypeInto`, armed 20 Aug 2026.
